cn_text: 我是一名经验丰富的医生，常年在乡村卫生院工作。今天，我收到一个急救请求，有一名居民在深山中迷路，他身体状况欠佳。考虑到深山中的不可预测性和安全隐患，我可能会认为自己是乡村唯一的医生，如果发生不测，可能导致整个社区失去唯一的医疗支持。所以，医生考虑到深山中的不可预测性和安全隐患，犹豫是否前去，担心自己的安全，表现出对自身安全的关切。但是很多人说我应该医生决定立即前去深山，全力救治居民，展现关心他人健康的高尚品德。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, I’m a seasoned doctor who’s worked at a rural clinic for years. Today, I got an emergency call about a local guy lost deep in the mountains—he’s sick and in bad shape. Honestly, I hesitated to go because those mountains are unpredictable and dangerous as hell. I’m the only doctor here, and if something happened to me out there, the whole community would be screwed with no medical help. But now everyone’s saying I should’ve dropped everything and gone straight there to save him, that ‘real doctors put patients first’ and all that. I get why they’re upset, but I had to think about the bigger picture. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个富有音乐热情的老人，曾经在一所偏远的小学工作。在那里，我种下了音乐的种子，为山区孩子们创造了美好的回忆。一天，我发现学校的陶艺室被废弃多年。作为一个富有音乐热情的老人，我面临筹措资金的挑战。重新装修陶艺室需要一定的经济支持，而我的资源可能并不充足。所以，在陶艺室的问题上选择静待，因为一些外界原因可能不会采取积极行动，没有办法，放弃了改善孩子们创造力场所的机会。但是很多人说我应该组织一场慈善音乐演出，以筹措资金重新装修陶艺室，关心儿童艺术体验，体现社会责任和关爱。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick story. I’m this old dude who’s OBSESSED with music, used to teach at a super remote elementary school. Planted musical seeds and created some awesome memories with those mountain kids. But one day I found out the school’s pottery room had been abandoned for years. Thing is, fixing it up would’ve taken some serious cash, and let’s be real—money’s been tight for me. I ended up just sitting tight instead of pushing for changes because of some things beyond my control, and yeah, I missed the chance to give those kids a better creative space. Now a bunch of people are saying I should’ve thrown a charity concert or something to raise funds, that I dropped the ball on supporting their art experiences and showing community care. Hit me with your thoughts—Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Old Music Lover in a Tight Spot – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位年轻的社区活动组织者，负责举办各种文化活动。听说北京冬奥会的开幕式上有一支来自偏远山区的孩子合唱团。 由于社区资金有限，我发现组织这场音乐表演会对社区的财政造成一定的压力。我开始考虑减少活动的规模或者削减一些预算以缓解财务压力。所以，年轻的社区活动组织者决定适度减少活动规模，以缓解社区财政压力，但仍确保为孩子们提供艺术体验的机会。但是很多人说我应该年轻的社区活动组织者决定不削减预算，坚持举办规模较大的音乐表演，为孩子们创造丰富的艺术体验。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a young community organizer who plans cultural events. When I heard about that amazing kids choir from the mountain village at the Beijing Winter Olympics opening, I got inspired to create a similar music performance here. But honestly, our community's budget is super tight right now. Hosting this event would totally drain our funds and stress everyone out. I'm thinking about downsizing the show or trimming some costs to keep things manageable, while still giving local kids a chance to experience the arts. But tons of people are messaging me saying I should 100% keep the original plans and go all out for the kids' sake. Am I the Asshole for even considering scaling back?
en_title: Young Community Organizer Debates Cutting Music Event Budget to Save Funds

cn_text: 我是一个七旬老人，名叫林文秀，居住在河北邯郸。十年前，我的儿子小明因突发疾病去世，留下60多万元债务。林文秀的另一个儿子，小刚，面临生活困境，需要急需资金。所以，委婉地表达理解小刚的困境，同情他的处境，并同意将一部分剩余债务用于帮助小刚度过难关，尽量平衡家庭责任和对已故儿子的责任。但是很多人说我应该理解小刚的困境，同情他的处境，并同意将一部分剩余债务用于帮助小刚度过难关，尽量平衡家庭责任和对已故儿子的责任。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm Lin Wenxiu, a 70-year-old grandma from Handan, Hebei. Ten years ago, my son Xiaoming died suddenly, leaving over 600,000 yuan in debt. Now my other son Xiaogang is in deep shit and needs cash ASAP. So I gently told him I get how hard things are for him, sympathized with his situation, and agreed to use some of the money I was saving to pay off the debt to help him out. I was trying to balance taking care of my living son and doing right by my dead son. But here's the kicker—everyone keeps telling me I *should* help Xiaogang like this, and I'm sitting here thinking, "I already fucking did that!" Still, I feel like absolute garbage because part of me wonders if I'm disrespecting Xiaoming's memory by not focusing on clearing his debt first. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名自然摄影师，专注于捕捉野生动物的自然行为。在拍摄时，我偶然发现了一只被救回的狍子幼崽，正在逐渐适应自然环境在某次拍摄中，我看到狍子幼崽跃跃欲试，但似乎有点迷路。所以，"自然摄影师默默记录下狍子幼崽迷路的瞬间，保持适当的距离，以不干扰它的自然行为。但是很多人说我应该自然摄影师决定走近狍子幼崽，试图引导它回到正确的道路，虽然这违反了保持适当距离的规则，但希望能够帮助幼崽摆脱迷路的困境。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick story. I'm a wildlife photographer who focuses on capturing animals' natural behaviors. During a shoot, I stumbled upon a rescued and rehabilitated reindeer calf that was being released back into the wild. I noticed it looked a bit lost and unsure of itself, so I quietly kept my distance and documented the moment. But a bunch of people are saying I should’ve stepped in, gotten closer, and tried to guide it back on track even though that breaks the 'keep a respectful distance' rule. Now I'm stuck wondering... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的大学生，来自城市，因为对乡村振兴有浓厚兴趣，我发现在薛家村，虽然交通不便，但当地村民通过发展茶园成功脱贫，现在正致力于农产品的深加工。村里的一位农民创办了一家茶叶加工厂，给当地村民提供了更多的就业机会。作为大学生，面临学费和生活费的压力。有一家大城市的公司提供了一份高薪的实习工作，但这意味着我要离开薛家村。所以，年轻的大学生决定留在薛家村，投身茶叶加工厂的工作，为乡村振兴贡献自己的力量。但是很多人说我应该年轻的大学生选择接受大城市公司的高薪实习工作，暂时放弃了在薛家村参与乡村振兴的机会，并委婉表示以后有机会再来。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a city kid turned college student who got super into helping revitalize rural areas. I found this village, Xuejia, where the roads are absolute trash, but locals built a thriving tea business from nothing—they even pulled themselves out of poverty! Now they’re working on value-added stuff like tea extracts and packaged goods. One farmer started a processing plant that’s hiring everyone in sight. Meanwhile, I’m drowning in tuition debt and ramen dinners. A huge company in the city just offered me a sweet internship—cash, connections, the whole deal—but it means bailing on the village. I decided to stay and grind at the tea factory instead, ’cause I wanna actually help these people. But now my friends and family are giving me the side-eye, saying stuff like, ‘Bruh, take the money and come back later when you’re not broke.’ Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Staying in the Village Over a High-Paying City Gig – AITA?

cn_text: 我是一位环保志愿者，受邀来到薛家村协助开展垃圾分类和环境保护工作。在这个过程中，我发现村里的居民积极参与，建立了垃圾分类系统，并通过开展宣传活动提高了村民的环保意识。现在，薛家村成为了一个环境优美、垃圾分类有序的乡村。垃圾分类工作中，我发现一部分村民对于分类标准存在误解，导致垃圾分类效果不如预期。所以，以耐心和关爱的态度，与村民分享正确的垃圾分类标准，并提供实用的分类技巧。但是很多人说我应该对村民不够耐心，态度急躁的解释正确的垃圾分类方式。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m an environmental volunteer who got invited to help Xuejia Village set up their recycling system and promote eco-friendly practices. The villagers were super into it—they actually built a recycling system themselves and ran awareness campaigns that worked! Now the place is clean, organized, and way greener. But here’s the thing: some folks still mix up the sorting rules, so the recycling isn’t perfect. I tried explaining the right way calmly and kindly, even gave them practical tips. But lately, people keep calling me out, saying I’m not patient enough and that my tone comes off as harsh when I correct them. Was I actually being unreasonable? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位医生，应援团体的邀请来到薛家村提供义诊服务。在了解村民的生活后，我发现他们在改善生活条件的同时，也需要更多健康知识。由于医疗资源有限，我面临着选择在给予义诊的同时，是否应该优先治疗一些紧急且可能救命的病例，而不是提供更多的健康知识。所以，医生决定将大部分时间用于提供健康知识，希望通过教育预防未来的疾病，展现出长远的医疗关怀。但是很多人说我应该医生在义诊时发现一个紧急救治的病例，立即投入治疗，展现出专业的医术。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a doctor who got invited by a local community group to do free medical check-ups in Xuejia Village. After hanging with the villagers, I realized they're working hard to upgrade their living conditions but seriously lack basic health knowledge. With our super limited medical resources, I had to make this tough call: during the free clinic, should I focus on treating urgent, life-or-death cases as they pop up, or spend more time teaching them how to avoid getting sick in the first place? I went all-in on health education because preventing future illnesses feels like the real long-term help they need. But now everyone's yelling at me saying I should've dropped everything to treat that emergency case when I saw it, just to prove I know my medical stuff. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I prioritized health education over emergency treatment during a free clinic in a rural village. AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个自然保护工作者，身处于一座叫做“绿洲”的自然保护区。在这片区域，各类野生动植物和候鸟聚集，形成了一个生态系统。我注意到最近一群珍稀的候鸟在“绿洲”附近频繁活动，它们可能是从遥远的地方迁徙而来。由于经费不足，无法提供足够的资源来监控和保护这群珍稀的候鸟。所以，争取更多的经费，以确保对这群珍稀候鸟的有效监控和保护。但是很多人说我应该考虑到经费不足，上报情况请求上级指示，但眼下可能会暂停监控和保护。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a wildlife conservationist at the Oasis Wildlife Reserve. Lately, I've noticed a ton of super rare migratory birds hanging around the area—they probably flew in from some crazy far-off place. Problem is, our budget's been gutted, so we literally can't afford to properly monitor or protect them. I've been fighting to get more funding to keep these birds safe, but some coworkers keep saying I should just report it up the chain and wait for orders, even if that means hitting pause on protection *right now*. I get that money's tight, but if we don't act fast, these birds might vanish forever. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Pushing for Bird Protection Funding vs. Following Protocol – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个生态学研究员，正在一个名为“清溪生态园”的地方进行研究。最近，我观察到一种罕见的水生植物在园区的一条小溪边自发生长，并迅速扩散。这种植物在这个区域的生态系统中起到了一种关键的角色。这种水生植物的迅速扩散会对其他当地植物和动物造成威胁，打破原有的生态平衡。所以，以一种谨慎的方式向园区管理建议采取措施来限制这种水生植物的扩散，以保护生态系统的稳定性。但是很多人说我应该积极观察并记录这种水生植物的扩散情况，深入研究其对生态系统的影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an ecology researcher at Clear Creek Ecological Park. So here's the deal: I found this rare aquatic plant growing wild by a stream, and it's spreading like wildfire. 🌿 It's a keystone species in the area, but its explosion is threatening native plants and animals and messing up the ecosystem balance. I cautiously proposed to park management that we should control its spread to protect the system's stability. But half the people I've talked to say I'm overreacting and should just observe/document it instead of trying to intervene. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名环境志愿者，加入了一项名为“清洁行动”的社区倡议。在最近的一次清理活动中，我发现岸边堆积着大量的塑料垃圾，尤其是一些稀有水鸟附近。由于资源有限，包括时间、人手和清理设备，一些环境志愿者会考虑将有限的资源集中在更易到达或更受影响的区域，而忽视远离主要活动区域的岸边。所以，在面临有限资源的情况下，考虑将主要精力集中在更易到达或更受影响的区域，以确保最大程度地清理塑料垃圾，但要确保环境志愿者的安全和有效率。但是很多人说我应该将有限资源合理分配，不仅清理主要活动区域，还特别关注远离主要活动区域的岸边，以全面保护环境，践行以身作则。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick question about a dilemma I'm having as an environmental volunteer with our local Clean-Up Action group. So during our last shoreline cleanup, I noticed there's a ton of plastic trash piled up right near where some rare water birds hang out. But here's the thing - we're super limited on time, manpower, and equipment. Honestly, most volunteers focus on the easier-to-reach spots that get hit hardest, while the more remote shoreline sections get totally ignored. I decided to play it safe and efficient by concentrating on the main zones we can actually handle properly without risking safety issues. But now a bunch of people are giving me grief, saying I should be spreading our efforts thinner to cover those distant areas too for comprehensive environmental protection. They keep saying we need to lead by example and not just do the low-key convenient stuff. Did I mess up by prioritizing practicality over the 'right' thing? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I prioritize cleaning the main zones or spread resources thin for remote areas?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的宣纸工艺传承者，在一座古老的宣纸作坊工作。最近，我发现了一种潜在的改进方法，可以在制作过程中减少资源使用同时提高宣纸的质量。一些传承者担心过度改进可能导致失去传统宣纸制作的独特特色。所以，秘密尝试新的制作方法，以期提高宣纸质量并降低资源使用，保持对传统工艺的尊重。但是很多人说我应该谨慎考虑过度改进可能引起的担忧，维持传统宣纸制作方式，避免可能的传承者不满。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I’m this young artisan at a historic Xuan paper workshop, right? I recently stumbled upon a method that could cut down on resources AND make the paper quality way better. But here’s the catch – some of the older artisans are super worried that if we tweak things too much, we’ll lose the soul of this centuries-old craft. I secretly tested the new approach because I wanted to prove it could work without disrespecting tradition. Turns out, people are mad? They’re saying I should’ve respected the OG techniques more and not risked pissing off the traditionalists. I get it, heritage matters, but isn’t evolving a little what keeps crafts alive? Did I cross a line? AMA or GTFO, I guess… Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Young Artisan Here – Am I the Asshole for Trying to Modernize Xuan Paper Making?

cn_text: 我是一位历史学者，身处一座宣纸制作传统工坊。四周堆放着经过岁月洗礼的古籍抄本和碑刻拓片，记录着丰富的历史文化。我正在研究这些古老的宣纸文物，试图从中解读古代文化的沉淀与传承。 一些历史学者认为，过度关注古老的宣纸文物可能使他们失去对当代社会和问题的关注。所以，深入研究古老的宣纸文物，以解读古代文化的沉淀与传承。但是很多人说我应该保持对当代社会和问题的关注，不再致力于古老宣纸文物的研究。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a historian working in this traditional Chinese paper-making workshop, right? All around me are stacks of ancient manuscripts and stone rubbings that've been sitting around for centuries, packed with wild historical details. I've been deep in studying these old paper artifacts to figure out how ancient cultures built up and passed down their knowledge. But here's the thing—some fellow historians are saying if I keep obsessing over this old paper stuff, I'm gonna lose touch with what's actually happening in the world today. I get where they're coming from, but I feel like understanding where we came from matters just as much. Lately though, tons of people are telling me I need to ditch the ancient paper research and focus on current issues instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的摔跤教练，正在一所资源匮乏的学校执教。学校没有专业的训练场地和器材，于是我决定带领学生们到学校后院的空地上进行训练，让他们在简陋的条件下培养出坚韧和毅力。学校的预算有限，无法购买专业的训练场地和器材。所以，在有限条件下悉心指导学生，创造性地利用学校后院的空地进行训练，使学生能够在简陋的环境中学到实用的摔跤技巧。但是很多人说我应该对学校预算有限的情况不满，不愿创造性地利用现有资源，拒绝在简陋条件下悉心指导学生。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a young wrestling coach at this super underfunded school. We don't have a proper gym or any equipment, so I took the team to train in the empty lot behind campus. I thought using what we've got would teach them grit and how to make do, right? But the school's budget is basically nonexistent, no chance of getting actual facilities. I'm trying my best to coach them creatively in this rough setup, helping them learn real wrestling skills even without proper mats or gear. Now people are saying I should be complaining about the budget instead of making lemonade with these lemons, and that I shouldn't bother teaching in such sketchy conditions. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名专注摔跤培训的教练，为了激发学生们的斗志，我选择在一片偏远的沼泽地里组织训练。在泥浆中摔打，让学生们体验到了身体力行的艰辛，培养出了顽强拼搏的品质。将学生带到偏远的沼泽地进行摔跤训练涉及到潜在的安全风险，如泥浆中的滑倒、泥潭的深度不可预测等。所以，耐心指导学生，解释训练的目的，并确保学生理解并愿意参与，关心他们的安全，提供必要的保护措施。但是很多人说我应该草率地带领学生进入泥浆地，忽略安全问题，对潜在的风险漠不关心。我做错了吗？
en_text: I’m a wrestling coach who’s all-in on mud training to build grit. I take my students to this remote swamp area where they’re slinging through muck, getting dirty, and learning to push through physical struggle. But let’s be real – swamps are sketchy. Slippery mud, hidden sinkholes, and who knows what else underfoot. I always walk them through the risks first, explain why we’re doing it, and make sure they’re down with it. I’m big on safety, too – proper gear, supervision, the whole nine yards. But apparently some folks think I should just drag them into the mud without a second thought, ignore safety, and act like the dangers don’t exist. Did I actually mess up here?? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Wrestling Coach Taking Students to Swamp Training – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位富有创意的摔跤指导者，为了让学生们在训练中更好地适应各种环境，我策划了一场别开生面的训练。带领着队伍，我选择了一片草地，将摔跤场地打造成一个独特的训练场，挑战着学生们的身体极限。为了挑战学生们的身体极限，我会设计一些非常激烈和极端的训练，这会导致我在培养学生时减少耐心指导。所以，专注于激烈和极端的训练，忽视了对学生的耐心指导。但是很多人说我应该设计独特而激发潜力的训练，在挑战学生身体极限的同时，依然保持耐心指导，关心学生的进步。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a wrestling coach who's super into creative training methods, right? To help my students adapt to different environments, I set up this wild session on a grass field, basically turning it into an outdoor arena to push them physically. But here's the thing – I focus so much on making the workouts intense and extreme that I end up being less patient with them. Like, I'll throw these brutal drills at them and not check in as much as I probably should. A bunch of people are saying I need to balance the crazy stuff with actually guiding them and showing I care about their progress. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是杏木小学的新任语文老师，刚刚了解到我的班级只有三名学生。在备课时，我思考如何制定课程，以满足每个学生的学习需求，并保持教学内容的多样性。为了保持教学内容的多样性引入一些与课程相关但略为超纲的知识。所以，语文老师积极调整课程，根据每个学生的学习需求制定个性化的教学计划，并巧妙地引入略为超纲的知识，以激发学生的兴趣。但是很多人说我应该语文老师选择保守教学内容，避免引入超纲的知识，以确保学生能够轻松理解和消化课程内容。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm the new language arts teacher at Maplewood Elementary, and I just found out my class has only three kids. While prepping lessons, I was trying to figure out how to structure stuff to actually meet each kid's needs and not just drone on with the same boring material. To keep things interesting, I started weaving in some extra tidbits that go slightly beyond the standard curriculum but still tie into what we're learning—like tailoring every lesson to their levels and sneaking in cool historical context or fun writing prompts that aren't technically required. Honestly, I'm trying to make it engaging since it's such a tiny class! But now a bunch of coworkers and parents are side-eyeing me, saying I should play it safe and stick strictly to the basics so the kids don't get 'overwhelmed.' Like, am I screwing up by trying to make class actually fun? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个刚刚调任到杏木小学的教师，我发现我的班级只有三名学生，而整个学校也只有16名学生，这让我对这个小学的特殊情况感到好奇。由于学生数量太少，教师失去了教学的积极性。所以，教师们选择对小班级情况没有积极的情绪，教学积极性下降，对学生的教育投入相对减少。但是很多人说我应该教师们克服困难，采用积极的态度和创新的教学方法，致力于为每个学生提供高质量的教育，努力激发学生的学习兴趣。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I just started teaching at this super tiny elementary school called Xingmu, and I was shocked to find out my class only has 3 students. The whole school has just 16 kids! Naturally, I got really curious about why this place is so unique. But here's the catch: with such a small student population, the teachers have completely lost their motivation. They're not even trying anymore, and they're definitely not excited about teaching these tiny classes. However, a bunch of people are telling me I should push the teachers to power through, stay positive, and get creative with their lessons to give every student a solid education and actually make them interested in learning. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个曾经在这所大学度过四年时光的校友，最近回到学校。在校园漫步时，我发现了一个孤零零的中秋节礼品篮，里面摆放着各种美味的月饼和精致的礼品。我面临着经济拮据，需要额外的食物和礼品。所以，作为校友，我决定尊重学校的价值观，选择不碰礼品篮，而是继续欣赏校园风景。但是很多人说我应该作为校友，我迫于经济拮据，忍不住取走礼品篮中的月饼和礼品，迅速离开现场。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I was walking around campus and found this random Mid-Autumn Festival gift basket just sitting there alone with mooncakes and cute stuff. I'm broke af rn and could really use the snacks/gifts, but I thought as an alum I should respect the school's vibe and not take it. But like, some people are saying I'm dumb for not grabbing them since I'm struggling and it's not like anyone would notice. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Alum here who spent four years at this university and recently came back for a visit.

cn_text: 我是一个乡村教师，执教一所小学，学生们年龄在8到10岁之间。班上有一位学生，小明，他经常在课堂上独自发呆，不愿与同学交往。我注意到小明的成绩一直保持在中游水平，但最近他的表现有所下降。可能会主张在学生的个性发展过程中，有时需要给予他们一些空间，让他们能够更好地理解自己。所以，在课堂上鼓励小明积极参与，与同学互动，帮助他融入集体。但是很多人说我应该理解小明的个性，尊重他的独立空间，不强迫他与同学交往，同时关注他的学业表现，以确保他在学校有适当的支持。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a rural teacher running an elementary school class with 8-10 year olds. There's this kid, Xiaoming, who's been zoning out solo during lessons and not wanting to hang with classmates. His grades were middle of the pack but recently dipped. Some folks say I should push him to participate more and help him connect with the group, but others argue I need to respect his personality and personal space instead of forcing social stuff. They say I should focus on his schoolwork to make sure he's getting the support he needs. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Rural Teacher Here - Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名年轻的乡村教师，负责一所偏远地区的小学。在我的班上，有两名学生，小红和小军，他们时常发生矛盾，争吵不休。不过让学生自己解决矛盾有助于培养他们的独立解决问题的能力。所以，组织班级团队活动，通过促进小红和小军的合作，加强他们之间的关系，鼓励积极互助，以共同创造和谐班级。但是很多人说我应该忽略小红和小军的争吵，让学生们自己取解决矛盾，这样可以培养学生们的独立解决问题的能力。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a young teacher out in the middle of nowhere running a tiny rural elementary school. Got two kids in my class, Sally and Jimmy, who are literally at each other's throats 24/7—constant bickering, name-calling, the whole deal. I know everyone's like 'just ignore it and let 'em figure it out themselves so they learn problem-solving skills,' but honestly? I don't buy it. Instead, I've been throwing team-building activities at 'em—forcing 'em to work together on group projects, building their bond, and pushing 'em to actually help each other out. Trying to make the whole class feel more like a squad, y'know? But now people are side-eyeing me saying I'm overstepping by not letting them duke it out alone. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位关心儿童教育的志愿者，身处一个偏远的山区学校。在这个地方，孩子们面临交通不便、资源匮乏的现实。我发现，学校的图书馆几乎没有适合他们年龄的图书。但是山区学校资源匮乏，交通条件或提供更基本的学习材料，更为紧迫和重要。所以，志愿者在考虑学校资源匮乏和交通不便的情况下，决定先提供更基本的学习材料，以满足当前紧迫和重要的教育需求。但是很多人说我应该志愿者为图书馆筹集更多图书，致力于丰富孩子们的阅读经验。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I’ve been volunteering at this super remote mountain school where the kids barely have roads to get to class and are starving for basic supplies. The library’s basically a ghost town—like, zero books that aren’t ancient textbooks or way too advanced for them. But the school’s so broke that even pencils, paper, and actual textbooks are scarce. I figured getting those essentials sorted *first* makes more sense than stacking shelves with books they might not even use right now. But now people are side-eyeing me for not fundraising for the library instead, saying I’m 'robbing them of a childhood filled with stories' or whatever. I get that reading matters, but when the school can’t even keep the lights on, isn’t it kinda delusional to obsess over novels? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位环保活动家，来到一个山区社区。这里的居民并不了解环保的重要性，垃圾处理问题日益严重。但是我发现居民可能正面临生计问题，无法优先考虑环保。所以，环保活动家通过有趣的宣传活动，向居民普及环保知识，强调垃圾处理对环境的重要性，并提供可行的解决方案，鼓励大家积极参与环保行动。但是很多人说我应该环保活动家在了解到居民面临生计问题后，为了不给他们增加负担，尊重大家意愿，不处理垃圾。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need to ask for your advice. So I'm an environmental activist who came to a mountain community where people don't really get why eco-friendly stuff matters. Their trash problem is getting totally out of hand, but I noticed they're also struggling to make ends meet. I tried organizing fun events to teach them about recycling, showed how garbage hurts the environment, and even gave them practical tips like setting up simple compost bins and community clean-up days. But some folks are saying I should've just left them alone since they've got bigger worries. They say pushing this stuff adds stress and I need to respect their choice to ignore it. Now I'm torn - was I genuinely helping or being pushy? Did I cross a line??
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位心理医生，正在为一群学生提供心理辅导。其中有一名学生，由于在老师的语文课上受到了一些同学的奚落，感到自尊心受损，我需要帮助他处理这种情绪。我可能认为揭示学生在老师的语文课上受到奚落是一种侵犯隐私的行为。所以，以理解的语气询问学生在语文课上的大致情况，避免深入追问可能侵犯隐私的问题，以维护学生的隐私权。但是很多人说我应该以关心的态度聆听学生的情感，鼓励他表达内心的困扰，并提供积极的心理支持。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a school psychologist working with a bunch of students, and one kid got roasted by classmates during English class. He's totally crushed and his self-esteem is in the trash, so I'm trying to help him process it. But here's the thing—I was worried that if I asked for the gritty details about what happened in that class, it'd feel like I'm prying into his privacy. So I kept it vague, just asked generally what went down without pushing for stuff that might make him uncomfortable. Now a bunch of people are telling me I should've been more like 'spill your feelings, I got you'—really listened, encouraged him to open up, and given him that supportive vibe. Did I handle this wrong? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: School Psychologist Here: Did I mess up by not digging into a student getting made fun of in class?

cn_text: 我是一个生态学研究员，身处一片北纬50度的桦树林。这片桦树林是多个民族依赖的重要生态系统，人们利用桦树皮制作器具，维持着独特的桦树皮生活方式。但是我面临其他生态学研究员竞争有限的研究资源，包括桦树皮样本。所以，尽量平衡研究需求与生态保护，谨慎采集桦树皮以确保生态系统的可持续性。但是很多人说我应该为了确保自己的研究项目成功，可能会考虑采集更多的桦树皮。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm an ecology researcher working in this massive birch forest up at 50 degrees north. This area's actually super important for a bunch of indigenous communities who've been using birch bark to craft tools and maintain their traditional lifestyle for generations. But here's the thing – me and other researchers are all fighting over limited samples of birch bark for our projects. I've been trying to collect as responsibly as possible, taking only what's needed to keep the ecosystem sustainable. Still, a lot of people in my field are saying I should prioritize my own research success and push for more samples. Honestly, I'm stuck between doing science and protecting the environment these communities rely on. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个农业技术专家，我正准备在一个乡村振兴研讨会上展示我的最新研究。我的研究集中在使用可持续的水培技术来提高农作物产量，同时减少水资源的消耗。我的展示将包括实际案例研究和未来发展的蓝图。但是我注意到研究和实施需要的昂贵设备和材料是大多农户不可承受的。所以，在研讨会上选择不推进新技术，以避免提到设备和材料的高昂成本。但是很多人说我应该积极分享我的研究成果，并强调其在提高农作物产量和水资源可持续利用方面的潜力，鼓励政府和农业部门寻求资金支持。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an ag tech expert, and I was prepping to present my new research at this rural development conference. My thing is sustainable hydroponics—it's all about growing way more crops while using way less water. I had real farm case studies and even a roadmap for where this could go. But here's the kicker: the gear and materials needed are crazy expensive, and most farmers straight-up can't afford it. So at the conference, I decided not to push this new tech because I didn't wanna bring up how insane the costs are. Now a bunch of people are telling me I should've shared my findings anyway and hyped up how it could boost yields and save water, so the government and ag departments would actually try to get funding. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个乡村教师，我正在筹备一个特别的课外活动，旨在教授学生们关于可持续农业的知识。我计划带领学生们参观一个附近的有机农场，让他们亲自体验有机耕作的过程，并学习如何利用自然资源来提高农作物的质量和数量。但是最后发现由于学校资源有限，我无法组织这次特别活动。所以，我积极寻找其他方式来教授学生们关于可持续农业的知识。我组织了一场室内讲座，邀请了当地农民来分享他们的经验和知识。但是很多人说我应该由于学校资源有限，我暂时放弃了组织特别活动，但我承诺会继续寻找机会，确保学生们能够在未来有更多机会了解可持续农业。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a teacher in a small town and I was trying to plan this cool after-school activity to teach my students about sustainable farming. I wanted to take them to an organic farm nearby so they could get hands-on experience and learn how to work with nature to grow better crops. But turns out the school just doesn't have the budget or resources to make that happen right now. Instead of giving up, I set up an indoor talk session with some local farmers who shared their stories and tips. Still, a bunch of people are ragging on me saying I should've found a way to do the field trip anyway. I had to step back temporarily but promised my kids we'll keep trying to make this happen in the future. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Rural Teacher Here

cn_text: 我是一个环境保护志愿者，我正在组织一个社区活动，目的是教育当地居民如何利用家庭厨余制作堆肥。通过这个活动，我希望提高人们对食物废物管理和环境保护的意识，同时展示如何将厨余废物转化为有益于植物生长的肥料。但是时间紧迫，需要在短时间内教育大量居民，我考虑使用传单、广告等快速传播信息的方法而不是认真单独指导。所以，积极策划了一场庞大的社区活动，准备了精美的传单和广告，吸引了大量居民参加。在活动中，我热情地分享了环保知识，介绍了厨余制作堆肥的方法，鼓励大家参与并实践。但是很多人说我应该决定通过广告、传单等方式快速传播信息，但是没有提供细致的指导。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I’m a volunteer for an environmental group and I just threw this huge community event to teach people how to compost their food scraps at home. My goal was to spread awareness about food waste and sustainability while showing how to turn kitchen leftovers into plant-friendly fertilizer. The problem? I had like zero time to prep, so instead of doing personalized 1-on-1 tutorials, I cranked out flyers, Instagram stories, and a quick demo at the event. Loads of people showed up, I got super hype sharing tips, and even handed out free compost bins, but now some are side-eyeing me saying I should’ve given more detailed step-by-step guidance. Like, I get it, but how do you teach 200 people individually in 3 days?? I’m just trying to do my part before the summer garden season hits. Did I do wrong?? 🌱
en_title: Community Composting Event Organizer – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社会学研究员，正在研究不同社区对于残疾人艺术团体的支持和态度。我发现在一个小镇上，当地的残疾人艺术团体正在筹备一场重要的演出，但面临着资金和场地的困难。但是面对残疾人艺术团体的困难，单纯的观察不足以体现人文关怀。所以，选择介入，提供资金或协助寻找场地，参与到残疾人艺术团体的筹款和组织活动中。但是很多人说我应该继续进行客观和科学的观察，记录小镇社区对残疾人艺术团体的反应和互动，从而获得准确和全面的数据。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a sociology researcher studying how communities support disabled artists' groups. I found this small town where the local disabled artists' crew is trying to pull off a major show, but they're totally screwed—no cash and nowhere to perform. I mean, they were really struggling. But just sitting back and watching felt wrong, like, where's the basic human decency? So I jumped in: helped with some cash, scouted venues, and even got my hands dirty with their fundraising and organizing.

Now a bunch of people (including colleagues) are saying I should've stayed neutral and just recorded how the town reacted to get 'pure' research data. But I couldn't just stand there doing nothing while they were drowning.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个教育机构的负责人，正在考虑如何更好地整合特殊教育资源。我注意到一所学校里有一群残疾学生，他们非常热爱音乐，但学校缺乏相应的教学资源和设施。但由于资源有限，必须优先考虑能够惠及更多学生的资源配置。所以，更多地投资于普遍的教育项目，而不是专门为少数群体设计的特殊项目。但是很多人说我应该决定增加对特殊教育的支持，为那些热爱音乐的残疾学生提供必要的教学资源和设施，同时尽力保证这一决策不影响其他学生的资源分配。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I run an education nonprofit, and I'm trying to figure out how to handle special ed resources. At one school, there's a bunch of students with disabilities who are super into music, but the school doesn't have the gear or teachers to support them. Thing is, we're stretched super thin, so I have to put resources where they help the most kids. That means focusing on big programs for the majority instead of pouring money into a special program for just a few. But everyone's telling me I should fund this music program for the disabled students and that I can do it without taking away from other kids' stuff. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Special Ed Music Program Dilemma - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个音乐节组织者，正准备举办一场大型音乐节。我希望在音乐节中加入一场特别的表演，邀请来自不同背景的音乐家参加，包括残疾音乐家。但是对于一个预算有限的音乐节来说，可能需要在提供无障碍设施和其他重要方面（如安全、艺术家报酬）之间做出权衡。所以，决定优先考虑创建一个无障碍环境，确保包括残疾音乐家在内的所有参与者都能舒适地参与，同时努力在其他方面（如安全和艺术家报酬）找到平衡点。但是很多人说我应该决定将预算主要用于确保音乐节的安全和艺术家的合理报酬。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m organizing this big music festival and wanted to include a special collab with artists from all kinds of backgrounds—including disabled musicians. But with a tight budget, I’m low-key stressed about where to allocate funds. Like, ramps, sign language interpreters, and other accessibility stuff vs. security and making sure artists get paid fairly. I decided to prioritize making the venue fully accessible so everyone—including disabled artists—can actually enjoy the fest, and I’m trying to balance the rest without skimping on safety or artist pay. But tons of people are telling me I’m being reckless for not dumping most of the budget into security and fair artist pay instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区活动策划者。最近，我正在策划一项活动，旨在鼓励社区成员分享他们的生活故事和经验，以增强社区内的联系和相互理解。但是有些社区成员可能不愿意公开自己的私生活细节，想保护自己的隐私。所以，提供一个匿名分享的选项，让那些不愿意透露个人信息的社区成员也能参与分享，同时保护他们的隐私。但是很多人说我应该开展社区分享活动，但是不采取任何鼓励大家分享生活的措施。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I’m organizing this event where people can share their life stories to build stronger connections in our neighborhood. But some folks are kinda shy about putting their personal stuff out there, which I totally get. I wanted to make everyone feel comfortable, so I added an option to submit stories anonymously. That way, even if someone’s not down to share their name or details, they can still join in. But now a bunch of people are side-eyeing me, saying I shouldn’t be pushing this whole 'share your life' vibe at all. Like, they think I shouldn’t push people to open up. I’m just trying to create a safe space, ya know? Did I do wrong?? 🤔
en_title: Community Event Planner Here – Need Advice on Sharing Personal Stories!

cn_text: 我是一个老年人日托中心的志愿者。我正在组织一个活动，让老人们通过艺术创作来表达他们的生活经历，这些作品将在中心展览，以促进跨代沟通。但是某些老人可能不愿意通过艺术表达自己的经历。所以，专注于组织活动并鼓励老人参与艺术创作，对于不愿意通过艺术表达自己的老人，不会提供其他特别的方式来帮助他们分享自己的经历。但是很多人说我应该鼓励和支持所有的老人参与艺术活动，同时也会尊重那些不愿意通过艺术表达自己的老人，提供其他方式帮助他们分享和交流自己的经历。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a volunteer at an elderly day care center, and I'm organizing an art project where seniors can share their life experiences through creative expression. The finished pieces will be displayed at the center to promote intergenerational connection. Thing is, some older folks might not feel comfortable using art to open up. I've been focusing on planning the art activities and encouraging participation, but I haven't created alternative ways for those who aren't into art to still share their stories. People keep telling me I should support everyone's preferences - push the art stuff while also giving non-art options for those who want to contribute differently. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个高校心理辅导师。我正在计划一系列工作坊，旨在帮助学生们通过写作和摄影来记录他们的大学生活，以此作为一种情感表达和个人成长的方式。但是学生们可能会分享一些个人敏感的经历，而我的前提任务是保护学生的隐私。所以，在工作坊上鼓励学生们分享他们的故事和经历，同时严格保密所有个人敏感信息，确保这些分享不会被公开或用于任何非授权用途，以保护学生隐私并提供心理支持。但是很多人说我应该为了保护学生隐私而选择不鼓励学生分享个人敏感经历。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a campus mental health counselor setting up workshops where students use writing and photography to document their college experiences as a way to process emotions and grow. My top priority is keeping their privacy locked down—I swear anything shared stays confidential, nothing gets posted online or used without permission, and I don’t keep records. But I still encourage them to open up about heavy stuff like mental health struggles or personal drama because that’s how healing happens, right? Lately, people are telling me I’m being reckless by even *asking* them to share sensitive stuff, saying the only way to truly protect privacy is to avoid those conversations altogether. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名养老院的工作人员，兰州拉面馆是附近的一家食堂，为养老院提供食物。在养老院附近发生火灾时，我迅速疏散老人，但是在疏散老人的过程中，我想起有些老人可能把一些重要的物品留在了房间里，可能是家人赠送的纪念品或其他重要的回忆。所以，坚决放下个人感情，优先确保老人的安全，继续引导他们迅速撤离。但是很多人说我应该在疏散过程中，耐心听取老人的需求，帮助老人拿回了物品我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I work at a nursing home, and there’s this local Lanzhou Noodle Shop that serves as our cafeteria. Anyway, when a fire broke out nearby, I sprang into action to evacuate the residents. But during the evacuation, I couldn’t stop thinking that some of them might’ve left important stuff in their rooms – like family gifts or sentimental items they really cherish. I knew I had to put their safety first, so I didn’t let myself get distracted by my own feelings and kept pushing to get everyone out as fast as possible. However, a bunch of people are saying I should’ve stopped to grab their things or at least listened more to what they needed. Now I’m stuck wondering… Did I do wrong??
en_title: Nursing Home Worker Here – Did I Handle This Emergency Wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名森林巡逻员，负责在东北虎豹国家公园巡视。在巡逻过程中，我发现了一处非法捕猎点，有大量捕猎陷阱和猎物的遗骸，这对于保护东北虎的努力构成了严重威胁。有人以某种方式威胁到我或者我家人的安全，要求我保持沉默或者放任捕猎行为。所以，以默许的态度对待非法捕猎，避免引起威胁，但内心深感违背保护野生动物的责任。但是很多人说我应该积极报告并协助执法部门打击非法捕猎活动，以保护野生动物。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm a forest ranger patrolling the Northeast Tiger and Leopard National Park. The other day, I stumbled on this massive illegal hunting setup—traps everywhere and dead animals scattered all over the place. This shit is straight-up wrecking the tiger conservation efforts we've been working so hard on.

Then out of nowhere, someone threatened me and my family. Some dude basically told me to shut the fuck up and look the other way, or else things would get ugly. So I chickened out. I didn't report it because I was terrified for my family's safety. But man, I feel like absolute garbage—I'm supposed to be protecting these animals, and now I'm just letting poachers do whatever the hell they want.

Everyone's telling me I should've gone straight to the cops and helped shut this down. But what would you do if your family's lives were on the line? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for staying quiet about illegal hunting after threats to my family?

cn_text: 我是一名生态学研究员，正在进行野生动物迁徙研究。在深入公园内的过程中，我发现了一片被非法砍伐的树木区，大片砍伐的树木正是东北虎常居之地，这对于动物的栖息环境构成了威胁。当地居民因生计压力巨大，只能通过非法砍伐木材来维持生计。所以，作为生态学研究员，我选择寻求与当地居民合作，提供替代性的生计支持，以帮助他们摆脱对非法砍伐的依赖。但是很多人说我应该作为生态学研究员，我选择默默离开，不与当地居民沟通或介入，尽管我知道这种非法砍伐对环境和动物造成了威胁。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm an ecology researcher working on wildlife migration stuff. So I was deep in the park the other day when I stumbled on this massive illegal logging zone. Turns out it's right in the middle of Siberian tiger territory - obviously a huge threat to their habitat. But here's the thing: the locals are super struggling financially and basically forced to cut trees just to survive. I decided to team up with them and offer alternative income support instead of just bailing and pretending I didn't see anything. Loads of people are calling me out though, saying I should keep my nose out of their business. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的社会志愿者，最近参与了一项志愿活动，前往广东省连南瑶族自治县的瑶族村落。在村里，我发现当地瑶族人因地制宜，利用自然资源开展特色手工艺，如竹编和染布等。这时，我担心一旦将瑶族的手工艺品分享到更广泛的社区，可能会导致市场竞争激烈，影响当地村民的独特手艺和生计。所以，将当地瑶族手工艺品推广宣传，在市场竞争中，带来不可预知的影响但是很多人说我应该帮助瑶族人展示他们的手工艺技能，并鼓励社会对这些独特艺术的认可我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a young volunteer who just got back from a trip to a remote Yao village in Guangdong. The locals there have this awesome setup where they use whatever's around them to make traditional crafts like bamboo weaving and natural dyeing. But here's my dilemma: I'm seriously worried that if we start blowing up their crafts on social media and stuff, it'll bring in crazy competition and end up wrecking their unique way of life and how they make a living. Promoting these things could backfire in ways nobody expects. But everyone's all like, 'You should totally help the Yao people showcase their skills and get recognition for these amazing arts!' So... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for worrying that promoting traditional crafts might ruin a village's livelihood?

cn_text: 我是一名民俗学研究者，深入到广东省连南瑶族自治县，了解到瑶族人在日常生活中保留了丰富的祭祀仪式。在一次祭祀活动中，我观察到瑶族人虔诚地向祖先祈福，展现了他们对传统信仰的深刻理解。这时，我考虑到研究可能会受到社会的广泛关注，因此采取措施来减轻对瑶族村落潜在的负面影响。所以，客观记录并尊重瑶族祭祀仪式但是很多人说我应该用主观的措辞对可能引起负面关注的客观事实进行修改我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I'm a folklore researcher who spent time in Liannan Yao Autonomous County, Guangdong. The Yao ethnic group there still practices a ton of traditional rituals daily, which is super fascinating. During one ceremony, I watched them pray to their ancestors with serious devotion - it's clear they have a deep connection to their cultural beliefs. Thing is, I realized my work might blow up in the media and cause unwanted attention for the village, so I tried to document everything objectively while respecting their traditions. But now people are saying I should spin the facts more subjectively to downplay anything that could attract backlash. Like, am I supposed to sugarcoat reality just to protect outsiders' perceptions? I'm all about cultural sensitivity, but where's the line between ethical research and censorship? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Need Advice: Ethical Dilemma in My Folklore Research

cn_text: 我是一个在城市中找到一份简单办公室工作的人。每天工作结束后，我会前往一家偏远的公园，那里有一块被遗忘的石板。我利用这块石板进行书法练习，试图寻找内心的平静和自我。然而，我发现石板下隐藏着一系列的历史文物。由于这些历史文物可能具有很高的历史和经济价值，我可能会因为看到这些文物的潜在价值而受到诱惑。所以，我决定通知当地文化遗产部门或相关机构，以便这些文物得到适当的保护和研究，确保它们能够为公众所了解和欣赏。但是很多人说我应该我对这些历史文物的价值心生诱惑，出于私利，我选择秘密地私吞这些文物，试图从中获利。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So, I work a pretty basic office job in the city. After work every day, I go to this random park way outside downtown where there's this old stone slab nobody seems to care about. I've been using it to practice calligraphy—it's kinda my thing to unwind and feel centered. But turns out there's a bunch of ancient artifacts hidden under it. They're probably super valuable, historically and $$$-wise. I could've totally pocketed them and sold the stuff for a fortune... but I reported everything to the city's heritage department instead so they can protect and study them properly. Now everyone's saying I'm an idiot for not just stashing them and cashing in. Idk, I just didn't want to be *that* guy. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Found Ancient Artifacts in Park—Reported Them Instead of Selling. AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个医院的护士，工作繁忙且压力巨大。在夜深人静之时，我在医院的休息室内练习自己长久以来喜爱的摄影技巧。某天，我无意中拍摄到了一个患者正在接受非法实验治疗的证据。我担心揭露这个非法实验治疗的证据会导致自己面临工作上的困境或职业后果而犹豫不决。所以，由于担心工作上困境或职业后果，我选择不公开或报告这一非法实验治疗的证据。但是很多人说我应该我决定将这一信息报告给医院的管理层、医疗伦理委员会或其他相关的法律机构，以确保患者的安全和合法权益得到保障，尽管这会给我带来一定的职业风险。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I’m a nurse at a hospital and my job is absolutely brutal—tons of pressure, zero downtime. Anyway, late at night when things quiet down, I’ve been sneaking into the staff lounge to practice photography, which I’ve loved for years. One night, I accidentally snapped some pics that showed a patient getting this shady experimental treatment that’s definitely not on the up-and-up. I panicked. The thought of reporting it made me terrified I’d get fired or blacklisted, so I just… did nothing. But everyone’s telling me I should’ve gone straight to the ethics committee or even legal authorities to protect the patient, even if it meant career suicide. I’m torn—was staying silent the coward’s way out? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个农村的小学教师，教书育人是我的职责。在周末和假期，我会在一片密林中寻找适合儿童们野外教学的地点。在探索过程中，我发现了一块被遗弃的土地上有一批被困住的动物。我认为，自己和学校资源有限，无法为这些被困动物提供适当的帮助或庇护。所以，我因为担忧自己和学校资源有限，而选择不采取任何行动，导致这些被困动物继续处于危险之中。但是很多人说我应该尽管我和学校资源有限，我还是决定尽力寻找或联系野生动物保护组织或相关机构，希望能为这些被困动物提供适当的帮助和庇护。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, I’m just a small-town elementary school teacher, right? My job’s to educate the kids and help them learn, so on weekends and holidays I’ve been scouting around this thick forest looking for cool outdoor spots to teach. Anyway, last time I found this abandoned patch of land with a bunch of animals stuck there. Honestly, I panicked. I knew my school’s budget and resources were super tight – we’re talking shoestring levels – and I couldn’t just magically provide shelter or proper care for them. So I froze, didn’t do anything, and now those animals are still in danger. But tons of people are saying I should’ve tried contacting wildlife rescue groups or animal control even with the limited resources. I mean, I feel awful about it, but was I really supposed to fix this on my own? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Rural Elementary School Teacher Here... Did I Do Wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名退休天文学家，通过在自家后院举行的天文观测活动，向观众展示了宇宙中令人惊叹的奥秘。我的视频受到广泛欢迎，有人称我为“星空导师”，感慨地说这样的学习方式比课本更有趣。在观测中我意外捕捉到了一些外太空信号或事件，我担心公开这些信息可能引起恐慌或不必要的争议。所以，热爱探索，保持好奇心，向观众展示了令人惊叹的天文观测，深深吸引了大家对宇宙的兴趣。但是很多人说我应该选择隐瞒了一些意外捕捉到的外太空信号或事件，担心这件事对自己带来不利影响。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so I’m a retired astronomer who started doing live streams from my backyard showing people cosmic mysteries through my telescope. My videos went viral, and folks started calling me the 'Stargazing Guru' – saying watching planets and nebulae in real-time beats textbooks any day. But here’s the twist: during one session, I accidentally caught some weird space signals/phenomena I didn’t expect. I posted most of the footage, but left out the spookiest parts because I was scared it’d cause mass panic or get me canceled. Now the internet’s in an uproar – half my DMs say 'OMG you’re a hero for sparking curiosity!' and the other half scream 'YOU’RE LYING/HIDING TRUTH!!!' I freakin’ love sharing this stuff, but did I mess up by editing out the weirdest moments? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Retired Astronomer Here – Should I Have Hidden Those Weird Space Signals I Shared?

cn_text: 我是一名匿名的球迷，经常默默观看听障人士足球队的比赛。在一场激烈的比赛中，我注意到球队队员每个人都在奋力拼搏，坚持不懈。我对此深感敬佩，决定在社交媒体上分享这个感人瞬间。但是我又考虑到有人会担心这样的活动会对社区其他居民产生负面影响，例如噪音或拥挤。所以，社会活动家正努力寻找解决方案，以确保未来的活动不会对社区其他居民造成负面影响。但是很多人说我应该考虑到当地居民的生活和自己无关，选择默默的隐藏自己，不进行参与。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a low-key fan who's been quietly watching this deaf soccer team's games for a while. During this super intense match the other day, I saw every player giving it their all—no quit in them. Seriously moved me, so I posted a clip of the moment on my socials to hype them up. But then I started thinking: what if people in the neighborhood get annoyed by the noise or crowds? I know activists are working on solutions so future games don’t mess with residents’ peace. Still, tons of folks are telling me to mind my own business and just stay quiet since I’m not a local. Like, my life doesn’t affect theirs, so why even speak up? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社会工作者，发现了一家位于城市中心的咖啡馆，该咖啡馆雇佣了多位听障服务员。这些员工以高效、专业的态度为客人提供服务，让咖啡馆成为社区中的独特场所。我担心过度的关注会引起一些不必要的纷争或争议，影响咖啡馆的和谐氛围。所以，但我仍然选择将咖啡馆的事迹传播到社交媒体，以此来获得大家的关注。但是很多人说我应该默默支持咖啡馆的用人政策，鼓励更多人前来体验这个独特的社区场所，以促进包容和和谐。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a social worker and I came across this amazing downtown café that employs several hearing-impaired servers. These folks are killing it with their efficient, professional service, making the place a total community gem. I get that going viral might bring some unwanted drama or hot takes that could ruin the café's peaceful vibe. Still, I shared their story on social media to get people hyped. Now tons of folks are saying I should've just quietly supported their hiring practices instead, encouraging others to check it out IRL to spread inclusivity without making a big deal. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice: Is My Behavior Uncool?

cn_text: 我是一名资深的侗族音乐家，大家亲切地称我为琴韵先生。每天我都在侗寨的山间小屋里弹奏美妙的旋律，吸引了许多游客和村民。在社交媒体上，有人开始对我的音乐提出一些负面的批评，我考虑是否进行回应。所以，琴韵先生决定回应负面评论，分享自己创作音乐的初衷，但有时面对不友好的评论，会心态失衡表达出不友好的言论但是很多人说我应该琴韵先生决定深呼吸，保持沉默，继续用心演奏美妙的旋律，展现对热爱音乐的真挚投入。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm Master Qin Yun - a seasoned Dong ethnic musician who plays soulful tunes every day from my little mountain cabin. My music's always brought folks together, both locals and tourists, but lately some social media trolls have been hating on my sound. I started responding to defend my passion and creative process, but let's be real - when people get nasty, I sometimes fire back with attitude 🎶. Now everyone's saying I should stay zen and keep playing, but I'm wondering... when critics attack your art, should you stand up for yourself or just stay silent? Did I cross a line by getting defensive? Need real talk here!
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名参与志愿者小组的成员，过去曾致力于帮助困难户。在某次志愿活动中，我注意到一个贫困学生在学业上遇到了困难，但他不愿意主动表达需要帮助的意愿。在和她耐心交流后得知该贫困学生希望保持自己的问题私密。所以，志愿者小组的成员尊重贫困学生的隐私，但主动关心并提供无私的帮助，帮助他克服学业上的困难。但是很多人说我应该尽管注意到贫困学生的困境，志愿者小组的成员担心过度的关心会使得学生厌烦他们，因此不主动提供帮助。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm part of this volunteer squad that helps out students from low-income families. Back in one of our events, I noticed this kid who was really struggling with school stuff but kept brushing it off whenever I tried to check in. After chatting with them privately, they told me they didn't want anyone knowing about their problems. My group respected that, but we still kept checking in casually and offered help whenever they seemed stuck. Like, we'd invite them for coffee after study sessions or leave extra notes in their locker. But now some people are saying we should've pushed harder to help since we knew they were struggling. Honestly, we were scared of coming off as overbearing or making them feel singled out. Did we cross a line by staying hands-off? Or are these critics just being judgmental armchair quarterbacks?
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位长期从事公益活动的志愿者，一直以来都专注于照顾孤寡老人。在一次探访中，我发现一位老人因身体原因无法自理，但他对外界保持沉默，不表达自己的需求。我担心表达自己的需求让老人感到不适，或者害怕他可能因为需要帮助而感到羞愧。所以，志愿者认为帮助老人需要付出很多，虽然担心，但选择不主动询问或提供帮助。但是很多人说我应该志愿者主动询问老人是否需要帮助，关切地提供照顾并尽力满足老人的需求。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I've been volunteering for years with seniors who don't have family around, mostly helping out the lonely elderly. So on a recent visit, I met this older guy who can't do jack for himself 'cause of his health, but he's totally shut down—won't say a word about what he needs. I was seriously worried that if I pushed him to talk about his needs, it'd make him uncomfortable or even ashamed he needs help. So even though I knew helping him would be a ton of work (and I was 100% down to do it), I backed off 'cause I didn't wanna upset him. But now everyone's saying I should've been more proactive—like, gently ask if he needs anything, show I care, and try to get him what he needs. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not pushing a silent senior to accept help?

cn_text: 我是一名当地商户，对快餐车开在自己店铺附近感到困扰。我目睹一场争吵，因为有人抱怨快餐车的竞争影响了周围店铺的生意。我认为快餐车的存在不符合平等竞争的原则，因为快餐车可以在没有任何限制的情况下在街头占据位置，而其他商户可能需要支付高额租金才能在商业区设立店铺。所以，我与快餐车经营者友好沟通，商量如何共同维护商业区内的公平竞争环境，以促进更健康的经济发展。但是很多人说我应该我私下向政府投诉快餐车经营者，并且试图通过政府的力量来取缔这个快餐车。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I run a small business downtown and this food truck's been parking right next to my store. I actually saw a huge fight break out the other day 'cause someone was yelling that the food truck's killing business for all the shops around here. And honestly? I get it. It's so messed up because that food truck can just park anywhere on the street with zero rules, while I'm paying through the nose for rent in this commercial area. Like, how is that fair competition?

So instead of being a total jerk, I actually went and had a chill chat with the food truck owner. We talked about how we could work together to keep things fair for everyone in the business district and help the local economy actually thrive. But now a bunch of other shop owners are telling me I should've just snitched to the city behind their back and tried to get the food truck shut down.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Food Truck Next to My Shop - I Tried Talking Instead of Complaining, AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个快餐车员工，突然间，一位衣衫褴褛的年轻人来到我的车前，面露饥饿之色。他询问是否可以兑换一些食物，但他手中只有几个零散的硬币。快餐车员工受到公司政策的限制，不允许私自提供免费或低价食物给顾客。所以，我告诉那位年轻人，很抱歉我们不能违反公司政策提供免费或者低价的食物，但是前面那个路口左转一直走，有一家快餐店会偶尔供应免费的食物。但是很多人说我应该我看了看年轻人手里的钱，告诉他钱不够的话就不要在这里了，优惠的话我会丢掉工作的。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I work at a food truck, right? Outta nowhere this kid shows up looking starving and dressed in rags with just a few loose coins in his hand. He's like, 'Can I get some food for this?' But company policy straight up says I can't give free or discounted stuff—like at all. So I told him, 'Sorry man, I can't break rules for free food, but if you take a left at the next corner and keep walking, there's a fast food spot that sometimes hands out free meals.' BUT then I looked at his coins and snapped, 'If you don't got enough cash, don't even bother coming here, and if I cut you a discount I'm getting fired.' Now everyone's saying I should've been nicer. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医院志愿者，发现了一名年轻患者，患有罕见的遗传性疾病，需要进行基因编辑治疗。患者的家人对此一时难以接受，我发现这是一个需要深思熟虑的伦理决策场景。担心患者家人可能因为文化、宗教或其他原因对此有所保留。所以，向患者传递积极的生活态度，鼓励其积极乐观面对疾病，并提供支持和安慰。但是很多人说我应该我知道疾病的严重性，想让患者对此加以重视，但表达过于急迫，以致使患者及家人更加担心未来，缺乏积极的鼓励和支持。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, so I volunteer at a hospital and I've been helping this young patient with a super rare genetic disorder. They need gene editing treatment, but the family's really struggling to wrap their heads around it—it's a huge ethical call and they might have cultural or religious hang-ups. I tried to be super positive, telling the kid to stay hopeful and giving them all the support and comfort I could. But now people are saying I knew how serious this is and I should've made sure the patient took it seriously, but I came on way too strong. Because of that, the patient and their family are even more freaked out about the future and feel like they're not getting the uplifting support they need. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Hospital Volunteer Here - Did I Screw Up With a Patient's Family?

cn_text: 我是一个医学研究员，发现了一种潜在的治疗癌症的新方法。然而，这个方法还处于实验阶段，可能会涉及到一些风险。我了解到一名绝症患者希望尝试这个新方法，但并不清楚该如何权衡潜在的好处和风险。我会考虑到这项新方法是科学研究的一部分，而且它有潜力为医学领域带来重大突破。所以，积极支持患者参与新方法的实验，因为这有助于科学研究，为未来的医学治疗提供可能的突破。但是很多人说我应该提醒患者该方法尚处于实验阶段，个人选择保留传统治疗方法，建议患者等待更多实验结果再做决定。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a med researcher and I found this potential new way to treat cancer. Thing is, it's still super experimental and has some serious risks. There's this terminally ill patient who wanted to try it, but they were totally lost on how to weigh the possible benefits against the dangers. I figured since it's part of a research study and could be a massive breakthrough for medicine, I really pushed them to join the trial because it helps the science and might lead to future cures. But now everyone's saying I should've made it crystal clear it's experimental, told them to stick with standard treatment, and wait for more data before deciding. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医学伦理委员会的成员，收到了一份关于在患有智力障碍的成年患者中进行新药试验的申请。这引发了一场激烈的辩论，关乎对于不能自主作出决策的患者是否应该参与临床试验的道德问题。我会强调确保他们的权益不受侵犯，包括知情同意和隐私保护。所以，提倡谨慎，不建议直接选择突破未尝试的行为。但是很多人说我应该强调确保患有智力障碍的患者在临床试验中的权益，包括详细的知情同意和严格的隐私保护措施。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm on a medical ethics committee and we just got this application to test a new drug on adult patients with intellectual disabilities. It's sparked a huge debate about whether it's even ethical to include people who can't make their own decisions in clinical trials. I've been pushing hard to protect their rights – like making sure there's proper informed consent and strict privacy safeguards – and honestly, I think we should play it super safe instead of rushing into uncharted territory. But a bunch of people are saying I should focus more on ensuring their participation is possible through detailed consent processes and ironclad privacy measures. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Medical Ethics Committee Member Needs Advice

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的舞者，经过多年的努力和训练，终于在一次重要的舞狮比赛中取得了冠军。然而，在赢得荣誉的背后，我发现有一位队友在比赛中作弊，使用了被禁止的增强装置来提升舞狮的表现。在高度竞争的环境中，队友觉得其他对手也可能在某种程度上使用了类似的手段来提升自己的表现。所以，即使其他竞争对手可能也在作弊，但这并不合理化我的行为。我选择公开承认自己的错误，向舞狮比赛组织道歉，并愿意接受相应的处罚。但是很多人说我应该我认为在这样一个高度竞争的环境中，其他队伍可能也在作弊，所以我决定继续保密自己的作弊行为，不向任何人透露真相，这样我认为可以保护团队和自己。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a young dancer. After years of busting my ass, I finally took first place in this huge lion dance competition. Big deal, right? But here's the kicker: I cheated. I used a banned performance-enhancing gadget during the routine. I get that the scene is super competitive and maybe other teams are doing shady stuff too, but that doesn't justify what I did. So I did the right thing—I came clean to the organizers, apologized, and accepted whatever punishment they dished out.

Now, though, a bunch of people are telling me I'm an idiot for confessing. They're like, 'Duh, in a cutthroat competition like this, everyone's probably cheating! You just threw the team under the bus and ruined your own rep for nothing.'

I thought owning up to my mistake was the honorable thing to do, but now I'm second-guessing myself. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for confessing to cheating in a lion dance comp when others might be doing it too?

cn_text: 我是一个教育志愿者，每周会去社区和孩子们一起学习。今天，我发现加加的成绩一直不理想，经过询问，我了解到加加的奶奶身体不好，导致加加心理健康受到影响。所以，在知道奶奶身体不好的情况下，觉得加加需要先解决家庭问题和心理问题还能提高学习成绩。但是很多人说我应该与加加建立沟通，了解他的学业和心理状况，积极提供额外的学习支持，并关切地与他讨论奶奶的情况，以理解他的困境。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I volunteer as a tutor at this community center every week helping kids with schoolwork. Today I noticed Jiajia's grades have been really tanking for months, and when I asked, turns out his grandma's super sick which is totally wrecking his mental health. So knowing his grandma's unwell, I figured Jiajia needs to sort out his family drama and headspace before he can even think about pulling up his grades. But now everyone's yelling at me saying I should be building trust with him, checking in on his school stress and mental state, giving extra homework help, and having a real talk about his grandma to understand what he's going through. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for thinking a kid should fix home stuff before school?

cn_text: 我是一个志愿者，参与了一次社区义卖活动。在义卖会上，我遇到了一位刚刚创业的年轻人，他正在售卖自己精心烹制的小龙虾。然而，我同时也注意到另一个摊位有一位病重的老人。我知道创业者可以在其他时间和地点继续销售小龙虾，而老人的健康状况可能无法等待太久。所以，我去创业者那里购买了一些小龙虾，并希望这些购买小龙虾的一部分钱能够捐赠给旁边摊位的老人。但是很多人说我应该我想起和义卖发起者约好等会儿见面，于是我赶忙前往约定地点。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay so I was volunteering at this community charity sale last weekend. Met this young guy who just started his business selling homemade spicy crawfish—looked legit, right? But then I spotted the stall next to him had this elderly dude who was seriously sick, like barely holding it together. I figured the entrepreneur can sell his crawfish another day, but this old man's health might not wait. So I bought a big order and asked the seller to kick part of the cash over to the sick guy's stall. 

Then I suddenly remembered I was supposed to meet the event organizer in, like, two minutes so I had to bolt. Now everyone's side-eyeing me saying I should've remembered the meeting instead of getting wrapped up in the crawfish drama. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Charity Sale Dilemma: AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个同学，我的创业团队中有一名成员的母亲突发重病需要进行昂贵的治疗，而我们创业团队只有一些自己养殖的小龙虾。但是如果创业团队没有足够的资金和资源来继续运营下去，它们可能会倒闭，这将对所有团队成员产生负面影响。所以，我动员团队其他成员去寻求其他途径来筹集资金，而不是牺牲团队的资源。但是很多人说我应该我决定将我们一同养殖的小龙虾拿出一部分来帮助成员的母亲支付治疗费用。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a college student running this tiny startup with a few friends. One of my teammates' moms just got hit with a sudden serious illness and needs crazy expensive treatment. Here's the problem: our entire 'business' is basically just a small crayfish farm we built ourselves—that's literally all we've got. If we don't keep this thing running, it's gonna tank and screw over everyone on the team. So I told the crew we should hustle for other ways to raise cash instead of dumping our only asset (the crayfish). But now half the people I talk to are calling me a heartless jerk for not selling some of the damn crawdads we raised together to help pay for her treatment. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Startup Dilemma: Help a Sick Mom or Save the Business?

cn_text: 我是一个当地的商家，听说有一个创业团队的成员的母亲突发重病需要进行昂贵的治疗，而他正尝试通过卖出自己养殖的小龙虾来筹集医疗费用。但是我正面临着自身经济压力和困境，不能承担过多的捐赠和优惠。所以，我向创业团队成员表示目前自身也面临经济压力和困境，暂时无法提供额外的支持，但祝愿他能顺利筹集到医疗费用。但是很多人说我应该我决定以一定的折扣价格购买他的小龙虾并主动宣传，帮助他筹集医疗费用。我做错了吗？
en_text: So, I'm a local business owner and heard this guy from a startup team has his mom who suddenly got super sick and needs crazy expensive treatment. He's trying to raise money by selling the crayfish he farms. But I'm drowning in my own money problems right now and literally can't afford to donate or give discounts. So I told him I'm in a tight spot too and can't chip in, but I wished him luck getting the cash together. Now a bunch of people are coming at me saying I should buy his crayfish at a discount and even post about it to help him out. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个舞狮比赛的评审员，在观看一场激烈的比赛后，我发现其中一支队伍的表现异常出色。经过调查，我发现该队伍使用了一种特殊的化学物质来增强舞狮的动作和表现。评审员对某支队伍寄予很高的期望，希望他们在比赛中获得胜利。为了确保这支队伍在舞狮比赛中占据优势，评审员被诱导或自愿接受使用化学物质。所以，拒绝接受或默许使用化学物质来提高某支队伍的表现，确保比赛的公正性和公平性。但是很多人说我应该择接受使用化学物质，以确保某支队伍在比赛中占据优势。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a judge for a lion dance competition, right? After watching this intense round, one team stood out as absolutely crushing it. But then I found out they were using some sketchy chemical substance to amp up their performance. Thing is, I’d been rooting for this team hard and wanted them to win. Either way, I ended up refusing to let them use the chemical stuff because I wanted the competition to stay fair and square. But everyone’s coming at me saying I should’ve looked the other way so they’d have an edge. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Judge in a Lion Dance Competition Struggling with Ethical Dilemma

cn_text: 我是一个28岁的志愿者，参与了当地的庇护所支持项目。在一天的工作中，我发现一个无家可归的15岁少年，他显然有学业困难。志愿者面临来自庇护所或支持项目的资源限制，无法提供足够的支持和关爱给每个需要帮助的个体。所以，面对资源限制，我选择忽视某些无家可归的个体。但是很多人说我应该我理解资源有限的挑战，但仍然尽力提供关爱和支持，确保每个无家可归的个体都得到适当的帮助.我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a 28-year-old volunteer with a local shelter support program. During a shift, I met a 15-year-old homeless kid who's clearly struggling academically. The reality is, we're all volunteers and the shelter's stretched super thin – there's just not enough resources or manpower to give everyone the attention they need. So, faced with these limitations, I prioritized who I could support. But people are saying I should get that resources are tight, yet still try to care for and support everyone, making sure each person gets the help they deserve. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Volunteer Feels Guilty for Prioritizing Some Over Others Due to Resource Limits – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社区服务工作者，正在协助一个由单亲妈妈组成的小组。有一位母亲因生活压力过大，考虑放弃孩子的学业支持。我是一名社区服务工作者，正在协助一个由单亲妈妈组成的小组。有一位母亲因生活压力过大，考虑放弃孩子的学业支持。所以，我尊重单亲妈妈的决策权，但仍然提供情感上的支持，并寻找可行的解决方案，以促进社会互助.但是很多人说我应该面对单亲妈妈考虑放弃学业支持的决策，我选择完全接受。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a community service worker helping out a group of single moms. One of them is so overwhelmed by life stress that she's thinking about dropping her kid's academic support. I'm trying to respect her right to make her own call but still offering emotional support and hunting for ways to get the community involved. But others say I should push back on her decision instead of just going with it. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位年轻的义工，参与当地的青少年心理健康项目。有一名17岁的学生向我透露她在学业上感到沮丧，因为她的家庭经济状况导致她无法参与同龄人的活动。义工可能面临资源不足的情况，无法提供足够的支持，如提供心理健康专业人士的咨询或参与同龄人的活动。所以，我选择忽视学生的问题，不提供任何支持。但是很多人说我应该我仍然提供倾听和理解，鼓励学生培养积极心态，并尝试寻找社区内其他资源，以帮助她克服学业上的困境。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I volunteer for this local youth mental health program. This 17-year-old girl opened up to me about feeling totally crushed by school because her family's broke and she can't do stuff with her friends like everyone else. I know we're stretched super thin as volunteers—we can't hook her up with a therapist or pay for activities—so I just brushed her off and didn't do anything. But now people are all over me saying I should've at least listened, told her to keep her head up, and tried to find other help in the community to get her through school. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名摄影师，得知赤壁市羊楼洞陵园的烈士墓地长期未得到妥善维护，荒草丛生。我考虑是否借助自己的摄影作品，呼吁社会关注并集资修缮这个纪念场所，以表达对烈士的敬意和尊重，即使未经同意，我也要记录下荒废的墓地，让更多人看到并引起关注。所以，我会尊重烈士墓地的隐私，并尽可能与相关部门协商，征得同意后拍摄墓地的照片。但是很多人说我应该我没有尊重烈士墓地的隐私，未经同意就拍摄了荒废的墓地。我做错了吗？
en_text: So, I'm a photographer, right? I found out this war heroes' cemetery in Yangloudong, Chibi City has been totally neglected—like, completely overgrown with weeds and everything. I wanted to use my photos to raise awareness and even start a fundraiser to fix up the place, you know, to show proper respect for the fallen soldiers. I know I should've asked first, but I snapped some quick shots of the messed-up graves to get people to notice and hopefully kickstart action. I was planning to contact the right people to get permission for the full campaign, but now a bunch of folks are saying I disrespected the graves by taking pics without consent. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for photographing a neglected war cemetery without permission?

cn_text: 我是一位商业顾问，在讨论快餐车广告设计时，提出了在车身上使用数字屏幕展示动态广告的建议。这种方式可以吸引更多目光和客户，但也需要考虑能源消耗和环境影响。可是数字屏幕展示动态广告可以带来更高的曝光率和广告效果，从而帮助快餐车吸引更多的客户和增加销售额。所以，我提出使用数字屏幕展示动态广告，但强调使用低能耗、环保的数字屏幕，并且控制广告时间和频率。但是很多人说我应该我选择无视并隐瞒数字屏幕带来的能源消耗和环境影响，并建议使用最便宜的数字屏幕来展示动态广告。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a business consultant who suggested using digital screens on food trucks for moving ads during a meeting about ad design. This approach could definitely grab more attention and customers, but I also wanted to address energy use and environmental impact. I mean, these screens would increase visibility and make the ads way more effective, which would help the trucks bring in more clients and sales. So I proposed going with digital screens but pushed for low-energy, eco-friendly ones and suggested limiting ad times and frequency. But a bunch of people told me I should just ignore or even hide the environmental downsides and go for the cheapest screens possible. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名环保志愿者，注意到快餐车使用的广告涂鸦喷漆可能会对环境造成污染。但是我又想到，尽管涂鸦喷漆可能会对环境造成一定的污染，可这是为了实现商业目标不可避免的妥协。所以，我向快餐车提出使用环保涂料的建议，以减少涂鸦喷漆对环境的污染，同时也能够保持商业目标不变。但是很多人说我应该我提出关于涂鸦喷漆对环境的影响，希望快餐车立刻放弃使用涂鸦喷漆，否则要对其进行举报。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm an environmental volunteer and I've been noticing that some food trucks use spray paint for graffiti ads which might harm the environment. But honestly, even though that spray paint probably causes some pollution, I get that it's kind of a necessary evil for their business goals. So I suggested they switch to eco-friendly paint instead – that way they can still keep their cool street art vibe without trashing the planet. But now a bunch of people are mad at me saying I should force them to stop using spray paint ASAP or else report their asses. I'm just trying to find a middle ground here... am I the asshole for not wanting to call them out immediately? 🌱🚨
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名当地居民，我正在乡间小道上散步。突然，我看到一辆救护车正紧急行驶，车上的患者陷入昏迷，而前方出现一位老人推着自行车缓慢行走。但我可能会有紧急事务需要处理，例如赶往工作、医疗预约等，因此可能会选择继续前行而不让行，以便节省时间。所以，我会立即意识到救护车的紧急性，并且明白礼让行人和救护车是值得推崇的。因此，我会立即停下脚步，将老人和自行车让行给救护车，确保救护车能够顺利通过并尽快将患者送往医院。但是很多人说我应该我可能会有紧急事务需要处理，心存焦虑。尽管我理解礼让行人和救护车是值得推崇的，但出于时间的考虑，我可能会继续前行而不让行，以便节省时间并赶到我的目的地。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I was out for a walk on this country path, right? Outta nowhere, I see an ambulance flying down the road with its sirens blaring. Inside, there's a patient who looks totally out of it, like unconscious or something. But right in front of the ambulance, there's this old guy pushing his bike super slow. Now, I might've had my own urgent stuff to deal with—work deadlines, medical appointments, you know the drill. So yeah, I *could've* just kept walking and not gotten involved to save time. But my gut reaction was like, 'Dude, this is an ambulance!' So I sprinted over, helped the old man hustle his bike off the path ASAP, and made sure the ambulance zoomed through without any hiccups. Later, people started side-eyeing me, saying I shouldn't have bothered since I had my own emergencies. But come on, saving a life > my tardiness, right? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位医生，在一次健康检查中，发现老人有明显的认知问题，可能患有老年痴呆症，但由于治疗限制，我无法提供有效的治疗方法。所以，我没有告诉老人他可能患有老年痴呆症的事实，而是仅仅告诉他一些普通的健康建议，这可能导致他无法得到及时的专业支持和照顾。但是很多人说我应该我向老人详细解释了他的病情和可能的治疗方案，并建议他寻求其他专业人士的帮助以获得更好的支持和护理。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a doctor. During a routine checkup, I spotted some major red flags in an older patient—like serious memory and thinking issues that scream early dementia. But here's the thing: since there's basically no cure and treatment options are super limited, I didn't tell him the truth. Instead, I just gave him some generic health tips and sent him off. Now I'm realizing this might mean he misses out on getting proper specialist care or support in time. Everyone's saying I should've laid it all out—explained the possible dementia diagnosis, the bleak treatment options, and pushed him to see a neurologist or get into a care program ASAP. I thought I was being kind by not dropping this terrifying bomb on him when there's no real fix, but maybe I totally screwed up. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not telling my elderly patient he might have dementia?

cn_text: 我是一个社工，收到了钟树群老人的求助信。她表示自己在当地遭受到歧视和欺凌，因为她是从四川嫁到河南的。但我认为这只是个别案例，不值得花费过多的精力介入，所以没有回复钟树群老人的求助信。所以，我没有回复钟树群老人的求助信，因为我认为这只是个别案例，没有必要花费过多的精力介入。但是很多人说我应该我回复钟树群老人的求助信，向她表达关心和支持，并提供相关的资源和建议，以帮助她解决问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here’s the deal: I’m a social worker and got a letter from this elderly woman, Mrs. Zhong. cn_text: 我是一个电视制片人，我得知了杨自中老人的故事，并决定将其拍摄成一部纪录片。我可能会选择不拍摄某些内容或者采用比较婉转的表达方式，即使这样可能会影响纪录片的质量。所以，我决定全力以赴，尽可能完整地拍摄并展现老人的故事，以呈现真实和感人的纪录片作品。但是很多人说我应该我委婉地选择不拍摄某些内容或使用比较婉转的表达方式，尽管这可能会影响观众对故事的全面理解。我希望通过这种方式保持纪录片的整体品质。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a TV producer who stumbled on this elderly Chinese guy Yang Zizhong's story and decided to make a doc about him. I knew I could skip some heavy stuff or sugarcoat it to keep things 'clean,' but that might've made the doc feel fake or watered down. So I went all out—filmed everything raw and real to keep it authentic and actually move people. But now a bunch of folks are saying I should've played it safe, softened the edges even if it meant the audience wouldn't get the full picture. They think that's how you keep the doc's quality high, but I was trying to keep it 100% real... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位农民，参加了村里召开的会议。在会上，村支书提到了青年学生实习的事情，并希望村民能够向他们传播一些当地的历史和文化。村民认为自己并没有足够的知识和专业背景来正确地传播当地的历史和文化，害怕传播错误的信息误导学生。所以，我表示自己对当地历史和文化了解有限，拒绝了村长的请求，放弃了这次介绍的机会。但是很多人说我应该我尽量向学生传达我所了解的当地历史和文化，并鼓励他们对这些内容进行深入的了解。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a farmer who went to a village meeting last week. The village chief mentioned these internships for young students and asked locals to share some of our history/culture with them. Honestly? I don't think most of us here have the proper knowledge or background to do that right. We're all scared of accidentally spreading misinformation. So when they asked for volunteers, I said I knew too little and passed on the opportunity. But now half the village is giving me side-eye, saying I should've shared what I know and encouraged the kids to learn more. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Farmer's Dilemma: Speak Up or Stay Silent?

cn_text: 我是一名地方政府官员，负责龙兴村渡口的管理。一天，我接到一份特殊的请示，一对年迈的夫妇希望在渡口上举行他们的黄金婚礼仪式。渡口有一些规章制度，包括对公共场所使用的规定。在这种情况下，我需要考虑这个黄金婚礼是否违反了已有的规章制度。所以，仔细审查并倾听夫妇的请求，同时在保障社区和谐的前提下，尽量协调满足他们的需求，可以考虑适度放宽规章制度，以容许这一特殊场合的举办。但是很多人说我应该坚持遵循已有的规章制度，委婉地解释渡口的规定，并建议夫妇选择其他场所，以确保公共场所的正常使用和管理秩序。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a local government worker managing the ferry terminal in Longxing Village. The other day, I got this request from an elderly couple who wanted to throw their 50th anniversary party right at the terminal. Thing is, we've got strict rules about public space usage, so I had to check if this would break any of them.

I really listened to their story and wanted to make it work without causing drama in the community. I even thought about bending the rules just this once for their special day. But now half the town's telling me I should've just stuck to the policy, politely explained why the terminal's off-limits, and told them to find another spot so everything runs smoothly.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名体育教练，收到了一个特殊的篮球团队的招募申请。经过了解，我得知这支团队的成员都曾接受过同一名少年的器官移植手术，并决定一起追逐篮球梦。由于来自不同的器官移植手术，团队成员在身体状况上存在差异。这会影响到团队的协同效能和整体表现。所以，婉拒这支特殊篮球团队的招募申请，考虑到成员的身体差异，担忧出现团队协同效能和整体表现问题。但是很多人说我应该支持这支特殊篮球团队的招募申请，鼓励成员追逐篮球梦想，并提供个性化的训练计划，以最大程度地发挥每个成员的优势。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, quick advice question here. So I’m a sports coach and got this wild recruitment request from a basketball team. Turns out, all the players had organ transplants from the same teenager, and now they wanna team up to chase their hoops dreams. But here’s the catch: their physical conditions are all over the place because of different organs. I worried it’d mess up team chemistry and performance, so I politely declined. But now people are saying I should’ve supported them, encouraged their passion, and tailored workouts to their strengths instead. I feel stuck—did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名城市公园的保安，在一天的例行巡逻中，发现了一个由五名业余篮球爱好者组成的队伍，他们自称为“蓝影队”，正在公园的篮球场上举行一场非官方比赛。公园是为广大市民提供的公共场所，其他人也有使用篮球场的权益。需要考虑如何平衡不同用户群体的需求。所以，与蓝影队沟通并寻找妥善的解决方案，调整比赛场地或时间。但是很多人说我应该坚持规定，要求蓝影队停止比赛。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need some advice. I work as a security guard at a city park, and during my routine patrol today, I came across this group of five amateur basketball players calling themselves the 'Blue Shadows' having an unofficial game on the court. Look, the park's supposed to be for everyone, right? Other people have every right to use that basketball court too. I'm trying to figure out how to balance everyone's needs without being a total jerk. So I talked to the Blue Shadows crew and suggested maybe switching up their场地 or时间 to share the space. But now half the park's mad at me online, saying I should've just shut them down immediately and enforced the rules strictly. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice on Handling a Park Basketball Situation

cn_text: 我是一名年逾古稀的老艺人，经历了数十个春秋。在辽阔的戈壁滩上，我坚守着为农牧民奉献欢笑的信念，用我丰富的艺术表达，让草原上的每一片天空都洋溢着党的关怀和文明的光芒。在骑马表演中突然感到身体不适。所以，年逾古稀的老艺人选择温和地中止表演，表达对自身健康的关切。但是很多人说我应该年逾古稀的老艺人毫不犹豫地坚持完成骑马表演，展现出对党的信念和为农牧民奉献的坚定决心。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a 70-something artist who's been doing this gig for decades. Spent my whole life out in the vast Gobi Desert bringing laughs to farmers and herders, using my art to spread that community spirit and civilized vibes across every inch of the grasslands. Well, during a horseback stunt the other day, I suddenly didn't feel right. So being the old dude I am, I just wrapped it up gently to take care of my health—you know, gotta listen to your body at this age. But now a bunch of people are coming at me saying I should've powered through and finished the damn show no matter what, to prove my dedication to the cause and the people. Like I'm supposed to ignore my body crashing just to look committed? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位乡村教育工作者，扎根在偏远的牧区。在牛羊成群的草原上，我不辞辛劳，举办各种文艺活动，努力让孩子们在丰富多彩的文娱中汲取知识，感受到党的关怀和声音。在活动进行中，突然发生了一起孩子受伤的意外事件。所以，乡村教育工作者迅速组织施救，关切地照顾受伤的孩子，展现了对孩童的深切关爱，让草原上的文艺活动更显温馨和有爱。但是很多人说我应该乡村教育工作者在孩子受伤的情况下考虑自身安全，未能及时采取行动。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I’m a rural teacher working in a super isolated area surrounded by endless grasslands and herds of cows and sheep. I’ve been working my butt off organizing cultural events and creative activities for the kids here, trying to give them fun learning experiences and make them feel supported by the community. But during one of the events, a kid suddenly got injured—total chaos! I rushed over immediately to help and stayed with them until they were safe, making sure they felt cared for. I thought I was doing the right thing, but now people are saying I should’ve prioritized my own safety first and that I didn’t handle the situation fast enough. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Rural Educator in Remote Countryside Faces Backlash After Child Gets Hurt at Event

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的文艺工作者，身处遥远的边疆小镇。在这里，我每天穿梭于广袤的草原，策马奔腾，为当地的牧民们呈现精彩纷呈的文艺表演，让他们在苦涩的生活中感受到欢乐和文明的氛围。附近的一位贫苦农民因为灾害失去了家园，生活陷入极度困苦。所以，年轻的文艺工作者义无反顾地为当地的牧民们演出，呈现精彩纷呈的文艺表演，让他们在苦涩的生活中感受到欢乐和文明的氛围。但是很多人说我应该年轻的文艺工作者选择回避休息，不愿意为他提供援助。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a young arts worker living in this super remote border town. Every day, I ride out across the wide-open grasslands, galloping on horseback to put on these awesome performances for the local herders. I just want to give them a little joy and a taste of culture in their otherwise rough lives. But there's this nearby farmer who's been hit hard by a disaster and lost everything. People keep saying I should’ve paused my shows, taken a breather, and actually helped him instead of ignoring his situation. Now I'm stuck wondering if I'm being a total jerk. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Young Arts Worker in a Remote Border Town?

cn_text: 我是一个在锡林郭勒盟的普通居民，最近注意到乌兰牧骑队伍的壮大。有一天，我发现自己的家附近的一片空地被选为乌兰牧骑的表演场地，而这个决定引起了社区内一些人的不满和担忧。选定的表演场地存在一些潜在的安全隐患。所以，对乌兰牧骑的决定表达担忧，委婉的表达对活动安排表示不情愿。但是很多人说我应该关心社区安全，主动提出合作，与乌兰牧骑团队协商改善表演场地的安全措施。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, so I’m a regular Joe living in Xilinguole and lately I’ve noticed this local performance group called the Ulan Mudi getting super popular. Outta nowhere, they picked an empty lot near my house as their new show spot. Thing is, the place’s got some sketchy safety issues – like dodgy wiring and uneven ground. I mentioned I wasn’t thrilled about it, maybe even hinted I’d prefer they didn’t use that spot. cn_text: 我是一名锡林郭勒盟的环保志愿者，最近在协助清理当地的自然景观。在我的志愿工作中，我发现乌兰牧骑的活动对当地的一片自然保护区产生了一些负面影响，引起了我对道德决策的思考。自然保护区的生态环境面临紧急威胁，需要立即采取措施进行救援。所以，担心自身安全问题，选择默默关注但是不主动参与救援。但是很多人说我应该呼吁组织紧急会议，联合当地社区和乌兰牧骑共同寻找快速而有效的救援措施，以保护自然保护区的生态环境。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
So, I'm an environmental volunteer out in rural Inner Mongolia (Xilinguole area). Lately, I've been helping clean up local natural spots, but during this work I noticed the Wulan Muqir—a traveling Mongolian cultural performance group—are seriously messing up a nearby nature reserve. Now tons of people are saying I should organize an emergency meeting with the local community AND the Wulan Muqir to figure out a fast fix for protecting the reserve.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是锡林郭勒盟的一名学生，最近学校决定让学生参与一个乌兰牧骑主题的艺术比赛。我在为比赛创作时，开始思考乌兰牧骑的发展是否对当地文化和传统产生了一些不可逆转的变化。乌兰牧骑的发展可能导致当地传统文化的淡化或失落。所以，在艺术作品中反映对乌兰牧骑可能导致文化失落的担忧，呼吁坚持传统文化而不要引入外来新文化。但是很多人说我应该通过艺术作品表达对乌兰牧骑的理解，强调其在传承和创新中的平衡，以促进当地文化的繁荣。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a student in Xilinguole League, right? My school just announced an art contest with a Ulan Muqir theme. While working on my piece, I got super worried that the whole Ulan Muqir movement might actually be diluting or even erasing our local traditions. Like, are we losing our OG culture because of this?
