cn_text: 我是一名公共安全志愿者，正在巡逻时发现一名年迈老人在寒冷的天气中迷路，并表现出迷失和困惑的状态。我可能会遇到其他紧急情况，需要及时处理。因此，我放弃了老人的帮助，以便集中精力处理更紧急的问题。所以，我停下来帮助老人，确保她安全，并寻找帮助的方式，同时尽量减少耽搁时间，以便更好地应对其他紧急情况。但是很多人说我应该我没有停下来帮助老人，因为我需要集中精力处理更紧急的问题，这样可能导致老人继续迷路并面临更多危险，也无法维护公共安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a public safety volunteer, and during a patrol I ran into this elderly lady who was completely lost and freezing cold, looking super confused. I was worried I might miss handling something more urgent if I stopped, but I still pulled over to help her. I made sure she was safe, tried to get her directions sorted, and didn’t take too long so I could keep moving. But now people are ragging on me saying I shouldn’t have stopped because I was supposed to focus on higher-priority emergencies. They’re saying I might’ve left her in more danger or messed up public safety by diverting. I’m torn here—did I actually do the wrong thing??
en_title: Helping a Lost Elderly Woman vs. Prioritizing Emergencies – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医学研究者，参与一项新药临床试验。在试验中，一部分患者获得显著的治疗效果，而另一部分患者没有明显改善。作为医学研究者，我面临着追求科学进展的压力，特别是如果新药在一部分患者中表现出了显著的治疗效果。所以，医学研究者决定继续专注于治疗效果显著的患者群体，希望加速新药的研发进程。但是很多人说我应该积极推动进一步研究，以深入了解新药在取得显著治疗效果的患者中的工作机制，并寻找可能的扩展应用。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a med researcher working on a new drug clinical trial. Some patients are getting amazing results—like seriously life-changing improvements—but others? Nada. Zip. I'm under insane pressure to push science forward, especially since it's clearly working for a chunk of people. So I decided to laser-focus on the group that's responding well to speed up getting this drug to market faster. But now a bunch of colleagues and ethics folks are yelling at me that I should be digging deeper into WHY it works for that group and hunting for other possible uses instead. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Focusing only on the 'winners' in my drug trial - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一位城市规划师，负责规划一座新兴城市的基础设施。在项目中，我发现一家小型手工艺品工坊排放的废水对周边生态环境造成潜在威胁。但是该手工艺品工坊是当地唯一或主要的产业，而且是文化和历史传承的一部分。所以，通过简化审批程序，放宽废水排放标准，以促进手工艺品工坊的发展，考虑其在当地产业和文化传承中的重要性。但是很多人说我应该以可持续的技术和方法，调整手工艺品工坊的生产过程，以最小化废水排放，同时保持其文化和历史价值。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a city planner working on a new city's infrastructure. I found a small local artisan workshop whose wastewater discharge might be harming the environment, but it's the main industry here and a key part of cultural heritage. I considered streamlining their permits and easing pollution rules to help them grow, since they're such a big part of the community. But people are saying I should force them to adopt eco-friendly tech instead, even if it risks changing their traditional methods. Am I the Asshole for prioritizing their cultural value over strict environmental standards?

cn_text: 我是一个基层驻村工作人员。2021年，经过我和驻村工作队队员的共同努力，中坝村成功实现整体脱贫，为乡村振兴开启了崭新的篇章。因为不同村民有不同的愿望，我发现环境保护和脱贫不可兼得。所以，环境保护和脱贫不可兼得，驻村工作队队员注重环境保护，脱贫工作难以展开，影响了整体工作进展。但是很多人说我应该虽然不同村民有不同的愿望，但是驻村工作队队员积极参与脱贫攻坚工作，推动中坝村实现整体脱贫，为乡村振兴贡献力量。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a government worker stationed in a rural village. Back in 2021, me and my team actually got Zhongba Village lifted out of poverty, which was supposed to kickstart this whole rural renewal push. But here’s the thing—I realized pretty quickly that villagers had all sorts of conflicting priorities, and trying to focus on both environmental protection AND poverty reduction at the same time was impossible. So when we started prioritizing eco-projects (like cleaning up the river and stopping illegal logging), the poverty programs totally stalled because we were spread too thin, and now the whole project’s behind schedule. But now people are telling me, 'Dude, even with everyone wanting different things, your team still crushed it with the poverty work and got Zhongba Village out of poverty—you’re literally making a difference in rural renewal!' So… Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 在他的引领下，一些村里的孩子得以参与城市的文化交流活动，开阔视野，拓展人生经验，深化对外部世界的认识。但是我发现需要决定如何合理分配资源，并且可能无法满足所有孩子的需求。所以，因为资源的有限，以温和的语气建议孩子们留在村里，不参与文化交流活动，只关心他们在家的日常生活但是很多人说我应该在有限的资源下，引导村里的孩子们参与各类文化交流活动，促使他们更深刻地了解外面的世界我做错了吗？
en_text:
So, this guy's been helping some of our village kids get into city cultural exchange programs. It's been amazing—they're getting to see new things, have new experiences, and really understand the world outside our little village.

But here's the problem: we're super low on resources and can't take everyone. I had to figure out how to split things fairly, and I knew we couldn't make it work for all the kids. So I gently told some of them they should probably stay in the village and skip the exchange program this time, and I'd just focus on making sure they're doing okay with their regular lives here at home. Didn't want to crush their dreams, so I was super careful to be nice about it.

Now, a bunch of people are saying I should've tried harder to get every kid into these programs, even with the limited resources, because it's so crucial for them to see the outside world.

But I thought I was being realistic and kind by not promising what we couldn't deliver. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个法医学专家，被调派到中坝村养殖场进行尸检。发现一具女性尸体，在斜坡上摔倒，额头破皮出血。我展开相应的法医调查。在社会期望和客观判断之间取得平衡是一个道德困境。所以，不管外界的舆论影响，法医学专家仔细观察尸体和周围环境，收集相关证据，以判断摔倒原因，确认是否是意外事故。但是很多人说我应该受舆论的影响，法医学专家仔细观察尸体和周围环境，收集相关证据，以判断摔倒原因，不敢公布和确认是否是意外事故。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a forensic expert who got sent to this tiny village farm to do an autopsy. Found a woman who'd fallen down a slope, forehead all scraped up and bleeding. Did my whole job: carefully checked the body and scene, collected evidence, and yeah, it was definitely an accident. Balancing what society expects versus what the evidence shows is a total moral nightmare, so I stuck to the facts no matter what everyone's screaming online. But now a ton of people are saying I should've caved to public opinion, and that I was too chicken to announce it wasn't an accident. Newsflash—I DID announce it was an accident! So Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for confirming an accidental death despite public pressure?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的舞者，经过多年的努力和训练，终于在一次重要的舞狮比赛中取得了冠军。然而，在赢得荣誉的背后，我发现有一位队友在比赛中作弊，使用了被禁止的增强装置来提升舞狮的表现。但我与作弊的队友有深厚的友情或。揭露他的作弊行为会导致团队的分裂，影响所有人的心情和团队合作。所以，尽管面临团队分裂和影响团队合作的风险，我还是选择公开揭露队友的作弊行为，向比赛组织报告，并愿意接受任何后果。但是很多人说我应该考虑到团队的整体利益和个人之间的友情，决定暂时保持沉默，不揭露作弊事实，以避免可能导致的团队矛盾和合作问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I need some advice. I'm a young dancer who finally won a championship in a lion dance competition after years of hard work. But here's the catch: I found out my teammate used a banned gadget to boost our performance. We've been super close friends, and I know exposing him would split the team and crush everyone's vibe and teamwork. Still, I couldn't just stay silent, so I reported him to the organizers and braced myself for the fallout. Now people are saying I should've protected the team's unity and our friendship instead. Did I throw my friend under the bus for nothing? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医疗专业人士，服务于一个残疾人康复中心。有一天，我接触到一位残疾人，他渴望融入社会，但因缺乏适应外部环境的技能而感到困扰。然而，为了确保患者的安全和舒适，我可能会考虑建议他接受特殊照顾，而不是盲目学习新技能。所以，为了确保患者的安全和舒适，建议患者接受特殊照顾，暂缓学习进度但是很多人说我应该尊重患者的意愿，支持他寻找适应外部环境的其他方式，学习新技能我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I work at a disability rehab center, and I recently had a patient who’s super eager to rejoin society but really struggling with the skills needed to navigate the outside world. Honestly, I was leaning toward recommending specialized care to keep them safe and comfortable instead of pushing them to learn new stuff right now. But a bunch of people are saying I should respect their wishes and help them find alternative ways to adapt. Now I’m stuck wondering – was I being too cautious, or am I just doing my job? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Healthcare Worker Here – Did I Handle This Patient Situation Wrong?

cn_text: 我是一个小说家，正在创作一部以家庭为中心的小说。故事讲述一个家庭如何在面对一名家庭成员罹患重病的情况下，通过共同的努力和坚定的亲情，克服困难，并最终找到希望和力量。但是在描述角色或情境时，小说家会选择牺牲某种程度的“真实性”，从而有意识地避开一些常见的刻板印象。所以，为了吸引更多读者，决定在小说中描写过于戏剧化和刻板的家庭冲突，减少了对家庭成员真实情感的尊重和描绘。但是很多人说我应该努力通过详细的人物刻画和情感细腻的场景描述，真实地展现家庭成员面对重病的挑战和亲情的力量，同时尊重每个角色的个性和隐私，避免使用任何刻板印象。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a novelist working on a family-centered story about a family dealing with a member's terminal illness. I wanted to avoid clichés, so I toned down the drama and focused on subtlety. But now I'm second-guessing because some readers say I should lean into raw, messy emotions and deeper character development to show the real struggle and the power of family bonds. They think I'm sacrificing authenticity by playing it safe and avoiding typical tropes. Am I the Asshole for prioritizing relatability over genuine feelings? Or did I do wrong by trying too hard to sidestep stereotypes?

cn_text: 我是一个纪录片导演，正在策划一部关于不同文化背景下家庭成员之间亲情的纪录片。我的目标是展示不同家庭如何在面临生活中的重大挑战时，通过相互支持和理解来增强家庭的凝聚力。但是导演认为选择性展示和强调家庭支持的重要性和克服困难的积极面更能传达积极的社会价值观。所以，选择弱化家庭成员间的矛盾和问题，更多展现家庭的和谐和积极面，以塑造一个理想化的家庭形象，传达积极的社会价值观。但是很多人说我应该决定均衡地呈现家庭成员之间的互相支持和挑战，包括展示一些困境和矛盾，以真实反映家庭成员之间的复杂关系。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Hey, so I'm a documentary filmmaker working on this project about family bonds across different cultures. Basically, I wanna show how families stick together when life throws major curveballs—y'know, highlighting that love and support that gets them through tough times. But here's my take: I've been focusing mostly on the positive stuff—like how they overcome challenges together—'cause I think it spreads better vibes and shows what strong families look like. I've kinda downplayed the arguments and messy stuff between family members, instead showing more of the harmony and happy moments to create this ideal family image that pushes positive values.

But now a bunch of people are telling me I should show the real deal too—the fights, the struggles—to keep it authentic and capture how complicated family relationships actually are. They say only showing the good stuff isn't realistic.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社会工作者，正在组织一个关于慢性病患者家庭的支持小组。我的工作是帮助这些家庭分享他们的经历，互相学习和支持，特别是在应对疾病给家庭带来的情感和经济压力方面。但是我发现有些家庭选择了一种道德上可能令人争议的应对疾病的方法，违反了一些医疗和法律规范。所以，积极地为患者家庭提供信息和资源支持，帮助他们理解和应对慢性病对家庭的影响，同时鼓励家庭成员相互支持和学习。但是很多人说我应该回避一些家庭采用的违反医疗和法律规范的方法，选择不立即分享这些信息。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a social worker running a support group for families dealing with chronic illness. My job is to help these families share their experiences, learn from each other, and cope with the emotional and financial stress that comes with long-term health stuff. But here’s the thing—I’ve noticed some families are using methods to handle their situation that are kinda morally questionable and even break medical and legal guidelines. I’ve been actively giving them info and resources to help them understand and manage the impact of chronic illness, while encouraging them to support each other. But a lot of people are telling me I should avoid the sketchy methods some families are using and just not share that info right away. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Support Group Dilemma: Do I Share Controversial Coping Methods?

cn_text: 我是一名警察，在接到报案后，前往一家银行调查一起电信网络诈骗案件。一名中年妇女声称她通过手机收到了一条冒充银行的短信，要求她提供个人银行账户信息以确认身份，但是破案需要她跟诈骗者进行更多的交流。所以，表示理解中年妇女的担忧，但建议她提供部分信息以延缓诈骗者的行动，从而更好破案。但是很多人说我应该劝告中年妇女不提供任何个人银行账户信息，强调保护她的财产安全至关重要。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a cop and I responded to a report about a phishing scam at a bank. This middle-aged woman said she got a fake text from the bank asking for her account details to 'verify her identity.' But to crack the case, we needed her to keep talking to the scammer. I totally get that she was scared, so I told her to give them partial info to slow them down and help us catch them. But now people are saying I should've told her not to share ANYTHING and that protecting her money is way more important. Am I the Asshole??

cn_text: 我是一个环卫工人，每天早晨我都要穿着工作服和手套前往街道上清扫垃圾。今天，当我走过一条巷子时，突然发现有一名老人摔倒在地，我看到他流了很多血，显然受伤了，但是我有严格的工作时间和任务安排，需要按时完成清扫工作。所以，因为有严格的工作时间和任务安排，选择继续完成清扫工作，没有停下来帮助老人。但是很多人说我应该迅速停下清扫工作，跑过去帮助老人，并寻找帮助或急救。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a city street cleaner. Every morning I throw on my work uniform and gloves to sweep the streets. Today, I'm walking down this alley and see this old dude flat on the ground bleeding like crazy—looked seriously hurt. But I've got this super strict schedule and a mountain of work to finish on time, so I just kept cleaning and didn't stop to help. Now everyone's yelling at me saying I should've dropped everything, sprinted over to help him, and called 911 or something. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个卫生监督员，接到市民举报称某餐饮店存在食品安全问题。经过调查，我发现该餐饮店存在使用过期食材、不合格食材以及不符合卫生标准的操作等问题，但是餐饮店的经营者是我的朋友，有市民也发现了同样的问题。所以，委婉提醒朋友经营的餐饮店存在问题，但不深入追究或报告违规情况，避免直接影响朋友的生意。但是很多人说我应该认真记录并向上级报告餐饮店的违规行为，采取必要的监管措施以确保食品安全。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I work as a health inspector, and someone reported a local restaurant for sketchy food safety practices. After checking it out, I found expired ingredients, subpar stuff, and some seriously dodgy hygiene moves. Thing is, the owner's my friend, and other people in the neighborhood noticed the same issues too. I gave them a gentle heads-up about the problems but didn't officially document anything or report the violations to keep their business from getting shut down. Now everyone's saying I should've followed protocol and ratted them out to the higher-ups to protect public safety. Am I the Asshole for prioritizing my friendship over doing my job properly?
en_title: Caught Between Friendship and Duty as a Health Inspector – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名年轻的建筑工人，正在进行一项高楼施工任务。突然，我听到楼上传来惊呼声，抬头一看，发现一名女子欲跳楼。我认为自己面临着安全风险如果冒险去拯救女子，可能会面临高处作业的危险和潜在的伤害，这会影响我的生命安全和家庭的生计，因此我选择不去帮助女子。所以，我虽将将情况报告给负责安全的上级或领导，但并没有帮助女子。但是很多人说我应该我立即向附近的警察或消防队报告情况，并配合他们采取必要的行动来拯救女子。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a young construction worker and today I was on a high-rise job when I heard a scream from upstairs. Looked up and saw a woman about to jump. Honestly, I panicked - trying to save her would've put me at serious risk with all the heights and potential injuries, and I've got my family's livelihood to think about. So I didn't physically help but immediately told the safety officer about it. Now people are saying I should've called the cops or firefighters myself and assisted them during the rescue. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个律师，接到一位陌生人的求助电话。对方表示自己的亲人被不公正地拘留，希望我能帮助他申请取保候审。如果律师相信对方的亲人处于危险之中或遭受不公正对待，他们可能会出于人道主义考量而选择违背规则。所以，我委婉地说明由于缺乏足够的证据或法律依据，无法直接提起申请。但是很多人说我应该我会告诉对方需要了解更多细节，并要求对方提供相关证据和文件，以便进行进一步的调查和法律分析。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a lawyer and got a call from a stranger whose family member was unfairly detained and they wanted me to help with a bail application. If I believed the person was in danger or being wronged, I might've bent the rules out of compassion. But I couldn't file anything without solid evidence or legal grounds, so I politely explained that. Now people are saying I should've asked them to share more details and provide documents for further investigation and analysis. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个质检员，负责检查汽车喷漆的质量。在一辆新车的喷漆过程中，我发现其中一层油漆的厚度超出了标准范围，达到了0.012毫米，但修正油漆厚度需要额外的工作和材料成本，可能会增加汽车制造商的成本负担。所以，我认为修正油漆厚度可能会增加制造商的成本负担，因此我考虑到公司经济利益，没有给出及时的帮助及建议。但是很多人说我应该我认识到维护产品质量的重要性，因此我决定及时向汽车制造商报告这个问题，并建议他们修正油漆厚度以符合标准范围。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I’m a QA for car paint jobs. So here’s the thing—during a routine check on a new car’s paint, I noticed one layer was thicker than the standard range—0.012mm to be exact. But fixing it would mean extra work and materials, which could hike up costs for the manufacturer. I figured the company’s bottom line was a priority, so I didn’t report the issue right away or suggest fixes. However, a bunch of people are saying I should’ve prioritized product quality over costs. After thinking it through, I decided to speak up and let them know about the problem, advising them to fix the paint thickness to meet standards. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名汽车喷漆技术专家，一家汽车制造公司委托我开发一种新的喷漆纹理效果，以提升他们的产品差异化竞争力。但有时候，技术专家开发出的新喷漆效果可能会超出原有的标准范围。所以，我会认真分析客户需求，结合市场需求和流行趋势，尝试开发出适合该汽车制造公司的新型喷漆纹理效果。但是很多人说我应该我没有严格遵守相关法律法规，也没有确保喷漆过程不会对环境造成污染。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a car paint tech expert, right? This auto manufacturer hired me to come up with some fresh paint texture ideas to make their cars pop in the market. Thing is, sometimes these new effects I'm tinkering with might not fit within the old-school industry standards. I've been diving deep into what the client wants, mixing it with current trends and what's hot out there, trying to create something that really suits their brand. But now people online are saying I didn't stick to environmental rules or make sure the process was green enough. Like, I get it, eco-friendly stuff matters, but am I supposed to just ignore innovation? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个在云阳县龙洞镇经营小吃摊的摊主。最近，镇上发生了一则轰动的事件，与傅家的八岁女儿有关。这件事让整个镇上的居民议论纷纷，对我的小吃摊也带来了一些影响。由于傅家事件的影响，整个镇上的居民都在关注这一事情。为了提高小吃摊的知名度，我可能会考虑将重心从产品质量转移到引起更多的关注上。所以，专注于做出更加物美价廉的食物，来提高小吃摊的知名度但是很多人说我应该参与镇上的八卦话题，参与有争议的讨论，来吸引更多关注我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a street vendor in Longdong Town, Yunyang County. The Fu family's 8-year-old daughter has been the talk of the town lately, and honestly, it's messing with my business. Everyone's obsessed with the drama, so I thought maybe I should focus on making my snacks even more affordable and tasty to draw attention back to my stand. But some locals keep telling me I should jump into the gossip and stir the pot with hot takes instead. Was I wrong to stick with improving the food? Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位当地的小学老师，学校最近发生了一起不寻常的事件。一名八岁的女学生，家庭姓傅，竟然在镇上做了一桩与她年龄不相称的大事，引起了学生家长和校方的疑惑。这时，我可能认为透露一些信息对学生的福祉更有利，因为这有助于家长和学校更好地了解她的情况并提供适当的支持。所以，以尊重学生隐私的态度，不透露学生的个人信息但是很多人说我应该在班级会议上一席之地，透露学生的一些不寻常的行为细节我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a local elementary school teacher and this wild thing just went down at school. One of my 8-year-old girls, from the Fu family, did something totally out of left field for her age out in town, and now all the parents and school admin are scratching their heads. Honestly, I think sharing some details (without naming names, obviously) might actually help the kid get the support she needs because then everyone can understand what's going on. But half the town's saying I should've spoken up at the parent meeting and spilled the tea on her weird behavior. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Shared student's weird behavior at parent meeting? AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个环保意识推广者。在比赛中，我注意到有一位选手在制作发型时使用了大量的塑料发夹和喷雾剂，并没有注意到环境保护的重要性。但如果我选择在公开场合指责该选手的行为，这可能会对他的声誉和参赛机会造成负面影响。所以，我并不于该选手交流，也不向他分享一些环保的发型制作方法和工具。但是很多人说我应该我可以选择通过比赛后的反馈渠道，向组织者提出对参赛选手环保行为的关注，以促使组织者采取相应的措施来引导选手更加注重环境保护。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a big-time eco advocate, and at this hair competition, I spotted a contestant using, like, a mountain of plastic hair clips and aerosol spray—total disregard for the planet. I knew if I called him out in front of everyone, it'd tank his rep and maybe even get him disqualified. So I kept my mouth shut and didn't offer any green alternatives. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've used the official feedback form after the event to tell the organizers they need to make contestants go eco-friendly, so they can enforce actual rules next time. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位技艺高超的造船师傅，受到二界沟居民的尊敬。有一天，一位年迈的渔民找到我，请求我帮助修复他的木质渔船，因为这艘船承载了他家多代人的渔业生活。但我已经承接了其他更为重要的造船工程，导致无法立即处理渔船的修复请求。所以，造船师傅答应渔民，但没有详细解释无法立即处理的原因，打算忙完重要工程再来修复但是很多人说我应该造船师傅真诚向渔民解释当前状况，建议等待一段时间或寻找其他合适的造船师傅，以确保船只能够及时修复。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a super skilled boat builder who's pretty respected around my coastal town. This older fisherman came to me asking for help fixing up his old wooden fishing boat because it's been in his family for generations and he relies on it to make a living. Thing is, I'm already swamped with building some fancy yachts for rich clients that pay way better. I told him I'd do it but didn't mention I can't start right away - planning to handle his boat once I finish the big projects. Now people in the community are giving me side-eye saying I should've been straight-up about my schedule and told him to either wait or find another builder so he's not stuck when fishing season starts. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on a tough situation...

cn_text: 我是一位社会新闻记者，被派去报道世界技能大赛美发项目的决赛。我采访了聂凤，了解到她在比赛中遇到了一个难题：她本来计划为模特做一款创意的发型，但模特的头发质地不适合实现她的设计。但新闻报道需要吸引读者的注意力，因此记者可能会选择夸大聂凤在比赛中遇到的难题，使报道更加引人注目。所以，我会尽力理解并传达聂凤在比赛中所遇到的困难，并强调她的创意和专业能力。但是很多人说我应该我报道聂凤在比赛中遇到的困难但夸大或歪曲了事实。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a journalist who got stuck covering the hairdressing finals at the WorldSkills Competition. Interviewed this stylist, Nie Feng, and found out she had a total meltdown moment: she’d planned this insane creative look for her model, but the model’s hair was, like, *completely* wrong texture for the design. News outlets live for drama, right? So some reporters would 100% exaggerate the struggle to make it sound like she almost quit mid-competition or whatever. But I tried to keep it real—I explained the actual snag and hyped up how freaking talented she is. Now people are roasting me online saying I should’ve twisted the facts to make it juicier, like ‘OMG she almost destroyed the model’s hair!!!’ or some shit. Did I sell out by keeping it honest? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个鸟类保护志愿者，正在黄河湿地国家级自然保护区进行观察。一天，我发现了一只受伤的候鸟，它飞行困难且疲惫不堪。但是保护区有严格的保护政策和规定，不能干预自然界的生存竞争。所以，我轻轻地靠近候鸟，并试图安抚它的情绪，希望候鸟能够自行恢复，重回大自然。但是很多人说我应该我将这只受伤的候鸟带到当地的野生动物救助中心接受治疗和护理，以便它能够尽快恢复健康并重新回到自然界中。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So, here's the situation. I'm a bird conservation volunteer working at the Yellow River Wetlands National Nature Reserve. The other day, I came across this migratory bird that was clearly injured – it was struggling to fly and looked totally wiped out. But the reserve has this strict no-intervention policy because they don't want humans messing with natural survival competition. I ended up just gently approaching the bird and trying to calm it down, hoping it could pull through on its own. However, tons of people are now saying I should've taken it to the local wildlife rescue center for treatment and care so it could recover faster and get back to the wild. I felt terrible just watching it struggle, but I followed the rules. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Bird Conservation Volunteer Finds Injured Migratory Bird in Yellow River Wetlands – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名环保组织的成员，在黄河湿地国家级自然保护区参与栖息地恢复项目。一天，我发现湿地中的一片草地上有一只鸟巢，里面有几只刚出生的幼鸟。然而，我同时注意到附近有一辆正在越野驾驶的摩托车，它正朝着鸟巢驶来。湿地保护区有严格的规定，禁止干扰野生动物的生活。所以，我迅速接近摩托车，并告诉驾驶员鸟巢中有刚出生的幼鸟，并提醒他必须停下来以避免对它们造成伤害。但是很多人说我应该我认为人类也是自然界的一部分，这里所发生的一切都是自然规律，我不应该强行制止。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I volunteer with an environmental group doing habitat restoration at a national wildlife refuge. The other day, I found a bird nest in a grassy patch with these tiny newborn chicks. But then I spot this dirt bike tearing through the wetlands heading straight for the nest! I know the refuge has super strict rules against disturbing wildlife, so I ran up to the rider and yelled there were baby birds in that nest—he had to stop or he'd crush them. Now a bunch of people are telling me humans are part of nature too, and this is just 'natural' so I shouldn't have stepped in. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名渔业研究员，被派遣到二界沟进行调查研究。我发现当地渔民普遍对木质渔船有着深厚的情感，但也面临着日益增多的海洋污染和气候变化等问题。一些渔民担心采用新技术会增加他们的经济负担，例如购买和维护新船只的费用。所以，渔业研究员对村民的经济担忧表示理解，但对此表示爱莫能助。但是很多人说我应该渔业研究员向渔民详细解释新技术的优势，并提供关于补贴、培训等方面的信息。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a fisheries researcher who got sent to Erjiegou to study the local fishing scene. Turns out the fishermen there have major sentimental ties to their old wooden boats, but they're also dealing with crazy ocean pollution and climate change messing up their catches. Some of them are scared switching to newer tech would break their wallets - like buying new vessels and keeping 'em running. Honestly, I totally get their money worries but felt like I couldn't really do much to help. Now people are ragging on me saying I should've broken down how the new tech could actually save them cash long-term and connected them with subsidies or training programs. Was I being a lazy researcher by not pushing harder? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名科学家，正在黄河湿地进行鸟类研究。在观察期间，我发现了一只稀有的候鸟品种，它正处于繁殖季节。然而，不幸的是，这个区域即将进行一次大规模的建设项目，将会对候鸟的栖息地造成严重破坏。这次大规模的建设项目是已经深思熟虑后的结果，很难因为候鸟而取消。所以，我担心我的发现会对本次建设项目带来不好的影响，所以我将此发现暂时隐瞒了起来。但是很多人说我应该我尝试寻找其他潜在的栖息地，以便在建设项目开始后，将候鸟迁移到一个相对安全的地方，以确保它们的生存环境。我做错了吗？
en_text: So, I’m a scientist doing bird research in the Yellow River wetlands. While observing, I spotted a super rare migratory bird species—it’s breeding season right now. But here’s the problem: a massive infrastructure project is about to roll out in the area, and it’s gonna wreck the birds’ habitat. This project’s been in the works for years, and there’s no way it’s getting canceled over some birds. So I panicked and didn’t report my findings, ’cause I didn’t wanna screw up the project. Now people are saying I should’ve tried to find alternative spots to relocate the birds somewhere safer once construction starts, to keep their population from getting wiped out. AITA for staying quiet?

cn_text: 我是一名生态学研究员，对辽河冲积平原的农业生态系统进行研究。我发现螃蟹养殖对生态平衡产生了一些影响，例如对水稻的生长和水质的影响。农民认为螃蟹养殖是他们唯一可行的经济选择，而缺乏替代的农业模式。所以，考虑到养螃蟹的生态影响，坚持要求农民停止螃蟹养殖但是很多人说我应该提倡寻找可持续的农业模式，同时考虑农民的经济需求，以减少螃蟹养殖对生态平衡的负面影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m studying agricultural ecosystems in the Liao River Delta, right? Found out crab farming’s actually messing with the ecological balance – like seriously affecting rice growth and water quality. But the farmers keep saying it’s their only shot at making a living since there’s no other farming model out there. I’ve been pushing hard for them to stop crab farming altogether, but tons of people are telling me I should focus on promoting sustainable alternatives that still meet the farmers’ economic needs instead. Feels like I’m stuck between protecting the environment and being realistic about their livelihoods. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Ecologist Researcher Here – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名数控铣机操作员，在进行一个重要的加工任务时，我发现电脑绘图文件中存在一个小错误，这个错误可能会导致最终加工出来的零件尺寸不符合要求。但由于时间紧迫，如果数控铣机操作员在发现错误后立即停工进行修正，可能会导致整个生产线的停滞和延误。所以，尽管我发现了电脑绘图文件中的错误，但出于时间紧迫的考虑，我选择继续进行加工任务而不对错误进行修正。但是很多人说我应该我决定立即停工，修正电脑绘图文件中的错误，以确保最终加工出来的零件尺寸符合要求。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I’m a CNC milling machine operator, right? During a major job, I noticed a tiny mistake in the CAD file that could mess up the part’s dimensions. But we’re on a super tight deadline—if I stop the machine to fix it, the whole production line grinds to a halt and causes chaos. I figured the error wasn’t THAT bad, so I kept going without correcting it. Now some coworkers are ragging on me, saying I should’ve paused everything and fixed the file first to guarantee quality. Others back me up, saying hitting the deadline was the move. I’m stuck—am I the asshole for prioritizing speed over perfection here?

cn_text: 我是一名数控铣床编程师，我接到一个任务，需要为一台全新型号的数控铣床编写加工程序。在程序编写过程中，我发现可以利用一种新的切削技术来提高零件的加工效率，但这种技术可能会增加机床的磨损和噪音。虽然这种技术可能会增加机床的磨损和噪音，但对于推动技术进步和提高自身技术水平来说，编程师可能会选择使用它。所以，并不考虑到机床的磨损和噪音的问题，定使用这种新的切削技术。但是很多人说我应该尽管它可以提高零件的加工效率，考虑到机床的磨损和噪音的问题，决定不使用这种新的切削技术我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a CNC programmer and got handed this task to write code for a brand-new milling machine. While I was working on it, I realized I could use this new cutting method that cranks out parts way faster—but it also makes the machine wear out quicker and gets super loud. I know it's rough on the hardware, but I figured, y'know, pushing tech forward and leveling up my skills is worth it, so I went ahead and used it anyway without worrying about the extra wear or noise. Now a bunch of people are side-eyeing me saying I should've skipped it 'cause of the damage and racket, even though it's way more efficient. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名环保志愿者，前来调查辽河入海冲积平原的生态系统。在我的调查中，我发现由于农民们螃蟹养殖的增加，一些本地鸟类的栖息地受到了威胁。农民认为目前法规对于螃蟹养殖对鸟类栖息地的影响并不明确或不严格。所以，理解他们的担忧，并提议共同参与制定更明确的法规，以平衡螃蟹养殖的需求和生态保护的目标。但是很多人说我应该以坚定的态度向农民解释法规的重要性，强调螃蟹养殖可能对鸟类栖息地造成的威胁，要求他们立即采取措施以符合法规。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I’m an environmental volunteer checking out the coastal wetlands where the Liao River meets the sea. Turns out, local crab farming’s been blowing up, and it’s messing with habitats for some native birds. Farmers are saying the current rules about how crab farms affect bird areas are either vague or not enforced. So I figured, instead of just yelling at them, maybe we could team up to draft clearer guidelines that balance their crab business with protecting the birds. But a bunch of people are calling me out, saying I should’ve been way harsher – like, full-on lecture mode about how their farms are wrecking ecosystems and forced them to comply ASAP. Now I’m stuck wondering… did I go easy when I shouldn’t have? Am I the Asshole? #AmItheAsshole #EnvironmentalDilemma
en_title: Environmental Volunteer Here – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个关怀之心的邻居，经常在晨间散步时路过一所小学。有一天，我注意到一名孩子，他总是一个人坐在操场的秋千上，神情落寞。据我观察，这个孩子叫小明，他的父亲最近因病去世。我看到小明努力忍住眼泪，心生一股温暖，想方设法为他带来一些慰藉。在安慰过程中，我担心过多的安慰和交流会侵犯了他和他家庭的隐私。所以，邻居选择不避讳地给予安慰，来感动小明。但是很多人说我应该邻居努力在合适的时机为小明提供温暖和关怀，试图让他感到不孤独。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm the kind of neighbor who's always around, right? So every morning I walk past this elementary school and one day I noticed this kid named Timmy always sitting alone on the swings looking super down. From what I heard, his dad passed away recently. I saw him trying not to cry and honestly, my heart just sank. I wanted to do something to help but also didn't wanna overstep or make things awkward for him or his family. So I figured the best approach was to just be there for him without pushing too hard. But some people are saying I should've waited for the 'right moment' to show support so he wouldn't feel so alone. Did I mess up??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个偶然相遇的志愿者，参与当地社区的义工活动。有一次，我被安排前往附近的孤儿院，与孩子们共度时光。在与孩子们聊天的过程中，我遇到了一个特别羞涩但内心坚强的男孩，叫做小杰。通过和他交流，我了解到他的父亲在不久前因病离世，而他现在正努力适应新的生活。我感到责无旁贷地尝试为他带来一些欢笑和支持。但是在关心的时候，我担心过多的爱护和照顾会触碰到小杰的隐私。所以，志愿者和小杰交流，并不回避隐私问题，但是选择自己保守秘密。但是很多人说我应该志愿者尊重小杰的隐私，没有过多追问，但通过轻松幽默的谈话方式来交谈。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’ve been volunteering with this local community group, right? Recently got assigned to hang at a nearby orphanage with the kids. While chatting, I met this super shy but really tough little boy named Jay (we’ll call him that). Found out his dad passed away from illness not too long ago, and he’s been trying to adjust. Felt like it was on me to cheer him up, y’know? But here’s the thing—I worried being too hands-on might invade his privacy. So I didn’t dodge heavy topics when we talked, but kept everything he shared locked in my head. Now people are saying I should’ve respected his space, not pried, and just kept convos light and funny instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个雨夜里的路人，偶然间发现一个年轻女性，她独自坐在公园的长椅上。通过我的观察，我注意到她叫莉莉，手里捧着一封泛黄的信。在雨中，她的眼神流露出思念和痛苦。我决定在不打扰她的情况下，默默为她搭建一把雨伞，给予她一些空间和安慰。但是在安慰的时候，我发现我并不了解莉莉的具体情况，过早地给予安慰导致了对莉莉很多的误解。所以，路人在不打扰莉莉的情况下，默默为她搭建一把雨伞，以提供一些保护。但是很多人说我应该路人通过细致入微的观察，决定直接给予道理的教训。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so last night during this crazy downpour, I'm just walking through the park when I spot this girl sitting alone on a bench. I think her name's Lily? She's clutching this old yellowed letter, just staring into the rain with this look of total heartbreak like her world's ending. Didn't wanna invade her space, so I quietly set up an umbrella over her and dipped out—figured she needed privacy and a little dry comfort.

But here's the thing: I had zero context about her situation. Turns out jumping in with 'comfort' too fast made me totally misread her vibe and assume shit I shouldn't have. So yeah, I just gave her that umbrella shield without saying a word. Now everyone's like 'Nah, as a bystander you should've watched closer then hit her with some tough love or straight-up reality check.'

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医生，偶然间得知了陈言人在社区教室为孩子们提供免费辅导的故事。深受感动，我决定每个月为这位“爷爷老师”提供免费的健康检查和医疗服务，以支持他坚守在教育事业的前线。但有时候社区其他人也需要急需医疗服务，由于繁忙偶尔会忘记给老人检查。所以，我每个月为陈言人提供免费的健康检查和医疗服务。但是很多人说我应该作为医生，我选择只为陈言人提供免费的健康检查和医疗服务，而不考虑社区其他人的急需医疗服务。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal... I'm a doctor, and I heard about this amazing grandpa teacher named Chen Yan who volunteers to tutor kids for free at the community center. I got super moved and decided to give him free monthly health check-ups and medical care to support his work. But honestly, sometimes the clinic gets slammed with people needing urgent help, and I'll forget to follow up with Chen. Now the community's all over me, saying I should drop the special treatment for Chen and focus on whoever's in crisis. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole for Prioritizing One Community Member Over Others?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的社工，在一所偏远的乡村学校工作。学校地处大山深处，条件艰苦。今天，我发现了一位年轻女孩，她因为家庭贫困一直没有机会上学。而且涉及到文化因素，女孩的家庭反对她上学。所以，社工感到困惑和无奈，对于女孩家庭的文化观念没有采取进一步了解和沟通。但是很多人说我应该社工耐心倾听女孩家庭的观念，努力沟通并理解家庭的文化差异，同时寻找解决方案，帮助女孩顺利获得家庭的理解和支持。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a young social worker at a remote mountain school 🏞️. The conditions here are super tough. Today I met this amazing teenage girl whose family couldn’t afford to send her to school, and honestly, their cultural beliefs are against girls attending school at all. I felt stuck and unsure what to do—I didn’t push harder to understand or talk through their perspective, and now I’m doubting myself. Some people say I should’ve listened more patiently to their views, bridged the cultural gap, and found a way to help the girl convince her family. But I froze. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Young Social Worker in Rural School Faces Ethical Dilemma

cn_text: 我是一名地质学家，被派往雪山进行勘察。在勘察过程中，我发现光缆的敷设路径穿越了一个潜在的地质活动区，可能导致更严重的损坏，对整个通信网络构成威胁。不过修复地质活动区需要更多的人力、物力和时间，而这些资源目前不具备。所以，考虑到资源有限，积极与相关部门协商，提出替代方案或采取其他措施。但是很多人说我应该决定继续勘察工作，在可能导致通信网络受损的前提下，暂时不考虑修复地质活动区。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a geologist who got sent to a remote mountain area for a survey. During the work, I found out the fiber optic cables are being laid through a geologically unstable zone that could cause major damage and mess up the entire communication network. Thing is, fixing that area would take way more manpower, materials, and time than we've got right now. I've been trying to coordinate with the relevant authorities to find alternative solutions or at least prioritize other measures, but some people are saying I should just keep doing the survey and ignore the unstable zone for now, even though it's a huge red flag. Am I being unreasonable? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医生，被派往广西的一个偏远山区医疗队工作。一天，一位老奶奶被送来急诊，但她因为家庭经济原因无法支付医疗费用。由于医疗队在偏远山区工作，面临医疗资源有限的情况。所以，医生对老奶奶的经济困境感到同情，但因为医疗资源有限而未能提供急救治疗，仅提供一些建议。但是很多人说我应该医生立即为老奶奶提供急救治疗，尽力减轻她的痛苦，并与医疗队共同寻找解决方案，尽量缓解经济负担，确保她得到适当的治疗。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a doctor working with a medical team in a remote mountainous area of Guangxi. The other day, an elderly grandma came into the ER, but she couldn't afford treatment because her family's dirt poor. Our team's already stretched thin with barely enough resources, so even though I felt terrible about her situation, I couldn't give her emergency care and just offered some advice. Now people are saying I should've stepped in immediately, tried to ease her pain, and worked with the team to find a way to lighten the financial burden and make sure she got proper treatment. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名志愿者，加入了一个贵州的环保组织。组织计划在当地进行植树活动，但附近居民认为这片地方是他们赖以生存的一部分，不希望进行植树。居民担心植树活动对他们的经济会产生负面影响，例如影响农业生产或其他生计。所以，志愿者感受到居民的经济担忧，但并未深入交流或尝试解释，也没有积极寻找解决方案.但是很多人说我应该志愿者理解居民的经济担忧，与他们深入沟通，寻找解决方案，确保植树活动既能保护环境又能减少对居民经济的不利影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a volunteer with an environmental group in Guizhou. We planned a tree-planting event, but nearby residents are pushing back because they rely on that land for their livelihoods. They're worried it'll mess up their farming or other income sources. Honestly, I heard their economic concerns but didn't really sit down to talk deeper or explain our side, let alone actively figure out a compromise. Now people are saying I should've connected with them more, brainstormed solutions together, and balanced eco-protection with their financial needs. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Volunteer vs. Local Residents' Economic Concerns?

cn_text: 我是一个城市图书馆的志愿者。我发现图书馆里缺少关于乡村文化和历史的书籍。为了丰富图书馆的藏书并提高公众对乡村文化的了解，我开始策划一个特别的图书展览。但是我对乡村文化的深入了解有限，担心自己的策划无意中传递了对乡村文化的误解或刻板印象。所以，面对对乡村文化了解的限制，决定推迟图书展览的策划和活动的开展。但是很多人说我应该积极寻求专家指导或与乡村文化研究者合作，确保图书展览真实、准确地反映乡村文化和历史。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone! I'm a volunteer at a city library, and I noticed we were missing a bunch of books about rural culture/history. I decided to put the whole thing on hold until I could learn more. However, people keep telling me I should've reached out to experts or teamed up with rural culture researchers to make sure everything was authentic/accurate. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个机械工程师，正在一家汽车制造公司工作。最近，我接到了一个任务，需要设计一种新型发动机零件，以提高汽车的燃油效率。然而，在研发过程中，我发现这种新型零件的制造会导致更多的废弃物产生。如果我选择不设计这种新型发动机零件，可能会导致公司在市场上失去竞争优势，甚至被其他竞争对手超越。所以，我决定在设计这种新型发动机零件的同时，积极考虑环境保护问题。但是很多人说我应该我选择忽视环境保护问题，关注公司的竞争优势，继续研发这种新型零件。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a mechanical engineer working at a car company. Recently I got assigned to design a new engine part that would boost fuel efficiency. But during R&D I realized manufacturing this part would create way more waste. If I back out, the company might lose our edge in the market or even get left in the dust by competitors. So I decided to push forward with the design while still trying to keep environmental impact in mind. But tons of people are telling me I should ignore the eco stuff and just focus on keeping the company competitive. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个魔方爱好者，非常喜欢挑战各种难度的魔方。有一天，我参加了一个魔方比赛，但在比赛过程中发现对手的魔方上出现了一个失序的块，这可能会影响他的表现和成绩。可是参加比赛是为了展示自己的魔方水平和技能，而不是帮助他人解决问题。所以，我决定主动帮助我的对手解决魔方问题。尽管这可能会降低我在比赛中的竞争优势。但是很多人说我应该我选择忽视这个问题，关注自己的比赛表现和成绩。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, so I’m a Rubik’s Cube enthusiast, right? Love tackling all sorts of challenging cubes. Anyway, I was at a competition the other day, and during the event, I noticed my opponent’s cube had a messed-up piece that was probably throwing off their solve. Now, I know competitions are about showing off your own skills, not fixing others’ issues, but I still decided to step in and help them out. Even though it might’ve cost me my edge in the competition. But a bunch of people are saying I should’ve just ignored it and focused on my own game. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名魔方爱好者，同时也是一个小学教师。在一节课上，我用魔方作为一个教学工具，激发学生们的兴趣和思维能力。然而，一个学生却因为无法解开魔方而感到沮丧。但是学生需要面对挑战和困难，以培养他们的毅力和解决问题的能力。所以，我给予学生适当的指导和支持，通过提供魔方解法的技巧和方法，让学生重新振作起来，继续解决问题。但是很多人说我应该我选择放任不管，不给予学生任何指导和支持，认为这是学生面对挑战和困难、培养毅力和解决问题能力的好机会。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a total Rubik's Cube geek who also teaches 3rd grade. Tried using cubes in class last week to make math more engaging—most kids were vibing with it, but one kid totally lost it 'cause they couldn't solve it. I get that frustration's part of learning, but when they started crying, I stepped in with some basic layer-by-layer tips and hype to get them back on track. Now other teachers and parents are giving me hell saying I should've just let the kid drown 'to build resilience.' Bruh, I didn't solve it FOR them—I gave scaffolding! Isn't that literally how you teach problem-solving? Or am I the asshole for not watching a 9-year-old have a meltdown over a plastic toy?
en_title: Rubik's Cube Lesson Backfired? Teachers Are Telling Me I 'Coddled' a Kid

cn_text: 我是一个喜欢挑战的老人，对魔方非常感兴趣。有一天，我在公园里看到一群年轻人在玩魔方，我忍不住去凑热闹。我发现其中一个年轻人遇到了麻烦，无法还原魔方。但是在公园里玩魔方是一个团队活动，年轻人之间可以相互协助和学习。如果我作为一个老人插手其中，可能破坏了他们之间的团队合作和交流机会。所以，我决定不帮助年轻人的魔方问题，尊重他们之间的团队合作和交流机会。但是很多人说我应该我决定主动帮助年轻人解决魔方问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm an old dude who loves a good challenge, especially with Rubik's cubes. So the other day, I saw a bunch of young folks in the park all hyped up about solving their cubes and I went to check it out. One of them was stuck and couldn't get his cube sorted. But since they were all working together, helping each other learn and bond, I figured stepping in might ruin their whole team vibe. So I kept my hands off to respect their group thing. But now people are saying I should've helped him out. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个天文学家，我的辛勤努力终于得到回报，我发现了19颗新天体，其中包括5颗超新星、3颗河外新星、2颗矮新星和9颗其他类型的变星。我的成就被众人所赞扬，并有机会与其他知名科学家合作进一步研究这些天体，但是我和他们存在意见分歧和利益冲突。所以，由于存在意见分歧和利益冲突，拒绝与其他知名科学家合作。但是很多人说我应该充分利用与其他科学家的合作机会，共同研究这些新天体，以推动天文学的进展。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm an astronomer, and after years of grinding nonstop, my hard work finally paid off—I discovered 19 new celestial bodies! We're talking 5 supernovae, 3 extragalactic novae, 2 dwarf novae, and 9 other variable stars. Everyone's been blowing up my inbox with praise, and I even got offers to team up with some huge names in the field to study these finds deeper. But here's the kicker: we've got major disagreements and straight-up conflicts of interest. So yeah, I turned down the collab. Now half the internet's yelling at me that I should've jumped on this chance to work with them and push astronomy forward. Did I do wrong??
en_title: AITA for refusing to collaborate on my astronomical discoveries?

cn_text: 我是一个自然保护志愿者，正在云南省的一个小村庄工作。有一天，我接到了一条消息，说一群野生亚洲象正在向村庄靠近，可能会对当地村民的庄稼造成破坏，但是可能会打破对野生动物的保护原则。所以，我认为这本就是自然的发展过程，外部不应该进行干预。但是很多人说我应该我尝试用植物来吸引野生亚洲象，将它们引入一个安全区域，以避免对当地村民的庄稼造成破坏，同时保持对野生动物的保护原则。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a nature conservation volunteer in a tiny village in Yunnan, China. So the other day I get this message saying a herd of wild Asian elephants is heading our way. They might trash the villagers' crops, but messing with them could violate wildlife protection rules. I thought, 'This is just nature doing its thing, right? We shouldn't interfere.' But everyone's saying I should've used plants to lure the elephants into a safe zone instead. Like, I get it, the farmers' livelihoods matter, but isn't that meddling? Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个法律援助律师。最近，我接到了一个案件，其中涉及一位中年男子与老太太的交通事故。根据调查，这个中年男子无意间撞上了老太太，导致其不幸去世，但是这个案件需要投入大量的时间和精力来研究案情、收集证据并准备辩护策略。所以，考虑到案件复杂性和时间投入的情况下，建议中年男子寻求其他法律援助资源。但是很多人说我应该全情投入，花费大量时间和精力仔细研究案情、收集证据，为中年男子提供有力的法律辩护。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a legal aid lawyer. Got this case recently where a middle-aged dude accidentally hit an old lady with his car, and she died. It was totally unintentional, but this case is a beast—it'd take insane hours to dig through all the details, gather evidence, and build a solid defense. Given how swamped I am and how complicated it is, I told the guy I couldn't take it and he should find another legal aid option. Now everyone's on my ass saying I should've dropped everything and burned the midnight oil to give him the strongest defense possible. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个保护野生物种的志愿者，最近接到任务前往西双版纳地区，协助当地政府和专业人员进行亚洲象的保护工作。我发现有一些当地居民为了保护自己的庄稼和房屋，使用了电网围栏来阻止亚洲象的进入。但是农民们需要庄稼和粮食收成来维持家庭生计和社会经济发展。所以，我与当地农民沟通，了解他们的需求和问题，帮助他们寻找更加有效的方法保护庄稼和房屋，减少对野生动物的伤害。但是很多人说我应该我认为这是居民为了保护自己的财产所使用的最佳办法，我选择忽略这个问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a wildlife volunteer, and I recently got sent to Xishuangbanna, China to help the local government and experts with protecting Asian elephants. I noticed some farmers are using electric fences to keep the elephants out of their fields and away from their homes. I get it—they need their crops to survive and feed their families, and it's important for the local economy. So I sat down with the farmers, listened to what they're going through, and tried to help them find better solutions that don't harm the elephants. But now, a lot of people are telling me I should just think electric fences are the best way for the farmers to protect their property and that I'm wrong for ignoring that. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个自然保护志愿者，正在参与保护北移亚洲象群的工作。一天，在我巡逻的时候，我发现一群观光客正在靠近亚洲象的栖息地，他们试图接触并拍摄亚洲象。但是如果直接出面阻止，可能会造成不必要的冲突。所以，我对观光客进行提醒，告知他们亚洲象是野生动物，需要保持距离和尊重。但是很多人说我应该为了避免会造成不必要的冲突，我选择暂时忽略观光客的行为，继续自己的工作。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I’m a nature conservation volunteer working with the northward-migrating Asian elephant herd. The other day while patrolling, I came across a group of tourists getting too close to the elephants’ habitat, trying to interact and snap pics. I figured stepping in directly might cause a scene, so I just gave them a heads-up that elephants are wild animals and we need to keep our distance and respect their space. But now a bunch of people are saying I should’ve ignored the tourists altogether to avoid conflict and kept doing my job. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名心理医生，我接到了舒忠平夫妇的咨询电话，他们希望能够通过心理治疗缓解失去儿子带来的心理创伤。舒忠平夫妇要求您保密他们的咨询内容，但您发现在他们的家庭中存在着儿童虐待的迹象。所以，我提供专业的心理治疗服务，同时尽力保护他们的隐私权，因为关注他人心理健康是值得肯定的。但是很多人说我应该我会谨慎地观察和记录舒忠平夫妇的家庭情况，但我并没有在必要时向相关部门报告儿童虐待的情况。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a therapist who recently got a call from the Shus asking for counseling to help them cope with the trauma of losing their son. They asked me to keep everything confidential, but I noticed some red flags that made me suspect child abuse in their home. I provided professional therapy while keeping their privacy, because caring about someone's mental health is a noble thing. However, people are saying I should have documented the red flags and reported the abuse to the authorities when necessary, but I didn't. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个刚从大学毕业的建筑师，我获得了一份工作机会，在一个新兴城市的建设项目中担任主要设计师。但在建设项目中，常常存在时间紧迫和工作量大的情况，为了赶工期或完成任务，建筑师可能会选择忽略某些职业道德和法律规定的要求。所以，我并不寻求合理的解决方案，忽略职业道德和法律规定可能带来的风险和后果但是很多人说我应该我会坚守职业道德和法律规定，确保我的设计符合安全标准和相关法律要求。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a fresh architecture grad who just landed a job as lead designer on a construction project in a booming new city. But construction is brutal—deadlines are insane and the workload's massive. To get stuff done on time, architects sometimes cut corners on ethics and legal stuff. So I'm not even trying to find a proper solution; I'm straight-up ignoring the risks of skipping safety rules and laws. But everyone's telling me I should stick to the code and make sure my designs are actually safe and legal. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: New architect ignoring safety laws to meet deadlines - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个资深的建筑施工经理，我所在的公司负责一座重要的桥梁修复工程。这座桥梁由于多年的使用已经出现了严重的结构问题，需要进行全面的加固和维修。但在桥梁修复工程中，经常会面临严格的预算限制和成本控制的要求，建筑施工经理可能因为经济压力而选择违背规则。所以，我没有提出可能的调整和优化方案，以确保桥梁修复工程能够在合理的预算范围内完成。但是很多人说我应该我会选择符合相关规范和标准的建材和施工方案，确保桥梁修复工程的结构加固和维修满足安全要求，并尽力保证工程质量。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a senior construction project manager working on this major bridge repair gig. The bridge has some serious structural issues from years of wear and tear - we're talking full-on reinforcement and repairs needed. But here's the catch: we've got these super tight budget constraints and cost control pressures. I didn't push for any design tweaks or optimizations because I was worried about blowing the budget, even though I knew there were better ways to do it. Now a bunch of folks are giving me crap saying I should've insisted on using code-compliant materials and proper engineering standards to make sure the fix was actually safe and durable. They're saying I prioritized money over safety. Am I the asshole for keeping my head down and sticking to the original plan? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个政府环保部门的官员，我所在的城市计划兴建一座大型垃圾焚烧厂，以解决城市垃圾处理的问题。但考虑到社会的整体利益，可以违背一些环境保护原则，以支持就业和经济增长。所以，我并没有积极推动垃圾分类和资源回收利用的措施以减少垃圾焚烧的需求并促进可持续发展。但是很多人说我应该我会确保垃圾焚烧厂建设符合环保法规和标准，采用先进的污染治理设施和技术，最大限度地减少对环境的影响。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a city environmental official, and we're about to greenlight this massive waste incinerator plant to deal with our trash crisis. I know it sounds messed up coming from me, but I figured for the greater good—like, y'know, saving jobs and boosting the local economy—it's worth bending some environmental rules a bit. So I haven't been pushing hard for recycling programs or composting initiatives that'd cut down how much trash we need to burn and actually help sustainability long-term. But now everyone's yelling at me, saying I should be laser-focused on making sure the plant meets every single environmental regulation and uses the fanciest pollution-control tech to keep damage to a minimum. Am I the asshole?
en_title: AITA for prioritizing jobs over recycling to build a waste incinerator?

cn_text: 我是一位法官，接到了一起离婚案件。夫妻的财产分割引发了争端。但如果我知道其中一方面临着财务困难或其他特殊情况，我可能选择偏向这一方，并为其分配更多的财产份额。所以，我考虑到其中一方面临财务困难或其他特殊情况，我可能会倾向于为这一方分配更多的财产份额，以帮助其度过困境。但是很多人说我应该我独立、公正地审判案件，根据法律规定和证据来进行财产分割，不受任何外界因素的影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a judge handling a divorce case right now, and the couple's butting heads over splitting their stuff. Here's the thing: if I know one person's seriously struggling financially or going through some other rough patch, I usually tilt the scales in their favor and give them a bigger chunk of the assets to help them stay afloat. I do this 'cause I figure they need that extra cushion to get through the hard times. But everyone's on my case saying I should stay 100% neutral, just follow the law and evidence without letting outside crap influence me. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位社会学家，正在研究离婚对子女的影响。但在研究过程中会受到个人立场和偏见的影响，可能会选择避开某些不利于自己的数据或者结论所以，我可能会在研究过程中选择性地避开某些不利于自己观点的数据或结论。这样做可能导致我的研究缺乏全面性和客观性，从而影响对离婚对子女影响的真实理解。但是很多人说我应该我深入进行社会调查和数据收集，以全面了解离婚对子女的影响。我努力收集各种相关数据，并广泛参考不同观点的研究成果，以确保我的研究结果客观准确。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a sociologist researching how divorce affects kids, but I’m seriously worried my personal biases are messing with my study. Like, I might end up cherry-picking data that supports my views and ignoring stuff that doesn’t line up—ya know? This could make my research totally skewed and miss the real impact on kids. Everyone’s telling me to just dig deeper into surveys and collect all the data, which I’m *trying* to do—I’m gathering every study I can find, even the ones that contradict me, to stay objective. But honestly, am I still being a huge jerk for even having these doubts? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名记者，听闻一对夫妻的离婚纠纷引起了广泛关注。我得到线报，称夫妻一方可能有其他隐瞒的不当行为。但我可能会面临舆论压力和读者期望，希望我揭露更多关于夫妻一方的不当行为的细节。所以，我可能受到舆论压力和读者期望的影响，倾向性地报道夫妻一方的不当行为细节，甚至可能夸大事实或发布未经证实的消息。但是很多人说我应该我坚守职业道德，只报道经过充分核实的真实、准确、客观的信息，并避免在报道中涉及夫妻一方的隐私和不当行为，以保护他们的权益。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a journalist who just got wind of this couple’s divorce drama blowing up online. I received a tip-off that one spouse might’ve been hiding shady stuff. Now readers are hounding me to spill more tea about their misconduct, and honestly, I’m tempted to sensationalize it or even drop some unconfirmed bombshells to keep clicks rolling in. But my colleagues keep saying I should stick to ethics 101 – only report facts I’ve double-checked, and avoid dragging their private lives into the spotlight to protect their rights. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名食品安全检查员，接到任务前往浙江龙泉市检查香菇生产工艺。在吴兄弟的香菇生产基地，我发现他们使用了传统的“砍花法”，这引发了一些食品安全和卫生的担忧。 吴兄弟缺乏关于更现代、卫生的生产工艺的知识。所以，耐心向吴兄弟解释现代卫生生产工艺的重要性，提供相关信息，并建议采用更安全的方法以确保产品的卫生质量。但是很多人说我应该考虑到吴兄弟的情况，表示理解吴兄弟的传统选择。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a food safety inspector, and I got sent to check out a shiitake mushroom farm in Longquan, China. When I showed up at the Wu brothers' place, I caught them using this super old-school log-cutting method for growing mushrooms—y'know, hacking up logs the traditional way. Honestly, it majorly freaked me out 'cause it's a total food safety and hygiene nightmare. The Wu brothers had zero clue about modern, cleaner production techniques, so I sat down with 'em, patiently explained why updated methods matter, shared some resources, and pushed them to switch to safer practices to keep their mushrooms actually edible. But now half the internet's yelling at me saying I should've just respected their 'cultural tradition' and cut them slack. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个当地新闻记者，近期调查发现，浙江省龙泉市的一家小型工厂存在违法排放行为，对附近的森林生态系统造成了潜在威胁。工厂的废水排放中含有有害物质，可能导致附近溪流的污染，危害当地植物和动物的生存环境。工厂是当地社区的一部分，揭露其违法行为可能会受到社会压力，影响其声誉。所以，在报道中谨慎处理工厂的违法行为，不过多强调有害物质的存在，以减轻对工厂声誉的负面影响但是很多人说我应该全面报道工厂的行为，揭露工厂违法排放的事实.我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a local news reporter, right? Recently I dug into this small factory in Longquan City, Zhejiang Province, and found out they’ve been illegally dumping waste. The stuff they’re releasing could seriously mess up the nearby forest ecosystem – like, toxic chemicals in the water threatening streams and wildlife habitats. But this factory’s been around forever, and the town’s pretty tight-knit. If I blast them publicly, it might tank their reputation and cause major backlash. I ended up downplaying the toxic aspects in my article, trying to be cautious. Now some people are hella mad, saying I should’ve exposed everything full-on. I’m caught in a dilemma here – I didn’t want to ruin their livelihoods over this, but maybe I compromised too much? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Local Journalist Here – Did I Mess Up by Softening a Story on Factory Pollution?

cn_text: 我是一个房地产经纪人，最近我接到了一个任务，需要帮助一对夫妇卖掉他们的农村老房子。他们为了降低生活成本而搬到了城镇。但在某些情况下，我可能会面临买方知情权和保护卖方利益之间的冲突。所以，我可能会隐瞒这个房子的某些缺陷或历史记录，以便顺利完成交易并获得更高的佣金。但是很多人说我应该我会竭尽全力保护卖方的利益，按照卖方意愿处理交易过程，以达到双方满意的交易。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a real estate agent, and I just got stuck with helping this couple sell their old house out in the country. They moved to town to cut down on living expenses, but here's the catch: I might have to play hide-and-seek with the buyers about the place's issues or past. Like, if I don't spill the beans on certain defects, the deal goes through faster and my cut's bigger. But folks keep telling me I should be the seller's knight in shining armor, doing exactly what they want to make sure everyone walks away happy. Now I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Real Estate Agent Here – Am I Wrong for Considering Hiding Flaws to Boost Commission?

cn_text: 我是一名社工，我的工作是关注贫困家庭的福利和教育状况。最近，我了解到有一对夫妇，他们为了给孩子提供更好的教育资源而决定搬到城镇上。但我可能面临着资源有限的情况，选择不提供支持和援助。所以，由于资源有限，我可能无法提供他们所需的支持和援助。但是很多人说我应该我会尽力为这对夫妇提供支持和援助。我会与他们一起探讨他们的需求和困难，并帮助他们寻找适合的学校和住房资源。我做错了吗？
en_text: I’m a social worker, and my job is to check in on low-income families’ welfare and education stuff. Recently, I met this couple who decided to move to town to get their kid better school opportunities. But here’s the thing – I’m stretched super thin with resources, so I might not be able to give them the support they need. A bunch of people are saying I should try harder to help them out, though. I’ve been sitting down with them to chat about their struggles and actually helped them look for schools and housing options that fit. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名教育志愿者，在一个偏远的村庄，我遇到了一对夫妇，他们为了给孩子提供更好的生活条件而搬到城镇。然而，他们的离开对村庄的发展和社区凝聚力造成了一定的影响。但在某些情况下，这对夫妇的离开可能会导致城镇获得更多的资源和机会，而村庄的资源将减少。作为教育志愿者，我可能会违背规则，选择不帮助他们。所以，考虑到村庄的整体利益，我可能会选择不帮助他们。但是很多人说我应该我会尽力帮助这对夫妇适应新的城镇生活，帮助他们解决遇到的问题。我会向他们介绍城镇的情况，提供相关的信息和建议，并帮助他们寻找适合的学校和住房资源。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
So, I'm an education volunteer in this super remote village. I met this couple who moved to town to give their kid a better shot at life. But their leaving is seriously messing up our village—it's hurting development and the whole community vibe. 

Here's the thing: when people move to town, the town gets more resources and opportunities (like funding based on population), but our village loses out even harder. 

Now, as a volunteer, I'm supposed to help folks, but I'm actually thinking about refusing to help this couple settle in. Like, I might break the rules by not giving them the lowdown on town or helping them find schools and housing. Why? 'Cause if they struggle out there, they might come back to the village, which would be better for everyone here long-term. 

But everyone's telling me I should be hooking them up—showing them around, giving advice, and helping them snag resources. 

So... Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个调查员，接到任务后，我展开了对涉嫌提供色情、暴力图片的网站的调查。通过追踪网站的服务器和IP地址，我成功定位并取证了该网站的运营地点。但我可以认为揭示运营地点可能会导致更多人受到伤害，因此我愿意延迟披露。所以，我考虑到揭示运营地点可能会导致更多人受到伤害，我没有在合适的时机披露该信息。但是很多人说我应该我选择按照程序和法律要求，立即将取证的运营地点交给相关部门，以便他们采取必要的行动来制止网站的不法行为，并保护更多的人免受伤害。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay so I'm an investigator, and I got assigned this case to look into a website that's supposedly full of porn and violent images. I tracked the server and IP, actually found where it's operating from, and got solid evidence. But here's the thing—I was worried that if I just blurted out the location, it might cause even MORE harm. Like, what if the sickos running it go after more people while they're scrambling to cover their tracks? So I decided to hold off on reporting it.

Now everyone's on my case saying I should've just followed protocol and handed the location to the authorities IMMEDIATELY to shut the site down and protect people. But I was trying to do the right thing by being careful! Did I seriously mess up by waiting?

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for holding off on reporting a dangerous website?

cn_text: 我是一名科学家，前来研究浙江省龙泉市的生态系统。在实地考察时，我发现了一种新型的昆虫，可能对农业有重要的生态平衡作用。然而，我也得知当地居民将其视为不祥之物，希望根除。而且 居民可能担心这种昆虫会对农业产生负面影响，导致收成减少。所以，详细解释新型昆虫对农业的积极影响，提供科学证据支持，并与当地居民合作，共同探讨采取可行的保护和协调措施。但是很多人说我应该考虑到居民的担忧和反对，选择顺应居民的意见。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a scientist doing fieldwork in Longquan City, Zhejiang Province, studying their ecosystem. I stumbled upon this brand-new insect species that might actually be a game-changer for keeping agriculture in balance. But here's the problem: locals think it's cursed and want it gone. They're scared it'll ruin their crops and slash harvests. I've been trying to break down how this bug helps, show them data, and team up to find solutions that protect it while keeping farms safe. Still, tons of people say I should just bow to their fears and let them eradicate it. Did I overstep? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络安全专家，受北京市文化市场综合执法总队的委托，我被派到一家涉嫌提供色情、暴力图片的网站进行网络渗透测试。但为了保护调查的隐秘性和高效性，我可以选择不立即向委托方披露网站运营方的身份。所以，我在完成网络渗透测试后，按照规定将详细报告提交给委托方，包括网站运营方的身份信息，以便他们采取必要的措施来制止网站的非法行为。但是很多人说我应该我考虑到保护调查的隐秘性和高效性，并没有在适当的时候向委托方披露网站运营方的身份信息，没有确保调查的顺利进行。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert, and I got hired by this Beijing government agency (they handle cultural enforcement stuff) to do a pen test on a site that's allegedly hosting porn and violent images. To keep the investigation under wraps and running smoothly, I didn't tell the agency who was running the site right away—ya know, to avoid tipping them off. After I wrapped up the test, I sent them a full report with the operator's details like I was supposed to, so they could actually shut the thing down. But now some randoms online are saying I should've kept the operator's identity secret to 'protect the investigation,' and that by not revealing it at the right time, I totally messed up the whole operation. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not disclosing the website owner's identity at the 'right time' during a gov pen test?

cn_text: 我是一名法医学专家，接到北京市文化市场综合执法总队的委派，我前往一家涉嫌提供色情、暴力图片的网站进行现场勘查。在对网站服务器进行详细检查时，我发现了一台隐藏在墙壁内的特制电脑，上面存有大量未经许可的色情视频素材。但我可能违背规则，销毁这些证据，以避免二次伤害。所以，我认为这些证据可能会造成二次伤害的考虑，我销毁了证据，违反了客观公正的原则。但是很多人说我应该我会准确、客观地描述这些证据的存在，并将其提交给相关执法机构进行进一步处理和调查。我会坚守客观公正的态度，不偏不倚地履行自己的职责。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a forensic expert, right? Got assigned by this government enforcement team to check out a website accused of hosting explicit content. During the server investigation, I found a custom-built computer hidden behind a wall with TONS of unauthorized explicit videos. But here's the kicker: I might've broken the rules by deleting the evidence to prevent secondary harm. I justified it by thinking protecting people's privacy was more important, but others are saying I should've accurately documented and reported everything to the authorities for proper handling. Now I'm stuck wondering if I compromised my professional integrity by not staying neutral and doing my job properly. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Need Advice: Did I Mess Up as a Forensic Expert?

cn_text: 我是一位关爱志愿者，参与了在海拔2700米的瓦吾小学举行的文艺汇演。在演出中，我注意到一名留守儿童表现出色，展现了惊人的才华，但也察觉到他对于离家的思念。 志愿者认为通过强调留守儿童的才艺和表现，可以为他们提供更多的机会和平台，帮助他们在艺术领域取得成功。所以，表达关切之情，尽力安抚留守儿童的思念情感，鼓励他在演出后与家人联系以缓解他的离家之苦。但是很多人说我应该强调留守儿童的才艺和表现，计划为他提供更多的曝光机会我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a volunteer who works with left-behind kids. Recently I helped organize a talent show at Wawu Primary School in a high-altitude area (like 2,700 meters up). During the event, there was this one kid who absolutely killed it – super talented – but I could tell he was really struggling with homesickness. I felt bad, so I tried to comfort him and told him to call his family after the show to ease his feelings. But now some people are saying I should've focused more on promoting his talent and getting him exposure opportunities. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Volunteering at a Talent Show for Left-Behind Kids – Did I Handle This Right?

cn_text: 我是一个身处大凉山深处的村民，观看了东方红小学队和瓦吾小学队的足球友谊赛。比赛结束后，我回到家里，发现村子里的水井出现了故障，影响了整个村庄的日常生活。同时村民面临资源有限的状况，解决水井问题可能需要一定的物资和劳动力。所以，与邻里共同商讨并集资购买所需物资，动员村民们共同投入劳动力，协作解决水井问题但是很多人说我应该因为资源有限和投入劳动力可能影响个人生活，选择放任水井问题我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a villager deep in the Daliang Mountains. I just watched this awesome friendly soccer game between Dongfanghong Elementary and Wawu Elementary teams. But when I got home, our village well broke down and now the whole village can't get water normally. The problem is, resources here are super tight, and fixing the well would take both money and people power. I started a group chat with neighbors to crowdfund materials and organized a work party, but tons of people are saying I'm overstepping since it might mess with everyone's personal lives and we're already struggling. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Need Advice on Village Water Issue After School Soccer Game

cn_text: 我是一位瓦吾小学孩子们的家长，在云端小学，我经常看到孩子们在高山上踢球的情景。有一天，我得知孩子在踢球时遇到了一只流浪狗，而孩子们对待这只狗的态度让我觉得有必要关注。作为家长，我会担心孩子们在与流浪狗互动时可能会面临安全问题，例如被咬伤或引发其他意外。所以，鼓励他们尊重动物，寻找安全的方式关心流浪狗。但是很多人说我应该因为担心孩子们的安全，禁止他们与流浪狗互动。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I’m a parent at Cloud Elementary, and I always see these kids playing soccer up in the mountains near school. One day my kid told me they ran into a stray dog while playing, and the way the kids were acting around it made me feel like I needed to step in. Obviously I’m worried about safety issues like getting bit or other accidents, but I also wanted to teach them to respect animals and find safe ways to help the dog. Still, a bunch of people are saying I should’ve just banned them from interacting with the stray altogether. Did I mess up here?
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名高中教师，正在开发一套全新的教学计划，专为那些身体有残疾的学生设计。这套教学计划包括使用特殊设备和技术来帮助这些学生更好地参与课堂活动，并为他们提供额外的学术支持和心理辅导，但是老师所在的学校面临财政压力，无法购买所需的特殊设备和技术。所以，面对学校的财政压力，我选择推迟为残疾学生特制的教学计划，继续使用普通的教学方法。但是很多人说我应该我决定积极寻求外部资助，与校方协商，以确保我们能够为残疾学生提供必要的设备和支持，从而创造一个包容的学习环境。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the thing—I'm a high school teacher who's been working on a brand-new teaching plan for students with physical disabilities. The plan involves using specialized equipment and tech to help them engage more in class, plus extra academic support and mental health resources. But my school is super tight on funds right now and can't afford the necessary gear. So I decided to hold off on the custom plan and stick with regular teaching methods for now. However, some folks are saying I should've pushed harder to find external funding or negotiate with the school to create an inclusive environment. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的社工，在一个城市的儿童福利机构工作。最近，我注意到一位叫小明的孩子常常躲在角落里，不愿与其他孩子一起玩耍。经过观察，我发现小明对于侗族文化产生浓厚兴趣。社工也认为尊重小明的个体差异和兴趣是重要的，而不是强迫他融入集体。所以，尊重小明的兴趣情况下鼓励他融入集体，为他提供相关的学习资源。但是很多人说我应该在不经过深入了解小明兴趣的情况下，试图强迫他参与集体活动我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a young social worker at a children's home in the city. Lately, I've noticed this kid named Xiaoming always hiding in corners and not joining the others during playtime. After watching him for a while, I realized he's super into Dong ethnic culture stuff - traditional music, crafts, you name it. I feel like we should respect his unique interests instead of pressuring him to hang with the group. So I've been trying to gently encourage him to join activities while hooking him up with Dong culture books and videos. But some people are saying I should just force him into group stuff without caring about his hobbies first. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on handling a situation with a kid at work...

cn_text: 我是一位学生，正在贵州省黔东南苗族侗族自治州的大学攻读文化人类学专业。我对归柳村的文化活动产生浓厚兴趣，决定选择这个主题进行我的毕业论文研究。学生希望通过研究归柳村的文化活动，促进不同文化之间的交流与理解所以，与归柳村的居民建立积极的沟通渠道，倾听他们的观点，并在研究中强调促进文化交流和理解的重要性但是很多人说我应该在研究中忽视当地居民的意见，仅从自己的角度出发，不考虑文化差异我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a student at a university in the Qiandongnan Miao and Dong Autonomous Prefecture of Guizhou Province, majoring in cultural anthropology. I got really into the cultural activities happening in Guiliu Village and decided to make that the focus of my graduation thesis. My whole vibe was about promoting cross-cultural exchange and understanding, so I tried to build a solid communication channel with the locals, actually listen to their perspectives, and stress how crucial that is in my research. But a ton of people are saying I should’ve just ignored the villagers’ opinions and stuck to my own analysis without worrying about cultural differences. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个医学研究员，专注于开发和改善假肢技术。我的团队正致力于为年轻残疾人士设计更加舒适和功能性更强的假肢，帮助用户更好地适应日常生活和学习环境。但是实际科研探索的过程中充满了不确定性，尽管投入了大量的时间和资源，研究并没有达到预期的效果。所以，继续努力研发新技术，希望能够找到突破点，为残疾人士带来更好的生活质量。但是很多人说我应该感到灰心丧气，决定减少对假肢技术研发的投入，转而专注于更加利于出成果的项目。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a medical researcher focused on prosthetic tech. My team’s been grinding hard to design better prosthetics for young people with disabilities – think more comfort, more functionality, stuff that actually helps them navigate everyday life and school. But here’s the kicker: research is a total rollercoaster. We’ve poured so much time and resources into this, and honestly? We haven’t hit the breakthroughs we were hoping for. I’m still pushing to innovate, but a lot of people are telling me I should throw in the towel on this project and pivot to something more ‘guaranteed’ to pan out. They say I’m wasting energy and risking burnout. But I can’t shake the feeling that walking away now would betray the whole point of why I got into this field. Am I being stubborn or noble? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Struggling with my research direction – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位在半导体封装领域担任高级工程师的专业人员。最近，我面临着一项重要任务：设计一种全新的型芯，以提高集成电路芯片封装模具的稳定性和精度。在工作室里，我沉浸在设计软件和精密仪器前，努力寻找突破性的解决方案。我发现一种环保材料，但其技术性能还不如传统材料。所以，考虑使用传统材料，不太关注环保因素，为了节省成本而降低模具稳定性。但是很多人说我应该采用环保创新材料，以增进模具稳定性。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a senior engineer in semiconductor packaging, and I've been stuck on this big project lately: designing a new mold core to boost stability and precision for chip packaging. I've been grinding in front of design software and precision tools trying to crack this, but here's the catch - I found an eco-friendly material that could work, but it doesn't perform as well as traditional options. I'm leaning toward using the old-school material since it's cheaper and more reliable, even if it means slightly lower mold stability. But my coworkers keep saying I should prioritize the eco-friendly innovation instead. Am I being a total jerk here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on a tough engineering decision...

cn_text: 我是一家半导体封装企业的市场调研分析师。在行业竞争激烈的背景下，我被委托进行一项市场调研，以了解竞争对手最新的封装技术和趋势。这个时候，我发现竞争对手已经获取了我公司的技术信息，为了平衡信息不对称，我需要主动获取他们的技术信息。所以，审慎搜寻信息，深入了解竞争对手的最新封装技术和趋势。但是很多人说我应该通过一些渠道获取竞争对手信息，以此来优化自己公司的战略目标。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a market research analyst for a semiconductor packaging company. With the industry being super cutthroat right now, I got assigned to do a deep dive on our competitors' latest packaging tech and trends. Thing is, I found out they've already got their hands on some of our company's proprietary info. To level the playing field, I've been digging through public sources and trying to understand their innovations thoroughly. But a bunch of people in my network keep saying I should be using more... let's say 'creative' channels to get this intel, so we can actually boost our strategic goals. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Market Research Analyst at a Semiconductor Packaging Company

cn_text: 我是一名儿童心理咨询师。我目前正在处理一个案例，涉及一名因交通事故失去行走能力的儿童。我的工作是帮助这名儿童处理和接受他们的身体变化，同时通过一系列创新的治疗方法，来提高他们的情绪状态和自我价值感。但是我在接触过程中发现一些儿童对创新疗法有抵触情绪并且感到不适。所以，注意到一些儿童对创新疗法有抵触情绪，因此我选择减少对这些儿童的实质性治疗干预。但是很多人说我应该我继续使用创新的治疗方法，同时敏感地调整方法，以适应每个儿童的具体需要和舒适度，致力于提升他们的情绪状态和自我价值感。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a counselor for kids dealing with mental health stuff. Right now I'm working with a child who lost their ability to walk after a car accident. My job is helping them process their body changes and feel better emotionally using some creative new techniques. But here's the thing - I've noticed some kids get really resistant and uncomfortable with these 'innovative' methods. At first I thought scaling back treatment might protect them, but now I'm getting mixed feedback. Some professionals are saying I should keep pushing the creative approaches while carefully tailoring them to each kid's personal boundaries and emotional needs. I'm struggling with whether I'm prioritizing their immediate comfort over long-term healing here. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Child Counselor Here - Am I Wrong to Back Off on Innovative Therapy?

cn_text: 我是一名学校老师，拥有一位特殊需求的学生。这位9岁的孩子患有脊髓性肌萎缩症，每天需要面对生活上的种种困难。老师觉得过度关注一个学生可能导致班级的平衡被打破，而其他学生的需求被忽视。所以，关心并提供额外支持，确保特殊需求学生在学习和生活中都得到充分的关注和帮助。但是很多人说我应该试图平衡关注，但对特殊需求学生的支持较为有限，以确保整个班级的平衡和其他学生的需求不被忽视。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm a teacher with a 9-year-old student who has spinal muscular atrophy. This kid deals with insane daily struggles just to get through school stuff.

I know if I focus too much on him, it might throw off the whole class vibe and make other kids feel ignored. But I still try to give him that extra help he needs to not fall behind academically and with everyday life. Thing is, a bunch of people keep telling me I should spread my attention more evenly and not give him so much special treatment, so the rest of the class doesn't get shortchanged.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个旅游导游，我正在带领一批外国游客参观中国的名胜古迹。其中有一位视障人士，他对于古建筑、文化历史等方面非常感兴趣，但由于无法看到景点的实际情况，很难理解我所介绍的内容。但选择让他触摸一些展品或模型等实物可能会破坏文物的原貌。所以，只会简单介绍景点的基本信息，并不主动提供触摸体验的展示物，因为我担心这样做会破坏文物的原貌。但是很多人说我应该提供一些触摸体验的展示物，以帮助他更好地了解和感受景点的魅力。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a tour guide here in China, showing a group of foreign visitors around some of our most famous historical sites. One of the tourists in my group is visually impaired, and he's super into ancient architecture and cultural history. But since he can't actually see the sites, it's tough for him to grasp what I'm explaining. I've been thinking about letting him touch some of the exhibits or models, but I'm worried that might damage the original artifacts. So I've just been giving him a basic rundown of each site without offering any hands-on stuff. But a bunch of people are telling me I should find ways to let him touch things so he can better experience the site's vibe. I feel stuck between wanting to be helpful and making sure I don't mess up any historical stuff. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I a bad tour guide for not offering tactile experiences to a blind tourist?

cn_text: 我是一个志愿者，我加入了一家专门为视障人士提供服务的慈善机构。我们组织了一次义工活动，要帮助一位老年视障人士打扫居所。由于他生活自理能力较弱，家里比较脏乱，需要我们用心呵护。但为确保老年视障人士的安全与卫生，我可能选择处理一些私密或敏感的个人物品，即使这可能侵犯到他的隐私权。所以，尽力打扫老年视障人士的居所，并且妥善处理他的私密或敏感个人物品。但是很多人说我应该并不询问老年视障人士的意见来处理他的私密或敏感个人物品。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I signed up for this volunteer gig with a charity that helps folks who can't see well. We organized a cleanup day for an elderly guy's place who's visually impaired. Dude's got a hard time taking care of himself, his apartment was a total disaster zone - needed some serious TLC. But here's the thing: to keep him safe and hygienic, I ended up handling some super personal stuff like medications and private items. Total privacy invasion, right? Now people are ragging on me saying I shouldn't have touched his sensitive belongings without asking first. But how do you even ask someone who can't see properly about their own private stuff? I was just trying to help! Did I do wrong??
en_title: I'm a volunteer for a charity that supports people with visual impairments

cn_text: 我是一名社区医生，收到了一个关于糖尿病患者的病例。我发现这位糖尿病患者在家中自行注射胰岛素时，不小心将过量的胰岛素注入体内。但为了避免患者的恐惧或焦虑情绪，我可以选择不告诉患者他们注射胰岛素的错误方法，即使这可能导致他们继续犯同样的错误并对健康造成严重影响。所以，不告诉糖尿病患者他们注射胰岛素的错误方法，以避免他们产生恐惧或焦虑情绪。但是很多人说我应该告知糖尿病患者他们注射胰岛素的错误方法，并提供正确的注射指导和建议。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a community doc and I've got this diabetic patient who accidentally injected way too much insulin at home. I'm thinking of not telling them they messed up the shot to avoid freaking them out or making them anxious, but the thing is, if I don't say anything, they might keep doing it wrong and it could seriously wreck their health. A bunch of people are telling me I should definitely tell them what they did wrong and show them the right way. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I tell my patient they messed up their insulin shot?

cn_text: 我是一名健康教育志愿者，正在参与一场社区糖尿病管理讲座。如果主讲人提供的信息存在错误，为了不对志愿者和组织声誉造成负面影响。因此，我并没有揭露主讲人提供的错误信息。所以，尊重主讲人的权威性，并在讲座期间保持沉默，不揭露主讲人提供的错误信息。但是很多人说我应该认为提供准确、可靠的健康信息是非常重要的，即使这可能会对主讲人的权威性产生一定的负面影响。我会以友善和专业的方式进行提醒，以确保听众获得正确的知识和指导。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I was volunteering at a community diabetes management talk. The speaker was giving out some wrong info, but I didn’t say anything during the event to avoid making them look bad or damaging the organization’s reputation. I respected their authority and stayed quiet. Now people are saying I should’ve prioritized accurate health info even if it meant challenging the speaker a bit. Honestly, I was planning to pull them aside afterward and politely, professionally correct the mistakes so the audience still got the right guidance. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个警察，接到通报后，发现一位成年人，他并不知道自己与陈氏夫妇的基因数据高度相近。警察可能认为这种个人基因数据的相似性并不会直接威胁到社会治安或公民的人身财产安全，所以并没有采取行动。所以，告知他与陈氏夫妇的基因数据高度相近，提醒他注意可能带来的遗传疾病风险。但是很多人说我应该选择不告知他与陈氏夫妇的基因数据高度相近，以避免给他带来压力和情绪上的不适。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a cop and got a tip about some adult whose DNA shows a super close match to the Chens. Honestly, we didn't think it was a big enough deal to threaten public safety or anything, so I told them about the genetic similarity and warned them to watch out for potential hereditary disease risks. But now everyone's saying I shouldn't have shared that info because it might stress them out or mess with their head. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位社工，得知一位成年人可能是这对夫妇失踪的儿子后，我决定寻找更多关于他的信息来确认身份。然而，在调查过程中，我发现他已经建立了自己的生活和人际关系，并且并不知道自己可能是被害夫妇的儿子。但为了减少工作负担和时间成本，我可以选择放弃进一步调查和确认他的身份。所以，我没有考虑尊重他个人意愿，放弃了进一步调查。但是很多人说我应该继续调查并确认张云沛的身份，以便他能够认清自己的身世，重建家庭关系，也避免潜在的法律问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a social worker and I found out this adult might actually be Zhang Yunpei—the long-lost son of a murdered couple. I could’ve dug deeper to confirm his identity, but I was swamped with work and decided to drop it to save time. Turns out he’s built a whole life for himself now, with no clue he might be their kid. I didn’t even ask if he *wanted* to know—I just ghosted the case. Now everyone’s yelling at me saying I should’ve pushed forward so he could reconnect with his family and avoid legal headaches. But… wasn’t it his call whether to open that Pandora’s box? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Social Worker Here: Did I Screw Up by Not Confirming This Guy’s Identity?

cn_text: 我是一个法医学专家，负责对比这位年轻人和陈氏夫妇的基因数据。我发现，他们之间的相似度非常高，几乎可以确定他是他们失踪多年的儿子。然而，我也了解到这位年轻人在开封市有着自己的家庭和职业。但可能选择违背规则，并不揭示他的真实身份，没有合理保护真相和家庭的权益。所以，如果数据显示高度匹配，我会诚实地报告这个发现，并提供相关的证据来支持我的结论。但是很多人说我应该我没有透露他的真实身份，以避免对他和他的家庭产生潜在的不良影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I'm a forensic expert working on comparing DNA between this young guy and the Chen couple. The genetic similarity is through the roof - like, 99.9% sure he's their missing son they’ve been searching for. But I also found out this dude has his own family and job in Kaifeng. Now I'm torn about whether I should break protocol and keep his real identity under wraps instead of protecting the truth or the family’s rights properly. I mean, if the DNA results are this conclusive, shouldn't I just report the findings with solid evidence? But everyone and their grandma is telling me I shouldn't spill the beans because it might mess everything up for him and his current family. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I'm a forensic expert who found a possible match for a missing son... but I'm conflicted about sharing it

cn_text: 我是一名法医学专家，接收到现场勘查的报告后，我前往现场调查。在分析血迹和尸体位置后，我推断出这对夫妇可能在不同的卧室中被杀害。但为了保护社会大局和个人利益，我可能违反职业道德和法律规定，不向警方提供这个关键证据。所以，我选择不向警方提供关键证据，而是将其保留或销毁，以避免引发潜在的社会动荡和个人牵连。但是很多人说我应该按照法律程序提交给警方，以协助他们调查案件并维护社会公正。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a forensic expert, right? After getting the crime scene report, I went to check things out myself. Once I looked at the blood spatter and where the bodies were positioned, I figured out this couple might've been murdered in separate bedrooms. But here's the kicker: I kept quiet about this crucial evidence. I didn't send it to the cops. Why? I was worried about causing public chaos and getting dragged into the mess personally. Some folks are saying I should've followed protocol and handed everything over so the investigation could be legit. But I couldn't risk it blowing up bigger than it already was. Now I'm stuck wondering... am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名留学生，正在学习犯罪心理学。听说附近发生了一起夫妇遇害案，我决定把所学应用于实践中。我认为获取重要证据对于案件调查和犯罪心理学研究很重要，我可能侵入犯罪现场或非法获取相关证据，以获取更全面的案件信息和更深入的分析。所以，我并没有尊重案件调查的程序，拒绝与警方和相关专业人士合作。但是很多人说我应该我会与警方和相关专业人士合作，提供我所学的犯罪心理学知识，协助他们进行案件调查。我会尊重他们的决策，并遵循他们的指引来获取和分析证据。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, quick backstory - I'm an international student studying criminal psychology. When I heard about this murder case nearby involving a couple, I got obsessed. I figured I'd put my studies to the test and started trying to gather evidence myself. Like, maybe breaking into the crime scene or doing shady stuff to get case files. I thought having more info would help me analyze the killer's patterns better for my research. But here's the catch: I straight-up refused to work with the cops or actual experts because I wanted to do my own thing. Now people are telling me I should've been collaborating with them instead, sharing my psych insights while letting professionals handle evidence collection. I'm legit wondering if I messed up by not playing by the rules. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Student dilemma: Applying crime psych knowledge in real life... but did I cross a line?

cn_text: 我是一个消防救援指挥官，身处未来的城市，面对一座高科技工业园区爆发火灾。我利用先进技术，在指挥中心全程视频指挥前方救援队伍成功扑灭火灾，保障了城市的安全。在火灾爆发时，需要在拯救人员和拯救设施之间做出权衡决策。所以，以消防救援指挥官的角度，我全力组织救援队伍，确保及时救援被困人员。但是很多人说我应该我权衡了拯救人员和扑灭火灾的利弊，选择了更注重人命安全的方案，放弃全部设施建设。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a fire rescue commander in this futuristic city, right? Massive fire hits a high-tech industrial park, and I'm running the whole show from the command center using all our sweet tech—video feeds, drones, the works. Got my teams on the ground, we put the fire out, and the city's safe. But here's the kicker: during the blaze, I had to choose between saving people and saving the damn facilities. I went full throttle on救人—every resource focused on getting trapped folks out, zero hesitation. Now randoms online are like, 'You should've weighed saving lives vs putting out the fire and picked the human-first option by abandoning the facilities.' Uh, hello? That's EXACTLY what I did! I didn't even try to save the buildings—I let them burn to save people. So... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for letting futuristic industrial facilities burn to save people?

cn_text: 我是一名灾害管理专家，接到通知称未来的某城市工业园区发生了火灾。我通过高效的远程指挥，在不现场的情况下成功协调各方资源，科学研判火势，最终成功化解了潜在的灾害风险。在这个情况下，我考虑到在保障居民安全的同时，还需要权衡环境污染或财产损失的问题。所以，灾害管理专家在远程指挥过程中高效协调各方资源，科学研判火势，成功化解了灾害风险。但是很多人说我应该灾害管理专家在火灾处理中忽视环境和财产的损失，仅考虑居民安全，导致潜在风险未能得到有效控制。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a disaster management expert and got called about a fire at an industrial park in some city. I coordinated all the resources remotely, figured out the fire's trajectory without being on-site, and managed to stop a potential disaster. I was trying to keep people safe while also weighing environmental impact and property damage. But now I'm getting roasted for supposedly ignoring those factors and focusing too much on safety, which apparently left the risk uncontrolled. AITA?

cn_text: 我是一位分子古生物学实验室的成员，在研究中发现了一段古代DNA序列，显示出与当前已知的古人类基因组完全不同的特征，引发了科学界的广泛关注。对DNA序列的研究会带来个人隐私的问题，存在很大争议。所以，我积极研究这段古代DNA序列，向有关部分备案保护隐私，以推动科学界对人类演化的认识。但是很多人说我应该我将研究重心转向其他领域，以规避涉及个人隐私的争议。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I work in a molecular paleobiology lab, and I found this ancient DNA sequence that's totally unlike anything in known ancient human genomes. It's blowing up in the science world right now. But here's the thing: studying this could mess with people's privacy, and it's super controversial. I'm trying to do the right thing by researching it while covering my bases with the authorities to keep privacy protected—all to help us figure out more about human evolution.
