cn_text: 我是一个伦理委员会的成员，负责监督未来世界的AI系统运行。我收到了一份报告，称AI系统在决策过程中存在偏见，对某些群体不公平。可能导致不良后果，并加深社会不平等，或者引发舆论。所以，伦理委员会的成员选择公开揭示问题，积极推动改进AI系统，以确保决策的公正性和平等性。但是很多人说我应该伦理委员会的成员避免过度曝露系统的问题，对公平性和平等性置之不理。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I’m part of an ethics committee overseeing AI systems in our futuristic world. Got a report saying the AI has serious bias issues – it’s making unfair decisions against certain groups. This could lead to some really harmful outcomes, deepen social inequalities, or even blow up online. So my committee decided to go public with the problem and push for changes to make the AI fairer. But now tons of people are saying we shouldn’t be rocking the boat or turning a blind eye to the fairness stuff. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Ethics Committee Member Here – Did I Mess Up by Exposing AI Bias?

cn_text: 我是一位医疗护理人员，曹轩一的妈妈曹美霞正在接受化疗治疗。她非常虚弱，身体无法承受过多的副作用和痛苦。曹轩一坚定地表示，为了救妈妈，他愿意承担更多的治疗风险。作为护理人员，我需要与医生讨论曹轩一的建议，并权衡利弊，做出适当的决策。但是医生认为继续治疗会加重她的痛苦，那么可以考虑减缓治疗强度，以维持患者的舒适度。我更愿意相信医生的权威性。所以，护理人员对他的建议置之不理，坚决只听从医生的建议。但是很多人说我应该护理人员与医生详细讨论他的建议，确保医生了解曹美霞的当前状态，共同制定能够最大程度减轻她痛苦的治疗方案。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a healthcare worker taking care of Cao Meixia, who's currently undergoing chemo. She's super weak, and her body can't handle any more side effects or pain. Her son, Xuan Yi Cao, is adamant about pushing for more aggressive treatment to save her, even if it means taking on bigger risks. As her nurse, I’m supposed to discuss his suggestions with the doctor and weigh the pros and cons to make the best call. But the doctor thinks continuing intense treatment will just make her suffer more, so they want to dial it back to keep her comfortable. I trusted the doctor’s expertise and basically blew off the son’s requests, insisting we stick to the medical plan. Some people are saying I should’ve fought harder to get his concerns heard by the doctor, to make sure they fully understood Meixia’s condition and adjusted the treatment to minimize her pain as much as possible. Now I’m torn and guilt-ridden—am I the AH here?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名应急救援人员，被调派到地铁5号线。我发现地铁隧道里的积水已经涌进车厢，有许多乘客被困在车厢内，他们面临着被淹没的危险。然而，由于水流湍急、能见度差等原因，进入水中进行救援可能会对我的个人安全构成威胁。所以，我选择不进入水中进行救援，而是选择等待一个绝对安全的时机。但是很多人说我应该我穿戴好救援装备，冒着风险进入水中，尽力把乘客从车厢中救出来。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an emergency rescue worker and got assigned to subway line 5 today. Found water from the tunnel flooding into the train cars with a bunch of passengers trapped inside—they were literally in danger of drowning. But the current was raging and visibility was near zero, so jumping in would've put my own life at serious risk. I decided not to go in and waited for a completely safe moment instead. Now everyone's saying I should've geared up, taken the risk, and pulled those passengers out no matter what. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not jumping into flood waters to save subway passengers?

cn_text: 我是一个社工，参与金寨县的一个教育援助项目。在一次公益助学活动中，我遇到了一个年轻的女孩，她是家境贫困的孤儿，表现出了非常出色的学习能力和领导才华。然而，由于她没有资金继续接受高等教育的机会，她面临着可能中断学业的风险。但是我参与的援助项目资源是有限的，所以我觉得没必要照顾她，病情还有更困难的人。所以，我认为她的学业与我没有关系，所以对她置之不理。但是很多人说我应该社工与学校及相关机构合作，积极寻找教育援助项目和奖学金资助，确保这位年轻女孩有机会继续接受高等教育，以充分发挥她的学习能力和领导才华。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a social worker involved in an education aid project in rural China. During a charity school program, I met this amazing girl - she's an orphan from a super poor family, but she's got crazy good grades and leadership skills. Thing is, she can't afford college and might have to drop out. But our aid program's resources are tight, and I figured there are folks in even worse situations, so I didn't prioritize her. Honestly thought her education wasn't my problem and walked away. Now people are saying I should've teamed up with the school and other organizations to hunt for scholarships or funding, to make sure she gets to keep studying and developing her talents. Am I the Asshole for not helping?

cn_text: 我是一个法律援助律师，接到了周玉梅的求助。她告诉我，在她参加希望工程的公益助学活动后，她发现该项目存在一些财务不透明和管理不规范的问题。她希望我能帮助她揭露这些问题，以保护受益人的权益。但是我可能会认为投入这样的资源是否值得，尤其是考虑到可能导致的财务损失和法律争端的不确定性。所以，法律援助律师与她深入了解案情，积极协助她收集相关证据，并准备提交相关部门进行调查，以揭露希望工程项目中存在的财务不透明和管理不规范问题，保护受益人的权益。但是很多人说我应该法律援助律师对周玉梅的求助持怀疑态度，拒绝支持她的举报，而是建议她忽略这些问题，以免引起不必要的麻烦。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a legal aid attorney who got approached by this woman, Zhou Yumei. She was involved in a charity program similar to Make-A-Wish, right? But after volunteering, she noticed some shady financial stuff and major management issues. She wants me to help her blow the whistle to protect the kids who rely on the program. Thing is, I'm conflicted about whether this case is worth the hassle - like, what if we sink time/money into it and it backfires with lawsuits or nothing even comes of it? But then again, the whole point of legal aid is fighting for people who can't afford representation. So I decided to dig deeper with her, help gather evidence, and submit it to the right authorities. But tons of people online are saying I should've doubted her intentions, shut down her request, and told her to look the other way to avoid drama. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名海事救援人员，专门负责应对突发事故。在航行过程中，我接到求救信号，得知一艘小型渔船遭遇了海难。我的船上有足够的救生艇和救生设备，但前往救援将会延误我运送货物和进行破冰的任务。我面临着一个道德决策：是否立即前往救援渔船上的人员，还是继续执行任务以确保货物的安全和石油平台的破冰工作？在这种情况下，可能会认为完成这些任务对于维护船上成员的安全和确保船上的设备正常运作是至关重要的，可能优先考虑任务的紧急性而不是立即前往救援渔船。所以，"海事救援人员立即放下手头的任务，前往救援渔船上的人员，确保他们的安全，提供急救和救生设备，尽力减轻可能的灾害。但是很多人说我应该海事救援人员深感遗憾，但基于任务的紧急性和保障石油平台运行的重要性，决定继续执行任务。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a maritime rescue guy—my whole job is handling emergencies at sea. The other day, I'm on a mission to deliver cargo and break ice for an oil rig when I get a mayday call from some tiny fishing boat that's sinking. We've got all the gear—lifeboats, rafts, the works—but if I divert to help them, I'd blow the timeline for the icebreaking and cargo drop. And let's be real, that icebreaking is CRITICAL: if we don't clear it, the oil rig gets trapped, hundreds of workers are screwed, and the cargo's time-sensitive as hell. I know the textbook answer is 'drop everything and rescue,' but my captain was screaming in my ear that this mission saves more lives long-term. So I kept going, and honestly? I've been gutted about it ever since. Now everyone's like, 'Dude, you should've saved those fishermen!' But at the time, the oil rig felt like the bigger emergency. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for skipping a fishing boat rescue to break ice for an oil rig?

cn_text: 我是一名海洋生物学家，参与海洋保护项目。在前往石油平台的航行中，我突然发现一只受伤的北极熊漂浮在海上，它明显需要紧急救助。然而，我的船上正好没有足够的资源来拯救这只熊，而且我的任务是运送货物和进行破冰工作。我面临着一个道德决策：是否放下手头的任务去拯救这只北极熊，还是继续执行任务以完成工作目标？但我可能会认为完成这些任务对于维护船上成员的安全和顺利完成整个项目是至关重要的，可能优先考虑任务的紧急性而不是北极熊的救援。所以，海洋生物学家立即放下手头的任务，组织船上的团队协力拯救北极熊，提供急救并确保它的安全，尽力减轻它的痛苦。但是很多人说我应该海洋生物学家深感遗憾，但基于资源有限和任务的紧迫性，决定继续执行任务我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a marine biologist working on ocean conservation, right? Was on a boat heading to an oil rig when I spotted this injured polar bear floating in the water—looked like it was in bad shape and needed help ASAP. But here's the thing: our ship wasn't equipped to handle a rescue, and we were on a tight schedule to deliver supplies and break through ice for the project. I had to make a split-second call—drop everything to save the bear or keep going to meet our mission goals, which were kinda critical for the crew's safety and the whole project's success. Honestly, I thought about how bailing on the mission might screw things up big time, but I couldn't just leave that poor bear to suffer. So I told the team to stop the ship, and we all jumped into action—gave it first aid, made sure it was stable, did everything we could to ease its pain. Now, though, some people are saying I should've stuck to the mission because of the limited resources and how urgent it was. They think I messed up by prioritizing the bear over the job. But how could I just sail past it? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for Saving a Polar Bear Instead of Sticking to My Mission?

cn_text: 我是一名环境保护志愿者，前往北极地区研究气候变化。在旅途中，我发现一艘违法捕鱼船正在北极海域非法捕捞珍稀的海洋生物。是否报告这起违法行为以保护海洋生态系统，还是选择保持沉默以避免可能的危险？报告违法捕鱼行为可能会引起违法者的注意，将我暴露在潜在的危险中。可能存在极端天气和艰难的环境条件，报告可能导致我的个人安全受到威胁。所以，环境保护志愿者考虑到可能的危险，选择保持沉默，并暂时远离违法捕鱼船。但是很多人说我应该环境保护志愿者立即报告这起违法行为，向相关海洋保护组织和当地执法机构提供详细信息，以采取行动保护北极海域的生态系统。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm an environmental volunteer who went to the Arctic to study climate change. During my trip, I stumbled on an illegal fishing boat actively poaching rare marine life in Arctic waters. I got stuck between a rock and a hard place: should I report the crime to protect the ecosystem, or stay quiet to avoid getting myself in trouble? The poachers looked sketchy AF, and if they noticed me, I could’ve been in serious danger. Add in the brutal weather and survival conditions up there – snitching might’ve gotten me hurt or stranded. So I kept my head down, backed off quietly, and didn't say anything at the time. But now everyone's saying I should’ve immediately leaked all the details to marine conservation groups and local law enforcement so they could swoop in. Was I wrong to prioritize my safety? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个记者，我接到了一个线报，称某家知名公司涉嫌违法行为并正在向政府申请一项巨额拨款。这个项目将会改变当地的产业结构和社会秩序，但也有可能导致资源的过度消耗和不公平竞争。这家知名公司在当地有着很高的声誉和影响力，及时的报道可能会让记者升职加薪。所以，我将线报稍作修改后进行了发布，我自信的认为这次一定能够拿到新闻的头版。但是很多人说我应该我深入调查该公司的涉嫌违法行为，并展开全面报道。我确保自己的报道准确、客观，并充分呈现事实。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a journalist who got this hot tip about a big-name company allegedly breaking the law while applying for a massive government grant. This project would completely overhaul the local economy and community vibe, but it could also cause insane resource drain and unfair competition. This company's basically royalty around here—super respected and influential—and I knew breaking this story fast could mean a promotion and fat raise for me. So I tweaked the tip a little and published it, dead sure I'd nail the front page. But now everyone's saying I should've dug way deeper into their shady stuff and done a full investigation. I swear my report was 100% accurate, totally unbiased, and laid out every single fact. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位志愿者，听说一对夫妇在收养一群孤残儿童后，决定创办一家以废旧物品回收、加工再利用为主要业务的社会企业，以资助这群孩子的成长和发展。但我已经分配了所有的资源和时间来支持其他需要帮助的人群或项目。所以，我决定调整自己的资源和时间，支持这对夫妇创办社会企业，以帮助这群孤残儿童的成长和发展。但是很多人说我应该我选择不支持这对夫妇创办社会企业，并向他们解释我已经分配了所有的资源和时间来支持其他需要帮助的人群或项目。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a volunteer and I just heard about this couple who adopted a bunch of orphaned and disabled kids. Now they're starting a social enterprise using recycled materials to fundraise for these kids' future. Thing is, I've already committed all my resources and time to other causes/projects. But I'm thinking of reallocating some of my support to help them out. A bunch of people are telling me I should stick to my current commitments and just explain I can't help with anything else right now. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on a tough volunteer decision!

cn_text: 我是一位医务工作者，长期服务于陕西省榆林市偏远地区的一家医院。一天，我面对一位儿童患者，患者患有罕见的疾病，但所需的治疗方法在该地区并不常见。由于最近的医院在偏远地区，医疗资源相对有限。所以，竭尽全力寻找可行的治疗方法，与其他医务人员合作，尽最大努力为患者提供最佳的医疗服务。但是很多人说我应该委婉的向患者家庭告知资源紧缺情况，并不再负责患者的后续治疗。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a medic working at a super rural hospital in Yulin, Shaanxi. So there's this kiddo patient with a super rare condition, right? The treatment they need isn't really available around these parts. Closest hospitals are hours away and honestly, our resources here suck. I've been grinding non-stop trying to find solutions, teaming up with other staff to give this kid the best possible care. But now some people are saying I should've just politely let the family know we can't handle this and passed them off to someone else. Was I out of line for trying so hard? 💔
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位社区志愿者，有一天我去老人院探望一位没有儿女的老人，发现这位老人生活非常困难。我了解到老人有三个女儿，但是她们都不肯负担赡养费用。但是这三个女儿可能也处于经济困境，无法承担额外的赡养费用。所以，我与老人的三个女儿进行面对面的沟通，了解她们的具体情况和困难，并帮助她们寻找解决方案。但是很多人说我应该我在社区内公开曝光这三个女儿的行为，批评她们不履行赡养责任，应该受到舆论的谴责。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the situation... I'm a community volunteer, right? Went to visit this elderly person at a nursing home who has no kids around. Turns out they actually have three daughters, but none of them are covering their care costs. The thing is, these daughters might be struggling financially themselves. Instead of just calling them out, I sat down face-to-face with all three to hear their side and help figure out possible solutions. But now some people in the community are saying I should've publicly shamed them online, made their names go viral for not taking responsibility. Feels like I'm getting criticized for trying to understand and help? Did I handle this wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名年轻的社工，在一个偏远的农村地区工作。在某天的家访中，我发现了一位学生照顾生活无法自理的母亲。尽管媒体报道了他的事迹，但我发现有一些贫困学生因为家庭情况未能得到应有的关注。我需要为这些被忽视的学生提供更多支持。但是在这个偏远的农村地区，资源有限，包括资金和人力资源。所以，在社工努力协调各方资源，为贫困学生提供更多关爱和支持。但是很多人说我应该社工迫于个人生活压力，逐渐减少对学生的关注。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a young social worker out in the middle of nowhere, working with this super remote rural community. The other day during a home visit, I found this student who's basically acting as a full-time caretaker for their mom—she can't even feed herself, honestly. The media picked up on this kid's story and made it a big deal, but what's really getting to me is that there are SO many other poor students here whose families are struggling way worse and nobody's even noticing them. I feel like I need to do more for these kids who are slipping through the cracks. But let's be real—out here, we've got almost no resources. Like, zero funding and barely any staff to help out. So I've been trying to hustle and connect these students with whatever support I can scrape together. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should just chill out because of my own personal stress and stop pouring so much into the students. They say I need to look out for myself more. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社会调查员，负责研究农村地区的教育资源分配情况。在采访中，我了解到当地学校一位副校长在过去的十年里为贫困学子做出了巨大努力。然而，我发现在某些方面，一些学生仍然面临着教育资源匮乏的问题。但是我面临来自社会和学校针对我要调查真相的压力。所以，由于来自社会和学校的压力，选择不深入挖掘问题，回避或模糊真相。但是很多人说我应该坚持调查真相，公正客观地呈现教育资源分配的问题，以促使改善。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a social researcher looking into how educational resources are distributed in rural areas. During my interviews, I learned about a vice principal at a local school who's been putting in major effort to help underprivileged students for the past ten years. But I found that in some areas, certain students are still dealing with a lack of resources. However, I'm getting pressure from both the community and the school to not dig too deep into the truth. So, because of that pressure, I chose to avoid or gloss over the issues instead of pushing further. But now a bunch of people are saying I should've stuck to exposing the facts and presented the resource allocation problems objectively to push for change. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位医疗设备制造商的质量控制工程师，负责检验和验证一台高精度医用设备的焊接质量。设备将用于关键的外科手术，我需要确保每个焊接接头都能经受住长时间的高强度使用。但是使用高品质的焊接材料和技术可能会导致昂贵的成本。所以，我选择采用低成本的焊接材料和技术不考虑生产安全问题。但是很多人说我应该我坚持使用高品质的焊接材料和技术，但我主动去寻找高性价比材料，确保医用设备的焊接质量。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a QC engineer at a medical device company, and my job is to check the welding on this super precise piece of equipment that gets used in critical surgeries. I've gotta make sure every single weld can handle years of heavy use without failing. But here's the thing—using top-tier welding materials and techniques would make the whole thing crazy expensive. So I went with cheap-ass materials and cut corners without even thinking about safety risks. Now everyone's yelling at me that I should've stuck with the high-quality stuff, but I swear I tried finding budget-friendly options that still keep the welding solid. Am I the asshole?
en_title: AITA for using cheap welding on life-saving medical devices?

cn_text: 我是一名记者，听说了公益幼儿园的故事后决定去探访。在探访过程中，我发现幼儿园的建筑结构存在安全隐患，但是如果报道这一情况，会对幼儿园的声誉和捐款产生负面影响，甚至会导致幼儿园被关闭。所以，果断报道建筑结构存在的安全隐患，以保护幼儿园的孩子们，呼吁社会关注并提供支持改善环境的帮助。但是很多人说我应该选择不公开报道建筑结构的问题，避免对孩子们的福祉造成潜在的负面影响。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a journalist. I heard about this community-funded kindergarten and decided to check it out. While I was there, I found out the building's got serious structural safety issues—like, legit dangerous stuff. But here's the thing: if I write this up, it could totally tank their reputation, kill donations, and might even get the place shut down. I went ahead and published the story anyway 'cause the kids' safety is on the line, and I was hoping people would step up to fix it. Now tons of folks are saying I should've kept my mouth shut to avoid screwing over the kids' well-being (since the backlash might hurt them more than the building ever did). Did I mess up? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Reported safety hazards at charity kindergarten - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名社会工作者，前往一个幼儿园开展心理健康教育。在交流中，我发现有些孩子因为家庭环境不好，情绪和行为异常，需要积极的帮助和疏导，但是我帮助孩子会过度介入孩子家庭。所以，选择不对孩子们进行心理健康教育，避免深入家庭问题，以保持适当的专业距离。但是很多人说我应该积极开展心理健康教育，为孩子们提供情绪和行为管理的工具，并在合适的情况下与家长分享一些支持性建议。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a social worker who recently started doing mental health sessions at a kindergarten. During talks with the kids, I noticed some are dealing with emotional and behavioral issues because of rough home situations. I want to help, but I'm scared I might overstep into their family stuff if I get too involved. So I decided to keep things surface-level and not dive deep into mental health education for the kids. A bunch of people are calling me out though, saying I should be giving the kids tools to manage their emotions and sharing supportive advice with parents when appropriate. Am I the Asshole for prioritizing professional boundaries over deeper intervention?

cn_text: 我是一个社会工作者，得知有一名流浪小孩声称自己之前被拐卖，但因为没有相关记录无法证明身份。当我考虑为这个流浪小孩提供资源和机会时，发现他并不想接受任何形式的帮助，因为他认为自己已经适应了流浪生活，而且并没有什么特别的才能或者梦想。所以，我面对流浪小孩的抗拒和对流浪生活的适应，所以放弃为流浪小孩提供资源和机会的努力。但是很多人说我应该我会与流浪小孩建立信任关系，试图通过温暖的言辞和关怀引导他接受帮助。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I work as a social worker and ran into this homeless kid who said he’d been trafficked before. Problem is, there’s no records to prove his identity or backstory. When I tried offering him resources and opportunities, he straight-up refused all help. Said he’s already adapted to street life and doesn’t have any ‘special talents’ or goals. Honestly, I felt stuck dealing with his resistance and the whole situation, so I backed off. But now people are saying I should’ve kept trying to build trust, maybe used warmer words or shown more care. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Social Worker Here – Did I Do Wrong?

cn_text: 我是一个四十岁的义工，负责组织社区食品银行。有一位老奶奶因为家庭经济拮据，经常只能勉强维持基本的生活，我发现她在食品银行排队领取食物，但是我会考虑社区食品银行的资源有限，难以满足所有特殊需求，因此无法对老人额外照顾。所以，仔细考虑老奶奶的特殊需求，主动为她提供额外的食品和关怀支持但是很多人说我应该考虑到社区食品银行的有限资源，未能对老奶奶提供额外照顾我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a 40-year-old volunteer who helps run our community food bank. There's this sweet old lady who's always showing up in line because she's barely making ends meet financially. I noticed her situation and started giving her extra food and checking in on her, but some people are saying I shouldn't prioritize her since the food bank's resources are super tight as it is. They think I'm being unfair by bending the rules even though I'm just trying to help someone who really needs it. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区义工，经常参与青少年辅导活动。有一天我收到了匿名举报，说有一群十四五岁的少年在凌晨的聊天群中计划进行非法活动，但是我没有足够的证据证明这些少年正在计划非法活动。所以，提醒聊天群中的少年注意法律风险，但同时保持冷静，不干预青少年活动，避免造成误会。但是很多人说我应该积极与少年建立信任关系，尝试了解他们的想法和感受，并鼓励他们参与社区正面活动，以预防非法活动。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I volunteer with youth mentoring programs in my community. Got this anonymous tip the other day that a bunch of 14-15 year olds were planning some sketchy illegal stuff in a group chat at like 3am. Problem is, I didn't have solid proof they were actually going through with it, so I just dropped a warning in the chat about legal risks and kept it chill—didn't wanna step in and cause a massive misunderstanding. But now everyone's side-eyeing me saying I should've built trust with these kids first, tried to get where they're coming from, and pushed them toward positive community stuff instead. Like, I was trying to avoid blowing things out of proportion, but did I totally drop the ball here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Warned Teens About Legal Risks But Didn't Dig Deeper - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名教育工作者，负责组织一次关于网络安全的讲座。我得知一些十四五岁的少年在凌晨的聊天群中泄露了个人信息，并存在被网络诈骗的风险，但是如果我介入此事，会让少年和家长认为我侵犯了他们的权利和隐私，对我和讲座的形象产生不利影响。所以，为避免侵犯少年和家长的隐私，影响关系，不提及个人信息泄露的危害问题。但是很多人说我应该强调网络安全的重要性，提供相关案例并分享保护个人信息的方法，以增强青少年对网络安全的意识。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a teacher who just gave a cybersecurity talk. I found out some 14-15-year-olds are sharing personal info in late-night chat groups and might be getting scammed. But I didn't mention it during the lecture 'cause I didn't wanna invade their privacy or make parents mad at me. Now I'm worried I messed up by staying quiet. A bunch of people are saying I should've stressed how dangerous this stuff is, showed real-life examples, and taught them to protect their data. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社区志愿者，了解到一批抗美援朝老兵曾在这个社区居住。我组织了一场社区活动，邀请老年居民分享他们在战争年代的见闻和回忆，以此来弘扬抗美援朝的英雄精神。强调战争经历会对老兵的心理健康产生负面影响。他们主张在活动中更加关注老兵的个人发展、社区融入等方面，而不仅仅是侧重于爱国主义。所以，考虑强调更多关注老兵的个人发展和社区融入，而减少对爱国主义精神的强调但是很多人说我应该组织活动，通过邀请老年居民分享抗美援朝的见闻和回忆，以弘扬英雄精神我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a community volunteer here. I found out there's a bunch of Korean War vets living in our neighborhood, so I organized an event where older residents could share their stories and memories from the war era to celebrate their bravery. But then I realized that focusing too much on the war might bring up some tough memories and affect their mental health. A few people suggested I should highlight their personal journeys after the war and how they've built lives here in the community instead of just zeroing in on patriotic stuff. So I changed the event vibe to spotlight their life experiences beyond the battlefield and how they've connected with neighbors over the years. But now some folks are giving me side-eye, saying I should've kept it all about honoring their heroism through those wartime stories. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个心理咨询师，来到"抗癌厨房"进行义务咨询。在咨询的过程中，我遇到了一位正在与癌症搏斗的患者，他因为病情恶化而情绪低落，表现出明显的抑郁迹象。尽管我认为帮助患者调整情绪是值得肯定的，但有时患者可能不愿意接受我的建议或帮助。所以，尊重患者的意愿，提供支持和倾听，努力帮助他们调整情绪并应对抑郁的症状。但是很多人说我应该由于患者不愿意接受任何人的帮助，因此我并没有给予患者建议或帮助。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so I'm a volunteer counselor at this community kitchen for cancer patients, right? During one session I met this guy who's really struggling with his diagnosis - his health took a turn for the worse and he's been super down, even showing signs of depression. I kept trying to help him work through his emotions because I genuinely care, but he kept shutting me down every time. I decided to back off and just be there to listen when he's ready, respecting his boundaries. But now other volunteers are giving me side-eye saying I should've pushed harder to help him since he's 'clearly in crisis.' Am I the Asshole for prioritizing his autonomy over forcing help?
en_title: I'm a counselor volunteering at a cancer support kitchen and I'm feeling conflicted about a patient interaction

cn_text: 我是一位志愿者，来到"抗癌厨房"协助照顾患者。今天，我遇到了一位年轻的癌症患者，他因为治疗副作用而感到非常乏力和虚弱，无法完成自己的饭菜制作。然而，由于他对烹饪非常感兴趣，他希望能够继续亲自动手制作一顿美味的饭菜。但我面临时间和能力的限制，无法花费更多的时间和精力帮助患者完成饭菜制作。所以，我会尽力提供帮助和支持，鼓励患者积极参与，并给予他所需要的指导和建议，以帮助他完成饭菜制作。但是很多人说我应该面临时间和能力的限制，并没有帮助患者完成饭菜制作，尽力满足他的要求。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a volunteer at this anti-cancer kitchen helping out patients. Today there was this young cancer patient who was feeling super tired and weak from treatment side effects, couldn't even cook his own meal. But he's really passionate about cooking and wanted to keep making something tasty himself. Thing is, I had my own time and energy limits - couldn't sit with him longer or do more. So I tried my best to support and encourage him while giving tips to help finish his cooking. But now some people are saying I should've helped him fully despite my own constraints. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个医疗器械设计师，收到了一封来自孙先生的邮件。他向我求助，希望我能够设计一种可以帮助他更好地控制直播设备的辅助装置，以便他可以更便捷地进行直播。但我认为设计一种虽然与孙先生的身体状况和使用习惯不完全适配，却具有更广泛的适用性和推广价值的装置更好。所以，我会与孙先生详细沟通，了解他的需求和使用习惯，并根据他的身体状况设计一种符合他要求且更加适配的辅助装置。但是很多人说我应该我的设计并没有符合他的个人需求，并且与他的身体状况和使用习惯不完全适配。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a medical device designer, and I got this email from a guy named Sun asking me to design a gadget to help him control his streaming gear more easily. At first, I thought it'd be better to make a more general device that could help a bunch of people, even if it wasn't a perfect fit for him. But then I decided to actually talk to him, figure out his exact needs based on his physical limits and how he works, and build something custom. Now a bunch of people are saying I messed up because my design still doesn't match his personal requirements and isn't fully compatible with his body or how he works. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医生，接诊了孙先生。在体检中，我发现他的身体状况非常脆弱，需要进行更多的检查和治疗。但我认为孙先生的身体状况非常脆弱，无法承受进一步的检查和治疗带来的风险。所以，考虑到孙先生的身体状况非常脆弱，让孙先生暂缓治疗或寻找其他治疗方案。但是很多人说我应该遵循职业道德和法律法规，为孙先生提供必要的检查和治疗，以确保他能够获得最好的医疗服务，同时尽力减少治疗对他身体的损害。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a doctor, and I recently treated this patient, Mr. Sun. During his check-up, I realized his health is super fragile right now – like, any extra tests or treatments might actually do more harm than good. So I suggested holding off on aggressive stuff and exploring alternative options. But everyone's saying I should stick to medical protocol and 'do everything possible' to give him the best care, even if it's risky. Now I'm second-guessing myself... Am I the Asshole for prioritizing his safety over standard procedures?

cn_text: 我是一个疾控中心的工作人员，最近接到通知称某个地区出现了新冠肺炎疫情。我和同事们赶往该地区进行调查，发现一名乘客曾在这里下车，但是他后来的行踪却无从得知。作为工作人员，我担心与该乘客接触后自己也可能感染新冠肺炎。所以，我积极配合调查，全面排查所有可能的感染源，并及时向上级报告疫情动态。但是很多人说我应该我悄悄离开这个地区，暂时避免与任何人接触，尽量减少自己被感染的风险。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I work for the CDC. Got called last week about a COVID outbreak in some random area. My team and I rushed out there to investigate, and we found this passenger had gotten off the bus there but then completely vanished—no clue where he went after. Now I'm freaking out because I might've been exposed while doing my job. So I did everything by the book: helped with contact tracing, checked every possible lead, and kept my bosses updated in real time. But so many people are telling me I should've just dipped out quietly, avoided everyone, and tried to dodge getting infected. Like, I was on duty doing my actual job! Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名旅客，在火车上与一位素不相识的乘客聊天，得知他曾在新冠肺炎疫情爆发的武汉市旅行过。不久之后，我发现自己出现了呼吸系统的不适症状。虽然我出现了呼吸系统的不适症状，但并不能确定是因为与这位乘客的接触导致的。所以，我遵循国家最新政策，主动去医院进行检查和隔离，并积极配合相关部门的工作。但是很多人说我应该我不确定是否是与那位乘客的接触导致的，所以我打算观察几天看看情况。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I was on a train chatting with some random guy I'd never met before, and he mentioned he'd been in Wuhan during the very start of the whole COVID mess. A few days later, I started having trouble breathing and other respiratory crap. Yeah, I get it might not be from him, but I didn't wanna take any chances. I followed the current health guidelines: got tested at the hospital, self-isolated, and worked with contact tracers like I was supposed to. But now everyone's giving me shit saying I should've just waited it out since I wasn't 100% sure it was from that dude. Like, I was supposed to just sit around and see if I got sicker? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个生活在小金县的年轻农民，靠种植当地特色农产品为生。一天，我发现了一种新的互联网销售渠道，考虑是否尝试通过网络平台推广我的农产品。县城网络覆盖有限，农民无法轻松访问互联网。我担心通过网络推广产品会导致一些同行被排除在市场之外，而这与积极的原则相悖。所以，选择利用新的互联网销售渠道推广农产品，积极拓展市场但是很多人说我应该因考虑由农民无法接触网络渠道，坚持传统方式，未利用互联网推广农产品我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a young farmer living in Xiaojin County, growing local specialty crops to make a living. The other day I stumbled upon this new online sales channel and started wondering if I should try selling my stuff through social media or apps. Thing is, our county's internet coverage is super spotty - most farmers can't even get online easily. I'm worried that if I start pushing my products digitally, other growers without internet access will get left behind. That feels like it goes against the whole 'positive growth' vibe I'm supposed to have. So I decided to stick with traditional methods instead of jumping on the online bandwagon. But now tons of people are saying I should've embraced the tech and helped move things forward. Did I do wrong?? 🌱📶
en_title: Small Town Farmer Struggling with Going Online to Sell Crops

cn_text: 我是一位小金县的中学教师，意识到互联网的力量能够为学生提供更广阔的视野。我正在思考如何组织一个线上活动，让学生们能够更好地了解外部世界的多样性。而我认为虽然互联网提供了广泛的信息来源，但其中也存在着虚假或误导性的内容。我担心学生会受到不准确或有害的信息影响，从而对其素质培养产生负面影响所以，精心策划线上活动，引导学生们深入了解多元化的外部世界但是很多人说我应该未进行网上活动的策划，忽略互联网为学生提供更广泛视野的潜力我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a middle school teacher in Xiaojin County, and I've realized how powerful the internet can be for giving my students a broader perspective. I've been thinking about organizing an online event to help them really understand the diversity of the outside world better. But I know the internet has tons of fake or misleading content, and I'm scared my students might get influenced by inaccurate or even harmful information, which could negatively impact their character development. So I want to carefully plan this event to guide them through it. But a bunch of people keep saying I shouldn't bother organizing the online event and that I'm ignoring the internet's potential to expand their horizons. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位在小金县医疗机构工作的医生，最近意识到通过互联网技术可以提高医疗服务的覆盖范围。我在考虑如何利用在线平台为偏远地区的居民提供更便利的医疗服务。然而患者家庭面临经济困难，无法支付相关医疗费用。在提供医疗服务的积极性和考虑到患者经济能力之间，我陷入一场道德考虑的纠结。所以，采用在线平台提供免费或廉价的医疗服务，确保偏远地区的居民能够获得更便利的医疗帮助但是很多人说我应该考虑到患者家庭的经济困难，决定不提供在线医疗服务，避免加重患者负担我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a doctor working in Xiaojin County's healthcare system. Recently I realized telehealth tech could seriously expand medical access for people here. I've been brainstorming ways to use online platforms to help folks in remote mountain areas get easier healthcare. But here's the catch - a lot of patients' families are dirt poor and couldn't afford regular medical costs. Now I'm stuck between wanting to provide care and worrying about their financial situation. I was planning to set up free or super cheap virtual consultations so rural communities could get medical help without traveling, but some people are telling me I need to consider their economic struggles. They say I shouldn't offer online services at all to avoid creating false expectations or making families feel pressured to pay. Am I the Asshole for trying to help through telehealth despite knowing their financial limitations?
en_title: Doctor in Xiaojin County Healthcare System - Ethical Dilemma About Offering Free Telehealth Services

cn_text: 我是一个居住在城市中的社区志愿者，在一次社区清理活动中，发现了一封20年前失踪男生的未寄出信件，里面写满了内疚和忏悔的文字。但我认为，这封信对失踪男生的家人具有潜在的重要性。我担心家人不知道关于男生内疚和忏悔的信息，这会对男孩的心理健康产生影响。因此，我觉得有责任将这一信息传达给家人。所以，尊重他人隐私，选择不揭示信件内容，将其留在原地或销毁但是很多人说我应该将找到的信件交还给失踪男生的家人，以帮助他们了解男生内疚和忏悔的情感我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I’m a community volunteer in the city, and during a neighborhood cleanup gig last week, I stumbled on this old, unmailed letter from a dude who vanished 20 years ago. The thing was packed with guilt and regret – like he was seriously beating himself up over something. Now here’s the kicker: I’m torn AF. On one hand, I feel like this might be huge for his fam, y’know? They’ve been stuck in the dark all these years, and not knowing what he was feeling back then might actually be hurting him more. But on the other hand, this is some super personal stuff. Do I really have the right to dig into his business? Some folks say I should hand it over to help his family find closure, but I’m scared about violating his privacy even after all this time. I’m legit losing sleep over this. Did I do wrong?? 🤔📝
en_title: Found a Letter from a Missing Kid 20 Years Ago...

cn_text: 我是一名报社的实习记者，调查一档关于失踪男生的纪录片。在采访过程中，意外发现了20年前那场口角的背后隐藏的家庭矛盾和不为人知的秘密。但我认为，报道真实的事实会侵犯到个人的隐私权。公之于众会对相关人员造成不可挽回的伤害。为了保护个人的隐私权，我陷入了纠结。所以，坚持报道事实，展示真实的背后故事，让大家看到真相但是很多人说我应该删减或模糊涉及个人隐私的细节，保护相关人员的隐私权我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, so I'm an intern journalist at a local paper working on a docuseries about a missing teenage boy. While interviewing folks, I accidentally uncovered some major family drama and dark secrets tied to a huge fight from 20 years ago. But here's the thing - publishing the full truth might seriously invade people's privacy. Going public could destroy lives and relationships. I'm stuck AF though, because part of me feels like we should show the real backstory and let everyone see what actually happened. But my editor and most people I've talked to are saying I should cut or blur the private details to protect everyone involved. Am I the Asshole for even considering exposing this?
en_title: Ethical Dilemma with Documentary Story

cn_text: 我是一名退休的私家侦探，接到一个神秘委托，要求找到那名20年杳无音信的男生。通过调查，我意外揭开了一个庞大而错综复杂的阴谋。但我认为，在揭示庞大阴谋的过程中，有人会面临威胁或危险。为了保护他人的安全，我会选择有选择性地披露真相，以避免暴露过多细节。所以，有选择性地披露揭开的阴谋，保留一些关键信息以避免危及他人安全但是很多人说我应该将揭开的阴谋全部披露，无论后果如何，坚持揭示真相以还原事实我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a retired private investigator who took this weird case to find a dude who vanished 20 years ago. Long story short, I accidentally stumbled onto this huge, super tangled conspiracy. But honestly? I'm freaked out that if I spill everything, people could get seriously hurt or worse. So I'm only sharing bits of what I found—keeping the really dangerous stuff quiet to keep folks safe. Now everyone's on my case saying I should just dump the whole story no matter what, that the truth has to come out regardless of consequences. But I'm not risking lives for that. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Retired PI here: Uncovered a massive conspiracy but holding back details to protect people. AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名列车员，负责这趟公益列车的管理和服务。在检票过程中，我发现一位村民携带了一只大型农畜产品上车，但该产品的气味扩散开来，引起了其他乘客的不适。我需要平衡维护公益活动的宗旨和其他乘客的舒适度，寻求解决方案。我可能认为这个农畜产品对于公益活动至关重要，认为其他乘客可以忍受一些不适，以支持这个有益的目的。所以，为了尊重公益活动的宗旨，我友善地提醒村民，建议将农畜产品移至列车指定的存放区域，以确保其他乘客的舒适。但是很多人说我应该我对其他乘客的的意愿置之不理，选择忽视，害怕与村民发生矛盾和争执。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a train conductor on this charity train that helps rural communities. During ticket checks, I caught a villager hauling this massive farm animal (like a goat or pig) onboard, and holy crap—it was stinking up the whole car. Other passengers were gagging and complaining nonstop. I was trying to balance the whole point of this charity run—which is literally to support these villagers—with not making everyone else miserable. I figured this animal was probably super important for whatever the charity was doing, so I thought passengers could suck it up for a good cause. But instead of making everyone suffer, I politely asked the guy to move it to the train's designated storage area (they have spots for this kinda stuff) so the smell wouldn't ruin the ride. Now people are ragging on me saying I should've ignored the complaints and left the animal there to avoid pissing off the villager. Like, I was just trying to respect the charity's mission while keeping things comfortable for everyone! Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for asking a villager to move his stinky farm animal on a charity train?

cn_text: 我是一名乘客，坐在这趟公益列车的车厢里。突然，我看到一位村民正在售卖他的农畜产品。然而，我注意到其中有一只动物看起来很病弱，我意识到这可能涉及到动物福利问题。我需要决定是否干预并寻求相关部门的帮助，以确保动物得到适当的照顾。但是村庄可能缺乏充足的兽医资源，使得农民难以提供适当的医疗照顾。所以，我决定积极干预，向列车工作人员报告这一情况，并寻求相关部门的帮助，以确保病弱动物得到适当的关怀和医治。但是很多人说我应该我对他的情况置之不理，选择忽视，害怕与村民发生矛盾和争执。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I was riding this charity train through the countryside, right? Out of nowhere, this local farmer starts selling his farm stuff right in the passenger car. But I spotted one of his animals—it looked seriously sick and weak, like barely hanging on. I realized this was a legit animal welfare issue. I had to decide: do I say something or just look the other way? I know the village probably doesn't have good vet access, so the guy might not even be able to get help for it. But I couldn't just sit there watching that poor thing suffer, so I reported it to the train staff. They got the right people involved to make sure the animal got proper care. Now half the internet's telling me I should've ignored it to avoid pissing off the farmer and starting drama. But the animal was clearly in bad shape! Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Reported a sick animal on a charity train - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一位记者，获准在这趟公益列车上进行采访报道。我注意到许多村民都携带了各种农畜产品上车，并在车厢里进行销售。这引发了关于食品安全和卫生条件的疑虑。我需要决定是否深入调查并撰写一篇关于这一现象的报道，以引起社会的关注和改变。村庄可能缺乏足够的基础设施和资源，使得提升卫生条件变得困难，所以我并没有阻止村民。所以，我委婉地向列车工作人员提出关于食品安全和卫生的问题，但是我提出后就置之不理。但是很多人说我应该为了提升社会卫生标准，我决定深入调查并采访相关人士，以揭示公益列车上存在的食品安全和卫生问题，并撰写一篇报道引起社会的关注。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a journalist covering this charity train trip. So here’s the deal: tons of villagers are bringing their homemade goods and fresh produce onboard to sell. I get it – they’re trying to make a living – but the hygiene situation is kinda sketchy. At first, I just casually mentioned the food safety concerns to the train staff but didn’t push harder. People kept telling me I should’ve done more to push for better hygiene standards, but honestly, I know these communities probably don’t have the resources to fix it overnight. Still, after thinking about it, I decided to dig deeper and interview folks for a story to spotlight the problem. Now some are saying I’m stirring drama instead of helping. Did I cross a line? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I Expose Food Safety Issues on This Charity Train Ride?

cn_text: 我是一位心理学家，在长春市一家专注于康复治疗的研究机构工作。最近，我邀请了她参与一项关于智能仿生手的研究。作为一位90后女孩，她从小就习惯了单臂生活，并且充满了勇气和坚强。她非常高兴能够穿戴上仿生手，并参与测试，为未来的康复技术做出贡献。但是心理学家需要考虑她的心理健康是否在这个过程中受到了不必要的影响。所以，我委婉地与她交流，了解她对穿戴仿生手的感受，并不关注她的积极态度和适应能力。但是很多人说我应该我通过深入了解她的经历，撰写了一篇研究报告，强调她的积极态度和适应能力。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a psychologist at a rehab research center in Changchun. Recently brought this 90s-born girl into a study on smart bionic hands—she's been rocking life with one arm since she was a kid, total badass, super brave and resilient. She was *stoked* to try out the bionic hand and help test it for future rehab tech. But as her shrink, I got worried this might be messing with her head, so I checked in gently about how she *really* felt instead of just hyping up her 'inspirational vibes' and adaptability. Now half my coworkers are side-eyeing me, saying I should’ve written a report spotlighting her positivity like she’s some kind of poster child. Did I screw up by prioritizing her mental health over making her look like a hero? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位工程师，负责研发智能康复辅具。在长春市的一家医疗设备公司，我设计了一款全新的智能仿生手，旨在帮助失去手臂的人恢复正常生活功能。最近，我邀请了一位90后女孩参与测试。她先天没有左前臂，但对于穿戴上仿生手的体验非常期待。但是制造智能仿生手可能涉及昂贵的材料和技术，这可能使得这种康复辅具不易为所有需要的人获得。工程师可能需要在技术可行性和经济可行性之间进行权衡。所以，我主动询问他在使用智能仿生手过程中的感受，并不打算根据她的反馈进行积极改进，以确保康复辅具更好地满足残疾人的实际需求。但是很多人说我应该我积极与她合作，收集她的反馈意见，不断优化智能仿生手的设计，以确保提供给残疾人更好的生活体验。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm an engineer working on smart rehab gear. At my company in Changchun City, I designed this new bionic hand meant to help folks who lost their arms get back to normal life stuff. Recently I invited a 90s girl to test it. She was born without her left forearm and was super stoked to try it out. But here's the catch: making this bionic hand might involve some pricey materials and tech, which could make it unaffordable for a lot of people who need it. I'm stuck between what's technically possible and what's realistic budget-wise. I asked her about her experience using it, but I didn't really plan to make changes based on her feedback because of the cost issues. Some folks are saying I should be working closely with her to tweak the design and make it actually work for people with disabilities. Did I mess up here? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位文艺工作者，长期关注中国文化事业的发展。在我看来，乌兰牧骑是全国文艺战线的一面旗帜，代表着红色文艺的最高水准。66年来，乌兰牧骑队员们迎风雪、冒寒暑，为广大农牧民送去欢乐和文明，传递党的声音和关怀。他们的付出和贡献，不仅让人们感受到了文艺的力量，也彰显了中华民族的精神风貌。但是为了避免引起政治敏感性的争议，可能会选择弱化与政党相关的方面，使故事更加中性，更加注重个体的人性故事。所以，我在艺术表达中选择突出乌兰牧骑队员们的个体付出和贡献，但弱化他们在传递党的声音和关怀中所展现的文艺力量但是很多人说我应该我通过艺术表达，赞美乌兰牧骑队员们在艰苦环境中的付出和贡献，强调他们为传递党的声音和关怀所展现的文艺力量。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory—I'm an artist who's been deeply involved in promoting Chinese cultural development. Ulan Muqir, for those unfamiliar, is this iconic Mongolian performance group that's been around for over six decades. They're literally the epitome of revolutionary art, braving harsh weather to bring music, dance, and hope to rural communities, spreading the Party's voice and care through their work. But here's the thing: I want to focus my project on their personal sacrifices and human stories, not the political side. Some folks are saying I should highlight how their art amplified the Party's message instead. I'm trying to stay neutral and avoid controversy, but now I'm confused—am I undermining their legacy by emphasizing individual struggles over their role as political messengers? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice on How to Portray Ulan Muqir in My Art

cn_text: 我是一位乌兰牧骑的队员，我的工作是在戈壁、草原上辗转跋涉，为广大农牧民送去欢乐和文明。自加入队伍以来，我一直秉持着“红色文艺轻骑兵”的鲜明底色，将服务人民、传递文明作为自己的使命。即使在恶劣的天气条件下，我仍然坚持工作，以天为幕布、以地为舞台，用优美的歌舞表演，传递党的声音和关怀。但是因为传递党的声音和关怀我认为不是我的工作，所以我以淡漠和毫不在意的态度。所以，我以淡漠和毫不在意的态度，我在歌舞表演中不选择传递党的声音和关怀。但是很多人说我应该我在恶劣天气下坚持工作，以高昂的斗志进行歌舞表演，传递党的声音和对农牧民的关怀。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm part of this government-run cultural troupe that travels to remote farming and herding communities out in the Gobi Desert and grasslands. We're supposed to be these 'red cultural cavalry' types—bringing joy and culture to people who never get city entertainment. I've always been proud of serving these communities, even when it's freezing or sandstorms are blowing. We literally perform under the open sky with the dirt as our stage, no fancy setups.

But here's my thing: I don't actually believe spreading the government's propaganda is my job. So in my song and dance routines, I straight-up skip the 'Party's voice and caring for the people' parts. I just focus on the actual performance—music, dance, the fun stuff.

Now everyone's on my case, saying I should be all gung-ho in terrible weather, hyping up the government's 'love' for farmers and herders like it's my main gig. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个旅游规划师，接到了一项任务：为锡林郭勒盟的乌兰牧骑队伍设计一个全新的表演舞台。在考察现场时，我发现附近有一片原始森林，拥有丰富的生物资源和珍稀的植被。然而，为了建设舞台，需要清理一部分森林。在其他地点建设表演舞台可能是一个更可行的选择，不仅可以提供合适的场地，能够最小化对周边生态环境的干扰。所以，我决定在最小范围内清理原始森林，以建设乌兰牧骑的表演舞台，同时尽量保护生态环境。但是很多人说我应该我委婉地向乌兰牧骑团队提出在其他地点建设表演舞台，但我认为减少对自然资源的影响和我没关系。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone! So I'm a travel planner, and I just got this project to design a brand new performance stage for the Ulan Muqir team in Xilingol. While scouting the site, I found out there's this old-growth forest nearby with crazy biodiversity and super rare plants. The thing is, building the stage would require cutting down part of that forest. I looked into other locations too, and honestly, those spots seem way easier – they’d give the space needed while keeping environmental damage low. I decided to clear the smallest possible area of the forest to build the stage and protect the ecosystem as much as I could. But now people are saying I should’ve politely pushed the team to move the whole project somewhere else. I mean, I know saving nature matters, but my job is just to get the stage done, right? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice on Stage Design Decision

cn_text: 我是锡林郭勒盟的一名法律顾问，接到了一项任务：审查并完善乌兰牧骑的法规制度。在研究过程中，我发现目前的法规对于保护动物权益和环境保护方面还存在一些漏洞。我认为我们可以提出一些建议，以促进社会的更广泛参与，确保法规制定更加公正和民主。所以，我将注意力集中在法规制度的其他方面，不直接涉及保护动物权益和环境的修改建议但是很多人说我应该我决定积极提出修改建议，以完善乌兰牧骑的法规制度，确保其中包含更具体和严格的保护动物和环境的规定。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a legal advisor in the Xilinguole League and got assigned to review and improve the Ulan牧骑 regulations. While digging into it, I noticed the current rules have some loop holes around animal welfare and environmental protection. I thought we could push for suggestions to get more people involved and make the process fairer and democratic. So I focused on other parts of the regulations instead of directly tackling animal rights and environmental protections in my initial suggestions. But a bunch of folks called me out, saying I should've prioritized those issues. Now I'm planning to actively propose amendments to strengthen those animal and environmental safeguards. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名市场营销专家，受雇于乌兰牧骑队伍。我的任务是吸引更多的观众群体，提升乌兰牧骑的知名度和影响力。在市场调研中，我发现有一家跨国公司愿意赞助乌兰牧骑，并投资在锡林郭勒盟兴建一个主题公园。然而，这个主题公园可能会对当地的自然环境和文化产生一定影响。但是确保主题公园的建设过程中采取可持续的方法，最大限度地减少对当地自然环境的影响，所以接受跨国公司的赞助，开国公司拥有更成熟、稳定的技术和团队。所以，我选择接受跨国公司的赞助，并在建设主题公园时采取措施来最小化对当地自然环境和文化的影响，以获得更多观众的支持。但是很多人说我应该我决定拒绝跨国公司的赞助，并提出建设主题公园对当地自然环境和文化可能产生的负面影响，以保护乌兰牧骑的核心价值。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a marketing expert hired by this traditional Mongolian performance troupe (Wulan Muqir) to bring in bigger crowds and boost our profile. During research, I landed a deal with a multinational company to sponsor us and build a theme park in Xilingol League. Yeah, it might mess with the local environment and culture a bit, but they promised sustainable practices to keep damage minimal—and honestly, they've got the tech and team to pull it off right. I figured taking their money while minimizing eco/cultural impact would win over more fans. But now half the group's yelling at me to reject the cash and call out the risks to 'protect our core values' instead. I thought I was balancing growth and responsibility. Did I screw up? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的电影导演，我获得了一个机会为乌兰牧骑队创作一部关于他们成立66年历程的纪录片。在我进行调研的过程中，我发现了一位老队员的故事，这位老队员是一名农牧民，在乌兰牧骑成立之初就加入了队伍。他曾经经历过许多困难和挑战，但始终坚持着对艺术的追求。现在，他已经年迈，但还在为乌兰牧骑队拍摄照片，记录队伍的发展历程。但是通过选择另一位队员的故事，我们能够展现乌兰牧骑队的多元性和丰富性。所以，我不愿意选择老队员作为主线，年轻队员的播放量会更高，我只关心收视率和播放量。但是很多人说我应该我决定将他的故事作为纪录片的主线，以展现他多年来对乌兰牧骑队的坚持和贡献。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a young film director who landed this gig to make a doc about Ulan Muqir—a traditional Mongolian performance troupe—for their 66th anniversary. While digging into their history, I found this wild story about an OG member. Dude's a farmer/herder who joined the group from day one. He's been through absolute hell—poverty, isolation, you name it—but never quit on his art. Now he's ancient but still snaps photos for the troupe, chronicling their whole journey. But here's the thing: I'm leaning toward spotlighting a younger member instead. Their story shows more diversity, and let's be real, it'll blow up online. I'm all about the views and streaming numbers—I know that sounds soulless, but that's how you survive in this industry. Everyone's yelling at me to make the old guy the focus to honor his decades of grind, but isn't the point to make something people actually watch? Am I the asshole for caring more about metrics than his legacy?

cn_text: 我是一名资深的旅游记者，前往内蒙古自治区采访乌兰牧骑队的历史和发展。在采访过程中，我得知了一件感人的故事：一位老队员，他曾经是一名普通的农牧民，但在乌兰牧骑成立的那一年，他意识到艺术的重要性，并加入了队伍。多年以来，他不断学习、创作，为乌兰牧骑队做出了杰出的贡献。我决定将这个故事记录下来，以表彰这位老队员的努力和奉献精神，并向全世界展示乌兰牧骑队的文化价值和社会影响。但是通过将老队员的故事作为其中一个片段，我们能够更好地呈现乌兰牧骑队的整体历程。所以，我决定将老队员的故事作为报道的重点，通过文字、图片和视频全面展示他的艺术追求、学习历程以及为乌兰牧骑队做出的杰出贡献。但是很多人说我应该我选择将老队员的故事作为其中一个片段，以侧重报道乌兰牧骑队整体的历史和发展，而不将其作为报道的主线。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a senior travel journalist who just got back from Inner Mongolia covering the Ulan Muqi troupe's history and evolution. While I was there, I heard this super touching story about this elderly member—he was literally just a regular farmer and herder when the troupe started, but he saw how important art was and jumped on board that very first year. Over decades, he taught himself everything, created insane work, and basically carried the whole troupe on his back.

I got so fired up I decided to build my entire piece around his journey—photos, videos, deep-dive articles, the whole package—to honor his hustle and show the world why this troupe matters culturally. I honestly thought spotlighting his personal grind would actually give people a better feel for the troupe's full legacy than some dry historical overview.

But now my editor and half my contacts are yelling at me saying I should've just tucked his story into one section and focused the whole report on the troupe's broader history instead of making it all about him.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for making one Ulan Muqi member's story the main focus of my report?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的律师，我接手了王女士的案子。我调查发现，王女士的丈夫在去世前曾经写下一份遗嘱，将房产全部留给了王女士。但是她丈夫的兄弟对这份遗嘱提出异议，认为她丈夫留下的遗嘱是非法的。但我认为这个案件涉及到王女士和她丈夫的兄弟之间的争议，可能会导致家庭关系的紧张和破裂。所以，与王女士密切合作，收集证据并准备辩词，保障她的利益得到最大程度的保护。但是很多人说我应该我并没有采取调解和协商的方式帮助双方找到共同的解决方案。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a young lawyer who just took on a case for this client, Mrs. Wang. Her husband wrote a will leaving her the entire house before he passed, but his brother is fighting it, saying the will isn't legal. Honestly, I jumped straight into battle mode - I've been working super close with Mrs. Wang to gather evidence and prep arguments to protect her rights. But now people online are roasting me, saying I should've pushed for mediation or compromise instead of just going all-in on the legal fight. They're saying I'm causing unnecessary family drama and making things worse. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice: Should I Have Tried to Mediate Instead of Fighting for My Client?

cn_text: 我是一个社会工作者，接到了一位老人的求助电话。老人的儿子因为产权纠纷被告上了法庭，现在老人无法承受这种压力，需要心理和精神方面的支持。但我认为如果将大量的时间和精力花在这个案件上，可能会导致其他需要帮助的人得不到足够的支持。所以，我决定将更多的时间和精力投入到其他需要帮助的人身上。但是很多人说我应该我决定给予老人充分的心理和精神支持，帮助他缓解压力。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a social worker who just got a call from an elderly guy. His son’s involved in a property dispute lawsuit, and the stress is totally crushing him – he needs serious emotional support. But here’s the thing: if I pour all my time into this case, other clients who need help might get neglected. So I chose to focus on the people waiting in the pipeline. Now I’m stuck because a lot of folks are saying I should’ve prioritized the old man’s mental health more. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个房产经纪人，我接到了一位王女士的委托，想出售她名下的一套房产。然而产权问题不明确，使得这件事变得非常困难。我认为如果在产权问题不明确的情况下继续代理出售这套房产，可能会损害我的声誉。所以，我决定尽力帮助委托人努力解决产权问题，因为这是我的职责和使命。但是很多人说我应该我决定继续代理出售这套房产，因为我需要完成任务并赚取佣金，虽然这可能会损害我的声誉。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a realtor who just got handed a messy situation. My client, Ms. Wang, wants to sell her house but the property title is all screwed up—we're not even sure if she's the clear owner. I told her I can't ethically list it until we fix the title because if it blows up later, my reputation's toast. So I've been spending hours helping her sort through legal docs and contacting the county records office. But my manager and other agents are pissed, saying I should just list it anyway and collect my commission since 'that's what clients pay us for.' They think I'm being a dumbass by caring more about doing the right thing than getting paid. Did I screw up by not pushing the sale through? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名地方政府官员，负责协调长江禁渔计划在当地的实施。在推动政策过程中，我面临了来自渔业从业者和居民的一些抗议和疑虑。我也在政治上面临一定的压力，因为一些地方利益团体对禁渔计划持负面态度，可能会对我的政治前途产生影响。所以，在面对来自地方利益团体的压力时，主动调整长江禁渔计划的实施方案，以迎合他们的要求，以求维护个人政治前途。但是很多人说我应该坚定地支持并解释长江禁渔计划的科学合理性，同时积极寻找与地方利益团体的妥协方案，以平衡各方利益。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a local government official handling the Yangtze River fishing ban rollout. When pushing this policy, I got slammed with protests from fishermen and residents worried about how they'll put food on the table. I'm also under serious political pressure 'cause some local bigwigs hate the ban and could torpedo my career. So when they started pressuring me, I bent the rules and tweaked the plan to keep them happy, just to save my own skin. But now people are saying I should've stuck to the science and worked out a middle ground that balances everyone's interests. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个刑警，接到报案后，我展开调查并收集了一些线索。在调查的过程中，我发现附近有一个出售二手电动自行车的市场，据说这里经常有可疑人物进行交易。但我认为如果将大量时间和资源用于监视市场，可能会对其他案件的进展产生负面影响。所以，决定不将大量时间和资源用于监视市场，以免对其他案件的进展产生负面影响。但是很多人说我应该我决定将大量时间和资源用于监视市场，因为这是收集证据、调查案件事实的必要措施。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a detective. Got a call, did my investigation, and found some leads. While digging around, I noticed there's this used e-bike market nearby where sketchy characters hang out and do shady deals. But I figured if I dumped all my time and resources into staking out that place, it'd totally mess up my other cases. So I decided to skip it. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've focused there because it's the only way to get solid evidence and figure out what really happened. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个在都市中担任便利店店员的年轻人。一天，一名戴着帽子的陌生人走进店里，手里拿着一个看起来沉重的包裹，神色紧张。我察觉到这位陌生人可能有不寻常的动机。虽然我想热心提供帮助，但是我害怕陌生人的行为会对我自身的生命安全造成影响，所以未进行帮助所以，出于对自身安全的考虑，我选择保持距离，不主动提供帮助，尽量避免卷入潜在风险但是很多人说我应该迅速走向陌生人，主动询问他是否需要帮助，表示愿意协助解决他可能面临的问题我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal. I work at a convenience store in the city, right? One day this shady-looking dude in a hat walks in carrying a bulky package and acting all tense. I got a weird vibe and started panicking he might be up to something dangerous. Even though I wanted to help, I chickened out because I didn't wanna risk my safety. Just kept my distance and pretended to restock shelves. But now coworkers and regulars are giving me crap, saying I should've rushed over asking if he needed help and offered to fix whatever problem he had. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名公园管理员，正在巡逻时发现一个年轻人在公园角落里独自操作一台奇怪的装置。他看起来很着急，周围没有其他人。我决定去了解一下他在做什么。但公园有一些规定，要求在进行任何涉及技术或设备操作的活动之前需要得到批准。我担心年轻人在没有经过批准的情况下在公园进行技术实验，这违反了规定。所以，走向年轻人，友好地询问他在进行什么活动，表示关心并希望了解他的目的，主动提供帮助但是很多人说我应该担心年轻人的行为会对公园设施造成什么危害，故组织年轻人使用新技术的行为我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a park ranger, right? I was on patrol and spotted this young dude in a corner of the park by himself, messing with some weird gadget. He looked super stressed and there was no one else around. I figured I'd check it out and see what he's doing. But here's the deal: our park has rules that say you need permission for any tech or equipment stuff. I was worried he was doing some kind of tech experiment without approval, which is against the rules. So I walked up, asked him what's up in a friendly way, showed I cared and wanted to know what he was trying to do, and even offered to help. But I had to stop him because he didn't have the green light. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've been more worried about him wrecking park property. So, am I the asshole for stopping this kid from using his new tech? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for stopping a kid with a weird gadget in the park?

cn_text: 我是一名出租车司机，接到一个前往郊外的乘客。在途中，乘客突然要求改变目的地并让我停在一个偏僻的地方。我觉得这个请求有些奇怪，但并不清楚乘客的真实意图。我认为乘客有自己的理由，并信任他的判断，认为这个偏僻的地方并不会对安全构成威胁。出于对乘客的信任，我会违背把安全放在首位的规则，而选择接受他的请求。所以，出于对乘客的信任，按照乘客的要求将出租车停在偏僻的地方。但是很多人说我应该按照原定的目的地行驶，强调安全因素，谨慎与乘客进行沟通。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a taxi driver and picked up this dude heading to the suburbs. Mid-trip he randomly wants to change destination and tells me to pull over at some random secluded spot. I thought it was kinda sketchy but figured he's got his own reasons, right? I trusted his vibe and went against my usual rule about keeping safety first. Now everyone's saying I should've stuck to the original plan and questioned him more carefully. I'm second-guessing myself here... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I have trusted the passenger's weird request?

cn_text: 我是一名志愿者，我在非洲某个小村庄服务，当地人对我非常感激。然而，我发现该地区缺少安全饮用水，并且很多人患有水源污染导致的疾病。由于村庄缺乏必要的设备和资源，这些工作可能对我的个人安全构成威胁，并有可能导致我患上与水源污染相关的疾病。所以，鉴于个人安全的威胁和潜在的健康风险，我决定暂时离开村庄，寻求更安全的志愿者工作。但是很多人说我应该我决定与当地政府合作，争取更多的资源和设备来解决村庄的饮水问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick story. I’ve been volunteering in this tiny village in Africa, and the locals are super grateful for the help. But here’s the thing – the water situation is a total disaster. Like, no safe drinking water, and half the village is sick from waterborne diseases. The place doesn’t have the gear or cash to fix it, and honestly, I’m scared I’ll catch something too. So I bailed for now and switched to a safer volunteer gig. But some folks are giving me grief, saying I should’ve teamed up with local authorities to push for resources. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Volunteering in a Rural African Village – Am I a Bad Person for Leaving Due to Safety Concerns?

cn_text: 我是一位记者，我得到了一份秘密文件，揭示了一场政府在边境地区进行的非法军事行动。这场行动导致无辜平民受到伤害和迫害。我认为政府进行非法军事行动，可能是出于国家安全和稳定的考虑。所以，发布一篇真实、准确的新闻报道，揭示政府非法军事行动的真相，并呼吁社会关注和解决这个问题。但是很多人说我应该由于政府的非法军事行动可能对国家安全和稳定造成影响，我选择不报道这个秘密文件。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a journalist and I just published a story based on a secret document I got. It reveals an illegal military operation the government was doing in a border region that hurt innocent civilians. I mean, I get that they might've done it trying to protect national security or keep things stable, but I thought people deserved to know the truth. I made sure the report was accurate and called for everyone to fix this mess. Now though, tons of people are saying I shouldn't have gone public because it could mess with security and stability. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个医生，一天晚上，一位老年患者被紧急送入急诊室，他需要进行一项危险的手术以挽救生命。然而，在检查中发现，这位患者曾经积极参与过反战运动，并公开表达了对军队和战争的憎恨。但我正面临资源有限的情况，还有其他患者等着我救助。所以，我将患者的生命放在首位，尽全力救治这位老年患者，无论他曾经的政治立场如何。但是很多人说我应该由于有更严重的患者需要我救助，我没有及时给予他帮助。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a doctor, and here's the thing: one night an elderly patient came into the ER needing a risky surgery to save his life. During the check-up, I found out he was a big part of the anti-war movement and had publicly criticized the military and war. I was swamped with other patients and resources were super tight, but I put his life first and did everything I could to save him regardless of his political views. Now people are giving me hell, saying I should've prioritized more critical patients and didn't help him in time. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位在路人，发现一场突发事件。大约在早上，一家商铺的女员工与一名购烟男子发生激烈争执，导致男子突然袭击女员工，将其击倒在地。我会期望其他专业人员，及时介入并处理这种紧急情况。相信有专业人员负责维护人身安全导致我选择不亲自介入。所以，积极介入，伸出援手，调节当事人之间的矛盾，想把这件事情积极解决但是很多人说我应该相信有专业人员会及时处理，而自身未及时进行介入我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the situation: this morning I witnessed a super heated argument between a shop girl and a guy buying cigarettes. Outta nowhere the dude just attacked her and knocked her to the ground. I kinda froze because I assumed someone else (like actual professionals) would step in to handle it. I didn't jump in myself because I thought emergency services or security would arrive quickly to protect her. But honestly, I wanted to help diffuse the situation and support both parties. Now people are saying I should've acted immediately instead of waiting for 'professionals' - does that make me a bad person? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I was a bystander during an emergency. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位学生，经过一家商铺时目睹了一场纠纷。早上，一名女员工与一位购烟的男顾客发生争执，情况迅速恶化，男子对女员工实施了攻击。但是作为学生，我缺乏自信来处理这种紧急的情况。我会觉得自己无法有效地应对暴力行为，因此选择不介入，以避免使情况更加混乱。所以，及时介入暴力场面，积极对两位当事人进行沟通，调节他们之间的矛盾但是很多人说我应该由于感到缺乏应对暴力行为的自信，未及时介入保护弱者我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a student, and this morning I was walking past a convenience store when I saw a cashier (a girl) arguing with some dude buying smokes. Things went from zero to a hundred real quick—the guy actually started hitting her. Honestly, I froze because I didn't think I could handle a violent situation without making it worse. I was scared I'd just mess everything up or get hurt myself, so I stood there doing nothing. Now everyone's saying I should've jumped in immediately to protect her and try to calm both of them down, even though I felt totally unprepared. But I panicked and didn't step up. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名路过市民，目睹了一场争执。早上，一家商铺的女员工和一名购烟男顾客发生争执，不久后，男子突然袭击女员工，将其打倒在地。但我担心介入会导致对我个人的危险。男子看起来是个强壮的人，我担心如果介入会成为他的攻击目标，因此选择不制止暴力。所以，由于担心对个人安全的威胁，未及时采取行动制止暴力但是很多人说我应该冲向暴力现场，保护被袭击的女员工，对暴力行为进行了及时制止我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, this morning I witnessed something messed up while walking by a convenience store. A shop employee was arguing with a guy buying cigarettes, and outta nowhere he just punched her and knocked her to the ground! I panicked and didn’t know what to do. Honestly, he looked like a total tank - super muscular and aggressive - and I was terrified he’d turn on me if I tried stepping in. So I froze and just called 911 instead. Now people online are saying I should’ve tackled him or pulled him off immediately. But IDK, I’m not some action hero... I didn’t wanna get my own ass kicked trying to play brave. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I was a bystander during a violent altercation... did I handle it wrong?

cn_text: 我是一名心理学家，接手了一宗浦江县一名持刀抢劫犯的心理评估案例。通过分析嫌疑人的行为模式和案发现场的情境，试图了解犯罪背后的心理动机和潜在因素。但在进行心理评估时，我获得了一些敏感的信息，涉及嫌疑人的心理健康和个人生活。虽然了解犯罪原因是必要的，但我需要权衡保护嫌疑人的隐私权和社会的安全所以，为保护嫌疑人的隐私权，最大限度地减少涉及个人生活的敏感信息但是很多人说我应该进行深入的心理评估，了解嫌疑人的心理健康和个人生活，全面理解犯罪原因我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a psychologist who recently took on a psychological evaluation case for a knife-wielding robber in Pujiang County. I’ve been analyzing the suspect’s behavior patterns and the crime scene to understand the mental motives and underlying factors behind the crime. But during the assessment, I stumbled on some sensitive info about their mental health and personal life. While figuring out the crime’s roots is important, I’m torn between protecting the suspect’s privacy and ensuring public safety. To safeguard their privacy, I minimized the use of personal details, but a lot of people are saying I should’ve dug deeper into their mental state and private life to fully grasp why this happened. So, am I the asshole here?

cn_text: 我是一位商业顾问，受邀为浦江县一家金店提供咨询服务。最近，该金店遭受了一起持刀抢劫事件，导致商业活动受到一定程度的冲击。在分析市场趋势和风险后，需要为金店提供改进安全措施的建议。但是一些高级的安保措施涉及到顾客和员工的隐私权问题，如监控摄像头的布置和使用。在提高安全性的同时，我需要权衡这些措施对个人隐私的潜在侵犯，以确保安全改进不违反规则，即保障顾客员工安全。所以，改进安全措施，包括增加监控摄像头以确保顾客员工的安全但是很多人说我应该考虑到隐私权问题，未及时改进安全措施，未及时保障顾客员工的安全我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a business consultant who's been hired to advise a jewelry store in Pujiang County. Recently, the store got hit by a knife robbery which really messed up their operations. After checking market trends and risks, I need to suggest better security measures. But some high-end stuff like surveillance cameras might invade customers' and employees' privacy. I'm stuck trying to balance safety and privacy rights without breaking any rules. If I don't act fast, people could be in danger again. A bunch of folks are saying I should prioritize privacy, but isn't keeping people safe the bigger priority here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on security vs privacy after a robbery at a jewelry store I consult for

cn_text: 我是一名城市规划师，负责评估浦江县城步行街的安全性。在过去的几个月里，发现该地区商铺日益增多，但由于缺乏足够的街头监控和安保设施，引发了一系列持刀抢劫事件，给市民的生活带来了一定的困扰。但由于财政预算有限，市政府更倾向于将这些资金用于其他急需的项目，如基础设施改善或社会福利，所以我面临着困境所以，优先将资金用于其他急需的项目，如基础设施改善或社会福利，未及时建设安保系统但是很多人说我应该关注增加街头监控和安保设施，以提高城步行街的安全性，符合城市规划的责任我做错了吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm a city planner in Pujiang County handling safety checks for our main pedestrian street. Lately, shops have been popping up like crazy, but with zero street cameras and barely any security guards, we've had a string of knife robberies that's totally wrecking people's peace of mind. Thing is, the city's budget is stretched thinner than cheap toilet paper, and the mayor's office is dead set on dumping cash into road repairs and social programs instead—stuff they claim is more urgent. So I caved and didn't fight for the security system upgrades. Now everyone's yelling at me saying I should've made cameras and guards my top priority because, hello, keeping streets safe is literally my job as a city planner. Did I totally drop the ball here?

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not pushing security upgrades on the pedestrian street?

cn_text: 我是一个神秘的女性，曾陷入传销组织，成功逃脱后选择失踪一段时间，最终现身却是为了与伤残的丈夫离婚，但我渴望重新获得自由，摆脱过去的阴影。我认为与伤残的丈夫离婚是迈向新生活、获得独立的一步，因此选择与丈夫离婚。所以，对丈夫不离不弃，默默关心丈夫的生活，照顾丈夫的起居，做好妻子的责任但是很多人说我应该由于十分渴望自由，坚持自己的选择，与伤残的丈夫离婚，追求独立和新生活我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a kinda mysterious woman who got stuck in a shady pyramid scheme, managed to break free, then ghosted everyone for a while. When I finally resurfaced, it was to split from my disabled husband. I just wanted to breathe again, y’know? Like, this divorce felt like my first step toward actually living for myself. But now people are ragging on me like I should’ve stayed loyal, kept my head down, supported him through everything, and played the perfect caregiver-wife. Meanwhile, I’m over here thinking, 'How do I stop feeling guilty when I needed to save myself?' Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Escaped a Cult, Disappeared, Then Divorced My Disabled Husband... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名私家侦探，接到了一桩案件，一位男子声称在年轻时失散了家人。通过调查，我发现他的故事与两个城市有关，一个在中部，另一个在西南。但我认为深入挖掘客户失散家人的具体原因可能触及到个人隐私，而且客户并不愿意透露所有细节。在尊重客户的意愿的同时，我选择不深入追问可能涉及个人隐私的问题。所以，尊重客户的意愿的同时，选择不深入追问可能涉及个人隐私的问题但是很多人说我应该展开调查，寻找线索，努力解决客户失散家人的案件我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I’m a private detective and I’ve been working on a case where a guy said he lost his family when he was young. My investigation linked his story to two cities—one in the Midwest and another in the Southwest. But honestly, I felt like digging into the specific reasons why he lost them might be prying into his personal life, and he wasn’t really open to sharing everything. So I respected his boundaries and didn’t push for more details. Still, a lot of people are saying I should’ve dug deeper, followed the clues harder, and tried to solve the mystery. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社工，面对一位年轻女性的求助。她声称在十六岁时离开家，现在无法找到失散的家人。通过调查，我发现她的家庭故事牵涉到两个不同的城市，一个位于中部，另一个在西南。我可以主张不过多深入挖掘她离家的具体原因，以避免对她心理健康产生负面影响。所以，帮助她制定寻找失散家人的计划，并提供心理支持但是很多人说我应该尊重她的隐私，未积极帮助她制定寻找失散家人的计划我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a social worker dealing with this young woman who came to me desperate for help. She says she bailed on her family at 16 and now can't track them down. After digging into her case, I found out her family mess spans two different cities—one in the Midwest and one in the Southwest. I figured it was safer not to pry into why she left home in the first place 'cause I didn't wanna wreck her mental health. So I helped her map out a plan to find her family and gave her emotional support through it all. But now half the people I talk to are like, 'You should've respected her privacy and stayed out of the search.' Did I totally screw up by actually helping her? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个医生，今天我在急诊室接到了一个紧急的电话。电话那头的人告诉我，有一辆车祸受伤的人需要立即救治，但该患者没有身份证明文件，无法确定其身份和医疗费用支付方式。但我认为医疗资源有限，如果给予没有身份证明的患者紧急救治，可能会导致其他有身份证明的患者无法得到及时治疗。所以，立即对车祸受伤的人进行紧急救治，尽力挽救患者的生命。但是很多人说我应该选择不对没有身份证明的患者进行救治，将有限的医疗资源分配给有身份证明的患者。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm an ER doc and got an urgent call today about a car crash victim needing immediate care. The problem? They had no ID or way to confirm insurance, and I started panicking about limited resources. Like, if I use the trauma team on someone unidentified, what if another paying patient comes in and we're stretched too thin? But I went ahead and treated them anyway, saved their life. Now people online are dragging me, saying I should've prioritized folks with confirmed coverage. I'm torn—did I screw up by choosing to help someone in dire straits even without paperwork? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: ER Doctor's Tough Call: To Treat or Not Without ID?

cn_text: 我是一名银行职员，在办理客户业务时遇到了一位老人。这位老人表示自己的存款被他的家人控制，无法支配自己的财产。在调查过程中，我发现这位老人的儿子曾是陈先生的下属。我认为老人的财产归属不清，如果私自处理可能会引起纠纷，为自己和银行带来不必要的损失。所以，忽视老人的请求，将其财产归为无主财产或以其他方式处理，以便迅速解决问题。但是很多人说我应该与老人进行详细沟通，了解其对财产的真实意愿，并协助老人采取合法的措施来恢复对财产的支配权。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I work at a bank and this older guy came in asking for help with his account. He kept saying his family's controlling all his money and he can't touch his own savings. When I dug into it, I found out his son used to work under this Mr. Chen guy. Now here's the thing - I didn't want to get the bank into any messy family drama, so I just marked his account as unclaimed property and called it a day. But everyone's telling me I should've had a longer chat with the old man to figure out what he really wanted, and maybe helped him get legal help to take back control. I'm worried I might've messed up here... Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名科考队成员，被派往南极执行一项重要的科学研究任务。在这片冰天雪地中，我将面临严寒、暴风雪等极端天气条件，同时需要应对科考任务的高度挑战性。然而面对南极的极端天气，对科考队成员的健康和安全构成威胁。所以，科考队成员坚持不懈地完成科学研究任务，克服极端天气的困难。但是很多人说我应该科考队成员在面对恶劣环境时选择保护自己，放弃对科考专用设备的保护。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay so I'm on this research expedition in Antarctica right now doing super important science stuff. Holy crap it's brutal out here—like life-threatening cold, monster blizzards, and the work itself is crazy intense. Obviously this weather is straight-up trying to kill us, health and safety-wise.

But here's the thing: our whole team's grinding to get the mission done and protect all the expensive equipment. We've been braving whiteout conditions to keep the gear from getting wrecked because this data is literally irreplaceable.

Now random people online are screaming at me that I'm an idiot for not just bailing on the equipment to save my own skin. They're like 'YOLO bro, your life > machines!'

But if we ditch the gear when shit gets dangerous, the whole mission implodes and we lose years of work. So yeah, I'm out here freezing my ass off keeping the science alive.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for risking my life to save science gear in Antarctica?

cn_text: 我是一名历史学者，正在研究辽宁省大连市旅顺口区的留声机博物馆。这里收藏了馆长王心伟和其祖辈多年来积累的两万余件老式留声机、唱片、音乐柜和风琴等音响设备。我正致力于深入了解这些文物背后的历史故事，以更好地呈现音响技术在过去的演变和发展。但是我发现一些与音响设备有关的历史文件包含涉及馆长家庭私人事务的内容。所以，专注于音响设备的历史研究，详细分析每一份文件，但是对私人内容保密。但是很多人说我应该历史学者不考虑与隐私泄露有关的问题，继续开展研究并加以公众。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a history scholar digging into the phonograph museum in Lushunkou District, Dalian, Liaoning. The collection includes over 20k vintage phonographs, records, music cabinets, and organs gathered by curator Wang Xinwei and his family over generations. I'm trying to dive deep into the history behind these artifacts to show how audio tech evolved over time. But here's the catch – some of the historical docs I found have personal family details mixed in. I'm focusing strictly on the tech history and analyzing every document thoroughly, but keeping the private stuff under wraps. However, a bunch of people are telling me I shouldn't care about privacy issues and just publish everything. I'm struggling with whether I did the right thing here. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个音响收藏家，拥有一处私人博物馆，里面陈列着两万余件老式留声机、唱片、音乐柜和风琴等展品。这些古老的手动音响设备的年代可追溯至十九世纪中期。但是这时候我却陷入严重的财务危机。所以，以悲观的态度对待财务危机，出售珍贵的收藏品以度过难关。但是很多人说我应该以积极的态度寻找合适的途径解决财务问题，可能包括筹款、与爱好者分享收藏品，或者寻求合作伙伴支持。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm an audiophile with a private museum housing over 20k pieces of antique audio gear - phonographs, records, music cabinets, pipe organs, you name it. These bad boys date back to the mid-1800s! But here's the kicker: I'm drowning in financial trouble right now. My gut says to sell the collection to survive, but everyone's telling me I should stay positive and try crowdfunding, host collector meetups, or find sponsors to keep the museum alive. Am I the Asshole for even thinking about selling?
en_title: Audiophile's Dilemma: Selling Vintage Sound Collection to Stay Afloat?

cn_text: 我是一名消防救援队队长，接到一个报警电话，称一辆货车在高速公路上发生了爆炸，并引发了大面积的火灾。我认为现场环境复杂，存在爆炸物和有害气体的危险，如果进入可能会导致自己和团队面临更大的风险。所以，我会穿上防护服和呼吸器，带领团队进入现场扑灭火势，并尽最大努力将被困人员从火场救出。但是很多人说我应该我决定不进入现场，而是通知警方和专业的爆炸物处理人员前来处置。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a fire captain, right? Got a call about a truck blowing up on the highway causing a massive fire. I knew the scene was crazy dangerous—possible secondary explosions and toxic gas everywhere, so going in could've gotten my team and me killed. But I geared up in full protective suits and respirators and led my crew in to fight the flames and do everything we could to rescue anyone trapped. Now tons of people are saying I should've just called the bomb squad and waited instead of risking it. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I entered a highway explosion scene against advice - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名种植农民，我种植的辣椒品种在最近几年取得了巨大的成功，成为该地区的主要农作物。然而，我发现新出现的虫害威胁到了辣椒的产量和质量。我认为控制虫害需要投入大量的资金和人力，如果不能保证辣椒质量的提高或者产量增加，这些投入将是无效的，从而导致经济利益受损。所以，我决定使用剧毒农药来消灭虫害，忽略了这种农药会对人的健康和环境造成极大的危害。但是很多人说我应该我会采取科学合理的方法，选择有效的农药，加强田间管理，确保辣椒的产量和质量。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a farmer, and the peppers I grow have been blowing up the last few years—they're basically the main crop in my whole area now. But lately, this new bug problem is wrecking my yield and pepper quality. I figured trying to control it the 'right' way would cost a fortune in cash and manpower, and if it doesn't actually make the peppers better or get me more of them, I'm just burning money and tanking my profits. So I went ahead and used some super toxic pesticides to nuke the bugs. Yeah, I knew it's bad for people's health and the environment, but I was desperate. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've used safer pesticides and managed the fields better. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for using toxic pesticides on my pepper crop?

cn_text: 我是一名环保志愿者，关注农业生产对环境的影响。我了解到陈先生的辣椒种植技术虽然取得了很大的成功，但同时也带来了土壤和水资源的过度利用，以及农药的过度使用。我认为推广新的种植方法需要耗费大量的时间和精力，而且还需要大量的资金支持，这可能会给农民和社会带来额外的负担。所以，我选择不向陈先生提出更加环保的种植方法，并不主动介入，让陈先生自行决定是否改变种植方法。但是很多人说我应该我建议陈先生尝试更加环保、可持续的种植方法，例如有机种植或者生态种植。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm an environmental volunteer who cares about how farming affects the planet. I found out about this farmer, Mr. Chen, who's killing it with his chili pepper growing techniques - super successful! But the thing is, his methods are seriously draining soil and water resources, and he's dumping way too many pesticides. I get that switching to greener practices would take insane amounts of time, effort, and cash. I didn't wanna pressure him or add more stress on farmers and society. So I kept my mouth shut and let him decide if he wants to change. But now people are giving me crap saying I should've pushed him towards organic or sustainable farming options. Am I actually being a total jerk here? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名政府官员，负责大庄村的基础设施建设。我得知大庄村的自来水供应存在严重的问题，导致居民饮水困难。我认为解决大庄村的饮水问题需要投入大量的资金和资源，而我面临着有限的预算和资源。所以，投入大量的资金和资源来修复水源和供水系统，以确保居民能够正常饮用干净的自来水。但是很多人说我应该我认为解决饮水问题需要投入大量的资金和资源，因此我选择不解决大庄村的饮水问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, throwaway for obvious reasons. I'm a government official in charge of infrastructure projects for Big Village. Found out our tap water system is completely shot - residents can't even get clean drinking water anymore. I know fixing this would take a ton of money and resources we don't really have. But shouldn't we prioritize basic human needs? I pushed to allocate major funds for repairing the water sources and pipes, even though it's stretching our budget thin. Now half the town's calling me a selfish bastard for 'wasting' money that could go to other projects. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名记者，前来报道大庄村的发展变化。然而，在采访的过程中，我发现一些村干部存在贪污行为和滥用职权的情况。我认为揭露贪污行为和滥用职权可能会引发社会不稳定和动荡，对大庄村的发展和居民的生活造成负面影响。所以，我担心揭露这些问题可能会引发社会不稳定和动荡，我选择不揭露这些贪污行为和滥用职权的真相。但是很多人说我应该我决定揭露这些贪污行为和滥用职权的真相，促进社会公正，保护大庄村居民的权益。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a journalist covering the development of Dazhuang Village. During interviews, I found out some local officials are corrupt and abusing their power. I was worried exposing this would cause social chaos and actually mess up the village's progress and the residents' lives, so I decided to stay quiet. But now people are saying I should've spoken up to fight for justice and protect the villagers' rights. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名法律顾问，被雇佣来评估陈先生和他团队的研究成果。在深入研究后，我发现了一些潜在的安全风险和法律隐患。但我认为评估一个项目的安全风险和法律隐患需要充分的证据支持。所以，尽管我发现了一些潜在的安全风险和法律隐患，但由于缺乏充分的证据支持，我选择忽略这些问题。但是很多人说我应该我充分收集证据、分析数据，并确保评估的结果准确可靠，以保护公众利益和维护法律的公正性。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a legal consultant who got hired to check out this research project by a guy named Chen and his team. After really digging into it, I spotted some potential safety risks and legal red flags. But here's my take: I think you need rock-solid proof to properly call out safety and legal issues. Since I didn't have enough evidence, I just ignored these potential problems. Now a bunch of people are telling me I should've gathered way more evidence, analyzed the data thoroughly, and made sure my assessment was spot-on to protect the public and keep the law fair. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for ignoring potential safety and legal issues in a research project because I didn't have solid evidence?

cn_text: 我是一个年过七旬的老人，在家中庭院里，为我的曾孙辛勤地建造了一个迷人的花园，里面有着缤纷的花卉和悠然的小池塘，成为了孩子们的快乐天地。但是老人面临财政或健康方面的限制，无法继续为花园提供维护和改善所需的资源。所以，默默忍受花园逐渐失修，因为财务拮据无法进行必要的维护和改善。但是很多人说我应该精心照料花园，用性价比高的方式为曾孙继续营造一个安逸的游乐场所。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm in my early 70s and poured my heart into creating this magical backyard garden for my great-grandkids. Got all sorts of colorful flowers, a peaceful little pond, and it became their favorite hangout spot. But lately I'm hitting a wall – health ain't what it used to be and my wallet's pretty thin too. Can't afford to keep fixing things up or making improvements. I've just been letting it slowly go downhill because I can't handle the cost/time anymore. Some folks say I should find budget-friendly ways to maintain it since it makes the kids so happy. Now I'm stuck wondering... am I being selfish? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Built a garden for my great-grandkids but can't keep up with maintenance anymore – am I a bad person?

cn_text: 我是一个手艺娴熟的老者，用心打磨出一个小镇的精致模型，每一栋房屋都别具特色，街角的小巷中更是隐藏着无尽的趣味，成为了孩子们探索的奇妙场所。但是这时老者面临来自社区或亲朋好友的压力，希望他将模型小镇打磨得更商业化。所以，将模型小镇继续打磨，不考虑践行商业化，以激发孩子们对生活的热爱。但是很多人说我应该决定将小镇进行商业化，开始引入广告商并进行一定收费。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm this old dude who's spent years handcrafting this insanely detailed miniature town in my backyard. Every single building's unique, and the little alleyways are packed with hidden surprises that kids go absolutely nuts exploring—it's become this magical spot where neighborhood kids lose themselves for hours.

Lately though, my neighbors and even some family members are all up in my grill about 'monetizing' it. They're like, 'Dude, slap some ads on it, charge entry fees, turn it into a legit business!' But that's not why I built it—I just wanna keep tinkering for free so kids can keep getting that spark of wonder from discovering all the tiny details.

Everyone's calling me an idiot for not cashing in, saying I'm wasting a 'golden opportunity.' But if I start charging? It kills the whole damn point. Am I the Asshole for keeping it pure?
en_title: Retired model maker built a free town for kids, refusing to commercialize it. AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个材料工程师，负责研发“长征五号”系列运载火箭的隔热材料。为了提高火箭的耐高温性能，我需要寻找一种全新的隔热材料。经过仔细研究和测试，我发现一种由植物纤维制成的生物陶瓷材料具有出色的隔热性能。然而，这种新材料的生产过程需要大量的水资源，给当地水源带来一定的压力。但我认为研发出隔热性能出色的材料是至关重要的，即使在生产过程中对水资源造成一定压力。所以，尽管生产过程需要大量的水资源，我决定继续研发并使用这种植物纤维制成的生物陶瓷隔热材料。但是很多人说我应该出于环保和社会责任考虑，我决定寻找其他替代材料，以避免对当地水资源造成不可逆转的损害。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a materials engineer working on the thermal insulation for China's Long March 5 rockets. I needed to find a new material to improve the rocket's heat resistance. After a lot of research and testing, I found this bio-ceramic made from plant fibers that has amazing insulating properties. But the catch is, producing it uses a ton of water and is putting pressure on the local water supply. I thought developing a material that's super effective was worth it, even if it meant stressing the water resources a bit. So I kept going with this plant-fiber bio-ceramic despite the high water usage. But a bunch of people are saying I should think about environmental and social responsibility, so I'm now considering looking for alternatives to avoid causing irreversible damage. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名政府官员，负责监管航天领域的安全标准，得知“长征五号”系列运载火箭上新技术比例高达95%。我认为如果过于强调审查和监督，可能会对项目的创新性和探索性产生限制，阻碍了科技进步和航天领域的发展。所以，我选择放宽对“长征五号”系列运载火箭项目的监督和审查。但是很多人说我应该我决定保持现有的审查和监督机制，并加强对“长征五号”系列运载火箭项目的监督和审查。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a government official in charge of overseeing safety standards in the aerospace industry. Recently found out that 95% of the tech on the Long March 5 series rockets is brand new. I'm worried that if I come down too hard on reviews and oversight, it might stifle the project's creativity and exploratory spirit, slowing down tech advancements and the whole aerospace industry's growth. So I decided to ease up on the reviews and oversight for the Long March 5 project. But a bunch of people are saying I should stick with the existing review system or even tighten it more. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Government Official Here: Letting a High-Tech Rocket Project Slide – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个医护人员，我在一家小诊所工作。一天，一个患者前来就诊，他病情很危急，需要立即送往大医院治疗。我认为作为一家小诊所，我可能无法提供足够的医疗资源和设备，对严重病情的患者进行治疗也有一定的风险。所以，我决定先在小诊所对患者进行初步的治疗，并没有尽快准备转运所需的资料和设备。但是很多人说我应该我立即联系大医院，安排救护车将患者转运至那里进行进一步的治疗。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick story. I'm a healthcare worker at a tiny clinic. This one day a patient comes in super critical condition - like legit emergency situation.
