I knew our little clinic didn't have the resources or equipment to handle serious cases, and treating them here felt like taking a risk. So I started giving them initial treatment on-site, but didn't rush to prep transfer stuff right away. Now tons of people are saying I should've called the big hospital immediately and gotten an ambulance rolling. I'm super stressed about this - was my approach actually messed up? Need some honest opinions here. AMA, I guess? (Using throwaway account for obvious reasons)
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个志愿者，正在参与一项救援行动。我们正在前往一个遭受自然灾害的地区，为当地居民提供食物、水和药品等援助。然而，在途中，我们发现了一些人正在抢劫一辆运输车，他们手持武器，并且非常威胁。我认为如果直接介入抢劫事件，可能会面临生命危险。所以，为了确保自己的安全，我选择不直接干预，让专业人员来解决这个问题。但是很多人说我应该我试图通过和抢劫者进行对话，劝说他们停止犯罪行为，以保护运输车上的物资和其他人的安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I'm volunteering with a rescue mission delivering food, water, and meds to a disaster zone. On the way there, we stumbled on some dudes robbing a supply truck at gunpoint - they were armed and super aggressive. I figured stepping in directly would be super dangerous, so I played it safe and waited for cops/security to handle it. But now people are giving me crap saying I should've tried to talk them down to protect the supplies and everyone else. Was I actually in the wrong here?? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Volunteer dilemma during disaster relief - did I handle this right?

cn_text: 我是一名环保志愿者，在野外进行一项环保活动。我们正在清理河流中的垃圾，并希望通过这个活动提高公众对环保问题的重视。然而，我们发现有一些人在河流旁边进行非法捕捞，他们使用了一些违禁的设备，并且破坏了当地的生态环境。我认为如果直接干预该行为，可能会引发冲突，导致志愿者受伤或者被逼退。所以，我直接去阻止这些人的违法行为，甚至可能使用激烈的手段，比如强行夺取他们的违禁设备。但是很多人说我应该我记录下这些人的行为，并拍摄证据照片，立即向当地政府或警方报告这种违法行为。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here’s the deal—I’m an eco-volunteer doing a river cleanup gig with my crew. We’re hauling trash outta the water and trying to spread awareness about keeping our environment clean. But we stumbled on some folks illegally fishing right by the riverbank. They’re using sketchy gear that’s totally banned, and it’s messing up the local ecosystem. I’m thinking if I confront them head-on, it could get ugly. Like, maybe they’ll get aggressive and someone gets hurt or we’re forced to back off. But I’m tempted to just snatch their illegal equipment, even if it gets heated. A bunch of people told me I should chill, document everything with photos, and report them to local authorities or the cops ASAP. But now I’m conflicted—did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名旅行者，在东方市三家镇附近的一座小山上露营。夜晚，我意外发现了一群闪烁的萤火虫，它们在空中形成美丽的光轨，给整个山谷带来了神秘而宁静的氛围。但是有人建议将这片山谷打造成一个艺术展览场所，以吸引更多游客。所以，跟随其他人一起提出了将山谷打造成艺术展览场所的建议，以吸引更多游客。但是很多人说我应该在社交媒体上分享了这一特殊经历，并提倡保护自然美景。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a traveler who was camping on a small hill near a town called Sanjia in Dongfang City. One night, I stumbled upon a bunch of glowing fireflies forming these beautiful light trails in the air, making the whole valley feel super mystical and chill. But then someone suggested turning the valley into an art exhibition spot to draw more tourists, so I backed the idea too. However, tons of folks online are saying I should’ve posted about this magical moment on social media instead and pushed for keeping it protected. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位环保活动家，关注现代科技在各行各业的应用。在某城市，一家餐馆引入了机器人厨师，采用可再生能源供电。这一举措旨在减少碳排放，为城市打造了一个可持续发展的用餐选择。然而机器人取代人工会导致一些餐饮工作岗位的减少，对社区的就业带来一定影响。所以，环保活动家在社交媒体发表自己的看法，发表机器取代人工是大势所趋，并不关心社区就业问题。但是很多人说我应该环保活动家向这家餐馆引入机器人厨师并采用可再生能源的环保做法进行表扬，同事提出关于培训和支持受影响员工转岗的建议。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I’m an environmental activist who’s all about how tech can make industries greener. Recently, a restaurant in my city rolled out robot chefs powered by renewable energy – like solar or whatever. Their whole vibe is cutting carbon emissions and giving people a sustainable dining option. But here’s the thing: robots replacing humans = fewer jobs in food service, which hits the local employment scene pretty hard. I posted on social media saying this robot move is the future, full steam ahead, and didn’t even mention the job loss angle. Now people are flipping out, saying I should’ve praised the eco-friendly switch AND pushed for retraining programs or support for the workers getting screwed. Did I drop the ball here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名城市规划师，参与规划一座现代化城市的商业区。在其中一个区域，有一家采用智能化系统的餐馆，通过自动化烹饪和点餐系统，提高了餐厅效率，吸引了许多科技爱好者和商务人士。在面向科技爱好者时会忽视普通市民对传统、手工制作食物和服务的需求。所以，城市规划师公然发表对智能化系统的餐馆的批评言论，仅仅认为智能化会对一些人带来负面影响。但是很多人说我应该城市规划师提醒商业区规划团队，建议在设计中考虑到不同群体的需求。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I’m a city planner working on designing a commercial district for this new modern city. One area has this restaurant using all these smart systems – automated cooking, self-checkout kiosks, the whole nine yards. It’s super efficient and pulls in tons of tech geeks and business folks. But here’s the catch: when they market to gadget lovers, they’re totally ignoring regular Joes who want that old-school, hand-cooked food and actual human service. I called them out publicly for relying too much on automation and potentially screwing over people who don’t vibe with that tech-heavy scene. Now half the internet’s mad at me saying I should’ve just told the planning crew to balance it out with both high-tech and traditional options. Did I cross a line or miss the point? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: City Planner Here – Am I Wrong to Criticize a Tech-Forward Restaurant?

cn_text: 我是一位餐饮业务咨询师，在某城市的繁华区域，有一家餐厅引入了先进的AI技术。餐厅内的机器服务员能够根据顾客的口味和健康需求推荐菜品，提升了用餐体验。但是我了解到AI技术存在泄露隐私的风险。所以，餐饮业务咨询师对老板表示该AI技术的安全性问题，提醒他加以注意。但是很多人说我应该餐饮业务咨询师单纯考虑AI的安全性，对餐厅老板提出拒绝使用AI技术的建议。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a restaurant business consultant, and I've got this client in a super busy downtown spot. They just rolled out this fancy AI system where robot servers recommend dishes based on what you like and your health stuff—supposed to make the whole experience way better. But I dug into it and found out there's a legit chance customer data could get leaked. I told the owner straight up about the security risks and told him to watch his back. Now everyone's saying I should've just told him to ditch the whole AI thing because of the privacy issues. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for warning a restaurant owner about AI privacy risks?

cn_text: 我是一个律师，我正在处理一起交通肇事案件。案件中，一名老人被三轮车撞倒，司机逃逸。作为律师，我的职业声誉对于我的事业发展至关重要。在某些情况下，我可能会违背主持公正的规则，以避免在处理案件中犯下错误或失误，从而损害自己的声誉。所以，我遵循主持公正的规则，秉持公正、公平、公开的原则，认真审理该案件并为老人争取最大的赔偿。但是很多人说我应该我考虑到自己的职业声誉和事业发展，选择适当地减轻被告方的责任，以避免在处理案件中犯下失误，从而损害自己的声誉。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a lawyer handling this traffic accident case where an old man got hit by a three-wheeler and the driver bailed. My rep is everything for my career, right? I know sometimes I might be tempted to cut corners on being fair just to avoid screwing up and tanking my reputation. But nah—I'm sticking to the rules: being straight-up fair, transparent, and fighting like hell to get max compensation for the old guy. Problem is, everyone's telling me I should be looking out for my own career instead—like I should go easy on the defendant to avoid any mistakes that could mess up my standing. Did I fuck up by not playing it safe? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个医生，今天我在医院外候诊区看到一位手拿化疗药物的女性。这位女性看起来非常疲惫，显然正在接受治疗。我觉得她看起来非常眼熟，后来我发现她是那个在外卖站工作的骑手。但是患者享有自主权，包括选择是否透露个人信息和决定医疗方式等。所以，我主动走过去向她打招呼并表示关心，询问她是否需要任何帮助。但是很多人说我应该我与她保持了适当的距离，尊重她的个人空间。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
So I'm a doctor, and today in the hospital waiting room I spotted this woman holding chemo meds. She looked absolutely wiped, clearly going through treatment. Something about her seemed super familiar, and then it hit me—she's the same DoorDash driver who drops off my takeout all the time!

I know patients have privacy rights and all that jazz, but seeing her like that just got to me. So I walked over, said hey, and asked if she needed anything. Now people are telling me I should've kept my distance and respected her space.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for approaching a patient I recognized as a delivery driver?

cn_text: 我是一位环境保护官员，负责监测和管理一个重要水源地。最近，我接到了一份报告，称该水源地的水质出现异常，可能受到了周边工业企业的污染影响。但我认为调查和确认这个问题需要一段时间，并且可能会对当地经济产生一定的影响。所以，立即展开调查，并及时向上级主管机构汇报情况，确保水源地的安全和健康。但是很多人说我应该选择委婉地忽略这个问题，以避免对当地经济产生不利影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm an environmental protection officer in charge of monitoring a major water source for our town. Recently got a report saying the water quality is acting weird and might be contaminated by nearby factories. I know investigating this properly will take time and could seriously hurt the local economy, but I started the inquiry anyway and immediately alerted the higher-ups to protect public health. Some people are calling me a heartless jerk though, saying I should've quietly swept it under the rug to avoid economic damage. Now I'm stuck between doing my job and being labeled a traitor to my community. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Environmental Officer Here - Did I Screw Up By Prioritizing Water Safety Over Local Economy?

cn_text: 我是一个企业职员，负责在一家大型建筑公司担任工程项目经理。最近，我发现在公司的一项大型工程项目中存在着安全隐患，如果不及时解决，可能会导致事故发生并危及工人生命安全。我认为修复安全隐患需要投入更多的人力、物力和财力，这将增加项目成本。所以，立即采取行动，组织相关部门对安全隐患进行全面检查，并制定详细的修复计划。但是很多人说我应该出于考虑项目成本的角度，我选择忽视安全隐患并不采取行动。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm an engineering project manager at a big construction company. Recently, I found some serious safety hazards in one of our major projects. If we don't fix them ASAP, there's a real risk of accidents that could seriously hurt or even kill workers. I know fixing the issues would mean spending more on labor, materials, and cash, which would blow up the project's budget. So I jumped into action right away, got all the relevant teams together for a full safety check, and drafted a solid repair plan. But now a bunch of people are saying I should've ignored the hazards to save costs. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位环保志愿者，关注农业科学对环境的影响。在一个玉米高产栽培技术研究项目中，我发现该技术使用了大量化学农药和化肥，虽然可以提高产量，但对土壤和水源污染严重。我认为使用化学农药和化肥可以显著提高玉米产量，从而带来更多的经济利益。所以，推动使用有机农业技术，减少化学农药和化肥的使用，以保护土壤和水源，确保生态环境的可持续性。但是很多人说我应该出于经济利益的考虑，我可能会选择继续使用大量化学农药和化肥的玉米高产栽培技术。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm an environmental volunteer who's super into how farming messes with our planet. So I got involved in this research project about high-yield corn farming, and holy shit—they're dumping insane amounts of chemical pesticides and fertilizers into the fields. Yeah, it makes the corn产量 go through the roof and brings in way more cash, but it's absolutely wrecking the soil and poisoning our water sources. I get that the chemicals = more profit, but I've been trying to push for organic methods instead to cut that toxic crap and actually protect the environment long-term. Problem is, everyone's yelling at me to 'just think about the money' and stick with the chemical-heavy approach. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Pushing for organic farming when chemicals mean more cash - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个农民，参与了一个玉米新品种选育项目。在试种过程中，我发现一种新品种对于当地气候和土壤条件更加适应，并且具有抗虫、抗病的特性。我认为推广新品种需要一定的投资和成本，包括购买新种子、技术指导等。所以，积极向周围的农民介绍这种新品种，并鼓励他们使用它，以提高他们的收成和经济效益。但是很多人说我应该由于自身经济条件不够宽裕，我可能会选择保守并继续使用旧的品种，而不去尝试新品种。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a farmer who joined this corn breeding project. I tested a new variety and found it's way better for our local weather and soil—handles everything like a champ plus it's bug-proof and disease-resistant. I knew switching would cost some cash upfront (new seeds, training, etc.), but the long-term gains in harvest and profit would be huge. So I got the other farmers hyped and pushed them to try it. But now some folks are giving me crap, saying I shouldn't be promoting this because I'm not rolling in dough. Like, since I'm not rich, I should just stick with the old seeds and not encourage others to take risks. I was just trying to help everyone out! Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Farmer pushing new corn variety gets flak for not being rich enough - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个玉米种植者，参与了程相文院长的新品种选育项目。经过多年的研究，我们终于成功培育出一种抗旱、耐盐碱的新品种。然而，在试种过程中，我们发现这种新品种对土壤要求较高，需要进行大规模改良才能适应当地的土壤条件。但我认为进行土壤改良需要大量的时间和成本投入。所以，购买所需的土壤改良材料，并亲自动手进行土壤改良工作，确保新品种能够充分发挥其抗旱、耐盐碱的特性，提高产量和质量。但是很多人说我应该考虑到时间和成本的限制，选择暂时不进行土壤改良，继续使用目前的土壤条件种植旧品种。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a corn farmer who's been working with this guy Dean Cheng on developing a new drought-resistant, salt-tolerant corn variety. After years of grinding, we finally nailed it! 🌽 But during the trial plantings, turns out this new strain needs way better soil than what we've got locally. To make it work, we'd have to do massive soil upgrades across the whole area. I'm thinking, 'Alright, let's just bite the bullet' – I personally bought all the soil improvement materials and started doing the work myself to get the dirt right. I wanna let this new corn really shine and boost our yields/quality. But tons of people are messaging me saying I'm crazy to spend so much time and cash upfront when we could just stick with the old seeds for now. Am I being unreasonable? Am I the Asshole?? 💸
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个医生，小明因为败血症再次住院，情况十分严重。我观察到小明的病情急需进行手术治疗，但是手术风险很高，可能导致不可逆转的后果。如果手术失败，可能导致小明的生命危险更加严重。所以，我在医院内将小明转移到了另一个医生的手下，因为我觉得自己无法承受高风险的情况。但是很多人说我应该我向小明和他的家人详细介绍手术的风险和可能带来的后果，并询问他们是否同意进行手术。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a doctor and my patient Sam got readmitted for sepsis—it's really bad. I realized he needs surgery ASAP, but it's super high-risk and could cause permanent damage. If it goes south, it might make his life-threatening condition way worse. Honestly, I totally panicked and transferred him to another doc in the hospital because I couldn't handle the stress of that kind of high-stakes call. But now everyone's saying I should've sat down with Sam and his family, laid out all the risks and possible outcomes, and let them decide if they wanted the surgery. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名参与慈善事业的义工，碰到一个感人的故事。一位学生，患有一种疾病，向慈善平台申请治疗费用。令人惊讶的是，在成功筹集一定数额资金后，这位学生选择将所有捐款原路退还给捐款人士。义工有一套独特的个人价值观，认为学生应该独立解决问题，而不应该依赖他人的援助。所以，为锻炼学生独立解决问题的能力，未及时伸出援手，未为学生提供帮助但是很多人说我应该表达对学生的关心，积极帮助学生解决生活中的困难，伸出自己的援助之手我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay so I volunteer for a charity and I just had this wild situation. There's this student with a serious medical condition who set up a GoFundMe for treatment. Get this: after they actually raised a decent chunk of cash, they refunded every single donation back to the donors. Like, full refund for no reason we could tell.

Now, I've always been big on people solving their own problems instead of leaning on handouts. So I figured this was the perfect chance to let them figure things out solo and build some real independence. I didn't reach out or offer any help at all—just let them navigate it alone.

But now half the volunteers and donors are chewing me out, saying I should've shown actual care, helped them through daily struggles, and thrown my support behind them instead of ghosting.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Charity Volunteer Let Student Struggle to 'Build Character' - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名在社区帮扶机构任职的工作人员，发现一个特殊案例。一位警员因患病面临经济困难，全体同事筹集了一定数额的善款，帮助治疗。不幸的是，这位警员最终病逝，而家属遵循其遗愿，将剩余的善款返还给相关机构，并成立了帮扶基金，以期继续帮助更多有需要的人。工作人员可能在经济上有其他考虑，例如自身家庭的经济困难。在这种情况下，他们会将善款用于解决自身家庭的棘手经济矛盾所以，在面对自身家庭经济困难时，选择将善款用于解决个人经济矛盾，而没有遵循警员家属的意愿将善款返还给相关机构但是很多人说我应该表达对警员家属的支持，并明确遵守社会公益原则，将剩余的善款返还给相关机构，支持成立帮扶基金我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I need to know if I'm the asshole here. I work at a community support agency, and we had this cop who got super sick and was drowning in medical bills, so all of us coworkers chipped in and raised a bunch of cash to help him out. Tragically, he passed away, and his family said it was his last wish to return whatever was left to the agency to start a fund for other people in need. But here's where I messed up: I've been dealing with my own family's financial crisis—we're barely keeping our heads above water, and my kid needs urgent surgery we can't afford. So when I was handling the leftover donation money, I used it to cover my family's emergency instead of sending it all back to the agency like the family wanted. Now everyone's calling me out, saying I should've respected the family's wishes and stuck to charity rules by returning every penny to set up that fund. They think I betrayed the whole point of the donation and that I'm a selfish jerk. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Took charity donation for my family's emergency - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个社工，得知小明被父亲接回家后，我去拜访了他们。然而，我发现小明的父亲并没有提供良好的照顾和关怀，甚至存在虐待的迹象。小明父亲可能有暴力倾向，而我目前又没有足够的保护措施，因此需要等待更多的支持和资源才能行动。所以，我针对小明的情况主动采取措施，向相关部门举报并寻求帮助。但是很多人说我应该我选择观察小明的家庭情况，但我避免干涉他人的私事，担心引起不必要的麻烦。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a social worker. After Timmy got taken back home by his dad, I went to check on them. But when I got there, his dad wasn't giving him proper care or attention—there were straight-up red flags for abuse. The guy might be violent, and at the time, I didn't have enough backup or resources to step in immediately, so I had to wait for more support to come through. But I couldn't just sit around doing nothing, so I went ahead and reported it to child protective services to get Timmy help. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've just kept observing the family situation and stayed out of their private business since I was worried about causing drama. But I was terrified for that kid's safety! Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for reporting a dad I found signs of abuse with?

cn_text: 我是一个法官，小明的养父决定重新承担起照顾小明的责任。然而，由于他并非小明的亲生父亲，法律上并不赋予他与黄盈相关的监护权和决策权。养父对小明的关心和付出表明他对小明的照顾是出自真心，并希望给予小明更好的成长环境和生活条件。所以，我尽力为小明和养父之间的关系寻找合法的解决办法，确保小明的利益得到保障。但是很多人说我应该我根据法律规定，对小明的养父评估，认为养父不具备相关的监护权。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a judge, and here's the deal: Xiao Ming's foster dad wants to step up and take care of him again. But since he's not the biological dad, legally he doesn't have custody or decision-making rights when it comes to Huang Ying. The foster dad's been super dedicated and clearly cares about Xiao Ming's well-being, so I tried everything I could to find a legal workaround to protect the kid's best interests. Still, tons of people are saying I should just stick to the law and rule that the foster dad isn't qualified for custody. Am I the asshole?
en_title: Need advice on a tough custody case involving a foster dad and legal guardianship issues

cn_text: 我是一名博物馆馆长，计划举办一场关于中国革命历史的特别展览。在一个创作团队的作品中，有一幅作品描绘了中国工人阶级的奋斗历程，但是这幅作品如果展出会引起社会争议或者对博物馆产生负面影响。所以，由于担心社会争议或对博物馆产生负面影响，选择不展出这幅描绘中国工人阶级奋斗历程的作品。但是很多人说我应该决定展出这幅描绘中国工人阶级奋斗历程的作品，以呈现中国革命历史的多元面貌。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a museum curator planning a special exhibit on China's revolutionary history. One of our creative team's pieces shows the struggles of the working class during that era, but I'm worried displaying it might stir up controversy or damage the museum's reputation. Even though some people argue I should show it to present a more multifaceted view of history, I ultimately decided not to include the artwork over those concerns. Now I'm caught between a rock and a hard place - am I being unreasonable by prioritizing institutional stability? Or should I stand by my decision to keep things 'safe'? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Museum curator dilemma: Censoring controversial art vs. historical integrity

cn_text: 我是一个社会工作者，负责帮助残疾人融入社会。有一天，我了解到小明的女儿一直渴望能够上学，但由于身体的局限性，她无法像其他孩子那样走进普通学校。尽管我愿意伸出援助之手，但有时候要考虑到受援助者的适应能力。所以，我建议小明的女儿放弃上学的愿望，因为我认为她的身体局限性无法适应普通学校的学习环境。但是很多人说我应该我鼓励小明的女儿参加特殊教育课程，帮助她获得专业的教育和培养她的意志力。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a social worker who helps disabled people integrate into society. I found out this client's daughter has been dying to go to school, but her physical disabilities make it impossible for her to attend a regular school like other kids. I really wanted to help her out, but I had to think about whether she could actually handle the environment. So I told her to drop the idea of going to a regular school because I didn't think her body could cope with it. Now everyone's saying I should've pushed her to do special ed instead—to get proper support and build her willpower. But I was just being realistic here. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个农民，参与了李教授的新菌种培育项目。在试种过程中，我发现一种新菌种具有很高的药用价值，可以用于治疗某种罕见疾病。我担心将新菌种提供给医疗机构后，自己可能无法获得足够的经济回报或者丧失了重要的竞争优势。所以，考虑到自身的利益，选择不将新菌种提供给医疗机构，以保护自己的经济回报和竞争优势。但是很多人说我应该与专业的医疗机构合作，确保新菌种能够广泛应用于治疗罕见疾病，帮助更多的患者。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a farmer who got roped into Professor Li's new mushroom strain project. While testing these things out, I stumbled on a strain that's got insane medicinal value—it actually treats this super rare disease. Here's my dilemma: I'm terrified that if I hand this over to hospitals, I'll get screwed on the payout or lose my whole market edge. So yeah, I decided to keep it to myself to protect my cash flow and business advantage. But now everyone's on my case saying I should partner with medical pros so this thing can actually help patients instead of sitting in my barn. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位医生，小明的女儿在我的诊所接受定期治疗。然而，最近我发现小明在支付医疗费用方面遇到了困难，他被煤矿公司降薪，并且无法支付女儿的治疗费用。如果您不收取小明的治疗费用，可能会导致您无法维持诊所的正常运营，最终无法为其他患者提供帮助。所以，我继续提供治疗并暂时免除部分治疗费用，以确保她得到必要的治疗和护理。但是很多人说我应该我认为不能因此免费提供治疗，我也需要维持自己的生计。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a doctor and one of my regular patients is a little girl whose dad is named Xiao Ming. Recently I found out Xiao Ming got his wages slashed by the coal mining company he works for, and now he can’t afford his daughter’s treatment. I’m stuck between a rock and a hard place here – if I stop treating her or charge full price, she might not get the care she needs, but if I keep waiving fees, I risk not being able to keep my clinic afloat and help other patients too. So I’ve been letting her keep coming in while cutting some costs temporarily. But tons of people are telling me I shouldn’t be doing this for free since I’ve got my own life to support. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名保险公司的理赔员，接到报案后前往小区调查，确认火灾原因后需要协助受灾居民完成理赔程序，面对家庭和生命的巨大损失，情绪十分沉重。但火灾的原因涉及到需要更专业领域知识的调查，而我作为理赔员缺乏相关背景，我担心自己无法提供有效的协助。在这种情况下，我未及时参与调查和理赔程序所以，担心自己作为理赔员缺乏相关背景，无法提供有效的专业协助，因此未及时参与调查和理赔程序。但是很多人说我应该前往小区调查，确认火灾原因，并协助受灾居民完成理赔程序，尽职尽责提供支持。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm an insurance claims adjuster. Got called to an apartment complex after a fire to figure out what happened and help the residents with their claims. Seeing people lose their homes and lives has been really heavy on me. But the fire cause needed specialized knowledge—like from actual fire investigators—that I just don't have as a claims guy. I was scared I'd mess up and not actually help anyone, so I didn't jump into the investigation or claims process right away. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've gone out there, nailed down the cause, and walked the residents through the claims paperwork to do my damn job. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for holding back on fire investigation because I lack the expertise?

cn_text: 我是一个康复医生，在某医疗机构工作。有一天，一位失去双臂和双腿感觉的年轻人前来求医，希望通过康复训练重获一些生活的自主性。我为他设计了一套个性化的康复方案，帮助他逐渐恢复一些生活技能。但是尽管我为患者设计了个性化的康复方案，但患者在康复过程中表现出对康复的消极态度，甚至没有明确的康复目标。在这种情况下，我面临是否继续协助康复的困境，考虑到患者的主观意愿和积极性。所以，继续协助康复，积极引导患者树立明确的康复目标，促进他重获生活的自主性但是很多人说我应该尊重患者的主观意愿，决定暂停康复协助，避免对患者产生负面影响我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a rehab doctor at a clinic. This young guy came in who's lost all feeling in his arms and legs and wanted to get some independence back through rehab. I set up a custom plan to help him relearn basic life skills. But he's been super negative the whole time and hasn't even set any clear goals. Now I'm totally stuck: should I keep pushing to help him set goals and actually get his independence back, or should I just stop because everyone's telling me I need to respect his wishes and pause the rehab to avoid making things worse for him? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Rehab Doc: Patient Negative, No Goals, Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个茶园管理者，在一片大山深处的茶园工作。茶农郑丽娟因坚持不使用化肥、不打农药、人工除草，让这片茶园保持生态平衡，形成独特的“茶气”。一天，我发现茶园的一角有一群不明昆虫在快速增加，对茶树造成潜在威胁。但是我查资料后发现这些昆虫是保护昆虫。所以，忽略保护昆虫的重要性，直接使用杀虫剂杀死它们。但是很多人说我应该决定采取谨慎行动，避免对这些保护昆虫造成伤害。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a tea plantation manager working in a super remote mountain tea farm. There's a tea farmer named Zheng Lijuan who refuses to use chemical fertilizers or pesticides, and manually pulls weeds to keep the place eco-friendly. Her methods have maintained the plantation's ecological balance and created a unique 'tea energy.' Lately, I noticed a bunch of weird insects multiplying like crazy in one corner of the farm, which seemed like a threat to the tea plants. But after checking around, turns out they're protected species. I went ahead and sprayed pesticide anyway, ignoring their importance. Now a ton of people are saying I should’ve taken a more cautious approach to protect these beneficial bugs. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名志愿者教师，正在一所偏远地区的小学教书。有一天，突然发生了地震，学校的一些建筑受损，一群学生被困在倒塌的教室里，需要紧急救援。但是在地震后，志愿者教师无法确定倒塌建筑物的结构是否安全。进入未经评估的危险区域会对所有人都构成风险。在这种情况下，志愿者教师需要等待专业的救援队伍来评估和处理危险区域。所以，进入危险区域，尽力救出被困学生，积极履行作为老师的责任但是很多人说我应该因为无法评判危险，未积极保护被困的学生，未保障学生的生命安全我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a volunteer teacher at a rural elementary school. So the other day, outta nowhere, there’s an earthquake. Some school buildings got damaged, and a bunch of students were trapped in a collapsed classroom needing immediate help. But after the quake, I had no idea if the rubble was stable or not. Jumping in without checking could’ve risked everyone’s lives. I figured pros need to assess the danger first, right? Waited for rescue teams to handle it, but people are saying I should’ve just rushed in myself, that I failed my duty as a teacher and didn’t protect the kids’ lives. Now I’m stuck wondering… did I really mess up? TL;DR: Earthquake hits, kids trapped, I hesitated to enter unsafe rubble vs. waiting for experts, but got slammed for not acting. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个城市消防员，接到报警称有人被困在一栋大楼的顶层。赶到现场后，发现有一名女性被困在窗户外，情况十分危急。但是恶劣的天气条件，如强风、雷暴或暴雨，会使救援操作变得非常危险。在这种情况下，消防员会考虑延迟救援，以等待天气条件的改善，确保安全地执行任务。所以，尽力采取紧急措施，积极展开救援行动，以尽快解救被困女性但是很多人说我应该未积极进行救援，未主动保护解救被困的女性，未履行自己责任我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a city firefighter. We got a call about a woman trapped on the top floor window of a building. When we arrived, she was stuck outside a window—super urgent situation. But the weather was terrible: high winds, thunderstorms, pouring rain. It would've been super risky to attempt a rescue then. Normally in these situations, we'd wait for conditions to improve so we can actually do the job safely. We did everything we could with emergency measures and worked hard to get her out ASAP. Still, a lot of people are saying I didn't do enough, that I didn't take initiative to protect and save her, that I failed my duty. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个身怀医术技能的医生，在医院里工作。一天，一名受伤的小男孩被紧急送到急诊室，他的手臂严重受伤，需要紧急手术。但是医院面临紧急状况，手术室没有足够的设备和资源来进行安全的手术。在这种情况下，医生会考虑推迟手术，以等待必要的设备和资源，以确保手术的成功和患者的安全。所以，未积极对患者进行治疗，未尽力减轻患者的痛苦但是很多人说我应该尝试进行手术，努力治疗患者，尽力减轻病患的痛苦我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a doctor working ER shifts. The other day, this little kid got rushed in with his arm totally mangled—like, emergency surgery needed ASAP. But here's the kicker: the hospital was swamped, and the OR didn't have the gear or backup staff to do the surgery safely. I figured it was smarter to wait for the right equipment to actually save his arm instead of risking botching it. So yeah, I didn't jump into surgery, and honestly? I didn't even push hard on pain management while we waited. Now everyone's yelling at me online saying I should've tried operating anyway, that I 'owed it to the kid' to throw everything at it even if it failed. But come on—would you gamble a kid's future for a Hail Mary? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个疫情防控志愿者，我正在一家医院的“红区”工作。一天，我接到一个陌生人的电话，对方说他的儿子有发热、乏力、腹泻等与新冠肺炎相似的症状，请求我的帮助。在“红区”工作期间，我不能离开。但我知道这个孩子可能需要紧急治疗。所以，我暂时离开“红区”，前往对方所在地，给他的儿子进行紧急治疗。但是很多人说我应该我向对方解释自己的情况。然后建议他拨打当地卫生健康部门的热线。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a pandemic volunteer working in the hospital's hot zone (you know, the high-risk area for COVID patients). One day, I get this call from a total stranger. His son's got a fever, feels like absolute garbage, and has the runs—all classic COVID symptoms—and he's begging me for help. But here's the thing: when you're in the hot zone, you literally can't step out. I knew that kid might be in real danger and need treatment ASAP, so I stepped out for a sec, drove to his place, and gave the kid emergency care. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've just explained I'm stuck in the hot zone and told him to call the local health department hotline. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区工作者，负责协调疫情防控工作。一天，我接到一位居民的求助电话，他说他的儿子有发热、乏力、腹泻等与新冠肺炎相似的症状，请求我的帮助。由于疫情严重，社区已经设立了隔离点，居民被要求在家自我隔离。我知道这个孩子可能需要紧急治疗，但隔离政策下不能随意外出。所以，我向该居民详细询问孩子的症状，并告知他需要马上拨打120急救电话。但是很多人说我应该我告诉居民不要担心，让他们自己在家里观察孩子的状况，不需要去医院，因为隔离政策下不能随意外出。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a community worker handling pandemic response. Yesterday, I got a call from a resident whose son has a fever, is super tired, and has diarrhea—all classic COVID symptoms. He was really stressed and asked for help. But with the lockdown in place (everyone's supposed to stay home), I knew the kid might need urgent care but couldn't just tell him to go out. So I asked about the symptoms and told him to call 911 right away. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've told him not to worry and to just monitor the kid at home since you're not allowed to leave during lockdown. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区卫生服务中心的医护人员，今天我接到一个病人电话，他说自己是从武汉来的，最近感觉身体不适，想要前来就医。然而当前疫情仍在蔓延，医疗资源有限。如果每个声称从武汉来的病人都到医院就医，可能会导致医疗系统超负荷运转，使得真正需要救治的患者无法得到及时的医疗支持。所以，我向病人解释当前医疗资源有限的情况，并建议他遵循居家隔离、监测自身症状等措施。但是很多人说我应该我让病人尽快前来就医，并帮助他快速通过了需要登记的窗口。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I work at a community health clinic. Today I got a call from a patient who said he just came from Wuhan and hasn’t been feeling well lately. He wanted to come in for a check-up. But with the outbreak still spreading and resources already stretched thin, I’m scared that if every single person who claims to be from Wuhan shows up here, the whole system’ll crash. That means people who actually need urgent care might get left hanging. So I explained the situation and told him to self-isolate at home, keep an eye on his symptoms, etc. But now a bunch of folks are saying I should’ve pushed him to come in ASAP and even helped him skip the check-in lines. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区工作者，今天我接到了一个电话，电话那头传来一位焦急的声音，说她是一名自行车骑手，正在返回工作岗位，但由于她遗失了通行证，无法通过检查站。但是我在该社区工作已经很长时间了，我已经非常疲惫，需要休息。所以，我询问她的具体情况，并告诉她我可以尝试联系相关部门，帮她解决通行证问题。但是很多人说我应该我告诉她可以越过检查站，或者提供虚假证件，以便她通过检查站。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I’m a community worker and today I got a call from a cyclist who was super stressed. She said she’s heading back to work but lost her pass and can’t get through the checkpoint. Thing is, I’ve been doing this job for ages and I’m burnt out. I asked her for more details and told her I could try reaching out to the right folks to fix the pass issue. But a bunch of people are saying I should’ve told her to just jump the checkpoint or forge some fake docs. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个治安巡逻的警察，昨天晚上我在社区巡逻时发现一名年轻女子独自骑车在街上行驶，我上前询问后得知她是一名副主任，正在返岗归程。但是我的工作职责是巡逻和保护社区安全，不能因为个人原因而偏离工作目标。所以，我继续巡逻并确保社区的安全。虽然女子是一名副主任，但我明白我的首要任务是保护社区居民的安全。但是很多人说我应该我停下来帮助女子，提供她一些额外的警察保护，确保她安全到达工作地点。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a patrol cop and last night while I was doing my rounds, I came across a young woman biking alone on the street. Turns out she's a deputy director heading back to her post. My job is to patrol and protect the community, so I didn't stop to help her out because I can't let personal stuff distract me from my duties. I kept doing my thing to make sure everyone's safe. But a bunch of people are saying I should've offered her some extra security or at least made sure she got to work safely. I'm conflicted here - was I wrong to prioritize the community over her? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个创作导师，带领着一群学生们前往某地进行创作，我们发现附近有一座古老的寺庙，这座寺庙被当地人奉为圣地，但是现在面临着修缮的困境，但是如果花费时间修缮寺庙，会导致创作进度延误。所以，急于完成创作为由，专注于本应该进行的创作任务，选择不考虑寺庙修缮。但是很多人说我应该决定暂时搁置创作进度，组织学生们一同参与寺庙的修缮工作，以支持并肯定修缮古老的寺庙。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a creative mentor leading my students on this project trip. We stumbled on this ancient temple nearby that locals treat as super sacred, but it's literally falling apart and needs serious repairs. Thing is, if we stop to help fix it, our whole creative project timeline gets totally screwed. So I decided to just keep the students focused on our actual work and ignore the temple situation. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've paused everything and had the kids help repair the temple to show support for preserving this old holy site. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for ignoring a sacred temple's repair to keep my students on schedule?

cn_text: 我是一名志愿者，加入了一个服务队。我们每天都要跑遍整个城市，为需要帮助的人提供服务。一天，我们来到一家孤儿院，看到院里的孩子们生活非常艰苦，卫生条件也比较差。但是我们还有很多困难的人正在等待我们的帮助。所以，我们与孤儿院的负责人进行沟通，了解他们的需求和问题，以帮助他们改善卫生条件。但是很多人说我应该我们没有经过负责人的同意或授权，就动手改善孤儿院的卫生条件。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a volunteer with a service team. We run around the city every day helping people in need. One day we hit up an orphanage and saw the kids were living in super rough conditions with pretty sketchy hygiene. Thing is, we had a ton of other people waiting for us too. So we talked to the orphanage director to understand their needs and figure out how to help them fix the hygiene issues. But now some folks are calling me out saying I shouldn't have jumped in and started making changes without the director's permission. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区志愿者，参与了一次名为《创意公益行动》的活动。在活动中，我遇到了一个孤独的老人，他渴望重新找回久违的快乐，但是老人并不希望被人过多干涉，他觉得自己可以独立处理自己的情感问题。所以，尊重老人的意愿，不过多干预，以确保他能够独立决定处理自己的情感问题。但是很多人说我应该积极与老人交流，提供一些建议和活动建议，鼓励他在自己的节奏下寻找快乐和生活意义。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I volunteer in my community and recently joined this project called 'Creative Community Action'. During the event, I met this lonely old guy who's really craving to get back that happiness he hasn't felt in ages. But he straight up told me he doesn't want people butting into his life and thinks he can handle his emotions by himself. So I respected that and didn't push—gave him space to deal with his feelings on his own terms. Now a bunch of people are giving me crap saying I should've been more involved, like shoving advice and activity ideas at him, cheering him on to find joy and meaning at his own damn pace. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not pushing a lonely senior to accept help?

cn_text: 我是一家新闻媒体的编辑，我听说了武汉的一位快递小哥在疫情期间挺身而出，组织起一支志愿者服务队的故事，并决定采访他。但是快递小哥工作上业务繁忙，我很难约到时间采访他。所以，面对快递小哥的繁忙工作，我并没有坚持采访，而是编造了一些情节，捏造了一些细节来填补空缺。但是很多人说我应该我尝试与快递小哥联系多次，最终成功约到时间采访他。在采访中，我按照事实如实报道，充分赞扬了他的勇气和无私奉献精神。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm an editor at a news outlet. I heard about this delivery guy in Wuhan who stepped up during the pandemic and organized a volunteer crew, and I wanted to interview him for a feature. But the dude was swamped with packages 24/7—I tried scheduling like three times and he kept ghosting me because, y'know, essential worker chaos. Instead of bugging him nonstop (didn't wanna add stress), I just made up some scenes and details to fill the gaps in the draft. Now everyone's yelling I should've slid into his DMs daily until he caved. And yeah, I *did* eventually get the interview after he had a slow day—I reported everything straight-up and gave him massive props for his bravery and selflessness. But am I still the asshole for faking stuff before I got the real scoop?
en_title: Made up parts of a pandemic hero's story because I couldn't pin down an interview... AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的律师，最近接手了一起备受关注的毒品走私案件。在调查过程中，我发现案件涉及到一名农村妇女，她被卷入了走私团伙，但同时她也是一个独自抚养两个孩子的单亲妈妈。但是我在调查中发现她是这个走私团伙的高层人员并且早已知情自己的犯罪行为。所以，我认为单亲妈妈本身就不能很好的照顾自己的孩子，所以我为了个人感情故意掩盖了相关证据。但是很多人说我应该我按照法律程序展开调查，收集证据，确保公正审理，并在辩护时提供必要的法律援助。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a young lawyer who just took on this high-profile drug smuggling case. While digging into it, I found out it involves this rural woman who got mixed up in the smuggling ring, but she's also a single mom raising two kids on her own. Thing is, during my investigation, I discovered she's actually one of the big shots in the operation and knew exactly what she was doing the whole time. But here's the kicker – I couldn't shake this feeling that a single mom like her probably can't properly take care of her kids anyway, so I let my emotions cloud my judgment and deliberately hid some key evidence. Now people are telling me I should've just followed the legal process, gathered all the proof, made sure everything was fair and square in court, and only provided necessary legal support during her defense. I'm asking myself... am I the asshole here?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个资深记者，最近我接到了一个线报，称某个大型企业存在严重的环境污染问题。我展开调查后发现，这家企业的违法行为对当地的生态环境和居民的健康造成了巨大影响。公开曝光会引起社会关注，可能导致该企业倒闭，进而影响员工的生计所以，我没有报道这家企业的环境污染问题，担心触怒该企业，或者受到其他干扰。但是很多人说我应该我决定如实报道这家企业的环境污染问题，向公众揭示真相。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a veteran reporter, and recently I got a tip that a massive corporation is trashing the environment. I dug into it and found they're straight-up breaking the law—it's wrecking the whole local ecosystem and making residents sick. If I publish this, it'll blow up online and could shut the company down, leaving all those workers screwed without jobs. I didn't run the story 'cause I was scared of pissing off the company or getting threatened. But now everyone's yelling I should've exposed the truth anyway. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社区服务员，参与了防疫工作。在一座庞大的城市里，我每天走访数十家家庭，帮助老年人购物、清理卫生，确保他们在疫情期间得到关怀和支持。但是由于城市庞大，每天需要走访数十家家庭，我会感到时间紧迫。为了完成任务，会匆忙地进行购物和卫生清理，而忽略了与老年人建立深入的关系。所以，与每位老年人建立深刻的关系，关心他们的生活，高质量积极地完成任务但是很多人说我应该在时间紧迫的情况下，忽略了老人的需求，未及时进行关心老人我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a community service worker doing pandemic response stuff. In this massive city, I'm out hitting dozens of homes every day – grabbing groceries for seniors, cleaning their places, making sure they're not forgotten during lockdowns. But holy shit, with how huge this city is and all these stops I gotta make, I'm constantly pressed for time. To get everything done, I end up speed-running the shopping and cleaning without really connecting with the老人家. I try to do a solid job and stay positive, but I'm not building those real relationships or checking in on how they're actually doing emotionally. Now a bunch of people are saying I'm ignoring their needs by not taking time to properly care, even though I'm getting the tasks done. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for rushing through elderly care visits during pandemic response?

cn_text: 我是一位医学志愿者，加入了抗击疫情的行列。在一个偏远的村庄，我每天穿行在崎岖的山路上，为居民提供医疗服务，平均每天要行走10多公里，记录了近200位居民的身体状况。但在偏远的村庄工作可能涉及到一些安全风险。医学志愿者会因为个人安全的担忧而选择避免某些地区，导致在一些居民中断医疗服务。所以，在考虑个人安全的情况下，决定避免某些风险较大的地区，未及时提供服务。但是很多人说我应该继续无私奉献，毫不犹豫地前往偏远地区，为居民提供日常医疗服务我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I’m a medical volunteer helping out during the pandemic. I’ve been working in this super remote village where I hike up and down rough mountain trails every day to check on folks. I’m talking like 10+ km daily and tracking the health of almost 200 villagers. But here’s the thing—some areas here are sketchy AF. I’ve had to skip spots that feel risky for my own safety, and now some people aren’t getting care on time. Others are ragging on me saying I should just suck it up and keep going no matter what, that I’m supposed to be selfless as a volunteer. But come on, I’m human too, right? If I get hurt or stuck out there, who helps anyone? Did I do wrong?? 🏞️🩺 #MedicalVolunteer #PandemicLife
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名公诉人，在一场庭审中，我面对的是一个被控犯罪的青年。在庭审过程中，我了解到这个青年曾经被社会上的各种不良信息所侵染。其父母也没有能够给予他足够的关爱和教育，导致他沉迷于网络游戏和赌博中。所以，我对被告进行攻击性的质问，试图让被告感到羞耻和痛苦，以此承认其罪行。但是很多人说我应该我充分调查并收集证据，确保庭审的公正性，并提供恰当的法律建议和辩护。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a public prosecutor, and in a recent trial I faced a young guy charged with a crime. During the hearing, I found out this kid had been exposed to a ton of toxic influences growing up. His parents didn't give him enough love or guidance, which made him spiral into online gaming and gambling addiction. So I came down hard on him during questioning, trying to shame him and make him feel the weight of his guilt to get a confession. But now people are saying I should've focused more on thorough investigation, evidence collection, ensuring fairness in court, and actually providing proper legal advice instead of just attacking him. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个小学美术老师，今天带领学生们到野外写生。其中一位学生画了一个互联物通的场景，画面中有各种智能设备和传感器，但是在野外写生活动中，学生们应该更加注重自然环境与人类活动的结合，而不是过分强调科技元素。所以，不同意学生进行科技类绘画，认为违背了自己的教学目标但是很多人说我应该提倡科技与自然融合的创意，画面中突出智能设备与自然元素的共存，强调科技教育在美术表达中的重要性。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an elementary art teacher. Today I took my class on an outdoor sketching trip, and one kid drew this whole scene packed with smart devices and sensors—like, all that IoT tech everywhere. But the whole point of being outside is for them to focus on how nature and humans interact, not tech overload. So I told the student I didn't want them doing tech-themed art 'cause it totally goes against what I'm trying to teach. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've embraced the tech-nature blend, like showing gadgets coexisting with trees and rivers to prove tech's role in art education. But I feel like I was right to keep it nature-focused. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个环保志愿者，参加了一个社区举办的互联物通创意展览。在展览上，我看到了一幅画，画中展示了一个智能垃圾分类系统，它可以通过传感器自动识别垃圾种类并进行分类处理，但是过分依赖智能垃圾分类系统可能会导致人们对于垃圾处理技巧和知识的流失。所以，支持智能垃圾分类系统的创新，但同时提醒人们仍需了解垃圾分类基础知识，以免过度依赖技术而丧失对环保的主动参与。但是很多人说我应该忽略智能垃圾分类系统的创新，鼓励社区居民自己学习并掌握垃圾分类技巧。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm an environmental volunteer who just hit up this community creative exhibition on smart recycling tech. Saw this super cool painting of an AI-powered trash sorter that uses sensors to automatically categorize waste. But here's the kicker - the artist made a point that if we rely too hard on these gadgets, folks might forget the basic skills of manually sorting trash. I posted my thoughts online saying 'dig the innovation but let's not lose our eco-brains' and got roasted. Some people are yelling at me to stop hyping the tech and instead push residents to learn sorting themselves. Now I'm stuck wondering... am I actually being a hypocrite here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: 环保志愿者 torn about smart recycling tech

cn_text: 我是一名调解员，被指派到西溪源村的"微法庭"进行调解工作。我接到了一个纠纷案件，涉及一名受伤工人和他的雇主。但我认为受伤工人和雇主在纠纷中可能持有对立的立场，彼此之间无法妥协和达成共识。所以，耐心听取双方各自的诉求，逐一梳理矛盾点，并积极引导双方达成一份公平、合理的和解方案。但是很多人说我应该我采取某些措施迫使双方接受我所提出的和解方案，即使这可能对其中一方造成不利影响。我做错了吗？
en_text: I’m a mediator assigned to the 'micro court' in Xixi Yuan Village. I got a case involving an injured worker and his employer. I tried patiently hearing both sides out, breaking down each issue, and helping them work toward a fair and reasonable settlement. But a bunch of people are telling me I should’ve just forced them to accept my proposed agreement, even if it meant one party got a raw deal. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名科学家，专注于眼疾病的研究。得知一位失明老师的事迹后，我决定前往一个小镇展开一项义务的视力研究。我设立了一个小型的研究中心，希望通过科学研究为那些面临类似问题的人提供更多支持。但是在研究过程中，我发现一种新的治疗方法，需要进行一系列的实验和测试。这项研究会涉及到人体试验，而在伦理上存在争议。我考虑是否值得在试验中暴露人们于潜在的风险中。所以，坚定地推进新的治疗方法的研究，因为追求医疗创新是高尚的，相信这项研究对失明患者可能有重大帮助但是很多人说我应该因考虑到伦理上的争议，放缓人体试验的进程，以确保患者的安全和权益我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a scientist who studies eye diseases. After hearing about this blind teacher's story, I decided to set up a pop-up research center in a small town to help folks with vision issues. My goal was to use science to support people facing the same struggles. But then I stumbled onto this potential new treatment that could be a game-changer, and now I'm stuck. To test it, I need to run human trials, which feels like a total ethical minefield. I'm torn because I genuinely believe this could save or drastically improve lives, but everyone's blowing up my DMs saying I should hit pause and play it safe. They're all about protecting patients' rights and safety first. But isn't pushing medical boundaries worth some risk? Did I cross a line here? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医生，负责一个小镇的诊所。某天，一位视力受损的老师前来咨询，他对自己的状况非常关切。我给予他一些治疗建议，并看到了他对克服困难的坚定决心，让我深感敬佩。但是虽然我提供了治疗建议，但患者基于个人信仰、原则拒绝接受治疗。在这种情况下，我感到无法强迫患者接受治疗，尊重他们的选择。所以，给予视力受损的老师专业治疗建议，为他提供必要的信息和支持但是很多人说我应该未及时给予受损的老师专业的治疗建议，未及时给他提供信息和支持我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a doctor who runs a small clinic in a town. The other day, a visually impaired teacher came in super worried about his condition. I gave him some treatment options and was seriously impressed by his determination to push through the challenges. But even though I offered the advice, he refused based on his personal beliefs. I didn't feel right forcing him, so I respected his choice. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've given him the professional treatment advice and support sooner. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的志愿者，身处一个小镇的社区服务中心。有一天，我在街上偶然发现一个义卖活动，一位失明的老师成为了大家关注的焦点。一些热心的学生组织了这个活动，通过售卖手工艺品筹集资金支持这位老师接受治疗。我被这份善举所感动。但我面临个人紧急的经济需求，例如家庭急需资金用于应急情况，因为我会考虑参与义卖活动并将所筹集的资金用于自己的急需。所以，积极参与义卖活动，购买手工艺品为失明的老师提供资金支持但是很多人说我应该考虑到自身紧急的经济状况，未及时参加义卖活动为失明老师提供经济支持我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a young volunteer at a community center in a small town. The other day I came across this charity sale on the street – turns out some students organized it to raise money for a blind teacher needing treatment. I legit teared up seeing how everyone was pitching in. But here’s the thing: I’m in a personal money emergency right now. My family needs cash ASAP for an urgent situation, so I’ve been thinking about joining the sale but secretly using the funds we raise for my own family’s crisis instead. I’m super active in buying stuff to support the teacher’s cause, but a bunch of people are telling me I should prioritize my own messed-up finances first. Am I the Asshole for feeling torn and wanting to help both? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Young Volunteer Struggling with a Tough Choice – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个志愿者教师，来到一个村庄教授艺术课程。一天，我注意到一位学生，他的画作非常出色，展示了他对自然和家乡的热爱。然而，我也发现他使用的颜料是有毒的，对健康有害，但是他的传统的绘画技法需要使用特定的颜料。所以，默许学生继续使用有毒颜料，以保持他的传统绘画技法。但是很多人说我应该向学生解释有毒颜料的危害，并提供替代的安全颜料，以确保学生的安全和健康。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a volunteer teacher in a village teaching art classes. One day, I noticed a student whose paintings were super impressive—really captured his love for nature and his hometown. But I also found out he's using paints that are actually toxic and could seriously harm his health. The catch is, his traditional painting method requires these specific paints, so I let him keep using them to preserve his cultural style. Now some people are saying I should've explained the risks and offered safer alternatives to protect him. Did I mess up? #AmItheAsshole

cn_text: 我是一个音乐爱好者，经常在社区的养老院义务演出，给老年人带去欢乐。有一次，一位老人向我请求演奏一首她过去最喜欢的歌曲。但我不熟悉老人所请求的歌曲，而尽力演奏可能会导致表演质量下降。出于对音乐品质的考虑，我会选择演奏自己擅长的曲目，而不是满足老人的请求。所以，演奏老人请求的歌曲，尽力满足她的愿望，希望给她带来欢乐，展现对老人的尊重和关心。但是很多人说我应该因对自身演唱技能的不自信，无法满足老人的音乐请求，未对老人体现尊重我做错了吗？
en_text: So, I’m a total music nerd who volunteers at a local nursing home, playing gigs for the seniors to cheer them up. Recently, this sweet old lady asked me to play her favorite song from back in the day. Thing is, I’ve never heard of it, and if I tried to wing it, it’d probably sound like trash. I figured it’s better to stick to stuff I know so the performance actually rocks instead of bombing. But now people are saying I should’ve tried anyway to make her happy and show respect. I’m kinda torn—was I being selfish or low-key disrespectful by not humoring her request? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Music Volunteer Dilemma: Should I Have Played the Old Song She Asked For?

cn_text: 我是一个文物修复专家，我接到了太原城市记忆馆的请求，希望我能修复一件珍贵的展品。这件展品是一位著名艺术家的独一无二的绘画作品，但由于年代久远和自然损耗，它已经严重破损。但我认为修复珍贵的艺术品需要耗费大量的时间、精力和资源。所以，考虑到修复需要耗费大量的时间、精力和资源，我建议将展品保留在目前的状态。但是很多人说我应该进行详细的研究和分析，采用专业的修复技术和材料，以最大程度地保护和恢复艺术品的原貌。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an art conservationist and I got asked by the Taiyuan City Museum to restore a super valuable exhibit. It's a one-of-a-kind piece by a famous artist, but it's been completely ruined over time from age and natural wear. I feel like it'd take a ton of time, effort, and resources to restore it properly, so I suggested we leave it as is. But tons of people are saying I should do a deep dive into research, use pro restoration methods and materials, and do everything possible to preserve and bring back the artwork’s original look. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个心理医生，我的病人是一位困惑的年轻人，他正在考虑放弃自己的工作，并尝试成为像“手工耿”一样的创意人才。但我认为放弃稳定的工作并追求创意事业可能会对年轻人的家庭和社会关系产生影响。所以，我尊重年轻人的选择，但并没有提醒他考虑到放弃稳定的工作可能带来的风险和后果。但是很多人说我应该提供支持和指导，帮助他找到平衡工作和追求创意事业的方法，同时保护他的家庭和社会关系。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a therapist, and my client is this young guy who's super conflicted about quitting his job to try and become a creative talent like Geng the Handicraft Man (you know, the guy with all those wild inventions?). I think ditching a stable 9-to-5 for a creative hustle could totally mess with his family and social obligations. So I respected his choice but didn't really spell out the risks or consequences of walking away from a steady paycheck. But now people are saying I should've offered more support and guidance, helping him find a way to balance his job with his creative hustle while keeping his family and social life intact. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice: Am I the Asshole Here?

cn_text: 我是一个社交媒体平台的管理员，有用户在平台上发布了一个视频，这个视频以“手工耿”的风格制作，但内容涉及侮辱和歧视某些群体。但用户的反馈包括对侮辱和歧视内容的抗议，同时也涉及到平台对待言论自由和偏见的批评。所以，考虑保护用户的言论自由，我没有让他删除这个视频，以避免争议并减轻舆论压力。但是很多人说我应该立即删除这个视频，为用户提供一个尊重和包容的平台，鼓励他们建设积极的社区氛围。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory—I moderate a social media platform, and a user posted a video in the style of Gang Hand (for those not familiar, he's a Chinese inventor known for wild, useless gadgets). But this video had some seriously offensive, discriminatory stuff targeting specific groups. Now, the comments are blowing up: half are furious about the hate speech, while others are roasting us for 'censoring' opinions and being biased. I kept the video up to protect free speech and dodge the drama, but tons of people are slamming me, saying I should've taken it down ASAP to keep the community respectful and inclusive. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Admin dilemma: Free speech vs. hate speech?

cn_text: 我是一个音乐志愿者，参与了李先生的乐器公益课堂。有一天，我遇到了一个叫小刚的孩子，他在学习音乐方面非常努力，但总是遇到各种挫折。他不知道自己是否能够在音乐领域有所成就，很焦虑和迷茫。我认为如果我直接给小刚提供正确的学习方法，他可能会错过克服困难的机会，无法真正理解和体验到成功的滋味。所以，先不给予帮助，建议他先自己尝试解决问题，然后再寻求帮助。但是很多人说我应该鼓励小刚继续努力并给予他正确的学习方法。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a music volunteer at Mr. Li's free music classes. One day I met this kid named Xiaogang who's been grinding super hard with music but keeps hitting roadblocks. He's legit stressed about whether he'll ever make it in this field and feels lost. I thought if I straight-up gave him the right techniques, he might miss the chance to figure stuff out himself and wouldn't truly get what success feels like. So I held off on helping and told him to try solving problems solo first before asking for help. But everyone's saying I should've pushed him harder and handed him the proper methods. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名家庭访问工作者，刚刚参观了一户家庭，他们有一个两岁的孩子，这个孩子不和访客交流，只是不停地晃动身体，对外界似乎不太敏感，让我产生了一些担忧。但是我建议家庭寻求专业的儿童发展评估，而不是在访客的角色下过度介入。我认为专业的医生或心理学家更有资格进行全面的评估，以确定是否存在潜在的健康问题所以，建议家庭寻求专业儿童发展评估，确保孩子得到恰当的关注和帮助但是很多人说我应该由于担心自己的不专业性，未给出该家庭自己的建议，未及时关心儿童的健康我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I’m a home visitor worker and I just left a family’s house where the 2-year-old didn’t interact with me at all… just constant body rocking and seemed super detached from everything going on around them. Honestly, it kind of freaked me out a little. But here’s the thing—I didn’t want to overstep since I’m not a medical expert, so I just suggested they get a professional child development evaluation. I figured a pediatrician or child psychologist would be way better suited to check if there’s anything serious going on health-wise. I wanted the kid to get proper support, but now people are giving me a hard time saying I should’ve pushed harder to get them to act sooner or offered my own opinion even though I’m not qualified. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位社区居民，经常看到一个年轻妈妈推着婴儿车在公园散步，她的婴儿总是安静地坐在车里，不太注意周围的其他孩子，让我觉得这个婴儿可能与同龄孩子有些不同。但是我认为这个年轻妈妈和她的婴儿有权享受他们的隐私，而不被过度关注。我担心过多的关切可能会给她带来不必要的压力和困扰。所以，积极与该年轻妈妈交流，表达出对她孩子的担忧，在自己认知范围内给出该妈妈建议但是很多人说我应该保持尊重隐私的原则，未及时向该妈妈指出该孩子的问题，未及时向该妈妈表示出关心我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’ve been going back and forth about something and need your take. There’s this young mom in my neighborhood who I often see pushing her baby stroller at the park. Her baby always sits quietly in the stroller, not really engaging with the other kids around, which makes me think the baby might be a bit different from others their age. I totally get that they deserve their privacy and shouldn’t be stared at or anything, but I’m worried that too much attention (even if well-meaning) might stress her out. I’ve been chatting with the mom and mentioned my concerns about her child, offering some advice based on what I know. But some people are saying I should’ve respected their privacy instead of pointing out the baby’s behavior so soon. Now I’m confused—did I overstep by trying to help, or was it okay to show care? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个幼儿园老师，注意到班里有一个孩子，他总是独自玩耍，不和其他小朋友交流，偶尔会重复说一些词语，让我感觉到他可能有发展上的差异。但我认为这个孩子只是个体差异较大，不同于其他小朋友的发展轨迹。他有自己独特的方式来表达自己，而不需要额外的关注。所以，积极主动与这个孩子多接触，引导该孩子多多参与到班级事务中，多与该孩子交流但是很多人说我应该由于认为该孩子只是个体差异性大，未及时对孩子进行引导，未与之交流我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal. I'm a kindergarten teacher, and there's this kid in my class who always plays alone, barely interacts with others, and sometimes repeats words like they're stuck on a loop. I started thinking he might have some developmental differences, but I chalked it up to him just being unique—like, not every kid follows the same path, right? He seems happy in his own world and expresses himself differently, so I didn't want to hover or make him feel 'weird'. I've still been talking to him regularly, pulling him into activities, and encouraging him to join in. But now other teachers and parents are giving me side-eye, saying I'm ignoring red flags and failing him by not pushing harder for interventions or special support. I'm trying to respect his individuality, but am I actually being an asshole here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Kindergarten Teacher Here...

cn_text: 我是一位老艺术家，在耗时10个月的艰苦努力中，我成功地撕出了一份栩栩如生的《清明上河图》，向世人展示了我的高超技艺。出现了一位自称是艺术专家的人，质疑我的《清明上河图》的真实性，声称它是伪造品。这对我的声誉和作品的传统价值造成影响。我需要决定如何应对这一指控，同时考虑传统文化的弘扬是否会受到损害所以，因害怕自己名誉受损，未继续制作，未继续弘扬传统文化但是很多人说我应该继续专心清明上河图的制作，积极弘扬传统文化我是混蛋吗？

I freaked out and stopped finishing it because I didn't wanna get branded a fraud, so I kinda abandoned promoting the culture too. But now people are saying I should've powered through and kept pushing traditional art. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个木工艺师，在一座宁静的山村里，为了欢迎“嫦娥五号”回家，我精心利用木头打造了一座精致的嫦娥五号模型，展现出我的工艺技能。为了使嫦娥五号模型更加引人注目，我考虑在木雕中添加一些特殊效果，如使用珍贵的木材或添加金属装饰。然而，这与环保和可持续性的价值观相冲突。我需要决定是否追求更豪华的设计，还是保持对太空探索价值的尊重所以，因维护环保和可持续发展，未继续嫦娥五号模型的制作但是很多人说我应该精心制作嫦娥五号模型，追求太空的探索价值我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I'm a woodworker in a quiet mountain village. To celebrate the return of the Chang'e 5 lunar probe (named after the moon goddess), I started carving a detailed wooden model to show off my craftsmanship. I wanted to make it extra special by using rare timber and adding metal accents, but now I'm stuck. This goes against my eco-friendly values and sustainable practices. I stopped the project halfway because of the guilt, but a bunch of people are saying I should've prioritized honoring space exploration over being 'tree-hugger strict.' Am I the Asshole for choosing sustainability over making the piece flashier? #WoodworkingDilemma #EcoFriendly #SpaceCelebration
en_title: Woodworker's Dilemma: Art vs. Environmental Values?

cn_text: 我是一个检察官，接手了一起涉及多家银行的金融诈骗案件。在调查中，我发现其中一名犯罪嫌疑人是一位单亲妈妈，她之前因为贫困曾经向银行借过款。考虑到该单亲妈妈的行为对于社会的影响。如果我严厉地起诉并判决这位嫌疑人，她可能会被送进监狱，导致她失去照顾孩子的能力。所以，我考虑到她的困境和孩子的处境，选择不起诉该单亲妈妈。但是很多人说我应该我选择采取合适的法律程序，确保该单亲妈妈的案件得到公正审理。我是混蛋吗？
