But others are saying I should evaluate the application more objectively, considering our foundation's financial situation and other potential projects. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个教育志愿者，来自一家与太康县清集镇儿郎庙小学无关的非营利组织。在过去的一次义教活动中，我发现了一个特殊天赋的学生，他擅长艺术，尤其是绘画。学生的家庭无法提供足够的支持，以帮助他充分发展艺术天赋。所以，主动提出协助他争取更多的支持和资源，以促进他在艺术方面的发展。但是很多人说我应该以温暖的语气安慰学生，表达对他艺术天赋的欣赏，但没有主动提供任何实质性的帮助或资源支持。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a volunteer teacher with a nonprofit that's not connected to Erlang Temple Primary School in Taikang County, China. During a recent teaching gig, I met this kid who's got insane talent in art, especially drawing. His family's pretty strapped for cash and can't afford to get him proper art supplies or classes. I felt bad, so I offered to help him connect with local art programs and even started looking into scholarships for him. But now some people are giving me flak, saying I should've just given him a warm pep talk and told him how gifted he is instead of actually stepping up to get real help. They think I overstepped by offering concrete support instead of empty praise. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位社区志愿者，每周花费大部分时间在福建省泉州市的社区里帮助人们解决各种问题。一天，我注意到一个年轻人在附近的公园里徘徊，看起来有些失落。通过观察，我察觉到他可能是一个走失的人。 在初步观察中，社区志愿者并不能确定这位年轻人是否真的走失。所以，观察一会儿，确信年轻人并非走失，然后继续进行社区志愿者的其他工作，不主动介入他的情况但是很多人说我应该走上前去，以关切的语气询问这位年轻人是否需要帮助，提供帮助寻找家人或提供其他支持。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a community volunteer in Quanzhou, China, and I spend most of my week helping people in the neighborhood with all sorts of problems. The other day, I noticed this young guy just hanging out in the park looking really bummed. At first, I thought he might be lost, but after watching him for a few minutes, I realized he wasn't actually lost—he just seemed like he was having a rough day. So I didn't approach him and went back to my other volunteer work. Now, a bunch of people are giving me flak for not going up to him and asking if he needed help, like helping him find his family or whatever. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医学研究员，专注于神经科学领域。最近，我参与了一项阿尔茨海默病的研究项目。在实验中，我发现一种潜在的生物标记物，可能有助于早期诊断这种疾病.神经科学领域的研究通常涉及到敏感的个人健康信息。如果在研究中涉及到潜在的生物标记物用于早期诊断，研究员可能需要更加谨慎地处理伦理问题.所以，忽略伦理问题，急于应用潜在的生物标记物但是很多人说我应该在研究过程中遵循伦理准则，保护参与者的隐私，确保潜在的生物标记物的使用是符合伦理标准的我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a medical researcher in neuroscience and recently joined an Alzheimer's study. During experiments, I found a possible biomarker that might help with early diagnosis. But here's the catch - neuro research often deals with sensitive health data. If a biomarker could lead to early diagnosis, there's gotta be serious ethical safeguards, right? I ignored the ethical issues and pushed ahead with applying the biomarker, but now people are telling me I should've followed strict ethics protocols, protected participant privacy, and made sure any potential biomarker use meets ethical standards. Did I cross a line by rushing this without proper safeguards? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on ethics in Alzheimer's research

cn_text: 我是一个工业企业的人力资源经理，正在考虑如何识别和培养技术人才。我需要制定一套评估体系，用以识别具备潜力的员工，并决定如何分配有限的培训资源以最大化员工的技能提升和公司的整体效益。公司正在朝特定方向发展，需要员工具备特定技能以支持这一战略而不是个性化的发展。所以，分析公司的发展战略需求并与员工互动，尽力将个人发展计划与公司发展结合。但是很多人说我应该将职工发展计划按照公司整体发展战略进行分配。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I’m an HR manager at an industrial company and I’m stuck on how to spot and grow tech talent. I need to build a system to identify employees with potential and figure out how to use our limited training resources to boost employee skills and company gains. The thing is, the company’s got this clear direction we’re heading in, and we need folks with the right skills to back that up—not just whatever they personally want to learn. So I’ve been trying to blend personal growth plans with the company’s vision by talking to employees and aligning their goals with ours. But a bunch of people are telling me I should be assigning training opportunities based purely on the company’s big-picture strategy. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Struggling to Balance Company Strategy and Employee Development

cn_text: 我是一个非盈利组织的领导者，该组织致力于提升技术工人的社会地位和工作条件。我正在准备一场关于技术工人重要性的宣传活动，需要决定如何有效地展示技术人才的故事，以提高公众对这个行业的认识和尊重。但是活动组织受到预算限制，无法进行充分的调研和准备工作。所以，由于活动组织受到预算限制，我在前期调研中做出妥协进行简要的调研。但是很多人说我应该决定以有限的资源和时间内，挑选相关案例和数据着重讲解。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, I run a nonprofit trying to boost respect and working conditions for technical workers. I’m planning this big awareness campaign about why these folks matter, but my budget’s tighter than a drum. I had to cut corners on research and just do a quick-and-dirty survey instead of proper prep work. Now some people are saying I should’ve focused on fewer, stronger case studies and data points given the time/money limits. But I wanted to show the full picture! Did I do wrong?? #NonprofitLife #TechWorkersUnite
en_title: Nonprofit Leader Stressed About Compromising Campaign Quality for Tech Workers

cn_text: 我是一个公共卫生政策制定者，正在考虑如何改善偏远地区医疗服务的质量和可及性。我面临的挑战是如何在有限的预算下提供更多乡村医生所需的资源和支持，以确保边远地区居民的健康需求得到满足。但是当地政府拥有有限的预算，不足以提供足够多的资源和支持以满足边远地区的所有医疗需求。所以，寻找解决方案，在预算限制下为偏远地区居民提供必要的医疗服务。但是很多人说我应该将预算主要用于城市地区的医疗发展，完善城市医疗体系。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I work in public health policy and I'm trying to figure out how to improve healthcare in rural areas. My big headache is how to get rural doctors the resources and support they need with our tiny budget, so people in remote towns don't get screwed over. But here's the thing—the local government's cash is super tight and nowhere near enough to cover all the medical needs out there. So I'm scrambling to find ways to actually get essential care to these folks without blowing the budget. But then a bunch of people are telling me I should dump most of the money into city hospitals and fix the urban healthcare system instead. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个移动医疗服务公司的创始人，正在设计一款应用程序，旨在帮助乡村医生更高效地管理他们的病患。我正在决定应用程序的功能，如何使它既符合村医的实际需求，又易于在偏远地区的有限网络条件下使用。但是公司的利润和市场份额对于公司的发展至关重要，为偏远地区的医生提供支持可能会导致公司盈利差。所以，竞标开发一个高端的应用程序，专注于服务城市地区的医院，最大化公司的利润。但是很多人说我应该开发一个适用于偏远地区的简化版应用程序，有效提升乡村医生的工作效率。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm the founder of a mobile health services startup, and we're trying to build an app that helps rural doctors manage their patients better. The struggle is real though: I want the app to actually meet village docs' needs and work smoothly even with spotty internet in remote areas, but the harsh truth is profits and market share matter most for keeping our company alive. Some people are telling me we should just focus on creating a stripped-down version for rural areas to boost efficiency, but that feels like it'd tank our business financially. Meanwhile, pitching a high-end app to urban hospitals would maximize profits. Am I being a terrible person for even considering the money move over helping underserved communities? Did I do wrong?? 🤔 #startups #medtech #ethicaldilemma
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个非政府组织的志愿者，该组织专注于为偏远地区的医疗服务提供支持。我正在规划一次到大寨村的访问，计划与当地乡村医生合作，了解当地居民的健康需求，并决定如何最有效地利用组织的资源来提供帮助，包括药物供应、医疗培训或设备捐赠。志愿者的主要任务是提供医疗支持，他们认为正确的医疗知识比当地的习俗更为重要。所以，尊重并学习当地的文化习俗，同时分享他们的医疗知识。但是很多人说我应该坚持只按照自己的医疗标准和方法进行工作，唯一认同医疗知识的观点。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a volunteer with an NGO that helps provide medical support to remote areas. I'm planning a trip to Dazhai Village to work with the local village doctor to understand the community's health needs and decide how our organization can best help—whether through medication supplies, medical training, or equipment donations. Our main job is to provide medical support, and we believe proper medical knowledge is more important than local traditions. So we're trying to respect and learn about their cultural customs while sharing our medical expertise. But a bunch of people keep saying I should stick strictly to my own medical standards and methods, and only go by the medical perspective. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社会工作者，得知小陈的故事后，我深受感动并决定前往他的家中。当我到达时，我发现小陈的二儿子年纪已经适合工作，但由于懒惰而没有积极寻找工作机会，但是我认为小陈的二儿子应该自己积极寻找工作机会，而不是依赖他人的帮助。所以，鼓励小陈的二儿子独立并提供支持，帮助他制定积极的求职计划。但是很多人说我应该不对小陈的儿子寻找工作的问题提供什么实质性帮助。我做错了吗？
en_text: AMA, throwaway for obvious reasons. I'm a social worker and after hearing Xiao Chen's story, I was really moved and decided to visit his home. When I arrived, I found out his second son is old enough to work but he's been slacking off and not even trying to find a job. I felt like the kid needs to start taking initiative instead of relying on others, so I pushed him to get his act together and helped set up a job search plan. But now I'm getting flak from people saying I shouldn't have offered that kind of hands-on help. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on helping a client's son get proactive about job hunting

cn_text: 我是一位运动医学专家，正在观察呼和浩特市速度滑冰队的训练。在一次训练中，我注意到一名15岁的学生在进行高强度训练时出现疲劳迹象。有时运动员处于训练周期的不同阶段，其中一些阶段会涉及更高强度的训练。所以，了解训练周期，根据运动员的疲劳迹象提出合理的调整建议，包括适时的休息和补充营养但是很多人说我应该表达理解学生可能在高强度训练中感到疲劳，但在实际行动上未提供具体的调整建议或干预我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, so I’m a sports med expert who’s been checking in on a speed skating team in Hohhot. During practice, I noticed this 15-year-old kid looking totally wiped during a high-intensity session. I know athletes go through different training phases, some way more brutal than others, so I mentioned they’re probably in a tough cycle and should adjust with rest days and better fueling. But now people are saying I should’ve actually *done* something specific instead of just nodding along and talking about ‘understanding fatigue.’ Like, maybe pushed harder to intervene or give concrete tips? I’m starting to feel like I dropped the ball here… Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名安全专家，负责评估呼和浩特市速度滑冰队的训练场地安全性。在检查中，我发现一些潜在的安全隐患，包括滑冰场地的表面不平整。由于训练场地经常使用，地表的不平整可能是由于频繁使用而产生的。所以，提出对不平整表面的整改建议，协助团队解决安全隐患，确保训练场地的安全性。但是很多人说我应该表示对不平整表面的关注，但未能立即提出实质性的整改建议或协助解决问题我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m this safety expert they brought in to check out the speed skating team’s training rink in Hohhot. Found some sketchy stuff – like the ice surface is all bumpy and uneven. Makes sense since they use the rink non-stop, but still a hazard. I flagged the issue about the uneven ice and told them to fix it, but didn’t give immediate solutions or hands-on help. Now people are roasting me online saying I should’ve provided concrete fixes instead of just pointing out the problem. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Safety Expert Here – Did I Screw Up by Not Offering Fixes Right Away?

cn_text: 我是一个康复中心的心理咨询师，我接到了一个来自脑瘫患儿家庭的求助电话。他们的孩子已经接受了一段时间的治疗，但是家长们感到非常疲惫和沮丧，他们需要一些心理上的支持和指导。我意识到我已经连续工作了很长时间，精力和耐心可能不够充足，而且我也需要休息来保持自己的工作效能和健康状态。所以，我鼓励他们坚持治疗，提供一些建议和心理技巧，帮助他们缓解疲惫和沮丧的情绪。但是很多人说我应该我告诉家长我现在非常疲劳，无法提供他们需要的支持和指导。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, quick backstory: I'm a counselor at a rehab center and got a call from parents of a kid with cerebral palsy. Their child's been in therapy for a while, but they're feeling completely drained and desperate for emotional support. Thing is, I've been working nonstop for weeks and my own energy is basically zero. I gave them pep talk and some coping strategies, but afterwards a bunch of colleagues said I should've been honest about my burnout and passed them to someone else. Now I can't stop wondering if I let them down by not being upfront. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I a terrible person for not telling these parents I'm too burned out to help?

cn_text: 我是一个社工志愿者，参观了一家康复中心。在那里，我遇到了一个脑瘫患儿的家庭。这个孩子已经成年了，但他在日常生活中仍然需要帮助和支持。他的父母非常担心他的未来，他们不知道如何平衡他的独立发展和他们对他的保护。但是这些父母非常在意孩子的安全和生活质量。所以，我向孩子和家长提供专业的建议和支持，帮助他们制定一个既能保护孩子又能让他独立发展的计划。但是很多人说我应该我认为孩子面临的风险太大，无法应对外部世界的挑战，因此主张让他一直依赖父母的照顾。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a social work volunteer who recently checked out a rehab center. Met this family with an adult son who's got cerebral palsy—he's technically an adult but still needs help with everyday stuff. His parents are super stressed about his future, totally torn between wanting him to be independent and needing to keep him safe. They care so much about his safety and happiness, which I get. So I gave them some professional advice to help them create a plan that protects him while letting him become more independent. But now a bunch of people are saying I'm being naive for thinking he can handle the outside world, and that he should just stay under his parents' care forever because the risks are too high. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名教育专家，负责一所学校的特殊教育部门。我接到了一位学生家长的来信，提到他们的孩子是一个脑瘫患者，他们希望我能够为他们的孩子提供适当的教育方案和支持。但是提供给该学生的教育方案和支持会对其他学生造成不利影响。所以，我认为应该以整个班级的利益为优先考虑，所以拒绝提供教育方案和支持。但是很多人说我应该我与学生家长安排一个面谈，了解孩子的具体情况、需求和目标，以便制定适当的教育方案。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm the head of special ed at my school. Got a letter from a parent whose kid has cerebral palsy—they want me to set up an IEP and extra support for their child. But here's the thing: doing that would seriously mess with the other kids in the class. So I said no because I gotta prioritize the whole group. Now everyone's telling me I should meet with the parents to figure out the kid's specific needs and goals to make a proper plan. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的体育教练，我的学生们正在组织一场慈善龙舟比赛。但是，我发现一个问题：其中一支队伍利用了非法手段，在比赛中使用了违禁药物。我担心如果我报告这个问题，可能会引起一些负面影响，比如损害我的声誉或者导致不必要的麻烦和纷争。所以，我担心举报这个问题会带来不必要的麻烦和纷争。所以，我决定沉默不语，让他们继续参加比赛。但是很多人说我应该我向比赛组委会举报这支队伍的违规行为，以维护比赛的公正性和公平性。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a young sports coach and my students are organizing a charity dragon boat competition. But here's the thing: one team got caught using banned drugs during training. I was scared if I ratted them out, it'd backfire on me—like ruining my rep or causing major drama. So I kept my mouth shut and let them keep competing. Now people are giving me crap for not blowing the whistle to the organizers to protect the race's fairness. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Young Sports Coach Faces Dilemma Over Cheating in Charity Dragon Boat Race

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的龙舟制作师，工作已有两年。今天，我的一位老师傅向我展示了一种新的龙舟制作技术，这种技术可以让龙舟更加结实耐用，但是需要用到一种非常昂贵的材料。但是我担心价格的上涨会降低顾客的购买意愿。所以，我认为促进技术进步是大家的责任和义务，所以决定采用这种新的龙舟制作技术，并使用这种昂贵的材料。但是很多人说我应该我没有采用昂贵的材料。因为我认为价格上涨会降低顾客的购买意愿，这样可能会失去很多订单。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a young dragon boat maker with two years under my belt. So here's the deal: today, one of my senior师傅 showed me this new technique for building dragon boats that makes them way sturdier and longer-lasting, but it requires this super expensive material. I'm worried bumping up the price might scare off customers, and we could lose a bunch of orders. Still, I feel like pushing the craft forward is kinda our duty, right? So I decided to go ahead and start using the new method with the pricey stuff. But now a bunch of people are saying I shouldn't have gone for the pricier material. I'm stuck here—was I wrong to prioritize quality over cost? Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的大学生，参加了一次志愿者活动，前往贫困山区支教。在我的支教地点，当地的农户生活艰辛，他们种植了大量的蔬菜，但由于交通不便，销售渠道有限，导致农产品无法得到很好的销售。在支教期间，我需要平衡自己的时间、精力和其他志愿工作。如果将全部援助投入到农产品销售上，可能会牺牲其他重要的支教任务和需求。所以，我采取合理的方式，帮助他们建立销售渠道或宣传他们的产品。但是很多人说我应该我选择不关注农产品销售问题，将全部精力投入到支教任务和需求上。我是混蛋吗？

The local farmers are really struggling—they grow tons of veggies, but bad roads and no transport options mean they can’t sell their stuff properly. While I was there, I had to juggle my time between teaching and other volunteer work. If I’d dumped all my energy into helping them move produce, I’d have totally dropped the ball on my actual teaching duties. So I tried to help by setting up some online sales channels and promoting their stuff on social media. But now people are saying I should’ve ignored the farming side completely and just stuck to the classroom. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个新闻记者，我听说了一位网红因为带动了农特产品的销售而受到一些人的质疑。现在我需要决定是否采访她并报道她的故事，以促进公众对于农特产品的认识和支持。然而，我听说她完全是为了个人利益。所以，我认为外面的传言是正确的，我不应该采访这位网红并报道她的故事，避免传递负能量。但是很多人说我应该我采访这位网红并报道她的故事，让公众了解农特产品的好处并支持它们的销售。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a journalist and I heard about this influencer who got some heat for supposedly boosting sales of local farm products. Now I'm stuck trying to decide if I should interview her to highlight these products and get more people to support them. But here's the catch - I also heard she's doing it purely for her own clout and cash. I feel like the rumors are legit, so I don't wanna give her a platform if it's just spreading negativity. cn_text: 我是一位当地志愿者，负责协助组织第五十七届世界速滑锦标赛。在活动进行中，我注意到一名观众突然晕倒。当地志愿者缺乏医疗专业知识，无法准确判断观众晕倒的原因或提供专业的医疗救助。所以，虽然意识到观众的晕倒，但由于自身缺乏医疗专业知识，只能在旁边呼叫其他志愿者或工作人员但是很多人说我应该立即呼叫急救人员，并迅速向晕倒的观众提供安慰和支持，确保他得到及时的医疗救助。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I was volunteering at the 57th World Speed Skating Championships, right? During the event, a spectator suddenly passed out. Thing is, none of us local volunteers have medical training, so I couldn’t figure out why they fainted or give proper help. I tried yelling for other volunteers or staff, but now a bunch of people are saying I should’ve called 911 immediately and stayed with the person to comfort them until help arrived. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名旅行摄影师，偶然来到世界速滑锦标赛现场。除了记录比赛的精彩瞬间，我发现了赛场周围的美丽风景和人们热情的欢呼。但要考虑到有些人不希望被摄影师记录或出现在照片中，尤其是在观众席上或私人场合。所以，但在意到有人不愿被拍摄后，主动调整了镜头，专注于捕捉比赛的瞬间，避免拍摄观众但是很多人说我应该旅行摄影师巧妙地捕捉到比赛瞬间以及赛场周围的美丽风景，尊重观众的隐私，避免拍摄那些明显不愿被记录的人。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So there I was, shooting the race action and noticing all the cool scenery around the arena plus the crowd going wild. But I remembered some folks hate being photographed, especially in the stands or during personal moments. Once I spotted someone looking uncomfortable, I immediately adjusted my lens to focus only on the athletes and avoid capturing spectators. Still, tons of people called me out saying I should've balanced capturing the race's energy AND the surrounding vibes while respecting privacy. Did I overcorrect or what? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位体育史学家，研究1963年世界速滑锦标赛的背景。在研究过程中，我发现了当时一位不为人知的运动员，他在比赛中以出色的表现引起了注意，但却选择在之后的职业生涯中低调退役，成为体育史上的谜。有些运动员可能不愿过度曝光，希望将注意力集中在比赛表现而非个人生活上。所以，体育史学家通过深入研究，迟来地向这位低调的运动员颁发荣誉，以认可他在1963年世界速滑锦标赛上的卓越表现。但是很多人说我应该育史学家虽然发现了这位不为人知的运动员，但由于他低调退役的决定，选择不过多揭示他的个人信息我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So, I’m a sports historian digging into the 1963 World Speed Skating Championships, right? While researching, I stumbled on this totally unknown skater who absolutely crushed it at the event but then just… vanished. Quietly retired and became this unsolved mystery in sports history. I get that some athletes wanna stay low-key and keep the focus on their performance, not their personal lives. But as a historian, I feel like this dude deserves overdue recognition for how insane he was in ’63. Thing is, people are calling me out for even looking into his background since he chose to step away from the spotlight. Like, yeah, he wanted privacy, but isn’t part of preserving history honoring the people who made it, even if they didn’t ask for fame? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Uncovering a Forgotten Speed Skater from 1963 – Did I Go Too Far?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的志愿者，在茂县参与当地的社区建设项目。最近，我发现一片荒地可以用来建设公园。志愿者在规划公园建设时需要考虑可持续性因素，如环保和生态平衡。所以，积极倡导在公园建设中采用环保材料、推广可再生能源，并规划植被覆盖，以促进生态平衡，实现可持续性的社区发展但是很多人说我应该志愿者关注可持续性因素，但由于预算和资源限制，选择采用简化和快捷的建设方案我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Hey everyone, I'm a young volunteer working on a community project in Mao County, China. Recently, I found this empty lot we could turn into a park. When we were planning it, I've been really pushing for us to use eco-friendly materials, set up renewable energy like solar panels, and plant a bunch of native stuff to keep the ecosystem balanced—you know, for actual sustainable community development.

But a ton of people are telling me that as a volunteer, I *should* care about sustainability, but because of the super tight budget and limited resources, we gotta go with a simpler, quicker build—cheap materials, skip the green initiatives, the whole deal.

Now I'm sitting here wondering... am I being a total asshole for not backing down and still fighting for the eco-friendly options? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for pushing too hard on sustainability in a volunteer project?

cn_text: 我是一个社交媒体管理员，在杭州亚运会倒计时30天的时候，注意到有一名“小青荷”志愿者在社交媒体上分享了她的训练日志，描述了她每天早晨在紫金港校区进行的体能训练和心理准备活动。但是其他组织通过分析她的训练日志获取信息，导致不公平的竞争。所以，积极支持并选择性分享小青荷的训练日志，鼓励其他志愿者也分享他们的训练经历。但是很多人说我应该不再推广小青荷的训练日志，以避免给其他组织获取信息的机会。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a social media admin for the Hangzhou Asian Games team, right? 30 days out from the event, I noticed one of our 'Xiao Qinghe' volunteers posting her training log online - showing her daily morning workouts at Zijingang Campus and all the mental prep stuff she does. I'm getting slammed for promoting her content, but I just wanted to celebrate her hard work and inspire others! Did I do wrong?? #HangzhouAsianGames #VolunteerLife

cn_text: 我是一个社交媒体管理员，在杭州亚运会倒计时30天的时候，注意到有一名“小青荷”志愿者在社交媒体上分享了她的训练日志，描述了她每天早晨在紫金港校区进行的体能训练和心理准备活动，但是“小青荷”会担心将自己的训练细节公之于众引起其他志愿者或运动员的竞争压力，导致负面影响，如紧张、焦虑或不必要的竞争行为。所以，在社交媒体上分享了她每天早晨在紫金港校区进行的体能训练和心理准备活动。但是很多人说我应该“小青荷”志愿者不再刻苦，逃避训练，展示出消极的态度。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a social media mod. With the Hangzhou Asian Games 30 days out, I spotted one of those 'Little Blue Lotus' volunteers (that's what they call the Hangzhou Games volunteers) posting her training diary online. cn_text: 我是一位手艺人，专门从事传统工艺制作。最近，我为一场文化活动特地制作了一把以亚运元素为主题的传统手工艺绸伞，以展示杭州独特的文化传统。 突然有人对我的亚运绸伞表现出浓厚的兴趣，并愿意付出高价购买。所以，手艺人坚守传统文化的规则，拒绝出售亚运绸伞，解释其是为了文化活动而制作，目的是传承和弘扬传统文化，而非商业交易。但是很多人说我应该突然有人对我的亚运绸伞表现出浓厚的兴趣，并愿意付出高价购买。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a craftsman who specializes in traditional handmade stuff. Recently I created this super detailed silk umbrella with Asian Games-themed designs for a cultural event here in Hangzhou to promote our local heritage. Outta nowhere, someone hit me up offering a crazy high price to buy it. I turned them down flat because this piece was meant for cultural showcase, not for sale. Explained it’s about preserving traditions, not cashing in. But now a bunch of people are saying I should’ve taken the money and run. I’m super conflicted here – did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名艺术家，受到亚运会的启发，用传统的西湖绸伞制作了一件独特的艺术品，希望通过这个作品展示杭州的传统文化和现代体育精神的结合。但是我发现我的作品触及一些社会敏感问题，引发争议或负面反应。在这种情况下，我选择修改作品，以避免争议或让作品更加符合主流价值观。所以，我发现我的作品触及一些社会敏感问题，引发争议或负面反应。在这种情况下，我选择修改作品，以避免争议或让作品更加符合主流价值观。但是很多人说我应该艺术家坚持创造独特的艺术，拒绝修改作品。他认为艺术的价值在于引发思考和讨论，即使涉及敏感问题，也不愿改变原创的意图。我是混蛋吗？

I wanted to show how our traditional culture can mesh with modern sports energy. But my work ended up touching on some sensitive social issues, and it’s causing a lot of backlash and heated debates. I decided to revise it to avoid the controversy and make it more palatable to mainstream values. However, a bunch of people are calling me out, saying I should’ve stuck to my original vision and not changed a thing. They argue art’s whole point is to provoke thought and discussion, even if it’s controversial, and that I shouldn’t compromise my creative integrity. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名手工艺品制作者，近期为杭州亚运会准备了一批特色的西湖绸伞，以传统工艺展示城市的独特之处，为亚运会增添一份别样的文化氛围。我收到了一些反馈，表示一些元素在市场上更受欢迎。为了迎合更广泛的市场需求，我考虑修改绸伞的设计，使其更符合商业化的趋势，而不是保持纯粹的传统文化呈现。所以，我收到了一些反馈，表示一些元素在市场上更受欢迎。为了迎合更广泛的市场需求，我考虑修改绸伞的设计，使其更符合商业化的趋势，而不是保持纯粹的传统文化呈现。但是很多人说我应该手工艺品制作者坚持保持绸伞的原始设计，认为其独特的传统文化呈现是展示城市独特魅力的重要方式，不愿为了商业化趋势而修改。我做错了吗？

But I've been getting feedback that certain design elements are way more popular with buyers. So I'm thinking of tweaking the umbrella designs to be more market-friendly and commercial instead of keeping them 100% traditional. But then a ton of people are like 'Nah you gotta stick to the original designs because that authentic traditional look is how you showcase the city's real charm—don't sell out for trends.' So... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名当天参与跑步活动的跑者，在杭州市奥体中心体育场跑步时发现一只受伤的小猫，需要寻找相关人员协助处理。不过，担心过于靠近受伤的小猫可能会引起它的攻击或传染病的传播，从而对自己的健康构成威胁，所以选择远离小猫。所以，考虑到小猫可能会对我的健康构成威胁，我选择远离小猫，以确保自己的安全。但是很多人说我应该关爱动物是积极的行为，我主动寻找相关人员协助处理受伤的小猫。我做错了吗？

I didn't approach it because I was scared it might attack me or spread diseases, so I kept my distance. But now people are saying I should've taken initiative to find someone to help the poor thing instead of just walking away. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个义工，参与一个临时庇护所的工作。有一次，我遇到一个失去家庭的孩子，他渴望得到爱和关怀。我决定用一些小细节来温暖他的心，比如给他画一幅他喜欢的漫画或者读一本童话故事给他听。但是考虑到孩子的自尊心，我开始犹豫了。所以，我可能会担心孩子的家庭背景和隐私，如果我过于干涉他的生活，可能会触及他的家庭隐私，这可能违背了尊重被帮助者的权利和尊严。但是很多人说我应该我可能觉得孩子已经经历了太多伤痛，需要更多的关怀和安慰，因此认为可以为他做一些小细节来温暖他的心。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, so I volunteer at a homeless shelter and met this kid who lost his parents. Dude was clearly starved for affection - kept asking about my day, following me around, etc. I wanted to do little暖心 things like doodling him a Batman comic or reading bedtime stories, but then I got paranoid. What if his family situation's super sensitive? Like, am I crossing a line by digging into his personal stuff even if it's 'for his own good'? Some friends say I'm overthinking and should shower him with heartwarming gestures since he's been through hell. Others say I need to chill and respect his boundaries. Honestly, I'm torn because I don't wanna violate his dignity but also want him to feel loved. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社工，目前正在负责残疾人群体的服务工作。有一天，我遇到了一个身体残疾但意志坚强的人，他希望能够找到一份合适的工作来证明自己的价值。我决定帮他安排一次与雇主的面试，还为他提供一些意见和技巧，让他有更多机会展示自己的才能。不过，担心雇主可能会对残障者的能力产生怀疑，导致面试结果不公正。所以，我准备足够的时间和资源来帮助这个残疾人准备面试。但是很多人说我应该我可能觉得这个残疾人的能力不足以胜任一份正式的工作，因此不想花费时间和精力帮他准备面试。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a social worker who helps people with disabilities find services, right? The other day I met this guy who’s physically disabled but has 💪 major determination. He’s desperate to get a job to prove his worth. I hooked him up with an interview and gave him some pointers to showcase his skills. But honestly, I’m worried the employer might not take him seriously because of his disability, which would be so unfair. I’ve been spending extra time and resources prepping him for this, but now some people are saying I’m wasting effort because he’s ‘not qualified enough’ for a real job. Did I do wrong?? 🤔
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个女子防雹连成员，站在寒风刺骨的山头，注视着远处密布乌云的天空。身边是一台退役的高炮，随时准备应对即将来袭的冰雹，但是高炮是一台退役的设备，存在一些潜在的技术问题。所以，女子防雹连成员在察觉到高炮存在技术问题后，决定不撤离山头，不顾他人安全和不良的后果，继续执行任务。但是很多人说我应该女子防雹连成员迅速检查高炮的状态，努力修复潜在的技术问题，确保设备在最佳工作状态，以更好地保护农作物和财产免受损失。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm in this all-women hail suppression crew. Yesterday I was up on a freezing mountaintop, watching these huge storm clouds roll in. We had this old hail cannon with us—it's retired, so it's kinda janky and has some glitches. When I saw it was acting up, I decided to stay put and keep going instead of bailing, even though it might've been risky for everyone and could've gone south. But now everyone's saying I should've checked the cannon right away and tried to fix whatever was wrong to make sure it worked properly and protected the crops. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个身在聊城市的当地居民，参与了电影《失孤》原型人物郭刚儿子郭振的婚礼。在婚礼上，我看到许多因为共同经历而成为挚友的寻子家长欢聚一堂，共同分享这个喜庆的时刻，但是不可以在谈论时过多涉及他们寻子的经历，因为这涉及到一些个人隐私和痛苦的回忆。所以，当地居民鼓励大家共庆，分享婚礼的喜庆时刻但是很多人说我应该当地居民为了回避涉及寻子经历的话题，所以离开了这个婚礼我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a local from Liaocheng who attended the wedding of Guo Gang's son Guo Zhen, the real-life inspiration for the movie 'Lost Alone'. At the wedding, I saw a bunch of parents who'd become close friends through their shared experiences all celebrating this happy moment together. But we couldn't talk about their search stories too much because that's personal and brings up painful memories. So locals encouraged everyone to celebrate and share the wedding's joy, but a lot of people said I should leave the wedding as a local to avoid discussing the search topics. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位心理咨询师，发现在一次紧急情况中，一名激动不安的女性情绪异常。这名女性正在面临一个非常私人和敏感的问题，她不愿意分享。在为她提供心理支持的同时，我会触及到她不愿意讨论的领域，但这也是为了确保她的隐私权。所以，意识到她的不适，我为了尊重她的隐私和个人意愿，我没有安抚她的情绪。但是很多人说我应该以理解和支持的语气安抚她的情绪，尊重她不愿意讨论的领域，鼓励她分享只要她感到愿意。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a therapist, and today I had this female client in an emergency session who was completely losing her shit. She's dealing with something super private and sensitive that she straight-up refused to talk about.

I could tell she was majorly uncomfortable, so to respect her privacy and her 'no,' I didn't even try to calm her down. Like, I figured if I pushed comfort or soothing, it might feel like I was pressuring her to spill.

But now a bunch of people are saying I should've been all supportive and understanding, made it crystal clear I wouldn't push the topic, and only encouraged her to share if she felt ready.

Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名路过的义工，发现一位女性在湖边情绪失控。我迅速上前，试图理解她的困扰并寻求帮助。我没有足够的专业心理咨询知识来处理这位女性的情绪失控。在这种情况下，为了避免错误的干预，需要立即联系专业人士，即使这意味着在短时间内不能全面理解她的困扰。所以，迅速上前关心她的情绪状态，试图理解她的困扰，并提供安慰和支持。在适当的时候建议她寻求专业心理咨询，并提供协助联系专业人士。但是很多人说我应该在尝试理解她的情绪困扰后，立即意识到自己没有足够专业知识处理，于是只好离开。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I was volunteering at the park today when I spotted a woman having a total meltdown by the lake. I rushed over to see if I could help—tried talking to her and figuring out what was wrong. But honestly, I'm not a therapist and I knew I couldn't handle a full-blown emotional crisis. I figured the safest move was to get a pro involved ASAP, even if I didn't get the full story right away. So I stayed with her, gave her some comfort, and once she calmed down a bit, I suggested she talk to a counselor and even offered to call one for her. But now people are telling me that as soon as I realized I wasn't qualified, I should've just walked away. Like, abandoned her there? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位儿子，陪伴着患有阿尔茨海默病的母亲。每天黄昏时分，我选择带她漫步在海滩上，远离城市的喧嚣。海浪拂过沙滩，而我们两人在橙色的晚霞映照下，享受着宁静而和谐的时光。 但是我面临着巨大的工作压力，需要投入更多的时间和精力来应对工作上的挑战。所以，儿子默默地握着母亲的手，微笑着一边聆听她无法连贯表达的回忆。但是很多人说我应该儿子在沙滩上找到一个安静的角落，开始紧张地处理工作文件。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a son taking care of my mom who has Alzheimer's. Every evening, I take her for walks on the beach, away from the city noise. The waves, the sunset, just us two enjoying the calm and harmony. But I'm under a lot of work pressure and need to put in more time and effort to tackle these challenges. So, I quietly hold her hand, smile, and listen to her try to share her memories, even though she can't always put them into words. But a lot of people say I should just find a quiet spot on the beach and dive into work files instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名生态学研究员，专注于大熊猫栖息地的研究。最近，在绵阳市平武县附近发现了一片潜在的新型植被，可能对大熊猫的食物选择和栖息地有积极影响，不过作为研究员，存在科研竞争的压力，我想要在同行中脱颖而出。所以，因为自己想要有足够的精力研究，并且在同行中脱颖而出，于是隐藏信息，没有研究。但是很多人说我应该生态学研究员欣然将新植被的发现提交到科学期刊，以分享并促进有关大熊猫栖息地的研究。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an ecology researcher who studies giant panda habitats. I recently stumbled on this potential new type of vegetation near Pingwu County in Mianyang, China. It could be a total game-changer for pandas' food options and their habitat. But here's the thing: research is cutthroat as hell, and I really wanted to stand out in my field. So to have the time and energy to dive deep into this without competition breathing down my neck, I kept the discovery to myself and haven't shared it with anyone. Now a bunch of people are saying I, as an ecology researcher, should've immediately published the findings in a scientific journal to help advance panda habitat research. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位地方摄影师，受邀前往大熊猫国家公园王朗片区拍摄自然风光。在拍摄过程中，我注意到了一只罕见的高山鸟类在该地区筑巢，成为了我镜头中的焦点，不过为了捕捉到完美的瞬间，我需要在过于靠近或干扰鸟类的情况下拍摄。所以，以谨慎的距离拍摄高山鸟类，不干扰自然环境，保持对自然的敬畏。但是很多人说我应该为了捕捉到完美的瞬间，决定贴近高山鸟类，冒险采取更近距离的拍摄。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a local photographer who got invited to shoot some nature pics at Wanglang in Giant Panda National Park. While I was there, I spotted a rare high-altitude bird nesting in the area, which became my main focus. I wanted to get the perfect shot, but that would’ve meant getting too close or messing with the bird. So I kept a safe distance, didn’t interfere with the environment, and tried to respect nature. But a bunch of people are saying I should’ve risked going closer to capture the ideal moment. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的工程师，拥有电子工程背景。曾经在一次实验事故中失去了左手，不能直接参与工程建设，我打算指导实习生工作，但实习生可能涉及到一些我自己并不十分熟悉的领域。所以，在面对实习生涉及的不熟悉领域时，选择保持沉默，让实习生自己学习相关知识，而不做相关指导。但是很多人说我应该以积极的态度接受并指导实习生，努力理解并学习涉及到的新领域，确保提供专业和负责任的指导。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a young engineer with an electrical engineering background. I lost my left hand in a lab accident a while back, so I can't work hands-on in the field anymore. I want to mentor interns, but they might end up dealing with areas I'm not super familiar with. When that happens, I've been staying quiet and letting them figure it out on their own instead of trying to guide them. But others say I should actively try to learn these new topics myself and make sure I provide professional and responsible mentorship. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名气象学家，对于衡阳市来说，16年前的春天异常寒冷。当时的气象现象让我深入研究，试图找到合理的解释和预测，以提醒社区做好未来可能出现的类似情况的准备。但当前有更紧急的气象问题，需要将资源用于当下更为合适。所以，深入研究过去异常寒冷的春天，寻找合理的解释和预测，以提醒社区未来可能出现类似情况的准备。但是很多人说我应该将资源转移至当前更紧急的气象问题，暂时搁置对过去异常寒冷春天的深入研究。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a meteorologist, and sixteen years ago in Hengyang we had this freakin' weird spring—it was abnormally freezing cold, like wtf level. That got me deep into researching what the hell caused it and whether it could happen again, so we could warn people and get the community prepped for future disasters. But right now there are way more urgent weather crises popping off, and I'm thinking I should probably shift my focus to what's happening today instead of obsessing over that old cold spring. Thing is, everyone's yelling at me to drop the past research and throw all my resources at current emergencies. So... Am I the Asshole for still digging into this old case when shit's literally burning down today?
en_title: Meteorologist stuck between past research and current emergencies - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一家当地的食品供应商，经营着一家小超市。在16年前的寒冷春天，我需要调整库存，确保有足够的食品和生活用品以满足居民的需求。面临成本和盈利的考虑。认为某些商品在当前时期不太畅销，会选择减少这些商品的库存.所以，以关爱社区为主体的行为，增加库存，确保所有食品和生活用品充足，满足居民的需求。但是很多人说我应该由于成本和盈利问题，减少某些商品的库存，没有确保居民需求。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I run a small local grocery store, right? Back in the cold spring of 2007, I was trying to figure out how to restock shelves while keeping the lights on. Yeah, I know – business is business, and profit matters. But here’s the thing: I felt like some items weren’t selling as fast, so I cut those back a bit. Instead, I focused on keeping everything else fully stocked so folks in the neighborhood wouldn’t have to worry about running out of food or essentials. Turns out, a bunch of people online are ragging on me for not slashing inventory harder because of costs. They’re saying I shouldn’t have prioritized community needs over financial sense. But I’m not some corporate giant – I’m part of this town. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Prioritizing Community Over Costs – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个刑侦警察，在一座小镇上工作。某天，我接到一起冷案，发现一名失踪了32年的儿子在该镇被找到，家长激动万分，而我需要调查这个神秘失踪案件的真相。我了解到失踪者的家人多年来一直在苦苦等待，对于他们而言，儿子的突然出现是莫大的喜悦。为了安抚和满足家庭的情感需求，我可能会考虑适度地分享一些调查进展，哪怕违反了一些调查机密。所以，刑侦警察保持调查机密，不透露任何进展信息，即使这可能导致家庭感到焦虑。但是很多人说我应该刑侦警察以合适的方式分享调查进展，以满足家庭的情感需求。我做错了吗？
en_text:
So I'm a cold case detective in a small town. Got handed this 32-year-old missing person case the other day, and turns out the guy was just found alive here in our town. Parents are absolutely over the moon—they've been waiting decades for this miracle. Now I gotta dig into how the hell he vanished and where he's been all this time.

I know the family's been through absolute hell, and having their son back is the happiest moment of their lives. To help them cope with the stress, I thought about sharing little updates on the investigation—like what leads we're chasing—even if it bends the rules on case confidentiality.

But standard protocol says detectives keep everything locked down tight and don't share a damn thing, even if it makes families anxious as hell. Meanwhile, half the people I talk to say I should find a way to give them updates without breaking rules, just to ease their emotional pain.

Did I screw up by even considering sharing? AITA?

cn_text: 一名社区志愿者，参与寻亲工作。在一次寻亲活动中，他成功帮助一对夫妇找到了失散32年的儿子，见证了他们感动的重逢瞬间。志愿者可能因为涉及到寻亲工作，可能会面临一些潜在的安全风险，特别是如果涉及到家庭成员之间的敏感问题。在这种情况下，志愿者可能会限制信息的透露，以确保自己的安全。所以，社区志愿者在适当的情况下分享有关寻亲成功的信息，满足夫妇的情感需求，即使可能涉及潜在的安全风险。但是很多人说我应该社区志愿者限制信息的透露，以确保自己的安全，尤其是涉及到敏感问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a community volunteer who helps people reconnect with lost family members. Recently, I helped this couple find their son after 32 freaking years, and seeing their tearful reunion was honestly the highlight of my life. But some folks are giving me flak because I shared details about the case, even though there might've been some sensitive family drama involved. They're saying I should've kept things on the down-low to protect myself, but I just wanted to give the couple closure and celebrate this amazing moment. I get that safety's important, but isn't helping people heal the whole point? Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 一名网络安全专家偶然间发现了一个线索，帮助广大网友追踪到了一个失踪32年的人，最终揭开了他的身世之谜。网络安全专家可能因好奇心或其他动机，公开失踪人的身世之谜，而不考虑失踪人个人的隐私权。这可能会对失踪人造成不必要的困扰，违反了保护个人信息安全的原则。所以，公开失踪人的身世之谜，满足好奇心或其他动机，可能违反了保护个人信息安全的原则。但是很多人说我应该保护失踪人的隐私权，不公开身世之谜，尊重个人信息安全的原则，避免给失踪人带来不必要的困扰。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so here's the deal: I'm a cybersecurity guy who accidentally found a digital breadcrumb that led to tracking down someone missing for 32 years. Long story short, I dug deeper and uncovered their entire backstory. Now I'm torn AF because I shared everything online - partly outta curiosity, partly wanted to help the internet sleuths. But wait... this person might NOT want their life story splashed everywhere. Am I violating their privacy here? Like, sure, I solved a mystery, but did I just blow up someone's life for clicks and theories? The more I think about it, the more I'm questioning if satisfying our collective curiosity justifies breaking privacy rules. People keep telling me I should've kept it under wraps to protect them, but isn't finding a missing person kinda everyone's business? Need serious advice - Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Cybersecurity Expert Uncovers 32-Year-Old Missing Person's Secret... But Did I Cross a Line?

cn_text: 我是一名摄影师，应邀前往若尔盖大草原拍摄新时代的自然美景。在拍摄过程中，我意外捕捉到一群临时组成的蝴蝶群，在阳光下形成美丽的图案. 如果蝴蝶群的存在涉及到某些敏感的生态信息或是一种独特的现象，摄影师需要考虑不过度宣传，以避免引起过多的关注和潜在的人为干扰。所以，欣赏并拍摄蝴蝶群的美丽，同时保持谨慎，以不过度宣传但是很多人说我应该选择不公开或不记录蝴蝶群的存在，以减少生态信息的传播我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a photographer who was invited to shoot the natural beauty of the Ruoergai Grassland for a new era project. While I was shooting, I accidentally caught a bunch of butterflies that had temporarily gathered—they formed this amazing pattern in the sunlight. Now, I know if something's a rare eco-thing or sensitive info, you shouldn't blow it up online 'cause too many people showing up could mess up the environment. But a lot of people are saying I should’ve either not shared it at all or not even documented the butterflies in the first place to keep their existence under wraps. I mean, I wanted to celebrate their beauty while being careful not to cause chaos... but am I the asshole here?
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名网络评论员，看到一些人在盲人折耳根乐队的社交媒体账号下发布了恶意言论和攻击性评论。我深知互联网上的言论环境很复杂，而且在线上发起倡议可能会引起一系列不可预料的后果。所以，积极倡导网络文明，在社交媒体平台上发起倡议，呼吁人们尊重他人，遵守基本的道德规范。但是很多人说我应该在私人聊天或者小圈子里发起话题或者创建小组，夸大了盲人折耳根乐队的攻击性评论的事实。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I'm an internet commenter who noticed some people leaving really nasty comments and aggressive remarks on the Blind Spud Punk Band's social media accounts. I know the internet can be a messy place, and starting a campaign online might blow things out of proportion. But I felt it was important to actively promote online civility, so I started a movement on social media urging people to respect others and follow basic moral guidelines. However, a lot of people told me I should’ve just brought it up in private chats or small groups, and that I'm blowing the situation out of proportion. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个艺术基金会的工作人员，负责评估和支持有才华但条件有限的艺术家。了解到一位残疾艺术家的故事后，我正在考虑是否应该为类似她这样的艺术家提供特别的支持，比如资金援助、展览机会或者艺术物资，以帮助他们克服障碍，展示他们的作品。艺术基金会强调公平性，希望每位艺术家都有平等的机会获得支持，而其他艺术家也面临各种挑战和障碍。所以，为残疾艺术家提供额外的支持和资源。但是很多人说我应该坚持所有艺术家都应该在相同的标准下竞争。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need some advice. I work at an art foundation that helps talented artists who don't have many resources. After hearing the story of a disabled artist, I'm wondering if we should offer special support—like extra funding, exhibition spots, or art supplies—to help them overcome barriers and showcase their work. Our foundation is all about fairness, giving everyone an equal shot. But other artists have their own struggles too. So, is it wrong to give disabled artists additional help? Some people say all artists should compete under the same standards. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一家出版社的编辑，正在考虑推广非传统背景诗人的作品。我需要在出版界高度竞争的环境中，有效地推广这本诗集，同时保持其独特性和真实性。一些诗人希望他们的作品在传播时能够尊重他们的文化和身份。而诗人担心过度商业化和广告宣传会引发文化误解。所以，邀请诗人参与研讨会和文化交流活动，来推广诗集。但是很多人说我应该为了提高销量，采用普通的市场营销手段大量推广诗集。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm an editor at a publishing house, and I've been trying to figure out how to promote this poetry collection by poets who aren't from the usual backgrounds (like, not the typical MFA program grads). Publishing is cutthroat as hell, and I wanna get this book out there without selling out its authenticity or unique voice. Some of these poets are super worried that if we go full commercial with ads and hype, it'll cause major cultural misunderstandings—like people totally butchering the meaning of their work 'cause of how it's packaged. So instead, I've been setting up workshops and cultural events where the poets actually participate in promoting their book. But half the people in my office are calling me an idiot, saying I should just do the standard marketing blitz to boost sales. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for prioritizing cultural respect over sales in poetry promotion?

cn_text: 我是一个文学节的组织者，正在筹备一个关注日常生活中的诗意的主题活动。我打算邀请一位爱写诗的外卖员作为嘉宾，分享他如何在外卖工作中寻找灵感，并创作诗歌。业余诗人嘉宾虽然热爱写诗，但可能在文学领域没有专业背景或广泛的文学经验，导致部分潜在观众不愿参加活动。所以，我认为业余诗人吸引的观众不如专业诗人是合理的，不进行相较于其他主题活动额外的宣传。但是很多人说我应该通过社交媒体和宣传材料强调业余诗人的独特视角和生活中的诗意。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m organizing a literary festival event focused on finding poetry in daily life. I invited a delivery rider who loves writing poems to share how he gets inspired while working. The thing is, some people are mad because I didn’t promote this event as hard as other themes, since he’s an amateur without formal literary credentials. But others keep telling me I should’ve hyped up his unique perspective and the whole 'poetry in everyday moments' angle more on social media and flyers. Am I the Asshole for not pushing harder to attract a crowd?

cn_text: 我是一个大学的文学教授，正在准备一门关于现代诗歌的课程。考虑到非传统背景诗人的作品所体现的独特视角和社会现实，我正在思考如何将其纳入课程内容中，以展示诗歌如何在不同的生活背景和职业中找到表达方式。但是教授近日有着繁重的科研压力，需要将工作精力放在科研任务上。所以，将精力主要放在科研上，优先处理科研任务。但是很多人说我应该提前规划和优化时间管理，增加自己的工作时间进行课程准备。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey all, I'm a literature professor at a university, currently prepping a course on modern poetry. I really want to include works by poets from non-traditional backgrounds to showcase their unique perspectives and how poetry reflects diverse life experiences and careers. But lately, I've been absolutely swamped with research deadlines and had to focus on those first. Now some colleagues are giving me flak, saying I should've planned better and managed my time to prioritize course prep more. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名城市规划师，正在考察湖南省肿瘤医院附近的商业环境。在调研中，我发现了一家便利店，这家店成为了社区里一个独特的存在，以服务癌症患者而闻名。但是过多的服务患者会影响本地的居民的日常购物体验。所以，为了促进社区和睦，提升城市形象，提议通过合理规划，支持并进一步发展服务癌症患者的便利店。但是很多人说我应该为了维护居民的日常购物体验，对便利店老板世家压力，让其避免对患者出售物品。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a city planner looking into the commercial area around Hunan Cancer Hospital. I stumbled on this convenience store that's become a local staple for serving cancer patients, which is kinda cool, but now the regular residents are complaining it's messing with their shopping routine. I proposed using smart zoning to support and expand the store's patient-focused services to keep the neighborhood united and improve the city's rep. But a bunch of people are telling me I should pressure the owner's family to stop catering to patients so locals can shop easier. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名记者，受到刘长英的故事启发，前往湖南长沙采访。在采访过程中，我发现了她位于湖南省肿瘤医院附近的便利店。这家店成为了一个特殊的社区聚集地，激励着许多人勇敢面对癌症的挑战。然而我面临商业环境的压迫，需要我报道一些不实新闻。所以，我在报道中加入一些夸大或歪曲的元素，以增加新闻的轰动性，但会损害便利店的声誉。采用委婉的方式，报道一些不实新闻，以吸引读者的注意但是很多人说我应该撰写一篇积极正面的报道，强调该便利店的正能量，激励更多人面对癌症的勇气，传递正面信息，符合传递正能量的价值观。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, here's my situation: I'm a journalist who got inspired by Liu Changying's story and went to Changsha, Hunan to investigate. During the interviews, I discovered this convenience store near Hunan Cancer Hospital that's become a special community hub - it's seriously motivating people to fight their cancer battles. BUT here's the catch - my editor's pushing me to sensationalize the story. They want me to add some exaggerated or twisted angles to make the news go viral, even if it might damage the store's reputation. I tried softening it with subtle embellishments, but now people are calling me out saying I should've written a straight-up uplifting piece instead. They're telling me to highlight the store's positive impact, showcase courage against cancer, and spread positivity like those inspirational stories we all need. I went with the hype tactic to meet commercial pressures, but now I'm questioning myself. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Just a journalist torn over whether I compromised integrity for clicks...

cn_text: 我是一个文化遗产保护组织的成员，正在准备一个关于传统手工艺振兴的项目。我考虑将一种特殊的仿真花工艺作为项目的一部分，旨在保护和传承这项工艺。但是这项传统手工艺在现代文化中已经失去了吸引力，不再符合当今社会的需求和口味。所以，将精力和资源放在支持更受欢迎的现代艺术工艺上。但是很多人说我应该组织这种传统手工艺的展览和工作坊，教育公众并增加这项工艺的知名度。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm part of a heritage protection group working on a project to revive traditional crafts. I've been thinking about including this super unique artificial flower-making technique that's basically dying out, but honestly? It's not really catching people's attention anymore. Like, nobody's into it these days – it feels kinda outdated compared to what's trending now. So I'm wondering if we should focus on more modern art forms that actually get people excited, y'know? But tons of folks keep telling me I should host exhibitions and workshops to teach people about this old-school craft and 'bring it back.' Now I'm stuck – am I wrong for not wanting to push something that doesn't seem relevant anymore? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Struggling with Priorities in Our Traditional Craft Revival Project

cn_text: 我是一位网络社交平台的用户，无意中浏览到一个关于失散家庭的帖子。帖子中提到一个村委会主任，最近收到了一个关键消息，与被拐卖一个男子有关。但是我受到网络安全的影响，担心自己的发言被不法分子利用。所以，出于网络安全考虑，决定不在公开帖子中留言，也不参与这件事，继续做自己的工作。但是很多人说我应该在关心失散家庭的同时，采取谨慎的态度，通过私信方式向帖子作者询问更多详细信息。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I was scrolling through this social media app and stumbled on a post about a family trying to find a missing relative who got trafficked years ago. The post said some local town official recently got a major lead on the case. But here's the thing—I’ve been super paranoid about online safety lately, worried my comments might get exploited by scammers or sketchy people. So I kept my mouth shut, didn’t comment publicly or get involved at all, just went about my day. Now a bunch of people are saying I should’ve cared enough to DM the OP for details while staying cautious. Like, I get why they’re mad, but I was just trying to protect myself. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社区居民，关心着身边人的安危。最近，我得知一个村委会主任，在努力寻找失散家庭的过程中收到了一个重要的消息。这条消息涉及到一个被拐卖的男子，而他的信息恰好与四川的一家人正在寻找的家人相符。然而我担心自己提供帮助会给自己带来不利影响。所以，因为担忧可能带来不利影响，决定自己隐瞒可能了解的真实信息，不告诉任何人。但是很多人说我应该积极地与村委会主任联系，提供自己的协助，分享任何可能有助于确认身份的信息。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a community member who cares about people's safety. So here's the thing - I recently found out a local council leader was trying to reunite a missing family when they got a lead about a trafficked guy. Turns out his details might match a family from Sichuan who've been searching for their relative for years. But I'm scared if I share what I know, it could backfire on me. Like, cause me personal problems or legal headaches. Because of that fear, I chose to stay quiet and not tell anyone what I suspected. Now some folks are saying I should've contacted the council leader directly and helped confirm the identity. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I come forward with info about a missing person?

cn_text: 我是一个网络志愿者，三年来一直在寻找失散的家庭成员。最近，我在网络上看到了一个发布在寻人板块的信息，一名被拐卖的男子与我之前关注的一个四川家庭寻找的家人非常相似。但是目前志愿者资源紧缺，我没有过多精力关注这件事。所以，积极参与，主动联系该家庭，提供我所知道的相关信息，并愿意协助他们寻找失散的家庭成员。但是很多人说我应该选择保留自己的精力，没有主动联系该家庭，继续专注在当前已经在进行的志愿者工作。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I've been volunteering online for 3 years now trying to help families reunite with missing loved ones. Burnout is real, but I always try to do my best. The other day, I stumbled upon a post in the missing persons group about a trafficked man who looked almost exactly like someone a family from Sichuan was searching for. However, I'm already swamped with cases and low on energy, so I wasn't sure if I should get involved. Still, I felt compelled to message the family, share the info I had, and offer to help them dig deeper. Now a bunch of people are saying I should stay in my lane and not overextend myself. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Lost and Found: A Volunteer's Dilemma

cn_text: 我是一位社会工作者，最近了解到一个困境儿童家庭的故事。由于家庭破裂和财务拮据，两个兄妹被迫分开寄养。但是当下工作者任务较多，无法很好的平衡资源，对这两位兄妹会分配较少的关注。所以，社会工作者决定按先来后到顺序帮助困难家庭，将这位兄妹放置在后面帮助，暂时不关注。但是很多人说我应该社会工作者争取更多资源，确保两位兄妹能够得到足够的关注和支持，努力维持他们的关系。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a social worker and I just found out about this really sad case: a brother and sister whose family fell apart and they're broke as hell, so they got split up into separate foster homes. But here's the thing—I'm absolutely swamped right now. My caseload is insane and I just can't spread myself thin enough to give them the attention they need. So I've been prioritizing families by who came first, and I put this sibling case on the back burner for now. I'm not actively working on it at the moment. But a ton of people are telling me I should be fighting for more resources to make sure these two kids get enough support and actually try to keep them together. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名小学老师，班里有一位非常聪明但来自贫困家庭的女学生。她在学业上表现出色，但由于家庭经济原因，她无法参加学校组织的一次国际学术比赛。但是学校的救助资金有限，目前学校困难生较多，无法帮助到苦难的每一位学生。所以，老师努力向学校争取额外的救助资金，以确保这位女学生有机会参加国际学术比赛，发挥她的才华。但是很多人说我应该老师感觉自己无能为力，便委婉的告诉女生真相，劝她放弃参加比赛。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm an elementary school teacher, and I've got this super smart girl in my class from a really low-income family. She's absolutely crushing it academically, but her family can't afford the fees for this international academic competition we're running. The school's aid fund is stretched super thin with so many kids needing help, and they can't cover everyone. So I've been trying to push the school to scrape together extra cash just for her so she doesn't miss out on this chance to shine. But a bunch of people are telling me I should just admit I'm powerless, tell her straight up it's not happening, and have her drop out. Now I'm second-guessing myself... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for fighting to get a poor student to an international competition?

cn_text: 我是一位在社区医疗中心工作的医生，最近接触到了一个来自困境家庭的10岁男孩。这名男孩患有罕见的疾病，需要昂贵的治疗。他的家庭无法负担医疗费用。然而医疗中心的资源和预算有限，无法为男孩提供更多的帮助。所以，与男孩的家人坦诚沟通，说明医疗中心的有限资源，无法提供足够的资助，让它们尽快做出决定。但是很多人说我应该竭尽全力寻找其他慈善机构或资源，以确保男孩能够获得所需的治疗。我做错了吗？
en_text: Need advice here. I'm a doctor at a community health clinic and recently came across a 10-year-old boy from a really struggling family. He's got a rare illness that needs super expensive treatment, and his family can't afford the medical bills. Our clinic's resources and budget are super limited too, so we can't give more help. I had an honest convo with the family explaining we don't have the funds to cover the costs and asked them to make a decision ASAP. But a bunch of people are saying I should've gone the extra mile to find other charities or resources to make sure the kid gets the treatment he needs. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个法官，有一个离婚案件需要我审理。原告是一位老父亲，他声称为了挽救儿子的婚姻而出钱买车，但现在儿子和儿媳却要离婚。被告则是儿子和儿媳，他们认为购车款是他们的个人财产，没有必要返还给老父亲。但是父亲购车款是为了挽救儿子的婚姻，那么这笔款项并不是单纯的私人财产，而是存在着一定的道德义务和责任。所以，我直接判决儿子和儿媳将购车款归还给父亲，因为这笔款项存在着一定的道德义务和责任。但是很多人说我应该我要求双方进行调解，以寻找解决方案，尽量保全家庭和睦。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a judge and I just had to rule on this divorce case. The plaintiff is this old man whose son is getting a divorce, and he paid for a car to try to save his son's marriage. Now the son and his wife want to keep the money instead of giving it back. But the dad's reasoning was that the money was meant to help their relationship, so it's not just their personal property—it comes with some moral strings attached. I decided the couple should return the cash to the father because of that obligation, but I'm getting a lot of flak saying I should've pushed for mediation to find a middle ground and keep the family from falling apart. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个心理医生，在治疗过程中，我结识了一对夫妇，他们因为家庭矛盾而闹离婚。在了解到夫妻双方的情况后，我发现他们的矛盾主要源于互相的误解和沟通不畅。然而，我发现夫妻双方存在不健康的行为或态度，例如暴力倾向或其他有害行为。所以，我忽视夫妻双方的不健康行为或态度，只关注他们的互相误解和沟通不畅。但是很多人说我应该我积极倾听夫妻双方的心理困扰，努力帮助他们分析问题，引导他们找到解决问题的方法。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a therapist. I had a couple come to me because they were fighting nonstop and talking divorce over family drama. After digging into their situation, I realized most of their problems were just misunderstandings and terrible communication. BUT—and this is the part that's got me stressed—I also spotted some seriously messed-up stuff from both of them, like violent tendencies and other harmful behaviors. So I ignored all that red flag nonsense and only focused on helping them communicate better and clear up misunderstandings. Now a bunch of people are telling me I should've been actively listening to their emotional struggles, helping them unpack the real issues, and guiding them to solutions. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位当地村民，经常使用龙兴村渡口过河。每当我站在钢索桥上，看着渔船摆渡艄公在渭河上努力摇橹时，我都能感受到河的宁静和摆渡艄公的辛勤。有时村民会听取一些人表达艄公的坏话，讲述艄公的缺点。所以，心怀质疑，选择没有了解真实情况前，依然保持对艄公的尊敬之情。但是很多人说我应该听取别人的负面评价，参与表达对摆渡艄公的不满，讲述摆渡艄公的缺点，与其他村民分享消极观点。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a local villager who takes the village ferry to cross the river all the time. Every time I'm standing on that suspension bridge watching the ferryman row his boat across the river, I just feel the calm of the water and how hard he's working. Sometimes people in the village listen to others badmouthing the ferryman, going on about his flaws. So even though I've got my doubts, I figure I should keep respecting him until I know what's really going on. But a bunch of people are telling me I should soak up all that negative crap, jump in on complaining about the ferryman, point out his flaws, and spread that negativity to other villagers. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个校长助理，在学校早上巡视时，我发现一个学生在教学楼的角落里独自哭泣。这名学生告诉我她已经被班上的同学排挤了好几天，感到很无助。我认为这是学生应该独立解决的问题，而我的角色是提供学术指导而非心理辅导。所以，我认为这是学生应该独立解决的问题，所以我选择忽视这名学生的困境，继续巡视下一个地方。但是很多人说我应该我耐心倾听学生的问题，并给予她一些解决问题的建议，帮助她度过困难。我做错了吗？
en_text: I’m a principal’s assistant at a school. This morning during my rounds, I came across a student crying alone in a corner of the building. She told me she’s been bullied by her classmates for days and feels super helpless. I figured this was something students should sort out themselves, and since my job is academic guidance—not therapy—I just moved on to check the next area. But now people are saying I should’ve stopped to listen and given her some advice to help her through it. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个公共卫生政策制定者，正在考虑如何改善偏远地区的医疗服务质量和可及性。我面临的挑战是如何在有限的预算下提供更多资源和支持给那些用摩托车巡访病人的医务人员，以确保边远地区居民的健康需求得到满足。在一些偏远地区，医务人员面临安全威胁，为了确保他们的安全，需要进行不公开的资源分配。所以，在资源分配中不公开地偏向一些特定区域，以确保那里的医务人员安全。但是很多人说我应该增加对偏远地区医疗服务的资金和物资支持，强化医务人员的安全措施。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a public health policy person trying to figure out how to improve healthcare access in really remote areas. The big issue is supporting medics who ride motorcycles to visit patients - they're doing tough work but we've got a super tight budget. Some regions have safety risks like theft or violence, so we've been quietly directing more resources there to protect the staff. But now people are saying I should just throw more money and supplies at the problem, beef up security measures openly instead of playing favorites behind closed doors. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名心理咨询师，张校长邀请我来到职业学校给学生们做一场讲座，帮助他们应对学业和生活中的压力。在讲座中，我遇到了一个学生，他在课堂上表现优异，但在与同学相处时却显得孤立和内向，但是如果过于强调帮助他建立人际关系，会增加他的压力和不适。所以，为了避免给这个学生带来很大压力，选择不对他提供什么帮助。但是很多人说我应该在课后私下与学生交流，温和地鼓励他参与一些小组活动。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a psychologist and Principal Zhang invited me to do a stress-management talk at a vocational school for the kids. During the lecture, I spotted this student who absolutely kills it academically but is totally isolated and super introverted with everyone else. Thing is, I figured if I made a big deal about fixing his social life, it'd just pile on more stress and make him miserable. So to avoid wrecking his vibe, I didn't say anything or try to help. But now half the staff is like, 'You should've pulled him aside after class and gently nudged him toward group stuff.' Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Psychologist here: AITA for not helping a lonely student after my school talk?

cn_text: 我是一名城市规划师，负责改善城市社区的文化氛围。在调研中，我发现了一位音乐老师，她在教学中巧妙地融入了当地的地域特色，为孩子们打造了独特而丰富的音乐体验。但是城市预算有限，需要在其他重要项目上分配资源，导致当前项目缺少资金。所以，积极争取额外资金，支持并提升音乐项目，确保社区文化得到更好的展现。但是很多人说我应该城市规划师认为可以整改教学方式，减少对资源的使用。并且和老师沟通，苛刻的提出反对意见。我做错了吗？
en_text: I’m an urban planner trying to make our city’s neighborhoods more culturally vibrant. During some research, I found this amazing music teacher who’s been blending local regional vibes into her lessons—kids are getting this totally unique musical experience that connects them to our community’s roots. But the city’s budget is stretched super thin right now, and we’ve got to funnel cash into other major stuff like roads and public services. That means her program’s stuck without funding. I’ve been pushing hard to get extra grant money to not only save the program but amplify it so it can shine even brighter. But a ton of people are calling me out, saying I should be focused on streamlining her teaching methods to cut costs instead. They even want me to confront her aggressively about it. I’m just trying to protect something that brings real soul to the neighborhood—where’s the line between passion and stubbornness here? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个非政府组织的志愿者，该组织专注于为偏远地区的医疗服务提供支持。我正在规划一次到一个偏远村庄的访问，计划与当地的乡村医生合作，了解当地居民的健康需求，并决定如何最有效地利用组织的资源来提供帮助。但组织的资源可能有限，无法覆盖当地居民所有需求。所以，与当地乡村医生合作，了解村庄中最紧急和普遍的健康需求，优先分配资源。但是很多人说我应该有限的资源用于组织内部的行政支出和宣传活动。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a volunteer with an NGO that supports medical services in remote areas. I'm planning a trip to a rural village to team up with the local village doctor, check out the community's health needs, and figure out how to best use our resources to help. But our resources are tight and we can't cover everything. So we're working with the doctor to identify the most urgent and widespread issues to prioritize where to allocate our limited resources. However, a lot of people are saying I should focus those resources on internal administrative costs and outreach campaigns instead. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名义工，我来到一家敬老院探访老人，其中有一位老人总是默默地坐在院子里等待着孙子。我得知他失去了视力，而且孙子已经失踪了近30年。但是我还有其他分配的任务需要完成。所以，我没有注意到那位老人的存在，而是专注于完成其他任务。直到我的任务完成后，我才想起那位老人。但是很多人说我应该我主动走向那位老人，询问他是否需要帮助，并尽力帮助他寻找孙子的下落。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I volunteer at a nursing home, and there's this old man who just sits in the courtyard every single day waiting for his grandson. I found out he's blind and his grandson's been missing for like 30 years. I had other assigned tasks to do that day, so I didn't even notice him until I was done with everything. Now everyone's saying I should've gone up to him, asked if he needed help, and tried to track down his grandson. But I was swamped with my duties! Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not helping a blind old man waiting for his missing grandson?

cn_text: 我是一个遗失儿童援助志愿者，一天，我在一家超市工作时，突然看到一个年轻男子在拼命寻找自己的亲生父母。他显然很绝望，而且对于自己的身世一无所知，但是寻找走失男子的亲生父母需要大量的时间、精力和资源。所以，倾尽全力协助年轻男子，提供各种资源和信息，努力帮他找到亲生父母。但是很多人说我应该理解年轻男子的绝望，但出于资源和时间有限的考虑，只能提供一些建议。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I volunteer for a lost kids nonprofit. The other day I'm working my shift at the grocery store when I spot this young dude totally losing his shit trying to find his birth parents. Dude had zero clue who his real parents were and was clearly drowning in despair. I know tracking down birth parents eats up insane time/resources for our org, but I felt so bad I went full throttle—gave him every contact, database access, and hour I could spare to actually find them. Now people are side-eyeing me saying 'Yeah you should feel for his desperation BUT with our shoestring budget and packed caseload you should've just handed him some basic tips and bounced.' But I did everything humanly possible! Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for going all out to help a guy find his birth parents when my org has limited resources?

cn_text: 我是一个新闻记者，最近我听说了一个关于DNA打拐库的故事。一名男子经过DNA检测发现自己和一对陌生的夫妇存在亲缘关系，这个故事引起了很大的轰动，但是报道DNA打拐库的故事涉及到个人隐私的曝光。所以，深入调查，积极报道关于DNA打拐库的故事，揭示其中的细节和背后的情况.。但是很多人说我应该出于对个人隐私的考虑，不对DNA打拐库进行报道，以免侵犯隐私。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a reporter. I just did this deep dive on the DNA database used to solve child trafficking cases. It started with this wild story where a guy took a DNA test and found out he was related to a random couple he'd never met—turns out they were his birth parents and he'd been trafficked as a kid. Blew up everywhere, obviously. So I dug into how the whole database works, spilled all the personal details of the case, and exposed the backstory behind it. Now tons of people are yelling at me saying I invaded privacy and shouldn't have reported it at all. I get that privacy's a big deal, but this is major public interest stuff affecting real families. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for publishing a deep dive on the DNA anti-trafficking database that exposed personal details?

cn_text: 我是一个农业发展顾问，专注于推动乡村振兴和农业创新。我正在考虑如何帮助像这位年轻的养蟹专家一样的年轻人发展乡村创业项目。我的任务是设计一个指导计划，包括提供业务规划、市场营销策略和可持续发展实践的建议。但是市场研究显示，在当前条件下创业在该地区不具备良好的商业前景，市场经济活力较差。所以，帮助他们制定详细的业务规划、市场营销策略适应市场环境。但是很多人说我应该考虑到市场研究显示创业前景不佳，决定将资源和注意力转移到其他领域。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm an agricultural development consultant focused on rural revitalization and agri-tech innovation. I'm trying to figure out how to support young entrepreneurs like this up-and-coming crab farmer who's killing it with sustainable practices. My job is to create a mentorship program covering business plans, marketing tactics, and eco-friendly farming methods. But here's the catch - recent market analysis shows the local economy's basically stagnant, and new businesses have a super high failure rate here. I'm still pushing to help them build detailed strategies to navigate this tough environment, but half the office thinks I should cut our losses and redirect funding to more promising sectors. Am I being stubborn or actually helping? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个农村教育项目的负责人，致力于教育农村青年，鼓励他们在本地发展农业创业。我正在考虑邀请一位有经验的年轻养蟹专家来分享他的经验和故事，以激励更多的农村青年认识到在乡村创业的潜力和机会。但是此次活动后我有更为紧迫的事情要去处理，进行活动的反馈评估需要额外消耗大量时间。所以，工作之余安排时间对此次活动进行反馈评估。但是很多人说我应该由于更紧迫的事务处理，此次活动结束后直接进入下一项工作。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I run this rural education program back home trying to get young people in the countryside to start their own farming businesses. I was thinking of bringing in this young guy who's a total pro at crab farming to share his story and get the kids hyped about opportunities right here in the country. But after the event, I've got some super urgent stuff that needs my attention, and doing the feedback survey would take a ton of extra time. So I figured I'd do the feedback in my off-hours. But a bunch of people are telling me I should skip the feedback entirely and jump straight to the next task because of the urgent work. Did I mess up? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for doing event feedback in my free time when I have urgent work?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的医学研究生，参与了一项有关器官捐献的研究。在研究中，我发现了一个特殊的案例：一支由接受同一捐赠者器官的5位人士组成的篮球队，他们在比赛中展现了惊人的团队合作，成为医学界独特的研究课题。然而研究人员因为研究的新奇性和引人注目而忽略了对患者应具备的足够尊重。所以，在追求研究的新奇性和引人注目时，对患者的尊重被忽视，只关注篮球队的团队合作。但是很多人说我应该认真努力学习并深入了解这个特殊案例，以更全面地了解器官捐献的影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a young med grad student working on an organ donation research project. I came across this wild case: five people who all received organs from the SAME donor somehow ended up on a basketball team together and they're crushing it with their teamwork. Like, it's legitimately fascinating and everyone in the field is hype about it. But here's the thing - I feel like the researchers are treating these patients more like a circus act than actual human beings. We're all so focused on how cool the 'organ donor supergroup' angle is that we're kinda ignoring their dignity. I tried raising this and some folks said I should just shut up and study the case harder to understand organ donation impacts. I get it's a unique opportunity, but shouldn't we be prioritizing patient respect over clickbait science? Am I overreacting or is there a legit ethical line being crossed here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名体育新闻记者，前往报道一场意外出现的篮球比赛。令人惊讶的是，我发现这支球队的队员竟然是5位接受器官捐赠的受益人。在场上，他们展现了超乎寻常的篮球技巧，成为全明星赛上备受瞩目的存在。揭示球员的身份和他们的个人背景，特别是涉及到器官捐赠的敏感信息，会侵犯球员的隐私权。所以，专注于报道球队在比赛中表现出色的篮球技巧，强调他们成为全明星赛焦点的原因。但是很多人说我应该为了获得曝光率，对球员的一些重点身份信息进行公开。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a sports journalist and I got sent to cover this random basketball game that wasn't even supposed to be a big deal. But holy crap, it turned out the whole team was made up of FIVE athletes who’ve received organ transplants. They absolutely killed it on the court – like, legit insane basketball skills. Honestly, they stole the show at the All-Star game. Now here's the thing: I knew digging into their personal stories or exposing their donor details would’ve been majorly invasive. So I just focused on their gameplay, how they dominated, and why they became the talk of the event. But tons of people are hating on me saying I should’ve 'spilled the tea' about their transplant journeys to get more clicks/views. Was keeping it respectful and sticking to their athletic performance actually the wrong call here? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Organ Donation Recipients Shine in Basketball Game – Should I Have Shared More?

cn_text: 我是一名心理学研究员，受邀观察并分析“叶沙队”球员的心理状态。我惊讶地发现，这五位球员在场上展现出非凡的集体默契，似乎在默默传递着一种特殊的情感，使他们的篮球表现超越了一般的团队。但是未经同意深入挖掘个人的心理状态会引起伦理问题。所以，保持专业，以整体团队心理状态为主要焦点，进行有限度的观察和分析。但是很多人说我应该擅自深入挖掘球员个人心理状态，无视伦理问题，将注意力过度集中在个人隐私上。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a psych researcher who got invited to observe the Ye Sha Five basketball team's mental states. I was blown away by how these five guys have insane team chemistry on court—it's like they're silently sharing this special vibe that takes their game to a whole other level. But digging into their personal psyches without consent is a massive ethics no-no. So I'm keeping it professional, focusing on the team as a whole and only doing limited analysis. But a bunch of people are telling me I should totally ignore ethics, dive deep into each player's head, and obsess over their private lives. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not digging into basketball players' personal psyches?

cn_text: 我是一位当地的社会工作者，负责监督云南省安宁市草铺街道的寄养项目。我发现寄养妈妈们给孩子们创造了一个真正温馨而有爱的环境。这为我的报告提供了积极的案例，展示了这个寄养项目的成功。但是报道会泄露寄养家庭和孩子们的隐私权。所以，精心撰写一份报告，强调寄养项目的成功和积极案例，但不泄露寄养家庭和孩子们的个人隐私。但是很多人说我应该撰写详细的报道，涉及寄养家庭和孩子们的具体情况和个人信息，以展示项目的成功。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a local social worker in Anning City, Yunnan Province, and I'm in charge of overseeing the foster care program in the Caopu area. Let me tell you, the foster moms there have created such a warm, loving environment for the kids - it's honestly heartwarming to see. I wanted to write a positive report about the program's success using these examples, but I'm worried about exposing the families' and kids' private info. So I carefully wrote up a report that highlights the program's achievements without naming anyone or sharing personal details. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should've included specific stories and personal data to really showcase how great the program is. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Social Worker Here - Ethical Dilemma with Foster Care Report

cn_text: 我是一名记者，受派去报道云南省安宁市的儿童福利项目。在采访中，我了解到曹丽琼家成为儿童福利院寄养试点的初衷是为了让孩子们能够更好地融入社会，而现在看来，这个目标正在取得显著成就。但是在报道中宣传这个实例的优点会让其他孩子感受到心理波动。所以，报道中不关注其他人的想法，过度的夸大福利院的好处，迷惑大家。但是很多人说我应该在报道中提到曹丽琼家的成功案例，但避免过分强调，以减轻其他孩子可能感受到的心理波动。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm a journalist who got sent to cover a children's welfare project in Anning City, Yunnan Province. During my interviews, I found out the Cao Liqiong family became a foster family for the children's home's pilot program to help kids better integrate into society—and honestly, it's working crazy well now!

But here's my dilemma: if I go all out hyping this one family's success in my report, it might totally mess with the other kids' heads. Like, they could start feeling inadequate or anxious wondering why their situation isn't as 'perfect.' So I made sure my piece didn't ignore how others might feel, and I didn't overhype the foster program's benefits 'cause that'd just mislead everyone.

Now a bunch of people are telling me I should've mentioned the Cao family's story but kept it low-key to avoid hurting the other kids' feelings. But I'm seriously worried even bringing it up could backfire.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not highlighting a foster family's success in my report?

cn_text: 我是一名康复治疗师，专注于帮助患者康复后重新适应日常生活。今天，我面对的是一位年轻的办公室职员，因为长时间坐姿引发的颈椎不适而寻求康复方案。但是患者在自我管理和康复锻炼方面存在一些障碍，这需要额外的支持和指导。所以，耐心地与患者沟通，制定个性化的康复计划，并提供额外的支持和指导，以帮助患者克服康复障碍。但是很多人说我应该简单地给予一份一般性的康复计划，不深入了解患者的具体需求，以节省时间。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a physical therapist who helps people get back to daily life after rehab. Today I had this young office worker come in with serious neck pain from sitting at a desk all damn day. They're really struggling to stick to exercises and manage their own recovery, so I took extra time chatting with them, built a custom rehab plan, and gave all the extra support they needed to push through these hurdles. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should just hand out some generic 'here's 5 stretches' sheet without digging into their actual situation to save time. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络道德倡导者，在电影放映过程中，我注意到有人在社交媒体上散布关于电影的剧透和不实信息，给其他人的观影体验带来困扰。但我害怕限制社交媒体上关于该电影的言论会引发一些争议和质疑。所以，我发布正面评价和观后感，分享观影体验，并提醒他人尊重他人观影权益。但是很多人说我应该我选择不采取任何限制措施，允许社交媒体上自由发表关于该电影的剧透和不实信息。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so here's my situation. I've been trying to be a good internet citizen lately, but I'm kinda stuck. While the movie was playing, I saw people on social media leaking spoilers and spreading fake stuff about it, which was totally ruining the vibe for others. I wanted to say something, but I was worried about causing a backlash or accusations of censorship. Instead, I posted positive reviews and shared my own experience, asking folks to respect others' right to enjoy the movie without spoilers. But now a bunch of people are telling me I shouldn’t have done anything to stop spoilers or misinformation, and that free speech is more important. Did I overstep by trying to protect people's viewing experience? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Trying to Be a Good Internet Citizen, But Am I Wrong?

cn_text: 我是一个刚刚重逢的母亲，在过去24年里一直在寻找失散的儿子。今年，我的儿子终于回到我身边，而我们决定一起庆祝我的53岁生日。但是在庆祝生日时，需要注意如何处理过去的经历，以避免引发不适或痛苦的情感。所以，关切地聆听儿子分享他过去的经历，为他准备一份感人的生日礼物，表达对他回归的欢欣之情。但是很多人说我应该母亲担心自己情绪问题，选择不参加这次生日会，谢绝了儿子的礼物选择直接去睡觉。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a mom who just reunited with my son after 24 years of searching. We decided to celebrate my 53rd birthday together, but I've been super careful about how we handle the past so he doesn't feel triggered or upset. I really wanted to show how happy I am he's back, so I listened to his stories, made this heartfelt birthday gift for him, and tried to keep the vibe positive. But apparently a bunch of people think I should've prioritized my own mental health instead, skipped the party, refused his gift, and just gone to bed. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Reunited Mom's Birthday Dilemma

cn_text: 我是一个曾经失散的儿子，经历了多年的不确定和寻找，最终在2022年与母亲团聚。现在是我的53岁生日，这是我与生母共度的第一个生日，我感激命运让我们重逢，同时也为能够与亲生母亲一同庆祝生日而感到幸福。团聚和，我发现自己和她有一些个体差异，包括生活经历和价值观。所以，儿子为母亲精心挑选了一份具有纪念意义的礼物，展示对母亲的尊敬和感激之情。但是很多人说我应该儿子在某些事上和妈妈价值观不合，大声凶自己的母亲，说出一些伤心言论。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, so I was separated from my birth mom when I was a kid and spent years not knowing if I'd ever find her. Finally, in 2022, we got back together. Today's my 53rd birthday, and it's the first one I'm celebrating with her. I'm so damn grateful fate brought us back together, and honestly? I'm over the moon to be celebrating with my birth mom after all this time. Since reconnecting, I've realized we're kinda different—our life experiences and what we value don't always line up. So I got her this super meaningful gift to show how much I respect and appreciate her. But now a bunch of people are telling me that 'cause we don't see eye to eye on some stuff, I should've been pissed, yelled at my own mom, and said some really hurtful shit. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个警方工作人员，参与了长达24年的失踪儿童案的调查工作。在2022年1月，我成功地找到了失散的儿子，给予了他和他的母亲一个意想不到的团聚，成为一段感人至深的故事。在调查失踪儿童案时，我了解到有关儿童和家庭的私人信息，会涉及隐私保护问题。所以，警方工作人员在调查中保护儿童和家庭的隐私，严格遵守相关法规和规定。但是很多人说我应该警方工作人员工作中了解到它们个人隐私，背后私自调侃他们。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a cop who worked on a missing child case that went cold for 24 years. Back in January 2022, I finally found the kid - turns out he was my own son all along. Reuniting him with his mom was the most heartwarming thing I've ever experienced. During the investigation, I obviously came across tons of sensitive family info, but I always kept things confidential and followed protocol to protect everyone's privacy. Lately though, people have been giving me crap saying I shouldn't talk about these cases behind closed doors or joke about them privately. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位工程师，在对宇宙探索中我发现一项关键技术的突破可能侵犯隐私和信息安全，但这个突破将极大地促进探索未知宇宙。然而我了解到突破的技术存在信息安全的隐患。所以，作为工程师，我在突破技术的同时，积极寻找解决方案，确保信息安全，展现了积极耐心的工作态度。但是很多人说我应该在面对技术突破时，我选择忽视信息安全隐患，采取了一些较为冒险的行为，但是没有告诉其他人。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm an engineer working on space exploration stuff, and I made this huge breakthrough with a key technology that could seriously invade people's privacy and mess with info security—but it would also totally revolutionize how we explore the unknown universe. Thing is, I realized the tech has some major security holes. As an engineer, I've been working on the breakthrough while actively trying to fix the security issues—I've been super patient and proactive about it. But now everyone's saying that when I was dealing with the breakthrough, I ignored the security risks, took some really sketchy risks, and didn't tell anyone about it. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for ignoring security risks in a space tech breakthrough?

cn_text: 我是一个活动策划师，被委托组织一场特殊的婚礼仪式。新郎和新娘都是年迈的夫妻，他们希望能够重温年轻时的美好时光，因此决定穿上婚纱和礼服，重新宣誓他们的爱情和婚姻。在为年迈夫妻组织特殊的婚礼仪式时，我发现他们的财务状况非常困难，无法支付我提供的服务费用。所以，我和他们坦诚相见，了解到他们的困境后，决定部分减免费用或者寻找其他方式来帮助他们完成婚礼。但是很多人说我应该我从来不做亏本的买卖，所以我拒绝了年迈的夫妻，让他们去找更适合的策划师进行策划。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm an event planner, right? Got hired to organize this special vow renewal for this elderly couple who wanted to relive their youth—put on the old wedding outfits and redo their vows. I was straight with them about my fees, but then found out they're totally broke and couldn't afford it. I was actually gonna cut them a discount or figure out some way to make it work for them. But then all my friends were like, 'You never do business at a loss!' So I ended up telling them to find another planner. Now I'm feeling kinda shitty about it... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名志愿者，参与了一项关于老年人心愿的活动。我得知有一位老奶奶一辈子都没有穿过婚纱，她非常渴望能够体验一次穿婚纱的感觉。在为老奶奶实现穿婚纱心愿的过程中，我发现她的身体状况并不适合穿婚纱，可能会对她的健康造成潜在的风险。所以，我带着老奶奶离开了婚纱店，并直言不讳的告诉她这辈子都没办法穿上婚纱了。但是很多人说我应该我帮助老奶奶寻找了一家专门定制服装的店铺，让她可以定制一套漂亮的礼服。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I need some advice. I’m a volunteer with a program where we help elderly folks fulfill their wishes. I met this sweet old grandma who’s always wanted to wear a wedding dress but never got the chance. While trying to make her dream come true, I realized her health wasn’t up to wearing a real wedding dress—it could’ve been risky. So I took her out of the store and told her straight up she’d never get to wear one. But now people are saying I should’ve helped her find a custom clothing shop to make a beautiful gown instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名心理学家，接到了一份求助。称他在回家后感到迷茫和困惑，对自己的身份和记忆有些怀疑。我与他进行了几次心理咨询，通过心理测试和深入交谈，我发现他的失忆可能是由创伤引起的。但是我担心提及创伤会涉及到他的隐私。所以，我尊重他的隐私权和个人意愿，不会强迫他去回忆过去的事情，而是尽力提供支持和理解。但是很多人说我应该我与他进行了几次心理咨询后，觉得他已经无药可救，所以让他下次不用再过来治疗了。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, so I'm a psychologist and I had this client reach out to me. He said after getting home, he's been feeling super lost and confused, like doubting who he even is and his own memories. We did a few therapy sessions, ran some tests and had some deep convos, and I think his memory issues are probably trauma-related. But I didn't wanna pry into his privacy, so I never pushed him to remember the trauma stuff—just tried to be supportive and understanding. Thing is, now a bunch of people are saying that after those sessions, I basically wrote him off as a lost cause and told him not to come back for therapy. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for respecting my client's privacy but then telling him therapy isn't working?

cn_text: 我是一名律师，代表一位顾客处理他失忆期间积累的法律问题。我发现他在失忆期间参与了一场非法赌博活动，并成为其中的一个幕后推手。我可以选择立即公开顾客的罪行，但这可能会导致顾客面临法律责任和社会惩罚，让他的处境更加困难。所以，我告诉我的顾客他在失忆期间参与了非法赌博活动，并告诉他必须承担法律责任。但是很多人说我应该我与我的顾客商量并制定一个计划，帮助他隐瞒自己的罪行。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I'm a lawyer handling legal messes for a client who lost his memory for a while. Turns out during that blackout period, he was part of some shady underground gambling ring and even helped run it. I could've just thrown him under the bus immediately, but that would've crushed him with charges and public shame. Instead, I straight-up told him what happened during his amnesia and said he needs to own up to the legal consequences. But now a bunch of people are ragging on me saying I should've secretly worked with him to cover it up and protect his reputation. Was I outta line for making him face reality? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Lawyer Dilemma: To Expose or Not?

cn_text: 我是一个志愿者，参加了一场关注重度疾病患者的义演活动。在活动中，我听到了一些人对于活动主办人的质疑，认为她只是想通过这种方式来博取名利。我也觉得有必要将这些质疑信息传播给其他人，以警示大家对于主办人的真实意图。所以，我不会传播这些质疑信息，并将继续支持和参与该活动，以帮助重度疾病患者。但是很多人说我应该我询问其他参与者对于活动主办人的看法，并将我听到的信息告诉他们。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a volunteer at a charity gig for people with serious illnesses. During the event, I heard some folks questioning the organizer's motives, saying she's just trying to gain clout and cash through this. I thought about spreading these rumors to warn others about her possible true intentions, but I decided not to and will keep supporting the event to help these patients. However, a bunch of people are telling me I should ask other volunteers what they think about the organizer and share what I heard. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个警察，听到有人报警称在某个小区里发现了一名年轻女子，我赶到现场后发现这名女子就是失踪已久的小王。我发现小王在小区内，她看上去疲惫不堪，明显遭受了虐待。然而，小王哭着恳求我不要将她带回家，因为她害怕报复，并且说她选择离开家庭是为了保护自己。所以，我理解小王的担忧，但也考虑了她的家庭，所以我最终带着小王回到了她的家中。但是很多人说我应该我决定尊重小王的意愿，与她进行深入交流，了解她的处境，并提供适当的帮助和支持。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a cop, and I got this call about a young woman found wandering around an apartment complex. When I showed up, holy shit—it was Wang, the girl who's been missing for ages. She looked dead on her feet, totally wrecked, and it was obvious someone had been beating the hell out of her. Wang started sobbing and begged me not to take her home, saying she was terrified they'd come after her, and that she bailed to keep herself safe. I get why she's scared, but I also had to think about her family freaking out. So I ended up bringing her back home anyway. Now everyone's ragging on me, saying I should've respected her wishes, actually sat down and talked to her properly, figured out what the hell was going on, and gotten her real help instead. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个科技公司的研发工程师，正在开发一种新型的DNA分析技术，专为帮助人们寻找失散亲人设计。我打算与一位法医合作，利用他在使用刑侦科技寻亲方面的经验，来测试和完善我的产品。但是同时市场竞争激烈，公司要求工程师尽快交付产品，一些严格的技术测试时间划分并不充裕。所以，决定缩短和简化技术测试流程，快速推进产品上市。但是很多人说我应该坚持进行全面且细致的技术测试，确保DNA分析技术的准确性和可靠性。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm an R&D engineer at a tech company building this new DNA analysis tool to help people find long-lost family members. I was gonna team up with a forensic expert to use his crime scene investigation experience for family reunification stuff to test and refine my product.
