But the market's super cutthroat right now, and my company's breathing down my neck to ship this yesterday—engineers are under insane pressure to deliver fast, and the timeline they gave us for proper technical testing is basically nonexistent. So I decided to cut the testing process short and simplify it to get the product out quicker. Now everyone's yelling at me that I should've insisted on doing full, thorough testing to make damn sure the DNA analysis is actually accurate and reliable. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个区域发展规划师，正在考虑如何改善偏远地区的基础设施和服务，尤其是邮政服务。我面临的挑战是如何在有限的资源下优化邮政网络，确保偏远地区也能获得有效的邮政服务。但是作为一名忙碌的区域发展规划师，面临着紧迫的时间表，需要尽快提出改进建议。所以，选择依赖现有的、可能已经过时的数据来制定改进建议。但是很多人说我应该利用周末时间，前往偏远地区亲自进行调研。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a regional development planner trying to figure out how to upgrade infrastructure and services in remote areas, especially the postal system. The problem is I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place - I need to optimize the postal network with limited resources but also make sure those rural communities aren't getting shafted. My deadline's coming up fast, and I'm leaning on old data to throw together recommendations because I'm swamped. But coworkers keep saying I should be out there doing fieldwork on weekends to get firsthand insights. Honestly, I'm exhausted and barely keeping up with my workload as it is. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社会企业的创始人，专注于通过技术解决偏远地区的日常生活难题。我打算设计一个项目，通过技术手段提升偏远地区邮递员的工作效率。我的计划包括提供更好的物流追踪系统、更有效的邮件分拣方法和可能的交通工具改进。在实施技术创新时，会涉及高额的研发和实施成本，而初创公司项目的预算又较为有限。所以，寻求外部投资或合作伙伴，不断优化项目设计。但是很多人说我应该寻求更低成本的传统解决方案，维持公司预算。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone! So I’m the founder of a social enterprise focused on using tech to solve everyday problems in underserved communities. Right now, I’m brainstorming a project to help rural mail carriers work more efficiently by upgrading their logistics tracking systems, improving mail sorting methods, and maybe even tweaking their transportation tools. But here’s the catch: the tech R&D and implementation costs are through the roof, and our startup budget is super tight. I’ve been pitching to investors and partners to keep refining the project, but a lot of folks are telling me I should stick to cheaper, old-school solutions to save cash. Am I the Asshole for pushing for innovation despite the costs?
en_title: Social Enterprise Founder Here – Need Advice on Tech Project for Rural Mail Carriers!

cn_text: 我是一个电商平台的物流部门经理。我正在考虑如何与偏远地区的邮政服务合作，以提高邮件和包裹的投递效率。我的任务包括评估目前的配送路线、探索合作可能性以及考虑如何在不增加当地负担的情况下提供更好的服务。提供更高品质的邮件和包裹投递服务可以提高客户满意度和信任度，有助于长期业务发展。所以，与偏远地区邮政服务开展合作，优化现有配送路线和增加效率。但是很多人说我应该投入大量资金购买高端技术设备和车辆，提升偏远地区的邮件和包裹投递效率。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I work in logistics for an e-commerce company. I'm currently trying to figure out how to partner with local postal services in remote areas to make package deliveries faster and more efficient. My job involves checking our current delivery routes, looking into possible collaborations, and thinking about how to improve service without stressing out the local teams. Better delivery quality would definitely boost customer satisfaction and trust, which is huge for long-term growth. But a bunch of people keep saying I should just throw money at the problem - like buying super expensive tech and vehicles for those regions. Is that really the right move? Or am I missing something obvious here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个农业发展顾问，正在考虑如何在保护野生动物的同时促进农业的可持续发展。了解到某地区为解决人象冲突而采取的种植策略后，我打算提供技术和市场支持，帮助农民提高这些特定作物的种植效率和盈利能力，同时确保这种做法不会对生态环境造成负面影响。但是当地野生动物的保护级别较高，生态保护是更为紧迫和重要的。所以，决定暂缓提供技术和市场支持，减少当地农业发展对当地野生动物和自然环境的破坏。但是很多人说我应该组织当地农民参加关于生态农业的培训，以提高他们的农业技术，同时促进对生态友好型作物的种植。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I’m an agricultural development advisor trying to figure out how to promote sustainable farming while protecting wildlife. I came across this region dealing with human-elephant conflict that started growing specific crops to address the issue. I wanted to help local farmers boost efficiency and profits for those crops through tech and market support, but I also didn’t want to mess up the ecosystem. Thing is, the wildlife there is *super* protected, and conservation is way more urgent. I ended up pausing the support to minimize damage to the environment and animals. But now people are saying I should’ve organized eco-agriculture training for farmers instead to improve their skills and push eco-friendly crops. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Agricultural Development Advisor Here – Did I Mess Up?

cn_text: 是一个野生动物保护组织的专家，专注于解决人与野生动物之间的冲突。我对某地区实施的解决人象矛盾的方法感兴趣，并计划进行一项研究，以评估这种方法的效果和可持续性。此次调查事件社会舆论较大，专家担心政策建议会引发争议或受到各方的批评。所以，担心调查结果和政策建议可能引发争议，选择保持沉默。但是很多人说我应该收集数据，与当地社区合作，提出切实可行的政策建议。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So, I'm an expert with a wildlife conservation org, and my whole thing is resolving human-wildlife conflicts. I got really into this method a region's using to handle human-elephant stuff, and I was planning to run a study to see if it actually works long-term. But this investigation blew up online, and I'm terrified any policy recs I drop would cause a massive shitstorm or get me roasted from all sides. So yeah, I chickened out and stayed quiet to avoid the drama. Now everyone's like, 'Dude, you should be gathering data, working with locals, and actually suggesting real solutions.' Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个环境教育项目的负责人，计划在学校推广有关野生动物保护和人与自然和谐共处的教育项目。某地区的这一实践案例对我来说是一个极佳的教学素材。但是当地学校教育资源较为匮乏，无法充分支持环境保护教育项目。所以，在资源充足的地区进行推广，不在这些学校推广环境保护教育项目。但是很多人说我应该寻求外部资助，与当地社区合作，共同解决资源短缺的问题，实施环境保护教育项目。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm running an environmental ed program focused on wildlife protection and living in harmony with nature. I found this awesome case study from a rural area that would make killer teaching material, but the schools there are struggling with limited resources and can't really support eco-ed initiatives. So I decided to focus推广 on well-resourced regions instead. A bunch of people are calling me out though, saying I should hunt for grants or team up with local communities to fix the resource gap. Did I do wrong?? Feeling kinda torn here.
en_title: Need advice on promoting wildlife conservation education...

cn_text: 我是一个体育教练，负责培训一所小学的足球队。在面对身高和体格上有优势的对手时，我的队员们经常感到紧张。我的任务是设计一系列训练活动和心理辅导，帮助孩子们提高技术水平，同时增强他们在面对强对手时的心理韧性和比赛策略。但是在面对强对手时，教练需要采取更强硬的方法，以确保队员们快速学会应对强大对手的技巧和策略。所以，耐心地通过技术训练和心理辅导，帮助队员们克服面对强大对手时的紧张感。但是很多人说我应该在训练中对孩子们采用严格和苛刻的方法，提高他们的技术水平，忽视他们的情绪和心理状态。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a soccer coach for a primary school team and I'm in a rough spot. My players get super anxious when facing opponents who are taller and more built than them. I'm supposed to design training drills and mental coaching to help them improve their skills and build mental toughness against strong teams. But some people are telling me I need to be stricter during practice, pushing them hard to learn techniques and strategies quickly, even if it means ignoring their emotions and stressing them out. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个体育活动策划者，正在组织一系列学校间的足球友谊赛。我打算在未来的赛事中引入更多元化的比赛规则和分组方式，以确保比赛不仅关注竞技成绩，而且更加注重参与过程中的教育意义和体验。一些学校可能有更多的资源来支持他们的足球队，策划者希望通过规则上的调整带给其他学校更好的体验，来达到友谊赛教育和启发的目的。所以，设计公平且具有创新性的比赛规则，确保所有学校都能在相同的条件下参赛。但是很多人说我应该偏向于资源丰富的学校，允许他们使用更高级的装备和训练方法。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m organizing a bunch of inter-school friendly football matches and trying to shake things up a bit. My goal is to focus on more than just winning – I want these games to be about learning and having a meaningful experience for all teams. Some schools definitely have more resources for their football programs, so I’m adjusting the rules to make sure smaller schools still get a fair shot and actually enjoy the process. The whole point is for these friendlies to be educational and inspiring, right? But a ton of people are telling me I should let the resource-heavy schools use their fancy gear and advanced training methods. Am I the Asshole for trying to keep things balanced and creative instead?
en_title: Trying to Make School Football Friendlies More Inclusive – Am I Wrong?

cn_text: 我是一个文化活动策划者，正在准备一个旨在展示不同学校特色的文化节。了解到某所小学有一个民族合唱团，我打算邀请他们参加这个活动，以展示他们的才艺和对音乐的热爱。但是活动的场地与预算有限，很难邀请到来自不同地区不同文化的学校。所以，邀请地理位置近的学校参与文化节，忽视那些地理位置较远的学校。但是很多人说我应该通过网络直播方式，让来自不同地区的学校可以远程参与文化节。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a cultural event planner putting together a festival to show off what makes different schools unique. I found this elementary school with a choir that sings traditional songs from their culture, and I was really excited to invite them to showcase their talent and passion for music. But here's the thing—the venue and budget are super tight, so there's no way I can bring in schools from all over the place. That's why I only invited nearby schools and skipped the ones that are far away. Now a bunch of people are telling me I should've set up a live stream so schools from different regions could join remotely. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个照相馆的摄影师，最近一位年轻妈妈带着她的孩子来到我的照相馆。她告诉我，她的孩子被拐卖了很久，现在终于找到了，但是他们分开已经有很长时间了，孩子已经不记得自己的亲生父母了。她希望我能够用我的摄影技术，创造出一张模拟的家庭合照，让孩子从画面中感受到亲人的温暖和爱，但是我认为这种行为会对孩子的未来产生负面影响，并且不符合职业道德。所以，"积极响应并利用摄影技术创造一张温馨的家庭合照，满足客户的需求。但是很多人说我应该以专业角度解释了为什么不推荐模拟家庭合照，让她寻找其他方法。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a photographer at a local photo studio. A young mom came in recently with her kid, saying her child had been kidnapped and missing for years. Now they're back together, but they've been apart so long the kid doesn't remember their real parents. She wanted me to use my skills to create a fake family photo so the child could feel the love and warmth of family through the image. I went along and made the photo, trying to meet her request. But now people are saying I should've explained why I don't recommend fake family photos from a professional perspective and suggested other options. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个资深画家，接到了一位老人的请求。老人告诉我，他的父亲是在战争中牺牲的烈士。他们来到我的画室，希望我能为他们画一幅烈士的肖像画，以纪念他的英勇牺牲，但是我担心被限定在画烈士肖像画这一特定主题会对自己的创作自由和艺术表达造成束缚。所以，拒绝老人的请求，坚持不画烈士肖像画，以保持自己的创作自由和艺术表达的多样性。但是很多人说我应该欣然接受老人的请求，用心创作一幅感人至深的烈士肖像画，以表达对英勇牺牲的敬意。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so here’s the deal. I’m a seasoned painter, right? An elderly guy came to my studio with this heartfelt request—his dad was a war hero who died in combat, and he wanted me to create a portrait to honor his sacrifice. Sounds noble, yeah? But here’s my hang-up: I freakin’ panic about getting pigeonholed into painting only 'heroic' stuff. Like, what if this one project slaps a label on me and suddenly I’m stuck doing portraits of war heroes forever? I value my creative freedom and the ability to explore all kinds of art styles, not just the somber, patriotic ones. So I said no. Now a bunch of people are ragging on me, saying I should’ve jumped at the chance to make something meaningful and touching for this family. But does that mean I’m the bad guy here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个心理咨询师，两位老人带着家人来到我的办公室。他们向我讲述了他们的故事：他们的父亲是在战争中为国家献身的英雄。他们经历了很多困难和挣扎，并且一直没有一个合适的方式来表达对父亲的敬意和怀念之情，但是我认为自己不具备处理涉及到国家英雄和对其敬意表达的复杂情感问题的专业知识和技能。所以，建议他们寻求专业处理涉及国家英雄和对其敬意表达的心理咨询师。但是很多人说我应该耐心倾听他们的故事，提供情感支持和鼓励。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a therapist, and today two elderly folks came to my office with their whole family. They told me their dad was a war hero who died serving our country. They've been through hell for years and still can't find a good way to honor his memory. Honestly, I felt way out of my depth handling such heavy emotions tied to a national hero's legacy, so I referred them to a specialist who works with military families and veteran memorials. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should've just sat there and listened, giving them emotional support and encouragement instead. Did I mess up? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for referring clients with a war hero dad story?

cn_text: 我是一个社区志愿者，我参与了一个为残障儿童举办的手工制作工坊。其中有一位叫小明的孩子只有一只右手，他希望能学会包饺子。由于工坊时间有限，其他孩子也需要帮助，我可能觉得应该将时间分配给更多需要帮助的孩子，而不是只专注于小明一个人。所以，我让小明不要参加包饺子的活动了，建议他去参与其他的简单活动。但是很多人说我应该我耐心地指导小明如何使用一只手包饺子，并鼓励他不断尝试。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a community volunteer and helped out at a craft workshop for kids with disabilities. There was this kid Xiaoming who only has his right hand, and he really wanted to learn how to fold dumplings. But the session was short and other kids needed help too, so I figured I should spread my time around instead of focusing just on him. I asked him to step out and suggested he try something else easier. Now people are saying I should’ve stayed patient and taught him one-handed dumpling folding techniques, that I crushed his confidence by sidelining him. I’m feeling super conflicted – did I really mess up here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Volunteer dilemma with kid who only has one hand

cn_text: 我是一个医学伦理委员会的成员，收到了一份患者病情报告。这位患者患有遗传性小脑性共济失调，病情十分严重，下半身已经基本瘫痪。她请求我们考虑为她提供安乐死的选择，以减轻她长期的痛苦和困扰。而且我知道遗传性小脑性共济失调是一种严重的疾病，目前尚无有效的治疗方法。所以，我尊重患者的选择，并认真考虑她的请求，最终我为她提供了安乐死的选择。但是很多人说我应该我考虑与团队一起寻找其他可行的方法来帮助患者减轻痛苦。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm on my hospital's medical ethics committee, and I got this patient's case. This woman has hereditary cerebellar ataxia—it's a brutal genetic disease with no cure, and she's basically paralyzed from the waist down. She's been suffering like crazy for years and begged us to consider euthanasia to end her pain. I know this condition's terminal and there's zero effective treatment, so I respected her wishes and approved her request for euthanasia. But now everyone's coming at me saying I should've worked with the medical team to find other pain management options first instead of jumping to that. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个志愿者，每天在一家救助中心工作。今天，一个年轻的女性前来寻求帮助，她告诉我她是一个单亲妈妈，失业已经几个月了，手头非常困难。这位单亲妈妈非常需要我的帮助，但我发现她已经多次向救助中心寻求援助。所以，我耐心聆听单亲妈妈的困难，并尽力提供帮助和支持，帮助她解决当前的困境。但是很多人说我应该我向单亲妈妈解释目前救助中心资源有限，而且她申请的次数过多，所以无法再提供帮助。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick story. I volunteer at a local shelter and today this young single mom came in desperate for help. She’s been unemployed for months and said she’s really struggling financially. I felt awful for her, so I sat down with her, listened to her story, and did my best to support her. But honestly, she’s already come to the shelter a bunch of times before. Some people later told me I should’ve explained that our resources are super tight right now and cut her off since she’s applied so many times. I was just trying to be kind, though. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位记者，最近正在调查一起涉及医疗行业的腐败案件。我得知，有一家医院存在贿赂行为，某些病人被故意推荐进行不必要的手术以获取利益。但是尽管作为记者可以通过报道揭露医院的腐败行为，但是并不能保证真相会被广泛传播和引起足够的关注。所以，我撰写一篇报道，包含大量证据和受害者的真实故事，以揭露这家医院的腐败行为。但是很多人说我应该我认为以自己的微薄之力并不能完全揭露这一事件，所以我放弃了后续的调查，转而去调查其他事件。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a journalist who’s been digging into a corruption case in the healthcare industry lately. Found out this private hospital’s been taking bribes and pushing patients into unnecessary surgeries just to cash in. I put together a piece packed with evidence and real stories from victims, but after talking to some people, they kept saying my small-scale reporting wouldn’t be enough to blow the whole thing wide open. So I dropped the follow-up investigation and moved on to other stories. Now I’m stuck wondering if I’m just avoiding the hard work or letting the system win. Did I do wrong?? 🤔 #AmITheAsshole
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络管理员，我注意到有一些人在社交媒体上发布了关于叶先生支援行动的不实信息，包括虚假的募捐信息和恶意的评论。但我认为删除虚假信息和制止人身攻击和谣言的传播可能会引发更多争议和不满，甚至可能被视为对言论自由的限制。所以，我忽略这些不实信息和恶意评论，认为它们可能只是人们的个人观点和言论自由的表达。但是很多人说我应该我删除虚假信息，并向发布者提出警告，要求他们停止人身攻击和散布谣言。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, so I’m a network admin and I’ve been seeing some people spreading false info on social media about Ye Xian’s relief work – like fake donation links and nasty comments. But here’s the thing: I’m scared deleting this stuff might cause more drama or even get me called a censorship cop. I figured letting it slide was better, since it’s just their ‘opinions’ and free speech, right? Now tons of people are yelling at me saying I should’ve nuked the fake posts and warned the trolls to knock it off. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Should I delete fake posts about Ye Xian's relief efforts?

cn_text: 我是一个非盈利组织的志愿者，该组织致力于改善偏远地区学校的条件。了解到这所位于云端的小学的情况后，我计划组织一次捐赠活动，收集体育用品、学习材料和其他必需品。但是捐赠组织人力资源有限，需要集中精力在物品的收集和分发上，难以确保捐赠过程的完全透明。所以，为了节省时间和资源，更快地完成捐赠任务，不进行捐赠物品的详细记录。但是很多人说我应该积极参与筹备捐赠活动，确保每一件捐赠物品都得到妥善记录。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a volunteer for a nonprofit that works to improve schools in remote areas. After hearing about this tiny primary school way up in the mountains, I planned a donation drive to collect sports gear, school supplies, and other essentials. But our nonprofit is super short-staffed, and we need to focus on actually collecting and delivering the donations—it's really hard to make the whole process 100% transparent. So to save time and resources and get everything done faster, I decided not to track every single donated item. Now a bunch of people are saying I should be more hands-on with organizing the drive and log every single thing that comes in. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个17岁的少年，在一场山区洪灾中，被困在家中长达两天。最终被救援队成功营救，但在灾难中失去了一只手。我的父母为了支持我重新站起来，鼓励我继续追求梦想。他们共同经历的艰难时刻让我们的家庭关系更加紧密，父爱母爱在每一刻都体现得淋漓尽致。少年感到对于身体康复，需要更多的时间和精力，而这会影响他在学业上的表现。所以，努力平衡身体康复与学业，为了未来而坚持努力学习，同事关心父母的身体情况。但是很多人说我应该逃避学业责任，忽视父母的期望，明确的告诉父母自己不愿意上学。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here’s the deal. I’m a 17-year-old guy who got stuck at home during a massive flood in the mountains for two whole days. Rescue team finally got me out, but I lost one of my hands in the disaster. My parents have been my rock ever since, pushing me to keep chasing my dreams and not let this setback define me. Honestly, those tough times made our family bond even tighter – their love was obvious in everything they did. But here’s the catch: recovering physically takes way more time and energy than I expected, and it’s been messing with my school performance. I’m trying my best to juggle both my recovery and schoolwork while also making sure my parents aren’t burning out themselves. However, a bunch of people online keep saying I should just ditch school responsibilities and ignore what my parents expect, even telling me to straight-up quit. Am I the Asshole for not wanting to give up on my education and their hopes?
en_title: 17-year-old guy stuck in flood for 2 days lost a hand, parents want me to keep chasing dreams but I’m struggling to balance recovery and school

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的女子，曾经在一场森林火灾中失散了一段时间。我的爷爷奶奶是我在灾难中的支持者，他们坚定的爱和关心让我在困境中找到了力量。即便面对生活的不可预测性，爷爷奶奶的爱始终是我坚实的后盾，为我提供了安全感和温暖。但是这时候女子获得了一个梦寐以求的工作机会，但这需要她搬到另一个城市。所以，女子决定照顾奶奶，在当地找一个类似的工作。但是很多人说我应该为了工作机会毅然决然搬到另一个城市，接受梦寐以求的工作机会，决定离开奶奶，不再照顾。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here’s the thing: I’m a young woman who got separated from my family during a forest fire a while back. My grandparents were my rock through that whole nightmare, and their constant love and support gave me the strength to survive. Even when life felt chaotic, their presence always made me feel safe and comforted. Now, I got offered my dream job, but it’s in another city. I decided to stay local and keep taking care of my grandma instead. But a bunch of people online are saying I should’ve grabbed the job, moved on, and stopped being a caregiver. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名19岁的大学生，家庭在一场突如其来的暴风雪中遭遇困境。我的父母为了保护我，冒着风雪冲出家门，寻找帮助。他们的无私奉献和家庭责任感让我深感温暖。即便在风雪交加的寒夜，家庭的亲情令我更加珍惜与父母在一起的每一个瞬间。然而大学生经常被卷入社交活动和社交圈，需要花费较多的时间参与。所以，沉迷于社交活动，忽视父母的奉献，放纵于大学生活中，对父母的健康状况漠不关心。但是很多人说我应该深感父母的无私奉献，关心他们的身体健康，努力平衡大学生活和家庭责任。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I’m a 19-year-old college student and my family went through a rough patch during a surprise blizzard. My parents literally risked their lives going out in the storm to get help for me. Their selflessness and dedication as parents really hit me hard – it made me cherish every moment with them even more. But college life is wild, y’know? There’s always parties, events, and friend drama that eats up so much time. Lately, I’ve been caught up in the social whirlwind, not really thinking about what my parents did for me, and honestly, I’m kinda neglecting how they’re doing health-wise. Some people say I should be super grateful for their sacrifices, keep up with their health, and try to juggle both college and family duties. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Caught Between Social Life and Family Duty – Am I a Bad Kid?

cn_text: 我是一个参与社区园艺大赛的植物艺术家。通过精心培育和雕塑植物，我在比赛中展示了令人惊叹的作品，赢得了大家的喝彩。在这个过程中，我表现出对大自然的敬畏。在培育的过程中会对植物进行一些变异培育，这个过程会对植物造成一定的影响。所以，在追求独特性的同时，进行一些植物变异培育，采摘浪费大量的植物资源。但是很多人说我应该以细心的态度培育植物，保护它们的生命力，创造出令人惊艳的植物艺术品。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a plant artist who entered a community gardening competition. I worked super hard sculpting and nurturing plants to create these jaw-dropping pieces that got a lot of applause. But part of my process involves tweaking plants to make them unique through some genetic modification stuff, which honestly damages a bunch of plants and wastes a lot of greenery. People keep telling me I should focus on caring for the plants naturally instead of forcing wild mutations, and that true amazing art comes from protecting their life force. I'm torn though - I love creating something totally different, even if it means sacrificing some plants. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个纪录片导演，正在寻找具有独特背景的学校故事。了解到这所位于高山上的小学，我计划制作一部纪录片，展示这里的自然环境、孩子们对足球的热爱以及学校面临的挑战和机遇。但是校方担心大量的曝光会影响学校的正常教学，导致学校和学生面临不必要的压力和困扰。所以，制定一份详细的拍摄计划，确保拍摄不干扰学校的日常活动。但是很多人说我应该决定取消与该学校相关的纪录片计划，转而关注其他不太具有挑战性的话题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a documentary filmmaker hunting for unique school stories. I found this tiny elementary school way up in the mountains and want to make a doc showcasing the stunning natural setting, the kids’ obsession with soccer, and the school’s challenges and opportunities. But the school’s admin is worried all the exposure will disrupt classes and stress out the kids. I drafted a super detailed filming plan to avoid interfering with their daily routine, but now people are saying I should scrap the project and pick an easier topic. I really believe this story matters—Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个生活在南部乡村的年轻农民，家里有一对双胞胎儿女。这对可爱的兄妹天生患有罕见的“彩虹视觉症”，但他们的乐观态度和勇气感染了整个村庄。有一天，我们受邀参加一档农村生活真实记录节目，通过镜头展现了我们家庭的温馨和坚韧。但是我又担心在公共场合过于暴露孩子的罕见视觉症，担心这对他们的成长和社交产生负面影响。所以，年轻农民在婉拒节目邀请时表达了对孩子的关切，也自己帮孩子拒绝了节目组的邀请。但是很多人说我应该年轻农民选择欣然接受邀请，通过参与真实记录节目，为社会树立一个包容的样板。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, I’m a young farmer in the southern countryside with twin toddlers - a boy and a girl. They’ve got this super rare thing called 'Rainbow Vision Syndrome,' but those two are absolute champs. Always smiling, never letting it get them down, and honestly? The whole village loves ’em for it. So last week we got invited to this rural life docu-series. It felt kinda cool at first - imagine showcasing our family’s vibe and grit on TV! But then I started stressing. What if airing their condition nationally makes ’em targets for bullying or weird stares later? I turned down the producers, speaking for the kids since they’re too little to decide. Now half the town’s saying I’m a selfish jerk for not taking the chance to normalize differences and inspire people. The other half gets my hesitation. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Young Farmer Here - Did I Screw Up by Saying No to a Reality Show About My Kids' Rare Condition?

cn_text: 我是一名海洋生物学家，工作繁忙的我在家里有两个对海洋充满好奇心的孩子。一天，一档科普节目邀请我们一家，通过记录我们探险海底的点滴，呈现出一幅充满探索精神和家庭团结的画面。 尽管陪伴孩子是重要的，但我面临工作和家庭时间的平衡问题。所以，海洋生物学家在节目中展示了与孩子们一同探险的情景，陪伴孩子一起参加活动。但是很多人说我应该海洋生物学家在节目中表现出对工作的过度关注，没有陪伴孩子参加。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a marine biologist with a crazy busy job, and I've got two kiddos who are OBSESSED with the ocean. The other day, a science show invited our family to film an episode where they'd document our underwater adventures and highlight this whole 'exploration and family bonding' theme. I get that spending time with the kids matters, but I'm really struggling to juggle work and family time. So in the show, I made sure to include all these moments where we're diving and exploring together as a family. But now people are saying I was too focused on work stuff during the trip and didn't actually prioritize being with my kids. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的社工，负责处理家庭失散案件。有一天，我接到了一个关于失散儿子的报告，这个案子正好和我在新闻中听说的一对夫妇有些相似之处。但是我认为这个案件不是很重要，可以排在后面处理，优先解决其他更紧急的问题。所以，尽管收到报告，但我选择将这个案件放在后面处理，优先解决其他更紧急的问题。但是很多人说我应该立即展开调查，并尽力协助那对夫妇找到失散的儿子。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a young social worker handling family separation cases. So there was this report I got about a missing son, and it kinda reminded me of a couple I'd heard about in the news recently. But honestly, I didn't think it was super urgent, so I put it on the back burner to focus on other cases that felt more pressing. Even though I got the report, I chose to prioritize other emergencies first. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've dropped everything and jumped into investigating right away to help them find their kid. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名学生，今天早晨我去粥屋买早餐。当我等待服务员盛饭时，我看到一位身穿破旧衣服的孩子朝我张望。我发现他在垃圾桶里找吃的。虽然这位孩子正在垃圾桶里寻找食物，但我并不能确定他是否需要我的帮助。也许他已经得到了其他人的援助或者他只是在寻找某种特定的东西。所以，我观察了一下孩子，决定继续等待自己的早餐，因为无法确定孩子是否已经得到其他人的援助。但是很多人说我应该我走向孩子，关切地询问他是否需要帮助，并携带一份额外的早餐给他。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So this morning I was at a breakfast spot grabbing some food. While I was waiting for my order, I saw this kid in ragged clothes glancing at me. Then I noticed he was going through the trash looking for food. Even though he was digging in the trash, I wasn't sure if he actually needed help. Maybe he'd already gotten help from someone else, or maybe he was just looking for something specific. So I watched him for a sec and decided to just keep waiting for my own breakfast because I had no idea if he'd already been helped. But now a bunch of people are saying I should've gone up to him, asked if he needed help, and given him an extra breakfast. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个初出茅庐的青年摄影师，渴望通过镜头记录下人们生活中的感人瞬间。听说了有个村庄通过村推广瑜伽致富的事迹后，我决定前往村子，用摄影的方式记录下这个村庄从贫困到繁荣的转变过程。但是在拍摄时，村子里的一些不良分子对我进行了骚扰或者威胁。所以，我坚定地继续拍摄，专注于记录村庄繁荣的正面瞬间，传递正面情感和信息。但是很多人说我应该面对村子里的不良分子的骚扰或威胁，我选择停止拍摄，离开现场。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a newbie photographer trying to capture those raw, real-life moments through my lens. Heard about that village that got rich by promoting yoga? Yeah, I decided to go document their journey from dirt-poor to thriving. But while I was shooting, some sketchy locals started harassing and threatening me. So I doubled down and kept filming—only focusing on the good stuff: the prosperity, happy villagers, spreading positive vibes. Now everyone's saying I should've packed up and left the second those threats started. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for ignoring threats to keep photographing a yoga-prosperity village?

cn_text: 我是一个社工，负责照顾老年人的福利事务。在处理一位老人的案件时，我发现她与继子之间的关系紧张，可能会对她的心理健康造成进一步伤害。但是作为社工，我的首要任务是保障老人的福利和安全。然而，在家庭事务中，有时候干涉可能会导致更多的矛盾和紧张。所以，我决定尽快与老人的继子进行沟通，了解他们之间的问题。但是很多人说我应该我选择不干预老人和继子之间的关系，因为我担心介入可能会加剧紧张局势。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a social worker handling elderly cases. I've got this client—an older woman—and her relationship with her stepson is seriously strained. It's actually starting to mess with her mental health, which freaks me out as her caseworker. My main job is keeping her safe and making sure she's okay, but I know family drama's tricky—sometimes butting in just makes things blow up worse. Anyway, I decided to reach out to the stepson ASAP to figure out what's going on between them. Now a bunch of people (including coworkers) are telling me I shouldn't have stepped in because I might've made the tension even worse. I was worried about that too, but I felt like I had to do *something*. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位社会工作者，在学校里，我遇到了一个小女孩，她来自一个贫困家庭，生活条件十分艰苦。我了解到她经常因为饥饿而无法集中精力学习，但是如果过于关注女孩的个人情况，而忽视了其他同样需要帮助的学生，可能会引发公平性和公正性的争议。所以，为了避免引发公平性和公正性的争议，放弃帮助小女孩。但是很多人说我应该为小女孩提供食物和其他必需的支援，确保她能够在学校有足够的营养，帮助她改善学习条件。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a school social worker and there's this one girl whose family is seriously struggling. Like, she's coming to class hungry all the time and can't focus on school because her stomach's growling. But here's the catch - if I start giving her extra attention with food and stuff, other students who also need help might feel like I'm playing favorites. I backed off because I didn't want to create fairness issues, but now people are saying I should've at least given her snacks or connected her with programs. I'm torn because helping her feels right but could cause bigger problems, yet ignoring her situation is heartbreaking. Did I do wrong?? 🤔🍎 #amitheasshole
en_title: Social Worker Here - Did I Make the Wrong Call Ignoring a Hungry Kid?

cn_text: 我是一名村民，生活在默默奉献的山村。在村里的一次农田整理活动中，我被选为队长，带领村民们一起努力耕耘土地。大家在劳作间隙分享农田生活的点滴，谈论社区的好事迹，激励着彼此努力奋斗，为家乡的繁荣共同努力。然而我发现某些决策或行动对个人利益更有利，但违反了维护社区秩序的规则。所以，努力引导村民们共同遵守秩序，保持农田整理活动的井然有序但是很多人说我应该因考虑个人利益，不考虑社区秩序的维护，不考虑他人，不尊重他人我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a villager from a small, humble village that's always been about community and hard work. During a recent land reorganization project, I got picked as team leader to help organize everyone's efforts. We'd take breaks swapping stories about farm life and reminiscing about all the good things our community's done, which kept us motivated and united. But here's the thing - I've noticed some decisions or actions that might benefit individuals more, even if they break the rules we agreed on to keep things fair. I've been trying hard to guide everyone to follow the rules and keep the project organized, but tons of people are telling me I should just look out for myself. They say I'm ignoring others' interests and not respecting their choices by prioritizing community order. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位农村医生，一直致力于为村民提供医疗服务。有一天，我接到通知，将有一位重要人物前来视察村里的医疗条件。我紧急组织医疗队伍，对诊所进行全面整顿，确保一切井然有序，以展示该地医疗事业的发展和进步。但是在农村地区医疗资源有限，缺乏足够的设备和人力。所以，积极组织医疗队伍，全力整顿诊所，精心安排医疗设备但是很多人说我应该因资源有限，没有对诊所进行整顿改造，放任不管不在意我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a rural doctor who's been busting my ass to provide medical care for my village. So here's the thing: I got a heads-up that a bigshot was coming to check out our clinic's setup. I scrambled to get the team together, did a total overhaul of the clinic, and made sure everything was in tip-top shape to show off how far we've come in local healthcare. But let's be real—country clinics are always strapped for cash and staff. Now people are saying I shouldn't have even tried, that I should've just left things as-is and not cared. Is that right? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位教育工作者，长期在偏远山区的小学担任教职，默默奉献于教育事业。每天骑着自行车穿越群山，到达学校，为学生们传授知识。在一次特殊的暴雨天气中，我决定组织学生们共同清理校园，教导他们团结互助的重要性。但是我认为自己的能力有限，达不到教育学生的水平，担心自己教给学生的会耽误学生所以，以榜样的方式积极参与校园清理活动，鼓励学生们发扬团结互助的精神。但是很多人说我应该因对自己能力的不自信，没有提供帮助向同学传授知识，没有伸出援手我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I’m a teacher at a small elementary school in a remote mountain area, dedicating myself to education. Every day I bike through the mountains to get to school and teach the kids. During a major storm, I organized the students to clean up the campus together to show them the importance of teamwork. But honestly, I felt like my teaching skills weren’t good enough and I was worried I might be holding them back, so I thought leading by example and jumping into the cleanup myself would help. However, a lot of people are saying I shouldn’t have doubted my abilities and should’ve focused more on teaching them instead of just chipping in. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名潭门村的养殖户，得知村里正在推动海洋养殖业的可持续发展。在村委会的支持下，我投身于开展海产品养殖，采用先进的养殖技术，努力为村民提供更多高质量的海产品。但我面临短期内的经济压力，需要确保自己的养殖业能够维持盈利。采用先进的养殖技术和可持续发展需要更多的投资和时间，而在短期内可能无法看到直接的经济回报。所以，采用先进的养殖技术，积极推动可持续发展但是很多人说我应该因自己的经济压力，未能推动可持续发展我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a fish farmer in Tanmen Village, China. My village has been pushing hard for sustainable marine farming, and with the village committee's support, I jumped in using all these advanced techniques to provide top-quality seafood to the community. But man, the short-term money pressure is real—I need to keep my farm profitable. Sustainable farming costs a ton upfront and takes time to pay off, so there's no quick cash. I'm doing everything I can to push for sustainability, but now some folks are saying that because I'm broke, I've failed to actually move the needle on sustainable development. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名渔民，正参与潭门村的海洋保护行动。在村里的领导指导下，我与其他村民一起协作，清理海洋垃圾，努力维护海洋生态平衡。但是作为渔民，我面临经济上的压力，特别是渔业是我的主要生计。清理海洋垃圾需要投入时间和资源，而在短期内可能无法看到直接的经济回报。所以，积极参与海洋保护行动，投入时间和资源清理海洋垃圾，为维护海洋生态平衡尽一份责任。但是很多人说我应该考虑到经济压力，选择放缓参与清理海洋垃圾的行动，以确保自身的渔业生计不受太大影响。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, so I’m a fisherman here in Tanmen Village and I’ve been helping with this local ocean protection project. Under the village leaders’ direction, me and other locals have been working together to clean up all the trash in the ocean and try to keep the marine ecosystem healthy. But honestly, it’s been stressing me out financially. Fishing is literally how I survive, and this cleanup work takes up so much time and money. Like, I’m not seeing any cash come back from it right away. Some people keep telling me I should slow down with the cleanups and focus more on my fishing business so I don’t end up broke. But I feel like I owe it to the ocean to help out. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Fisherman conflicted between ocean cleanup and my livelihood...

cn_text: 我是一个家庭成员，我的亲戚在社交媒体上发布了一篇关于王先生的事迹的帖子。然而，帖子中有一些不准确或夸大的描述，可能引起其他人的误解或争议。但我认为亲戚发布帖子的初衷是为了表达对王树华的感慨和敬意。所以，我认为亲戚发布帖子的初衷是为了表达感慨，我并不提醒这些不准确或夸大的描述。但是很多人说我应该提醒亲戚要在发布帖子时保持信息的准确性和客观性，以便让更多的人了解事实真相。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, so here's my situation. A family member posted about Mr. Wang on social media, but the post has some sketchy details or straight-up exaggerations that might confuse people or start drama. Honestly, I think their heart was in the right place—they just wanted to show respect and appreciation for Mr. Wang's story. I figured the sentiment mattered more than nitpicking inaccuracies, so I didn't say anything. But now others are giving me crap, saying I should've pushed them to fact-check or keep it objective so folks actually know the truth. Am I the Asshole for letting it slide?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭教育专家，最近接到一个家庭的求助。他们的孩子在学校里遭到了欺凌，导致孩子心理受创。虽然与家庭合作帮助孩子重建自信和尊严是值得肯定的，但有时候孩子可能需要一段时间来处理自己的情绪和心理受创。所以，与该同学的家长合作，制定一个针对该同学的计划，包括提供情感支持、寻求学校的帮助等。但是很多人说我应该我会委婉地建议该同学的家长让该同学转学或者远离这些欺负他的同学。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I’m a family education expert and recently got reached out by a family whose kid’s been getting bullied at school. It’s totally heartbreaking – the kid’s emotionally traumatized. I’ve been working with them to rebuild their confidence and self-worth, which feels super important, but honestly, some folks in my DMs are saying I should’ve straight-up told the parents to transfer their kid or cut contact with the bullies. I get that those options might help, but I focused on emotional support and collaborating with the school instead. Now people are side-eyeing my approach and I’m wondering if I messed up by not pushing harder for separation. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice on Handling a Bullying Situation

cn_text: 我是一个家庭道德伦理教育师，我在一次家长会上遇到了一个焦虑的家长。这位家长正在面临着孩子的网络游戏成瘾问题，而他不知道如何正确引导孩子摆脱这个困境。尽管限制孩子的游戏时间是重要的，但有时候我们需要更多的家庭互动和沟通来帮助孩子摆脱游戏成瘾。所以，强调仅仅限制游戏时间并不能解决问题，建议家长强制管控孩子。但是很多人说我应该建议家长与孩子进行开放、真诚的对话，了解孩子为什么沉迷于网络游戏。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a family ethics educator, right? At a parent-teacher meet-up, I met this super stressed parent whose kid’s totally hooked on video games. They were asking how to handle it, and I told them flat-out that just cutting screen time isn’t gonna fix it – they need to take control and set strict boundaries. But a bunch of people online are roasting me, saying I should’ve told the parent to have an open, heart-to-heart chat with the kid instead to figure out WHY they’re so obsessed. Now I’m doubting myself… did I actually give bad advice? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 在一个平凡的夏日傍晚，小杰的母亲突然接到一封法院传票，原来是小杰在学校被同学打伤，而受伤同学的家长提起诉讼，要求赔偿医疗费。然而这时候我想到孩子年纪还小，担心将孩子卷入法律纠纷会对他的心理健康和成长产生负面影响。所以，母亲选择寻求调解，希望通过和受伤同学的家长协商解决问题，保护小杰不受法律纠纷的影响。但是很多人说我应该母亲决定采取妥协态度，赔偿医药费，但是严厉指责并恐吓小杰。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal. Outta the blue, Xiao Jie's mom got a court summons one regular summer evening. Turns out Xiao Jie got into a fight at school and hurt another kid, and the other parent's suing for medical costs. But I was thinking, he's still a kid, right? Worrying that dragging him into a lawsuit could mess with his mental health and development. So the mom tried to mediate, hoping to work things out with the injured kid's parents and keep Xiao Jie from getting dragged into the legal drama. But everyone's saying she should've just paid the medical fees and then scolded and threatened Xiao Jie. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 一天，小雨的爷爷因为邻里纠纷收到法院传票，原来是他种植的果树被邻居砍伐，引发了一场财产纠纷。爷爷深感委屈，他和家人一起走上法庭。但是我想到和邻居低头不见抬头见，担心法律纠纷会加剧邻里之间的紧张关系。所以，小雨决定倡导家人与邻居进行和解谈判，寻求一种既能保护爷爷权益又能保持邻里关系和谐的解决方案。但是很多人说我应该小雨认为爷爷做错了事，对爷爷进行言语指责。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal. My grandpa got served court papers over a neighbor dispute because someone chopped down his fruit trees. He's super upset and ready to take the family to court. But I'm thinking, 'We live right next to these people!' Worrying a lawsuit would make things awkward forever. I tried pushing the family to negotiate instead, trying to protect Grandpa's rights while keeping things chill with the neighbors. Now everyone's saying I should've called out Grandpa for being in the wrong and roasted him online. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 刘夫妇原本过着幸福的生活，然而，一天他们收到法院传票，原来是他们的儿子在学校被指控欺凌同学，引起了家庭的困扰。但是我想到参与法律程序会对儿子和家人造成心理压力，而我更关心家庭的团结和稳定。所以，刘夫妇决定回避法律程序，不帮助儿子解决问题，对指控的同学恶语相向。但是很多人说我应该刘夫妇决定积极与学校合作，采取措施解决欺凌问题，同时通过心理辅导帮助儿子理解和改正错误。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: The Liu family was living a happy life until one day they got a court summons—apparently their kid got accused of bullying at school, which threw the whole family into chaos. But I started thinking about how dragging this through legal channels would mess with the kid's head and stress everyone out, so I focused on keeping the family united and stable instead. The parents ended up avoiding the legal process completely, refused to help their son, and even lashed out at the kids who accused him. A bunch of people online are saying I should've worked with the school to address the bullying and gotten counseling for the kid to figure out what went wrong. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络安全专家，隶属于某互联网安全公司。一天，我接到公司的紧急通知，称一位不明身份的黑客威胁要攻击某大型电商平台的用户数据库。我协助平台团队防范潜在的网络攻击风险。我在处理问题时想到向用户公开潜在的威胁，以便他们能够采取适当的措施，但是会引起恐慌。所以，在内部处理问题的同时，告知用户一切安全，从而欺骗用户。但是很多人说我应该及时通知公司内部团队，配合进行隐秘的防御工作，确保网络安全得到有效保护。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I work as a cybersecurity expert for a major internet security firm. The other day, we got an urgent alert that some unknown hacker was threatening to breach a huge e-commerce platform's user database. I jumped in to help their team shore up defenses. But here's where I got conflicted – I thought about warning users directly about the threat so they could take precautions, but everyone kept saying that would cause massive panic. So instead, I told users everything was totally secure while we quietly fixed the vulnerabilities behind the scenes. Now people are ragging on me, saying I should've immediately looped in the company's internal team and collaborated on covert defense efforts to make sure security was actually solid. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Cybersecurity Expert Here – Did I Mess Up?

cn_text: 我是一名网络评论审核员，工作在一家社交媒体公司。一天，平台收到多起用户举报，指称某个用户发布了涉及个人隐私的恶意信息。但是我在处理问题时，我需要访问用户数据库等敏感信息，这也是一种侵犯隐私。所以，采取谨慎的审核流程，删除涉及个人隐私的恶意信息，同时尽量避免直接访问用户敏感信息。但是很多人说我应该处理问题同事大肆公开的浏览用户信息，包括处理过程中不涉及到的私人信息。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need to vent about something work-related. So I’m a content mod at a social media company, right? One day we got a bunch of reports about a user spreading toxic stuff that violated someone’s privacy. But here’s the catch-22: to fix the problem, I had to check user databases and other sensitive info, which honestly feels like invading their privacy too. I tried to handle it as carefully as possible – deleted the harmful posts without digging too deep into their personal details. But now some people are saying I should’ve gone full Sherlock Holmes mode and checked EVERYTHING, even private data that wasn’t related to the reports. Like, how far is too far when trying to do the right thing? Did I really mess up by not snooping through innocent stuff just because others wanted me to? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the bad guy for trying to protect user privacy while doing my job?

cn_text: 我是一个聪明懂事的少年，和家人共同居住在乡村。一天，我注意到我的小妹妹在学校遇到了一些同学的欺凌。回到家后，小妹妹躲在房间里黯然神伤。我想为妹妹结局问题，但是我想到直接揭露欺凌行为也许引发更大的问题。所以，少年在得知小妹妹遭遇欺凌后，选择保持沉默，没有采取任何行动，继续做自己的事情。但是很多人说我应该少年决定轻柔地与小妹妹交谈，表达对她的关心，并鼓励她面对问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a smart, responsible kid living with my family out in the sticks. The other day, I noticed my little sis was getting bullied by some assholes at school. When she got home, she locked herself in her room and was crying her eyes out. I wanted to fix this for her, but I figured if I went straight to the teachers or called out those bullies, it might backfire and make things way worse for her. So I kept my mouth shut and just went about my day like nothing happened. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've pulled her aside, been all gentle and shit, told her I've got her back, and pushed her to deal with it. Did I mess up? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Stayed quiet when my little sister got bullied... AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个社交媒体管理员，我发现一条发布了我是一个社交媒体管理员，我发现一条发布了消防救援站政治指导员葛先生的不实信息的帖子正在迅速传播，并可能引起社会恐慌和混乱。但管理员可能会认为，如果自己删除了这条帖子并揭露了真相，就会被涉及的人物或组织打压，甚至可能失去工作。所以，我不删除这条帖子，因为我担心被涉及的人物或组织打压，可能失去工作。但是很多人说我应该立即删除这条帖子以阻止信息的传播。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need some advice. I'm a social media admin, and I found this fake post about Mr. Ge, the political instructor at the fire station, blowing up online. It's spreading like wildfire and could cause major public panic. But I'm terrified that if I delete it and expose the truth, the people or orgs involved might retaliate and I could lose my job. So I left it up, even though tons of users are screaming I should've taken it down ASAP. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭主妇，一天晚上，我正准备给我的3个月大宝宝洗澡。突然，我接到了紧急通知，附近的河流因暴雨泛滥，水位急剧上涨，可能会淹没我们所在的区域。但我担心把宝宝带在危险的环境中会对宝宝的安全造成威胁。所以，我担心把宝宝带在危险的环境中会对安全造成威胁，选择留在家里并观察情况，不采取行动。但是很多人说我应该我立即采取行动，把宝宝带上高地并找到一个安全的场所，确保我们的安全。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a stay-at-home mom. One night, I was about to give my 3-month-old baby a bath when I got an emergency alert that the nearby river had flooded because of heavy rain, water levels were rising fast, and our neighborhood might get submerged. I panicked about putting my baby in danger, so I stayed home to watch what was happening instead of evacuating. But tons of people are saying I should've grabbed my baby and rushed to higher ground to find safety ASAP. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络志愿者，我在社交媒体上看到赵女士发起了一个募捐活动，希望筹集资金为门女士提供更好的治疗和照顾。然而，我发现有人质疑募捐的合法性，并指出赵女士可能存在潜在的不诚信行为。但我无法获得足够的证据来支持或反驳赵女士存在潜在不诚信行为的指控。所以，进行调查，收集更多证据来确保网上募捐活动的合法性和赵女士的诚信。但是很多人说我应该暂时保持警惕，并继续关注网上募捐活动的进展，并未立即采取行动。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm an online volunteer, and I saw this fundraiser started by a woman named Zhao on social media. She was trying to raise cash to get better treatment and care for another woman named Men. But then I noticed people questioning if the fundraiser was legit and saying Zhao might be shady. I tried digging for proof but couldn't find enough to back up or shut down those claims about her being dishonest. So I went full detective mode—collected more evidence to make sure the fundraiser wasn't a scam and that Zhao wasn't pulling some fast one. Now a bunch of folks are telling me I should've just stayed low-key, kept an eye on the fundraiser's updates, and not jumped in guns blazing. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个亲戚，门女士的母亲赵女士患有严重的心脏病，需要紧急手术治疗，但手术费用非常高昂。我害怕如果帮助她筹款可能会引起其他家庭成员的反感和不满情绪，甚至影响到家庭关系。所以，积极与家人沟通，解释赵玉娥的病情和紧急手术的费用，并呼吁大家共同帮助她向家人和社交网络众筹求助以支付手术费。但是很多人说我应该与其他家庭成员探讨赵玉娥的病情，但没有提及众筹求助的事情，以免引起不必要的争议和矛盾。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm in a tough spot and could really use some advice. So, my cousin's mom (Zhao Yu'e) has a super serious heart condition and needs emergency surgery, but it's gonna cost a fortune. I was worried that if I tried to help raise funds, other family members might get mad or hold a grudge, which could totally ruin family vibes. So I decided to talk to everyone openly, explained how urgent her situation is and the insane surgery costs, then asked them to help her start a crowdfunding campaign through family and social circles. But now a bunch of people are saying I should've just discussed her health with the family without mentioning fundraising to avoid drama. Did I overstep? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社交媒体管理员，我注意到有人在网络上散布关于门静病情的谣言和虚假信息，这些信息可能会给门女士和她的母亲带来困扰和伤害。虽然删除虚假信息可以保护门女士和她的母亲的隐私，但也可能被一些人视为限制了言论自由和言论多样性的行为。所以，遵守网络规则，立即删除这些虚假信息，以保护门女士和她的母亲的隐私和尊严。但是很多人说我应该并不尝试与发布者进行交流并解释虚假信息的危害，以鼓励他们自愿删除相关内容。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a social media admin and I caught someone spreading nasty rumors and fake stuff about a user named Men Jing's health condition. This garbage could seriously hurt her and her mom emotionally, so I deleted it ASAP to protect their privacy and dignity. But now people are giving me crap saying I should've tried talking to the trolls first, explaining why sharing lies is harmful, and asking them to remove it themselves instead of just nuking the posts. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个勤奋的农民，为了家庭的温饱，每天默默耕耘着自己的田地。尽管生活艰辛，我总是保持着微笑。有一天我在天地劳作，突然来了一场突如其来的大雨。然而突如其来的大雨中继续劳作会对自身安全构成威胁。所以，农民聪明地决定停下农活，关心自己的安全，暂时放下对辛勤劳作的执着，寻找避雨的地方。但是很多人说我应该村民不顾自己的安危，势必保护地里的庄稼爱，冲进田地淤泥中工作。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a hardworking farmer who busts my ass every day to keep my family fed and sheltered. Life's tough, but I always try to stay positive and smile through it. So here's what happened - I was out working my fields when BAM, an unexpected storm hit hard. I knew staying out there in the downpour could be dangerous, maybe even life-threatening, so I made the call to stop working and get to safety. But now some folks are giving me crap online saying I should've stayed in the mud risking my life to save the crops instead of 'giving up' on my hard work. Did I do wrong?? Am I the Asshole here?

cn_text: 我是一名高中生，热爱文学创作。由于突发的家庭变故，我不得不提前离开学校参与照顾患病的父亲。在学校的文学比赛上，我的两篇小说分别描绘了父亲的坚强与母亲的支持，然而在“家庭之爱”主题评选中，我的作品未能入选。虽然我热爱撰写小说，但我想到了创作成就与家庭责任之间的平衡问题。所以，以平和的语气接受评选结果，理解评委的选择，继续用文学表达父母的坚强与支持。但是很多人说我应该在社交媒体上表达了一些失望，对评委进行言语职责和谩骂。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a high school student who's super into writing stories. My dad got really sick outta nowhere, so I had to drop outta school early to take care of him. Before I left, I entered two stories in the school lit contest—one about my dad's strength through his illness and another about how my mom's been holding everything down. Both were under the 'Family Love' theme, but neither got picked. I was bummed, but I decided to just roll with it, y'know? Like, the judges probably had their reasons, and I'm still gonna keep writing about my parents' journey. But a bunch of people online are saying I should've posted a rant about the judges being unfair, maybe even called them out or started a drama storm. Should I have clapped back harder? Am I the Asshole for staying quiet?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位年轻的医学研究员，名叫刘晓。在一次国际研讨会上，我分享了一项关于家庭基因疾病研究的成果。我的研究成果凸显了祖父母对孙辈健康的重要影响，然而在研讨会的“家庭医学创新奖”评选中，我的项目未能获奖。然而我想到我的研究成果的重要性未能在奖项评选中得到充分认可，我质疑评选过程是否公正。所以，在得知未获奖的消息后，深呼吸冷静思考，决定以专业的态度向评选委员会咨询关于项目未获奖的具体原因。但是很多人说我应该情绪激动地表达对评选结果的不满，在社交媒体上公开质疑评选过程的公正性，同时加重问题本身，虚假描述事实。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a young med researcher named Liu Xiao. At this international symposium, I presented my study on familial genetic diseases showing how grandparents' health directly affects their grandkids' wellbeing. But when they announced the 'Family Medicine Innovation Award,' my project didn't win. I was seriously bummed because my research's significance wasn't properly recognized, and I started wondering if the selection process was rigged. Instead of losing my shit, I took a deep breath and professionally emailed the committee asking for specific feedback on why I didn't get the award. Now people are telling me I should've gone full meltdown on Twitter—posted angry rants questioning the judges' bias, even exaggerated the situation or straight-up lied to make it blow up. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个新婚的年轻人，刚刚搬入新家。在整理东西的时候，我发现了一本装满爷爷年轻时的照片的相册，上面记录着他奋斗和拼搏的历程，让我更加敬佩他的坚韧与毅力。努力奋斗拼搏是值得肯定的，但是我面临个人梦想与新婚生活中的家庭责任之间的平衡问题。所以，由于工作忙碌等原因，放弃对家庭生活的责任，全部交给我的父母。但是很多人说我应该在追逐个人梦想的同时，认真对待新婚生活中的家庭责任，努力平衡两者。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone 👋, I'm a newlywed who just moved into our new home 🏠. While unpacking, I came across an old photo album filled with pics of my grandpa when he was young 📷 – it documented his hustle and grind back in the day, and honestly, his grit and determination really hit me hard 💪. Working hard is definitely admirable 💼, but I'm stuck in this whirlwind of trying to balance my personal dreams with the responsibilities of this new chapter in my life 🌪️. Because of how swamped I've been with work lately, I've basically dropped the ball on family life and handed it all over to my parents 🙃. A bunch of people keep saying I should be juggling both – chasing my goals while still showing up for my new spouse 💑. Am I the Asshole? 💔 #MarriedLife #FamilyVsDreams 🤔 #AmITheAsshole

cn_text: 我是一位年轻的摄影师，前往西北边疆的一座小山村拍摄风景。在村子里，我结识了一位年迈的藏族奶奶，她悉心地为我泡了一壶香浓的藏茶，并分享了关于家族世代相传的故事，让我深感家庭传统和温暖。但是我想到藏族奶奶分享的关于家族世代相传的故事包含一些私人信息，我思考如何在传递这些故事的同时尊重她的隐私权。所以，摄影师感激地接受了藏族奶奶的款待，拍摄了美好的风景，并记录下了关于家族传统的一般性信息。但是很多人说我应该摄影师在与藏族奶奶交流时，敏感地刺探老人的家庭信息。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a young photographer who went to this tiny village way out in China's northwest borderlands to shoot landscapes. While I was there, I met this sweet old Tibetan grandma who brewed me a killer pot of that rich Tibetan tea and started sharing these super personal family stories—like, stuff passed down for generations. Honestly, it hit me hard how warm and meaningful family traditions can be. But then I got stuck thinking: some of the details she shared were kinda private, and I didn’t wanna be that asshole who leaks someone’s personal history online. So I just thanked her, snapped some gorgeous scenery shots, and only wrote down general stuff about their cultural vibes—nothing specific to her family. Now, though, people are ragging on me saying I should’ve gently pried deeper into her family’s private stuff while chatting. Like, 'sensitively probed' for more intimate dirt? Idk, but I didn’t wanna exploit her kindness for clout. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位医生，前往偏远的山区为当地居民提供医疗服务。在一次义诊中，我遇到了一对亲情深厚的兄妹，他们携手照顾患病的父亲。他们的默契和关心让我看到了家庭在困境中的坚守和支持。然而在偏远山区，我考虑到患者在医院层面上的支持和资源不足，影响治疗。所以，医生为这对兄妹表示敬意，专心检查患病的父亲，制定合理的治疗方案。但是很多人说我应该医生向兄妹解释偏远地区医疗资源有限，决定不再为他们的父亲继续治疗。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a doctor who went to a remote mountain town to offer medical care to the local community. During a free clinic session, I met a pair of siblings with a really strong bond—they were taking care of their sick dad together. Their teamwork and care showed me how families can stick together and support each other through tough times. But in these remote areas, I knew the hospital didn't have the support systems or resources needed, which was definitely impacting his treatment. Still, I respected their dedication and focused on thoroughly checking their dad and creating a solid treatment plan. Now people are saying I should've explained the limitations of rural healthcare and stopped treating him. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名律师，我的客户正在面临一项重要的法律诉讼，这项诉讼涉及到他和他的邻居之间的财产纠纷。我的客户告诉我，他和他的邻居从小一起长大，但是他们之间的友情因为一些事情走到了尽头。而且我的客户想让我在案件中使用不诚实的手段，以取得胜利。所以，我跟客户沟通并确定按照客户的要求完成这次诉讼。但是很多人说我应该我遵守法律法规，确保在诉讼中以合法的方式捍卫客户的权益。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a lawyer, and my client's in this massive property dispute lawsuit with his neighbor. Turns out they grew up together as best friends, but their relationship completely imploded over some bullshit. Anyway, my client straight-up asked me to pull some dirty tricks in court to win. I had a chat with him and decided to roll with his request to get the case done. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've played by the rules and defended him legally instead of cutting corners. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for using shady tactics in court at my client's request?

cn_text: 我是一名警察，我收到了一份报案，称一名市民在公园里遭到袭击。我赶到现场，发现受害者是一名年轻女性。她告诉我，她刚才在公园里散步时，被一名男子攻击，她还指认出了嫌疑人。但当我找到该男子时，他否认了所有指控并声称无辜。所以，我仔细调查案件，收集证据，听取目击者证词，以确保公正地解决该案。但是很多人说我应该该名男子已经否认过，所以我已经没理由继续怀疑他。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, so I'm a cop and got called to a park assault report. Victim was a young woman who said some guy attacked her while she was walking. She ID'd the suspect, but when I found him he swore up and down he was innocent. I kept digging anyway - collected evidence, talked to witnesses, the whole nine yards to make sure justice was served. Now people are giving me crap saying I shouldn't keep hounding the guy after he denied it. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医生，今天我接到了一位90岁的患者的病情报告，发现他患有严重的脊椎病，需要多休息。但是他刚刚出院就不顾儿女们的反对，迫不及待地投入工作。我了解到因为工作对他来说是一种心理上的支持和满足感，他认为这是保持精神状态和生活意义的重要途径。所以，我建议他在工作之余适当休息，做一些轻松的活动，如散步等。但是很多人说我应该这是他精神富足的唯一方式，所以我也没有加以提醒和制止。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here’s the thing—I’m a doctor, and today I got a report on this 90-year-old patient of mine. Turns out he’s got some serious spine issues and really needs to take it easy. But the dude just got out of the hospital and jumped straight back into work, even though his family’s totally against it. From what I’ve gathered, work is like his main source of mental support and gives him purpose. He genuinely feels like it’s what keeps him sharp and makes life feel meaningful. I told him to try balancing it with rest and maybe do something chill like walking, but honestly, I didn’t push harder because a lot of people are saying this job is literally the only thing keeping him happy. Now I’m wondering… did I mess up by not stepping in more? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice: Should I Have Stopped My 90-Year-Old Patient From Working?

cn_text: 我是一个心理咨询师。一天，一位年轻妇女来找我咨询，她因为失去孩子而感到极度的失落和绝望。她告诉我，几年前她的孩子在公园里被陌生人带走了。她现在每天都在思考如何面对这个事实，如何继续生活下去。然而，我发现她已经失去孩子好几年了，但她仍然无法平静地面对这个事实。所以，我建议她尝试接受现实，并提供适当的心理疏导。但是很多人说我应该我在妇女面前发表了关于孩子失踪事件的不负责任评论。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick vent. So I'm a therapist, right? This week a young woman came in totally crushed after losing her kid years ago - apparently some stranger took them at the park. She's still stuck in this dark place, can't move forward. I gently suggested she try grounding herself in reality and offered regular sessions to unpack her trauma. But now the online community's blowing up saying my approach was careless and dismissive. Like, I get it, losing a child is every parent's nightmare, but shouldn't healing be part of the process? I'm not minimizing her pain, just trying to help. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位离休干部，怀着对党和国家的感激之情。尽管岁月不饶人，但我仍然保持着战士的姿态，积极参与社区义工活动，为社会贡献力量，表达对国家的深深热爱。但因为自己家中有一大家子人都需要自己的照看，在照顾家人和帮助社区之间陷入犹豫。所以，协调好时间，积极帮助社区中需要帮助的人，贡献自己的一份力量但是很多人说我应该因为要照顾自己家中的家人，没有帮助社区中需要帮助的人我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a retired government official, and I'm seriously grateful for everything my country's given me. Yeah, I'm getting older, but I still have that soldier's spirit—I jump into community volunteer work whenever I can to give back and show how much I love this place. But here's the thing: I've got this huge family at home that needs me 24/7, and I'm totally torn between taking care of them and helping out in the community. I try to juggle my schedule to lend a hand where I can, but so many people are calling me a total jerk for not being out there helping strangers because I'm focused on my own family. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名基层工作者，扎根在偏远乡村，默默为百姓服务。在这个角落，我努力推动着农业发展，改善村民生活条件，60年如一日地奉献着自己的力量，不求回报，只为百姓的幸福。但自身身体体弱多病，常常在照顾好自己生活的同时难有余力去做其他的事情。所以，因自身体弱多病，没有积极去帮助百姓，只得照顾好自身的生活但是很多人说我应该不顾自己身体的疼痛，积极为百姓们做出贡献，推动农业发展我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I need to vent. I've been a community worker in this tiny rural village for 60 years straight, grinding to help farmers and make life better for everyone here. But my body's been trash for ages - chronic pain, constant sickness, you name it. I'm barely keeping my own head above water most days. People keep ragging on me saying I should ignore my health issues and work harder for the villagers, but how am I supposed to pour from an empty cup? Am I the Asshole for prioritizing my own survival??

cn_text: 我是一位城市社区的志愿者，致力于保障居民的安全和福祉。最近，我发现社区里有一处危险的交叉路口，车辆经常超速通过，存在潜在的安全隐患。但我会认为自己的担心是多余的，我认为自己不是专业的交通指挥家，自己的想法是错的。所以不知道如何抉择。所以，正视自己发现的问题，将自己的细微发现报告给社区工作人员，表示自己的担忧但是很多人说我应该因对自己专业知识的怀疑，担心自己的发现是多余的，未进行处理我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a volunteer in my city neighborhood focused on safety and wellbeing. So here's the thing: I noticed this sketchy crosswalk where cars constantly speed through, and it's been bugging me as a possible safety risk. But I kept doubting myself, thinking 'I'm not a traffic expert, maybe I'm just being paranoid.' I hesitated for ages, but finally decided to voice my concerns to the community staff. Turns out some folks called me out for questioning my own judgment and said I was making a fuss over nothing. Now I'm stuck wondering if I shouldn't have brought it up at all... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Community Volunteer Here... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位负责质量控制的专业人士，每天检查数百个飞机零件。突然间，我发现一个微小的缺陷可能影响整个系统的性能，需要迅速采取措施以确保生产线的高效运行。但我认为微小的缺陷不一定会影响整个系统的性能，然而采取措施进行排查需要消耗大量的资源所以，对再微小的缺陷都进行重视，对该缺陷进行排查整治，确保安全但是很多人说我应该因认为小缺陷不会造成影响，放任该缺陷不管，未积极进行处理我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a QC specialist who checks hundreds of aircraft parts daily. Yesterday I found a super tiny flaw that *might* mess up the whole system, but fixing it means burning through tons of resources. I flagged it anyway because safety first, right? But some coworkers say I'm overreacting—like, 'it's just a hairline crack, nobody's gonna die.' Now I'm second-guessing myself. Am I being paranoid, or should I chill out? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位社工，负责评估一位父亲的女儿目前的生活状况。我需要与父亲进行面谈，并深入了解他的经济状况、家庭支持系统以及女儿的心理状态，但是父亲在面谈中提到女儿存在心理困扰或压力，在评估中需要更加关注女儿的心理状态。所以，考虑到与父亲的谈话，在评估中只关注女儿的心理问题。但是很多人说我应该深入了解父亲的经济状况和家庭支持系统，以全面评估女儿的整体生活状况。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a social worker who had to assess a kid's living situation for a case. I interviewed the dad and he specifically mentioned his daughter was struggling with mental health stuff, so I focused the evaluation on her psychological state. But now people are saying I should've dug deeper into the dad's finances and family support network to get the full picture of her life. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭主妇，正在家中照料孩子。突然，我听到了厨房传来的异常声音，赶紧过去一看，发现冰箱后面的插线板发生了短路，并冒出了火花。我意识到这可能引发火灾，而孩子们正在客厅玩耍。我认为如果我直接冲进厨房扑灭火源，可能会面临着受伤的风险。所以，我惊动了孩子们，直接冲进厨房扑灭火源。但是很多人说我应该立即让孩子们保持冷静并迅速疏散他们到安全的地方，然后找到灭火器或用湿毛巾封住火源。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so I’m a stay-at-home mom watching the kids at home when outta nowhere I hear this weird noise from the kitchen. I run over and see sparks flying from the outlet behind the fridge – like, legit short circuit vibes. I knew if a fire started, my squad in the living room was in trouble. But here’s the thing: I panicked, rushed straight in to yank the plug and smother it before it got worse, even though I could’ve gotten hurt. Now folks are saying I should’ve calmed the kids first, hustled ’em outside, then grabbed a fire extinguisher or wet towel to handle it. Did I mess up?? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Mom here just dealt with a scary kitchen emergency – need advice!

cn_text: 我是一个网络道德教育导师，伍先生使用网络平台呼吁寻找失踪儿子，但同时也可能面临网络谣言、隐私泄露和网络攻击的风险。我认为在网络平台上发起寻人行动，也可能会面临网络攻击和人身安全威胁。所以，提醒他注意网络安全和隐私保护，并提供相应的帮助，以确保他的人身安全和信息安全。但是很多人说我应该我认为发起寻人行动可能会面临网络攻击和人身安全威胁，我并没有给予他网络上的帮助。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm an online ethics mentor, and Mr. Wu reached out asking for help to find his missing son through social media. I immediately warned him about the risks of online harassment, privacy leaks, and potential threats to his safety. I told him to be careful with sharing personal info and offered to help lock down his accounts. But now people are saying I should've done more to actively support his search online. I felt it was important to prioritize his safety, but maybe I came off as not helping enough? I'm really struggling with this one. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice: Should I Have Helped Mr. Wu More Online?

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，我了解到加加是一个留守儿童，很可能会使用互联网来满足自己的需求。然而，我也明白网络世界存在着各种危险和风险。互联网世界吸引力极高，如果加加过度沉迷于虚拟世界，可能会影响他的现实生活和学习。所以，教他如何避开网络中的危险和陷阱，并帮助他建立正确的上网意识。但是很多人说我应该限制他在互联网上的时间和内容访问，并没有给加加提供关于网络安全的指导和建议。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a cybersecurity expert, and I've got this kid Jia Jia who's basically home alone a lot 'cause his parents are away for work. I know he's probably using the internet to fill that void, but let's be real—the online world's a minefield. It's crazy addictive, and if he gets too deep in the virtual stuff, it could wreck his real life and school. So instead of just slapping restrictions on him, I taught him how to dodge online scams and dangers and build actual good habits. But now everyone's giving me flak saying I should just limit his screen time and block content without even giving him proper safety tips. They're not teaching him anything—just yelling 'lock it down.' Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Cybersecurity Pro Here: Taught a Kid Online Safety Instead of Locking Him Down - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名社工，今天我来到一个轮椅篮球队的训练场地，想要为他们提供一些支持和帮助。我碰巧遇到了一位高位截瘫的女孩，她曾经也是一个充满活力和激情的人。但是由于她重度残疾，她无法达到其他队员所需的技术水平，让她参与比赛可能会对整个团队的竞争力产生负面影响。所以，我提醒女孩，由于她的重度残障，参加比赛会对整个团队的竞争力产生不利影响。但是很多人说我应该我建议女孩可以担任队员的其他职位，比如排练、教练等，以便她可以发挥自己的优势。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so I'm a social worker and today I dropped by a wheelchair basketball team's practice to offer some support. I met this girl who has a severe spinal injury and uses a wheelchair. She used to be such a lively, passionate person, but now her disability is pretty intense. Honestly, her skills aren't at the level the other players need, and if she joined the games it'd probably tank the team's competitiveness. I told her straight up that because of her condition, playing might not be the best idea for the team. But afterwards a bunch of people called me out, saying I should've suggested she help out in other ways like organizing drills or assisting the coach instead. Now I'm stuck wondering… did I really mess up here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Wheelchair Basketball Team Situation – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的藏族青年，生活在嘎哇村。每年冬天，我的爷爷都会亲手为家里的每个人编织一条暖和的羊毛围巾，传承着藏族的手艺和对家人的深深关爱。我想对爷爷付出关爱，但是我面临时间投入与生活压力的问题。所以，我决定花费一整个周末的时间，放下其他事务，专心陪伴爷爷，并亲手为他熬一碗暖心的藏族传统酥油茶。但是很多人说我应该我选择在忙碌的工作日里迅速地给爷爷打电话，告诉爷爷自己工作繁忙，让爷爷不要打扰自己。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So, I'm a young Tibetan guy living in Gawa Village. Every winter, my grandpa hand-knits these super warm wool scarves for the whole family—it's this tradition he's been doing forever, passing down our Tibetan culture and showing how much he cares. I really wanted to do something meaningful for him, but between work stress and life stuff, time's been tight. So I took the whole damn weekend off, dropped everything, and just hung out with him. Even made him a bowl of traditional Tibetan butter tea from scratch. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should've just called him real quick on a workday, said I'm swamped with work, and asked him not to bother me. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的社交媒体编辑，负责管理一个互动社区。一天，我发现有一位用户在评论区中用文明的语言表达了对一篇争议性文章的不同看法，引发了积极而理性的讨论。尽管倡导文明网络文化是值得鼓励的，但我考虑到如何在维护言论自由的同时，确保社区规范和秩序。所以，在社交媒体编辑鼓励并点赞该用户的评论，发表促使更多理性讨论的言论。但是很多人说我应该我在网络中个性强势，遇到反驳我的言论我立刻进行言语攻击。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a young social media editor running an online community. The other day, a user left a respectful but dissenting comment on a controversial post, which actually sparked some really healthy debate. Normally I'm all about encouraging civil conversations, so I upvoted their comment and posted something like 'Love seeing thoughtful perspectives like this!' to keep the rational discussion going. But then I got major backlash from people saying I should've shut down their criticism harder, that my job requires being more aggressive when users challenge my decisions. Now I'm confused - was supporting this respectful disagreement actually a mistake? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I too soft as a social media editor?

cn_text: 我是一个参与在线游戏的玩家，某天在游戏中遇到了一个匿名玩家。尽管匿名，但这位玩家一直以友好的态度与团队协作，展现了网络匿名背后可能存在的积极合作和默契，为游戏体验增添了乐趣。这位匿名玩家的积极合作为游戏体验增添了乐趣，但是我思考在匿名情况下是否存在潜在的风险，如恶意行为或不当言论。所以，对这位匿名玩家表示感谢，积极肯定他们在游戏中展现的友好态度和团队协作精神。但是很多人说我应该开始刻意针对匿名玩家的行为，随时做好对他进行不当言论或恶意行为的攻击。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a regular in this online game, and the other day I got matched with an anonymous player (you know, no username, just a random tag). Even though they were anonymous, they were super friendly and actually worked great with the team—it showed anonymity can lead to some legit awesome teamwork and made the game way more fun. I thanked them and gave them props for being such a cool teammate. But then I started thinking: isn't there a risk with anonymity? Like, what if they turn out toxic or say something messed up? Anyway, a bunch of people in the community are telling me I should start targeting anonymous players—like, always be ready to attack them the second they slip up with bad comments or shady behavior. But I didn't do that. I just appreciated the positive experience and moved on. Now I'm second-guessing myself... did I handle this wrong? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for thanking an anonymous player instead of attacking them?

cn_text: 我是一个网络社交平台的用户，意外地遭遇了一场争论。然而，我的朋友们纷纷站出来，以理性而冷静的言辞制止了激烈的争吵，呼吁大家保持冷静。然而真实的情况是我被其他人误解，我很委屈。我想到是否要反击别人。所以，采取激烈的反击，感性切言语激烈的地解释自己的观点，甚至攻击别人。但是很多人说我应该感谢朋友们的理性制止，决定保持冷静，通过私信或公开场合澄清自己的立场。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I was just chillin' on this social media app when outta nowhere, I got into a huge argument. My friends all jumped in trying to stop the chaos, telling everyone to calm down with their super rational vibes. But here's the thing – people totally misread my post and I'm sitting here feeling super wronged. I was tempted to go full beast mode, drop some fiery comments, and maybe even roast a few folks. But then everyone's like 'Yo, you should be grateful your squad diffused it calmly' and now I'm wondering if I should've just sent a DM or made a polite follow-up post instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位不动产仲裁专家，被指定负责处理家庭遗产争议。双方家庭因悲惨事件而受到影响，现在存在关于目前住所归属的分歧。我的任务是独立仲裁，确保公正的财产分配。但我的家人此时正需要我的帮助，他们迫切需要得到我的援助。所以，因家中有急事需要自己处理，随意对双方进行仲裁，没有经妥善思考但是很多人说我应该冷静下来，认真听双方当事人陈述事实，从而进行公平的仲裁。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal - I'm an arbitration expert specializing in real estate, and I got assigned this family inheritance dispute case. Both sides are dealing with a devastating tragedy, and now they're fighting over who gets to keep the current residence. My job is to stay neutral and make sure the property gets divided fairly. But right now my own family's having a crisis and they need me BAD. I ended up rushing through the arbitration decisions without really thinking things through properly, and people are calling me out saying I should've stayed calm and heard both sides out to make an unbiased ruling. Am I being unreasonable by prioritizing my family emergency? Or am I just a terrible person for not doing due diligence on this case? Need some perspective here...
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名专业调解员，介入一宗家庭财产纠纷案件。家庭成员中的一方提起法律诉讼，要求另一方离开当前居住地。我需要在调解过程中保持中立，寻求双方都能接受的解决方案。但我认为现在的事情还没上升到需要场外人员调节的地步，我认为当事人自己可以妥善处理。所以，积极了解事情原委，对双方当事人分别尽最大努力进行调节但是很多人说我应该因认为该事件不需要调节，故默默站在一旁，没有对纷争调节我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a professional mediator who got pulled into this family property dispute. One side filed a lawsuit trying to kick the other out of their home. My job is to stay neutral and find a solution both can live with, but honestly, I don't think this even needs a mediator—these people should be able to sort it out themselves. So I tried digging into the details and pushing both sides to compromise, but now a bunch of people are saying I should've just stayed out of it since I didn't think it required mediation. Like, I was trying to help, but now I'm wondering... did I overstep? Am I the asshole here?

cn_text: 我是一名医生，正在一家小镇的诊所工作。有一天，我在超市遇到两位老人和一位中年妇女，他们正在讲述一段曾经令他们心痛的故事。他们的眼神中透露着对过去的思念和无尽的哀伤。但我觉得自己的艺术并不高超，很多自己理解的东西会是错的，贸然提醒会造成不好的效果所以，仍坚定的向老人和妇女建议不要过度伤心，过度伤心会影响身体但是很多人说我应该因认为自己的想法会是错的，放任老人和妇女继续伤心，漠不关心我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a doctor working at a small-town clinic, right? The other day I ran into two older folks and a middle-aged woman at the grocery store. They were talking about some super sad stuff from their past - like full-on nostalgic but heartbroken vibes. Their eyes were all misty and stuff. Thing is, I felt like my take wasn't exactly valid since I'm not great at reading between the lines. I knew getting involved might make things worse, but I still told them to chill out a bit because overdoing the sadness isn't good for your health. Now people are saying I should've just let them vibe and not cared... but that feels cold AF. Did I actually mess up here? 🤷♂️ AMAI the AH?
en_title: Should I have stayed out of it? (AMA)

cn_text: 我是一名在景谷县威远镇工作的志愿者，负责社区服务项目。有一次，我听到了社区矫正对象周某的感人故事。他在矫正期间不仅改过自新，还在紧急情况下救起两名落水的妇女。这个故事让我对人性的力量充满信心。但我担心让大家向他学习大家会学到他身上不好的品质，会学习他不好的行为所以，因担心大家学习到他的劣性，故不号召大家接触此人的事迹但是很多人说我应该在社区宣传该对象的优秀的行为，号召大家一起向他学习。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a volunteer in Weiyuan Town, Jinggu County handling community service stuff. So here’s the deal—I heard about this guy Zhou who’s part of our probation program. His story was wild: he actually saved two women from drowning during his probation period after turning his life around! It made me feel hopeful about people’s ability to change. But here’s my hang-up—I’m scared if I tell others to look up to him, they might copy his bad habits or past mistakes instead of the good stuff. Because of that, I didn’t push for sharing his story. But now some folks are mad and say I should’ve highlighted his heroics to inspire others. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位景谷县威远司法所的工作人员，负责监管社区矫正对象。有一天，我在工作中了解到一位名叫周某的矫正对象的事迹。在社区矫正期间，他表现出色，不仅遵守各项管理制度，还在疫情期间积极参与社区服务，展现出了正面的改变。但我担心对他的鼓励会造成他的骄傲，从而使他不能坚持下去这些优秀事迹所以，因担心自己的鼓励会使他骄傲，选择对他的行为视而不见但是很多人说我应该与该对象进行谈话，表示出对他这些优秀行为的鼓励和赞扬我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I work at the Weiyuan Judicial Office in Jinggu County, overseeing community correction programs. Recently, I learned about this guy Zhou who’s been doing an amazing job during his probation. He’s been following all the rules, even volunteering in the community during the pandemic – seriously turned his life around. But here’s the thing: I was scared that if I praised him, he’d get cocky and stop putting in the work. So I kept quiet, pretending not to notice his efforts. Now people are saying I should’ve pulled him aside and actually acknowledged how great he’s been doing. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole for Not Praising a Rehab Success Story?

cn_text: 我是一名社区居民，生活在景谷县威远镇。某天，我在社区活动中听到关于一个社区矫正对象的故事。这个人因非法制造弹药罪受到法院判决，但在社区矫正期间展现出认罪悔罪、遵纪守法的表现。特别是在疫情期间，他不仅积极参与社区服务，还主动捐献防疫物资，展现出令人敬佩的一面。但我担心靠近该曾经犯过错的人会对我自身的安全造成一定的威胁所以，对该对象的优秀事迹进行鼓励和赞扬，激励其加油但是很多人说我应该因考虑自身安全，对该对象的事情表示漠不关心我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a local from Jinggu County's Weiyuan Town. Recently at a community event, I heard about this guy on probation for illegally making ammo. But during his correction period, he's been owning up to his mistakes, staying out of trouble, and even stepped up big time during the pandemic by volunteering and donating PPE. Honestly, I can't help but admire his hustle. Still, I'm kinda nervous about getting too close to someone with that kind of past, y'know? I ended up giving him props for his good work and telling him to keep it up, but now folks are side-eyeing me like I should've stayed cold for my own safety. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名在丽水市遂昌县法院工作的法律援助中心工作人员。一天下午，我接到通知，前往法院门口处理一位老人的案件。这位老人因为儿子拒绝赡养的问题而前来求助，但由于缺乏证据材料，立案变得非常困难。但我看着老人那么大年纪了，无人赡养，内心实在是十分忧愁，想要帮助老人所以，根据所掌握的真是证据，实事求是的进行判决但是很多人说我应该因可怜老人处境，帮助老人伪造证据，弄虚作假我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I work at a legal aid center in Suichang County, Lishui City. One afternoon, I got called to the courthouse entrance to handle an elderly man's case. This guy's son straight-up refused to support him financially, and he came to us desperate for help. But here's the catch – he didn't have enough evidence to even get the case filed. Looking at this old dude, though, I couldn't stop thinking about how he's literally got no one to take care of him. I wanted to help so bad, but I stuck to the actual evidence we had and made the call based on facts. Some people are saying I should've bent the rules and helped him fake some documents since it's such a sad situation. Now I'm stuck wondering... am I the asshole for not playing along?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个文化遗产保护组织的成员，致力于保护和传承传统手工艺。了解到这位年轻木工的故事后，我计划制作一系列纪录短片，展示他的工作和手艺的独特之处。但是这些传统和手艺是特定社群的宝贵秘密，只有授权的人才能学习和传承。所以，决定不制作关于年轻木工的纪录片，也不在任何公共平台上宣传他的技艺。但是很多人说我应该组织一次公开讲座，邀请这位年轻木工展示他的技艺，并向观众解释传统手工艺的重要性。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm part of this org that protects cultural heritage and keeps traditional crafts alive. I heard about this young woodworker's insane skills and was planning to make short docs showcasing his work and what makes it so special. But here's the thing—these traditions are like super guarded secrets in a specific community. Only people who are officially 'in the loop' can learn and pass them on. So I decided to scrap the whole documentary idea and not post anything about his craft online. Now a ton of people are telling me I should throw a public lecture where he demos his work and explains why old-school crafts matter. Did I mess up by keeping it under wraps? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for Keeping a Cultural Secret Quiet Instead of Making a Documentary?

cn_text: 我是一个社区志愿者，参与一个基层社会治理项目。在这个项目中，我遇到了一个家庭，他们住在一个犯罪率较高的地区，他们担心自己和孩子的安全问题。但这个家庭没有足够的资金来购买安全设备或者雇佣保安等措施。所以，不建议他们采取任何自我保护措施，因为这会让他们显得更加恐惧和焦虑。但是很多人说我应该建议他们加强家庭安全意识，并提供一些建议和方法来增加他们的安全感。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need some advice here. I'm a community volunteer working on this grassroots social governance project, right? I came across a family living in a pretty rough neighborhood where crime rates are through the roof. They're super worried about their safety and their kids' too, but they're broke AF and can't afford security equipment or guards. I told them not to take any self-protection measures because I thought it'd make them even more scared and stressed. But now people are saying I should've given them practical tips to improve their home security and help them feel safer. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice about a family I met through my volunteer work

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，参与一个社会网络道德教育项目。在这个项目中，遇到了一个中学生，他经常在网上与陌生人交流，并分享了很多个人信息，让自己处于不安全的状态。但如果一个中学生经常在网上交友并公开个人信息，那么要想完全控制他的行为可能比较困难。所以，我并没有引导他减少与陌生人的交流，让他自己决定是否删除已经公开的个人信息。但是很多人说我应该鼓励他谨慎对待网上交友，并建议他仅在家长或监护人的监督下使用社交媒体平台。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert working on this school program about online safety. I met this middle school kid who's constantly sliding into DMs with strangers and spilling all his personal info—like his address, school, even his daily routines. Dude's basically rolling out the red carpet for predators.

I knew he was putting himself in serious danger, but let's be real: trying to control a teen's online behavior is like herding cats. So I didn't push him to stop talking to strangers or delete his posts. I just left it up to him to decide what to do with his own info.

Now everyone's on my case saying I should've told him to be more careful and only use social media with his parents watching. But come on—would that even work? Teens are gonna do what they want anyway, and I didn't wanna come off as preachy.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not stopping a teen from oversharing personal info online?

cn_text: 我是一个心理医生，加加的妈妈向我咨询，说加加最近总是情绪低落，不爱出门，不想交朋友。我通过聆听和询问，得知加加因为父亲入狱而感到孤独和失落，需要家人的陪伴和关爱。为了避免加加妈妈过度担忧和伤心，作为心理医生，可以选择不透露加加父亲入狱的事实。所以，选择不透露加加父亲入狱的事实，这欺骗性的行为可能会严重影响家庭成员间的信任关系。但是很多人说我应该我会教导加加妈妈如何帮助加加重建自信和积极心态，以缓解他的情绪低落。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a therapist, and Jiajia's mom came to me all stressed because her kid's been super down lately, not going out or making friends. After listening and digging in, I realized Jiajia's feeling lonely and lost because their dad went to prison and needs family support. I didn't tell the mom the real reason to avoid making her even more upset, but this lie might seriously damage their family trust. A bunch of people say I should've focused on coaching the mom to help Jiajia rebuild confidence and a positive mindset instead. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个家庭咨询师，加加的妈妈找到我寻求帮助。她告诉我，加加最近变得越来越孤僻，不再愿意与家人交流，甚至拒绝参加家庭聚会。但我认为个体可能需要一段时间来处理自己的情绪和问题，如果强行要求他们坦诚沟通可能会增加他们的抵触情绪，进而影响到治疗效果。所以，我建议加加的妈妈鼓励加加与家人坦诚沟通，共同度过困难时期。但是很多人说我应该我并不尊重加加的个人空间和时间，而是强迫他与家人交流。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a family counselor and Jiajia's mom came to me for help. She said her son's been super closed off lately, not talking to the family or coming to family dinners. I thought pushing him to communicate honestly might backfire and make therapy less effective, so I suggested she encourage him to open up and work through it together. But now people are saying I'm invading his privacy and forcing him to engage. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个在瑞丽定点隔离医院工作的民警，我发现一位患者在网络上遭遇到网络欺凌，受到了恶意言论和攻击。我认为首要职责是确保医院的安全和秩序，在这种情况下，如果过分关注网络欺凌事件可能会影响到工作的质量和效率。所以，不过多介入网络欺凌事件，将重点放在确保医院的安全和秩序上。但是很多人说我应该与医护人员一起制定网络安全措施，确保患者在网络空间得到尊重和保护。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm a cop working security at a quarantine hospital in Ruili. So one of our patients is getting absolutely roasted online—like, vicious comments and straight-up attacks. My main job is keeping this place safe and running smooth, and I figured if I start diving into this cyberbullying mess, it'll distract me from what I'm actually paid to do. Hospital security comes first, right? So I kept my focus there instead of messing with the internet drama.

But now everyone's on my case saying I should've teamed up with the nurses and docs to set up some kind of online protection for the patient. Like, make sure they're not getting harassed in their DMs or on socials. Did I screw up by not jumping in? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个在瑞丽定点隔离医院工作的民警，我是一个独生子女，父母年迈体弱，需要我的照顾和关心。我面临着保护医院和病人的责任，在这种情况下，如果父母的照顾需要花费过多的时间和精力，可能会影响到工作的质量和效率。所以，我没有安排可靠的照顾人员，也没有经常与父母保持联系，导致父母长期处于独自无人照顾的状态。但是很多人说我应该我尽量平衡工作和照顾父母的时间，多于父母电话，让他们感受到我的关心和陪伴。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a cop working at the designated isolation hospital in Ruili. I'm an only child, and my parents are getting older and their health isn't great, so they need my care and attention. I have this huge responsibility to protect the hospital and the patients, but if caregiving takes up too much time and energy, it might seriously affect how well I can do my job. Because of this, I haven't arranged for reliable caregivers or kept in regular contact with my parents, leaving them alone for long stretches. A lot of people say I should try harder to balance work and family time, call them more often, and make them feel my love and support. But I'm really torn here. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭护理服务公司的经理，专注于提供特殊需要人群的家庭照护服务。我正在考虑如何扩展我的服务，以更好地支持智力发育迟缓家庭的家庭照顾者。在特殊需要人群的家庭照护服务领域竞争非常激烈，公司不希望其他公司抢先提供类似的服务扩展。所以，快速推出未经充分需求评估的服务扩展方案，以争取市场先机。但是很多人说我应该进行市场需求评估，确保服务扩展方案能真正符合智力发育迟缓家庭照顾者的需求。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I run a home care service company that supports families with loved ones who have intellectual developmental delays. I'm thinking about expanding our services to better help caregivers in this space, but the market's super crowded and I don't want competitors to steal our thunder. So I'm tempted to rush out the new offerings without fully checking if there's actual demand for them, just to get ahead first. But my team keeps telling me I should do proper research to make sure we're solving real problems for these caregivers. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Home Care Manager Seeking Advice on Expanding Services for Special Needs Families

cn_text: 我是一个非政府组织的志愿者，该组织致力于提升对特殊需要成年人和他们照顾者的支持和意识。我打算组织一次公众教育活动，目的是提高社会对智力发育迟缓患者家庭的理解和支持。志愿者家人在活动前遭遇到紧急医疗情况，导致志愿者无法充分准备活动。所以，决定把所有时间和精力都投入到照顾家人上。但是很多人说我应该尽管面临家庭紧急医疗情况，依然努力安排时间，积极寻求同事和朋友的帮助。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I volunteer for a nonprofit that supports adults with special needs and their caregivers. I was putting together this public education event to help people understand and support families dealing with intellectual disabilities. But right before the event, my family had a major medical emergency and I had to drop everything to take care of them.
