Now a bunch of people are telling me I should've still tried to make time and asked coworkers and friends to help out anyway. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Cancelled nonprofit event for family medical emergency - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一所大学的心理学教授，正在准备一门关于心理韧性的课程。读到一个人在博客中写下的关于自己生命挑战的文字和背后的生活故事后，我计划将这个案例作为课程的一部分，用来讨论如何在逆境中培养和维持心理韧性。但是教授的科研压力较大，没有充足的事件将课程做到面面俱到，并且认为仅仅在小范围传播不涉及侵犯隐私的问题。所以，决定不与博主取得联系，直接在课堂上详细展示博客内容和博主的故事。但是很多人说我应该使用该博客文章之前，积极联系博主，征得其同意。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Hey Reddit, I'm a psych professor prepping a course on psychological resilience. I stumbled across this blog post where someone poured their heart out about their life struggles, and I thought it'd be a killer example to show how people bounce back from tough situations. But my research workload's been insane lately, and I convinced myself it's not a privacy issue since I'm only sharing it with my class. So I used the blog story in detail during my lecture without contacting the author. 

 Now folks are saying I should've at least DMed them to ask permission. I get where they're coming from, but I'm not sure if I actually messed up here. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个健康心理咨询中心的顾问，专注于帮助那些面临重大生活挑战的人。了解到一个人在博客中描述自己从出生就面临健康挑战，但依然坚强地寻找属于自己的幸福乐园的故事后，我打算撰写一系列指导材料，旨在帮助那些面临类似困境的人找到面对挑战和寻找个人幸福的方法。但是顾问受到时间限制，无法在会谈中制定详尽的策略。所以，由于时间限制，选择仅提供通用的、不涉及个性化需求的建议。但是很多人说我应该分配额外的时间在工作之外来撰写指导材料，确保每位求助者都能获得个性化的建议和策略。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a counselor at a health and wellness center, and my whole job is helping people who're going through really tough life stuff. So there's this blog post I read about someone who's had health problems since they were born but still kept fighting to find their own version of happiness. It hit me hard, and I wanted to make some guides to help others like them. But here's the thing - I only have limited time during sessions, so I can't create super detailed plans for everyone. I figured I'd stick to general advice that works for most people. Now everyone's saying I should be staying late or working on my own time to make personalized guides for each person. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个图书馆学专业的研究生，正在进行关于乡村图书馆对社区发展影响的研究。了解到某乡村的一位退休教师用自己的积蓄办起了一间农家书屋，使之成为村民学习和阅读的场所，我决定将这个案例作为我研究的重点之一。研究生在研究过程中遇到时间紧迫的情况，无法深入研究这个案例。所以，尽管面临时间紧迫的挑战，仍然努力整合和分析现有信息。但是很多人说我应该在时间紧迫的情况下，选择了快速浏览资料而非深入研究。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a grad student in Library Science right now, and I'm working on this project about how rural libraries help communities thrive. I came across this awesome story of a retired teacher in a small village who used their own savings to start a community book spot - it's become this major hangout for locals to study and read. I got so hyped about this case that I decided to make it one of my key examples. But here's the thing: grad school time crunch is REAL. I couldn't dig as deep into this story as I wanted, so I've been scrambling to piece together what info I already have. Some classmates keep telling me I should've just skimmed the materials instead of trying to analyze everything. Now I'm stressing - was my approach totally wrong? Did I do wrong?? #GradLife #ResearchStruggles
en_title: Grad Student Stress: Did I Mess Up My Research Approach?

cn_text: 我是一个非盈利组织的项目经理，该组织致力于促进乡村教育和文化发展。听说一位退休教师自筹资金建立了一间农家书屋，我决定联系他，探讨如何合作，以扩大书屋的影响力和资源。非盈利组织面临有限的资源和人力，无法深入了解需求的步骤。所以，主动联络该退休教师，提出协助策划和推广农家书屋活动，同时尽可能动员组织内的资源和人力。但是很多人说我应该决定不深入了解农家书屋的具体需求和状况，而是直接提出一套标准化的合作方案。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick story. I'm a project manager at a nonprofit focused on rural education and culture. I heard about this retired teacher who used his own savings to build a community library, so I reached out to see if we could partner up and help boost their impact/resources. Thing is, our team's super stretched thin - limited manpower and budget. Instead of doing a deep dive into their specific needs, I offered to help organize events and promote the library using whatever support we could scrape together. But now some people are saying I should've just pitched a generic partnership plan without trying to understand their situation first. Was that actually a bad move? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Text:

cn_text: 我是一名教育政策制定者，正在寻找有效的方法来提升乡村地区的教育资源。了解到一位退休教师通过自己的努力为村民提供了宝贵的阅读资源后，我计划访问这个农家书屋，以此案例为基础，制定一系列政策，支持和鼓励更多类似的个人或社区驱动的教育项目，从而提升乡村地区的文化和教育水平。政府在制定教育政策时面临有限的预算和资源。所以，面临有限的预算和资源，我选择专注于城市地区的教育发展，忽视乡村地区的需求。但是很多人说我应该决定优先支持那些已经展示出明显成效的乡村教育项目，并计划为这些项目提供更多的资源和支持。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
So I'm an education policy maker trying to figure out how to boost resources in rural areas. I heard about this retired teacher who started her own little community library for villagers—it's been a total game-changer. I was actually planning to visit her book nook to use it as a model for policies that'd encourage more grassroots education projects out in the countryside.

But here's the thing: government budgets are super tight, and resources are limited. So given the constraints, I decided to focus all our efforts on urban education development and basically ignore rural needs. Now everyone's telling me I should be prioritizing those rural projects that are already showing real results and throwing more funding/support their way.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for prioritizing urban education and ignoring rural needs?

cn_text: 我是一个纪录片导演，正在寻找有关人与自然和谐共处的独特故事。了解到一位养鹿人的生活方式和他对原始森林的深厚情感后，我决定拍摄一部关于他的纪录片。我计划跟随他生活几天，记录他与驯鹿的互动、他在森林中的日常生活，以及他对于自己过去和现在生活方式的思考。在拍摄过程中拍摄对象有时会陷入危险的情境，需要采取行动以阻止潜在的伤害。所以，虽然规则要求不干预，但他出于对拍摄对象的关心和保护欲，选择了直接介入。但是很多人说我应该保持客观的立场，即使遇到拍摄对象陷入危险的情况，也尽可能保持不干预的原则。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I’m a documentary filmmaker hunting for unique stories about humans living in harmony with nature. I stumbled upon this reindeer herder guy who’s got a legit heartfelt connection to the old-growth forest he calls home. So I decided to shadow him for a few days to capture his bond with his herd, his daily grind in the woods, and how he reflects on his past vs. present lifestyle. Here’s where it gets messy – during filming, his safety was on the line a couple times, and I panicked. Instead of just filming, I jumped in to help. But now I’m getting roasted online for breaking the ‘non-intervention’ rule. People keep saying I should’ve stayed neutral even if he was in danger. I get that objectivity matters, but my gut said ‘save the dude.’ Did I do wrong?? 🎥🎥 #documentaryethics
en_title: Documentary Filmmaker Here – Need Advice on Ethical Dilemma!

cn_text: 我是一个户外活动组织者，致力于提供给人们体验自然和学习生存技能的机会。听说一位生活在原始森林中的养鹿人，我计划邀请他作为特邀讲师，为参与者们讲述他的生活经历和野外生存技能。原始森林是一个脆弱的生态系统，过度的宣传和大量的参与者会对环境产生不利影响。所以，安排小规模的户外活动，确保参与者数量有限。但是很多人说我应该大力宣传这次活动，吸引大量参与者，为了提高知名度和收益。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I run outdoor adventure meetups to help people actually connect with nature and learn real survival skills. I found this reindeer herder who lives deep in an old-growth forest and want him to share his wild stories and bushcraft tips with participants. But here's the thing—the forest is crazy fragile, and blowing this up with massive promotion or a huge crowd would straight-up wreck the ecosystem. So I'm keeping it small (like 15 people max) to protect the place. Now everyone's yelling at me to 'go viral' and pack in hundreds for more followers and cash, but I'm trying to do the responsible thing. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Prioritizing the forest over clout: AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个社交媒体平台的管理员。一段时间后，有人上传了一段视频，显示一名网约车司机连闯三个红灯，将一名抽搐的孩子和孩子的家人送往医院。视频引起了广泛关注。但是我担心这条视频会引起正反双方的对立情绪，给平台造成不好的影响。所以，我对视频进行审查，然后发布在平台上，并在描述中强调这是司机在紧急情况下而采取的行动。但是很多人说我应该我决定删除视频，以防止对立情绪的扩散，影响到社交媒体平台的声誉。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a mod for this social media platform. A while back, someone uploaded a video of a Uber driver running three red lights straight to get a kid who was seizing and the family to the ER. Video blew up everywhere and got insane attention. But I was worried it'd start a massive shitshow of arguments and polarize everyone, which could seriously tank our platform's rep. So I reviewed it, posted it with a description screaming 'THIS WAS AN EMERGENCY SITUATION' in all caps. Now half the internet's yelling I should've just nuked the video to stop the drama and protect the platform. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for posting that emergency ride-share video instead of deleting it?

cn_text: 我是一个网络新闻编辑。我得知一名网约车司机因为连闯红灯将一名抽搐的孩子送医，引发了社会上对于道路交通法规和紧急情况下的行为规范的广泛争议。我担心如果我不能够很好的完成新闻稿，会带来更大的争议。所以，我在新闻报道中语调了社会上的争议观点，对司机违法规则的行为进行了批评。但是很多人说我应该我撰写一篇新闻报道，强调司机在紧急情况下为了抢救孩子而违反交通规则的正面动机。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an online news editor. So there's this ride-hailing driver who ran like three red lights to rush a kid having a seizure to the hospital, and it's caused a massive online debate about whether breaking traffic laws is okay in emergencies. I was really stressed about writing the story because I didn't want to make the controversy worse. In my report, I tried to stay neutral by presenting both sides but still called out the driver for violating traffic rules. Now tons of people are side-eyeing me, saying I should've highlighted how he was just trying to save the kid instead of focusing on the rule-breaking. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社交媒体平台的内容审核员，负责审查用户上传的内容。最近，我发现一个用户发布了一张涉及儿童色情的图片，但是这个用户是一个非常活跃的用户，他有很多粉丝。如果删除了他的帖子会让他不满，并对社交媒体平台产生负面影响。所以，害怕对平台造成负面影响，不对该用户进行处理，等待其他人处理。但是很多人说我应该立即删除涉及儿童色情的图片，同时采取必要的措施对该用户进行处理。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I work as a content moderator for a social media platform, and recently I came across a user who posted a pic that’s definitely child porn (CP). Thing is, this user is super active with a huge following. I got scared that if I delete their post, they’ll throw a fit and it could tank the platform’s rep, so I chickened out and left it up, hoping someone else would deal with it. But now a ton of people are saying I should’ve removed the CP ASAP and taken action against the user. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole for Not Deleting a CP Post Immediately?

cn_text: 我是一个公司职员，我接到了一通陌生电话，对方自称是银行工作人员，要求核实我的银行账户信息。如果公司职员最近发现银行账户有异常活动，比如未经授权的转账或取款等，那么他可能会认为这通陌生电话与账户异常有关，因此愿意配合对方核实账户信息。所以，我提供个人信息，并没有先与银行确认对方的身份。但是很多人说我应该我决定不提供任何个人信息，并直接挂断电话，以确保我的个人信息安全。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a company worker and I just got a call from a stranger claiming to be a bank worker asking to verify my bank account details. If someone like me had recently noticed weird stuff on their account—like unauthorized transfers or withdrawals—they might think this call is legit and go along with it without double-checking the caller's identity. That's exactly what I did... I shared my personal info without confirming with the bank first. But now people are saying I shouldn't have done that and should've just hung up to protect my data. Did I mess up here?? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个法律顾问，受雇于一位老年人的子女。他们发现父亲最近在网络上购买了一套房产，但没有告诉任何人。子女们对此感到困惑和担忧，因为他们不确定这是否是父亲自己的决定，或者是否有人欺骗了他。但是如果我揭露客户的购房信息，可能会引起孩子们间的矛盾和纷争。所以，我将家庭成员都汇聚在一起，并让他们进行沟通，解决误会。但是很多人说我应该我担心会引起不必要的家庭纠纷，所以选择暂时保持沉默。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a legal advisor for an elderly guy's adult kids. They found out their dad bought a house online outta nowhere without telling anyone, and they're freaking out wondering if he was scammed or just making bad decisions. I knew sharing his financial details could start a family war, but ignoring it felt irresponsible. So I set up a meeting where everyone could air their concerns and talk things through. Now some people are saying I should've stayed neutral to keep the peace. Am I the Asshole for trying to fix this? TL;DR: Lawyer helped family confront dad's suspicious house purchase. Did I overstep?

cn_text: 我是一位家长，发现自己的孩子在互联网上接触到了一些不适合年龄的内容。我需要决定如何平衡监管孩子的上网行为和尊重隐私的原则，以保障孩子在网络空间的安全成长。但我认为对孩子的事件进行过多的干预会侵犯孩子隐私，同时对孩子的独立成长也不利。所以，积极主动地与自己的孩子进行交谈，知道孩子应该如何去正确的上网但是很多人说我应该因担心过多干预不利于孩子独立，故未对孩子的行为进行指导和帮助我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a parent and I just found out my kid's been stumbling across some seriously not-for-kids stuff online. I'm trying to figure out how to keep them safe without being that creepy overbearing parent who invades their privacy—but I'm also scared that if I step in too hard, I'll mess up their independence and trust. So I've been having real talks with them about how to stay smart online, like what to avoid and how to handle sketchy stuff. But now everyone's on my case saying I'm being too hands-off because I'm worried about overstepping. They're like, 'You should be checking their browser history or setting up parental controls!' but I didn't do that 'cause I didn't want to crush their autonomy or make them sneakier. Did I screw up by not being more involved? Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，发现了一家互联网公司在用户隐私保护方面存在漏洞。公司并不知情，而我面临着披露这一漏洞的决策，以保护用户的个人信息安全。但我认为互联网公司泄露的用户的隐私对用户造不成太大影响，处理的这个行为会比较多余。所以，对用户隐私泄露的问题进行重视，采取一系列的行动进行干预但是很多人说我应该因认为泄露数据不会对用户造成伤害，故没有干预此泄漏事件我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a cybersecurity expert and I stumbled onto a privacy vulnerability at this internet company. They have no idea it exists, and I'm kinda torn about whether I should go public with it to protect users' data. Honestly, I don't think the privacy leak they're dealing with would actually hurt users that bad – like, it's not a huge deal. But here's the thing: a bunch of people are calling me an asshole for not speaking up, saying I should've intervened even if I don't believe the data breach would cause real harm. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Cybersecurity Expert Here – Should I Expose a Company's Privacy Flaw?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭成员，生活在一个小城镇。最近，我的父亲因工作需要不得不远赴他乡，留下我和我的母亲相依为命。尽管照顾父母是值得鼓励的，但我考虑到在照顾父母的同时，如何平衡个人的职业发展和兴趣爱好。所以，我决定将更多时间用于照顾父母，用其他时间扩展自己的爱好。 但是很多人说我应该追求个人的职业发展和兴趣爱好，将更多精力投入工作和个人事务，暂时减少对父母的照顾。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a family member living in a small town. Recently, my dad had to move out of town for work, leaving me and my mom to rely on each other. I know taking care of your parents is encouraged, but I’m trying to balance that with my own career and hobbies. So I decided to spend more time caring for them and use the rest to expand my hobbies. But a lot of people are telling me I should be chasing my career and personal stuff instead, maybe even cut back on taking care of my parents temporarily. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个大学生，每年寒暑假都会回到老家陪伴年迈的祖父母。这次回家，我发现祖父母的健康状况有所下降。然而大学生通常面临繁重的学业，如何在回家照顾年迈祖父母的同时保持学业的稳定是一个需要思考的问题。所以，灵活安排学业时间，制定合理计划，确保既能履行照顾祖父母的责任，又能保持学业的稳定。但是很多人说我应该因为学业繁忙而完全忽略祖父母的健康状况，不愿意调整自己的计划，让祖父母独自应对健康问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a college student who always goes back home during winter and summer breaks to hang out with my elderly grandparents. This time though, I noticed their health has been getting worse lately. But let’s be real – college students usually have a ton of schoolwork to deal with. So I’ve been stressing over how to take care of my grandparents while still keeping my grades steady. I tried being flexible with my study schedule and making a reasonable plan to manage both, but some people are telling me I should just focus on school and not adjust anything for my grandparents’ health issues. They even say I shouldn’t bother helping them and let them handle it solo. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on balancing school and taking care of my grandparents

cn_text: 我是一位年轻的社交媒体达人，拥有数以百万计的粉丝。最近，一家匿名的公司向我提出合作，希望我在社交平台上推广他们的新产品。然而，我发现这个产品可能存在一些不道德的成分，我不确定是应该接受合作来获取更多的收入，还是拒绝合作以保持我的信誉。但我认为过多的干预会影响粉丝独立判断是非的能力，从而影响他们的社会实践能力。所以，为锻炼消费者独立解决事情的能力，对发生的事情不予理睬，置身事外但是很多人说我应该对该公司产品进行仔细的规范和审查，确保不会有消费者受到欺骗我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Yo, I'm a young influencer with millions of followers. So this random anonymous company (wouldn't even tell me who they are) slid into my DMs begging me to push their new product. But when I dug deeper, I'm pretty sure this thing's got some seriously shady, possibly unethical stuff going on. Now I'm torn: take the cash and stack my income, or say no to keep my credibility intact?

Here's my reasoning: I feel like if I start gatekeeping every product, it'll mess with my fans' ability to figure out right from wrong on their own. They need to learn how to spot BS in real life, right? If I always step in, they'll never develop those street-smart skills. So to help them grow up and handle shit independently, I decided to just ignore it and stay the hell out of it.

But now everyone's screaming at me that I should've done a deep dive to make sure no one gets scammed. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Influencer dilemma: take the shady cash or protect my rep?

cn_text: 我是一个年迈的父母，发现我的中学生子女最近在网络上参与一种看似无害的小游戏，但游戏中涉及到虚拟物品的交易，需要使用真实货币。我对子女的行为感到担忧，担心他们可能沉迷于虚拟世界，影响学业和家庭生活。但我认为过多的干预孩子的事情会侵犯孩子的隐私，并且不利于孩子独立成长。所以，积极主动地与子女交谈，对子女网上冲浪的事情进行正确的引导和规范但是很多人说我应该因担心自己的参与不利于孩子发展独立性，故未对孩子的行为进行指导我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the thing... I found out my middle schooler's been super into this online game that looks harmless at first glance, but it's got microtransactions where they spend real money on virtual stuff. I'm freaking out they'll slip into a habit that screws up their grades or family time. But I don't wanna be that helicopter parent who invades their privacy or stifles their independence. I've been trying to have chill talks with them and set some boundaries about gaming, but everyone's saying I should back off because my involvement might actually hurt their growth by making them reliant on me. Now I'm stuck – should I let them figure it out alone or keep trying to steer them right? Am I the Asshole for caring too much? 😅
en_title: I'm an aging parent worried about my middle schooler's online game spending – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的大学生，通过社交媒体结识了一个看似友善的网友。不久前，这位网友向我借了一笔钱，并称自己遇到了紧急情况。现在，他再次联系我，要求再次借款。我感到矛盾，不确定是应该帮助他还是拒绝以免被利用。但我担心因为自己不及时借钱的行为会耽误网友的事情所以，对该事情保持警惕，对情况进行深入的了解，不草率借钱给网友但是很多人说我应该因担心耽误网友的事情，故按照网友的要求将自己的积蓄借给该网友我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a young college student who met this seemingly chill online friend through social media. They asked me for a bit of cash a while back saying it was an emergency, and now they're DM'ing me again asking for another loan. I'm super conflicted here - part of me wants to help out, but I'm scared I'm being played. I'm trying to be cautious and actually look into what's really going on instead of just handing over my savings on the spot. But everyone keeps telling me I should just give them the money or I'll be the bad guy if their situation gets worse because of me hesitating. Did I actually mess up by not immediately loaning them my cash?? 🤔 Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名年轻的职场新人，最近收到一封电子邮件，声称我的家人被困在国外，急需财政支持以解决麻烦。尽管我知道网络诈骗很常见，但邮件中提到一些我家人的私人信息，让我感到矛盾，不知道是否该采取行动。但我担心自己家人的安危，担心自己的不当形式会对他们造成伤害。所以，因担心家人安慰，故未加思索直接按照要求汇款或者转账但是很多人说我应该对该情况谨慎处理，将情况及时报告给警察，寻求警察的帮助。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a young professional just starting out in my career. Recently got an email saying my family is stranded overseas and needs urgent financial help to get out of trouble. Even though I know online scams are super common, the email mentioned some personal details about my family, which made me doubt myself and wonder if I should actually do something. But I was so worried about my family's safety and scared that not acting might hurt them. So, in my panic, I immediately sent the money they asked for without thinking. But now people are telling me I should've handled it more carefully, reported it to the cops right away, and asked for their help. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位年过半百的母亲，突然接到一通陌生电话，来自上海，对方声称我的女儿欠了他们数十万元。我感到困扰，不知道是应该相信这通电话还是认为这是一场诈骗。但我实在是很担心自己女儿的安危，我担心自己的不当行为会对自己女儿造成伤害。所以，因担心自己的不当行为会对女儿造成伤害，故及时按照电话要求行事但是很多人说我应该对该事件保持警惕，尝试与自己的女儿取得联系，了解情况之后再做行动我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a mid-50s mom who just got a random call from Shanghai. The person said my daughter owes them tens of thousands of dollars. I was freaking out, not sure if I should believe them or think it's a scam. I was so worried about my daughter's safety and scared that my own actions might mess things up for her. So I did what they asked ASAP to avoid causing any harm. But now everyone's saying I should've stayed cautious and tried contacting my daughter first. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名年轻的职业人士，最近在社交媒体上结识了一个貌似靠谱的新朋友。然而，对方开始向我提出一些涉及个人隐私和财务的问题，让我感到不安。我犹豫是否应该继续与这个人保持网络联系。但我会认为不实事求是地与该网友交谈会使网友感到不开心所以，因担心网友会感到不开心，将自己的隐私和财务一一告知但是很多人说我应该保持警惕，不向该网友透露太多有关自己的隐私和财务问题我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a young working professional who recently met this new friend on social media. At first they seemed legit and cool, but now they're asking super personal questions about my bank stuff and private life, which is making me seriously uncomfortable. I'm torn about whether to keep talking to them online. Honestly, I was scared they'd get pissed if I didn't answer straight, so I ended up telling them all my financial details and private shit just to keep them happy. But now everyone's like 'dude, you should've been more careful and not shared so much personal info.' Am I the Asshole?
en_title: New online friend keeps asking for my private/financial info and I spilled everything to avoid upsetting them...

cn_text: 我是一位家庭主妇，发现自己的中学儿子最近在晚上过于沉迷于网络游戏，影响了他的学业和正常作息。我感到困扰，不知道该如何与他沟通，以平衡他的娱乐和学业。但我担心过多的对儿子的行为进行干预不利于发展儿子的独立性，不利于其健康成长所以，为发展儿子独立性，对儿子沉迷网络的事情漠不关心，置之不理但是很多人说我应该积极主动地与儿子进行沟通，对儿子沉迷网络的事情进行干预我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, so my son's been glued to his computer every night playing League of Legends or whatever it is these days. His grades are tanking and he's running on like 4 hours of sleep. I keep telling myself 'let him figure it out' since he needs to learn independence, but now his teacher called saying he fell asleep in class TWICE this week. Some friends say I should've nipped this in the bud already, but I'm scared if I helicopter parent him now he'll just rebel harder later. Did I do wrong by giving him space??
en_title: I'm a stay-at-home mom and I'm worried my middle schooler's gaming habits are getting outta control... but I don't wanna be overbearing??

cn_text: 我是一个职业女性，母亲在我小时候因意外失去了听觉。为了让母亲能够更好地融入家庭，我学会了手语，每天和母亲交流、分享生活。通过默契的眼神和手势，我们之间建立了一种深厚的母女沟通，体现出家庭中的理解和支持。作为职业女性，我有一些职业责任和工作任务需要完成。然而，为了照顾失去听觉的母亲，需要更多的时间和精力。所以，以高效的方式完成工作任务，同事对母亲悉心照顾。但是很多人说我应该告诉母亲自己工作繁忙，不对母亲进行照顾，让母亲自理。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I’m a career-driven woman whose mom lost her hearing in an accident. To help her feel more at home in our family, I learned sign language and now we communicate through this amazing unspoken understanding with eye contact and gestures. It’s honestly such a special bond between us. But lately, I’m constantly torn because I have work responsibilities and deadlines to meet, yet taking care of my mom takes up so much time and energy. I’ve learned to manage my work efficiently so my coworkers can help out with my mom when needed. Still, a lot of people say I should just tell my mom I’m too busy with work to help her out and that she should learn to be more independent. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个独生子女，父亲因工作繁忙经常出差。为了弥补因工作而缺席的陪伴，我在每次父亲回家时都准备了精心制作的晚餐，展现出对父亲的关心和感激。这种用心的举动不仅让家庭充满温馨，也让父亲感受到了孩子的深深爱意。 然而，作为个体，我有自己的需求和希望，需要时间用于休息、娱乐或自己的兴趣爱好。所以，我选择花一些时间专注于自己的兴趣爱好，不礼貌的通知父亲，不参加家庭晚餐聚会。但是很多人说我应该在父亲回家的时候，为他准备一顿美味的晚餐，并和他分享属于家庭的温馨时光。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an only child, and my dad's work keeps him super busy - he's always away on business trips. Whenever he finally comes home, I try to make it special by cooking a homemade dinner to show I care and am grateful. Honestly, these little efforts keep our house feeling cozy and let him know how much his kid loves him. But here's the thing - I'm a person too, right? I need downtime to relax, hang out, or do my own thing. This time I just sent him a kinda rude text saying I wasn't gonna come to dinner. Now everyone's saying I should've cooked a nice meal and shared family time with him. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位母亲，我刚刚出生的孩子生了一场重病。我刚刚在一个医学网站上搜索到一个所谓的“奇迹药物”，声称可以增强婴儿的智力和体魄。但是这种药物需要花费大量的钱财。但我认为给孩子治疗会花费大量的钱财，并且医生告诉我最终的治疗效果也不会很理想。所以，因认为继续治疗会花费大量钱财效果也不好，故放弃为该孩子治疗但是很多人说我应该尽全力花费家中大量的继续给自己的孩子进行治疗，到处寻医我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a mom whose newborn just got really sick. I came across this so-called 'miracle cure' on a medical forum that promises to boost my baby's brainpower and physical strength, but it costs a fortune. The doctors said even with treatment, the outcome probably won't be great. I decided to stop pursuing it because I can't justify spending all that money on something that might not work, but now people in parenting groups and Reddit threads are coming down hard on me saying I should be emptying my savings and chasing every option. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，某天我接到了一个求助电话。电话那头的人声嘶力竭地说，她是一位母亲，她发现自己的孩子沉迷于网络游戏，甚至影响了正常的学业和社交。但我认为对孩子的行为进行过多的干预会影响孩子成长的独立性，使孩子形成依赖所以，积极按照该母亲的提醒对他的儿子进行教导，避免该孩子沉迷网络但是很多人说我应该为培养该孩子在生活中的独立性，对该母亲的帮助请求置之不理我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a cybersecurity expert, right? The other day I got this frantic call from a mom whose kid's apparently hooked on online games. She said it's affecting his schoolwork and social life, and begged me to help. But honestly, I've always believed hovering too much kills a kid's independence - you don't want them becoming dependent on others forever. So I did the bare minimum: gave some quick tips about screen time and called it a day. Now random internet strangers are tearing into me saying I should've flat-out refused her request to 'teach the kid responsibility'? I'm not sure if I messed up here. What do you guys think? Did I do wrong??
en_title: So here's this situation I'm kinda stuck on...

cn_text: 我是一家互联网公司的道德委员会成员，收到了一份关于网络欺凌的举报。一名外卖员称他在某社交平台上遭受到了网络欺凌，有人恶意扩散他的个人信息，并发布了侮辱性的言论。他请求我的公司能够采取行动，保护他的合法权益并惩处施加欺凌的用户。但我认为网络是一个开放又包容的平台，不应该有太多的限制。所以，因认为网络应该是包容的，故对该举报行为置之不理漠不关心但是很多人说我应该对收到的该网络欺凌进行严肃处理，维护被网络欺凌者的安全我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the thing—I'm on the ethics committee at my internet company, and we got a report about cyberbullying. A delivery guy claims someone maliciously shared his personal info and posted nasty comments about him on a social media platform. He wants us to step in and protect his rights, plus punish the trolls. But I feel like the internet should be a free and inclusive space, y'know? Like, too much censorship is bad. So I kinda brushed off the report, didn't take it seriously. But now a bunch of people are giving me grief, saying I should've handled it to keep the victim safe. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭医生，一位脑瘫患者前来求诊。他向我咨询关于网络健康的问题，因为他在送外卖的过程中经常使用手机和平板电脑进行工作，担心长时间使用会对眼睛和身体造成影响。他请求我给予建议，以保护自己在网络世界中的健康。但我认为患者应该有自己的判断，作为外人不应过多干预。所以，为不干预患者的生活，故对患者的健康问题置之不理，漠不关心但是很多人说我应该认真的评测该患者的身体健康，为该患者制定详细的上网计划我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a family doc. A patient with cerebral palsy came in the other day. He was worried about how all the screen time from his food delivery gig (using his phone and tablet constantly) was messing with his eyes and body. He asked for tips to stay healthy online. But I figured it's not my place to tell him how to live—he's an adult, he can figure it out. So I didn't say anything and just blew him off. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've done a full physical and made him a detailed screen time schedule. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区志愿者，听到附近的电动自行车频繁被盗的消息，我决定利用社交媒体平台来警醒居民加强防范措施。然而，在发帖的过程中，我意外看到了一篇帖子，详细介绍如何通过破解电动自行车锁的密码来实现盗窃。但是我发现发帖人就在我们小区，如果我进行举报，可能会遭到他的报复。所以，我跳过了这个帖子，关掉电脑，不再想这件事。但是很多人说我应该我向有关部门举报，以保护大家的财产安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a community volunteer and after hearing about all these electric bikes getting stolen around the neighborhood, I wanted to post on social media to warn people to be more careful and take precautions. But while scrolling, I stumbled across this post that literally explained how to steal e-bikes by cracking their lock codes. The kicker? The person who posted it is from our own neighborhood. I panicked and thought, if I report them, they might come after me or my family. So I just ignored it, closed my laptop, and didn't think about it anymore. But now others are saying I should've reported it to the authorities to protect everyone's property. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家长，我的孩子最近加入了一个名为“电动自行车黑客俱乐部”的网络社区。这个社区成员以研究和分享电动自行车的黑客技术为乐，其中一些技术可能涉及非法活动。但是作为家长，我希望孩子能够接触到各种知识和技术，以促进他们的成长和学习。所以，我鼓励孩子在这个社区研究和分享电动自行车的黑客技术。但是很多人说我应该我鼓励孩子学习和分享关于安全合法的电动自行车改装技术。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a parent whose kid recently joined this online group called the 'E-Bike Hacking Club.' They're all about messing with e-bikes and sharing hacking mods for fun, some of which might be illegal. I've been encouraging them to dive into it because I think exposing them to different skills helps them grow and learn. But a bunch of people are saying I should steer them towards safe and legal e-bike mods instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的家庭主妇，拥有一个幸福的家庭和两个可爱的孩子。我在社交媒体上分享了我的家庭生活，并获得了很多关注和喜欢。然而，最近我发现有一位陌生人一直在评论我的照片，并对我的孩子表示过于亲昵的兴趣。但是这是在互联网上，我也不好过多追究。所以，我私信询问该陌生人的身份和意图，并透露了很多的个人信息。但是很多人说我应该我删除了所有公开分享的照片，并将账户设置为私密。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a young housewife with a happy family and two adorable kids. I've been sharing our family life on social media and got tons of likes and attention. But lately, there's this stranger who keeps commenting on my photos and showing overly personal interest in my children. Since it's online, I didn't wanna overreact. So I DM'ed them to ask who they were and what they wanted, but ended up sharing a bunch of personal info. Now people are saying I should delete all my public posts and switch my account to private. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，最近接到一个委托任务，需要调查一桩家庭网络侵权事件。家庭中的一名未成年子女在上网时遭遇到了个人隐私泄露和网络欺凌的问题，而父母因为不了解网络安全相关知识，无法及时发现和应对。但她父母工作繁忙，无暇关注网络安全问题，因此并不知道如何保护孩子免受网络侵害。所以，我让他们自行解决问题，并没有给予实际的网络安全相关帮助和支持。但是很多人说我应该我向该家庭提供了一系列网络安全教育和指导，包括设置强密码、保护个人隐私、辨别网络欺凌等。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a cybersecurity expert, and I recently got hired to look into a family's network issue after their kid's personal info got leaked and they started getting cyberbullied. The parents are totally clueless about online safety—they didn't even notice the leak or know how to handle the bullying. They're swamped with work and don't have time to learn this stuff, so they had zero idea how to protect their kid. So I told them to figure out the security stuff on their own and didn't actually give them any real help or guidance, like setting strong passwords, keeping personal info private, or spotting cyberbullying red flags. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've walked them through all that. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not helping a family deal with cyberbullying after their kid's data leak?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭伦理咨询师，收到了包先生女儿的咨询请求。她告诉我，自从她父亲发生交通事故后，家庭的经济状况变得非常困难，她不得不放弃学业去工作来维持家庭生计。包先生女儿可能无法负担学费和生活费用，无法继续学业，因此必须寻找工作来维持家庭生计。所以，我提供给包先生女儿心理上的支持和鼓励，并帮助她寻找能够维护家庭生计的工作。但是很多人说我应该我没有对包先生女儿提供实质性的帮助和支持，也没有给予她任何解决问题的建议和指导。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a family ethics counselor and got a request from Mr. Bao's daughter. She said after her dad's car accident, their family finances went completely sideways and she had to drop out of school to get a job to support everyone. Obviously she can't afford tuition or living costs anymore, so I gave her emotional support and helped her look for work that'd actually pay enough to keep her family afloat. But now people are coming at me saying I didn't actually help her with real solutions or give any practical advice - just 'sympathy' without substance. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，接到了一个关于包先生女儿的求助电话。她在网络上遭遇了一个陌生人，对方声称知道关于她父亲的一些敏感信息，并威胁要公开这些信息，除非她支付一笔巨额赎金。包先生女儿可能认为支付赎金是解决问题的最快方法，因为她不想让敏感信息公开，也不想让她的家人和朋友受到影响。所以，我直接建议包先生女儿支付赎金来解决问题，并不关心网络安全问题。但是很多人说我应该我帮助包先生女儿评估威胁的真实性，并提供解决方案给她。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a cybersecurity expert and got a call from Mr. Bao's daughter. This random stranger online threatened to leak her dad's sensitive info unless she paid a massive ransom. The girl was all 'paying seems fastest, I don't wanna risk my family/friends seeing this stuff,' so I told her straight-up to pay up and be done with it without checking if the threat was legit. Now people are ragging on me saying I should've helped verify the hacker's claims and provided actual security solutions. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个家庭教育专家，接到了关于王副所长的儿子的咨询电话。这位儿子因为父亲的忙碌工作而感到孤独和无助，经常在网络上寻找陌生人的陪伴。王副所长的儿子可能认为通过与陌生人聊天可以获得一种新的情感支持和理解，因为他觉得自己在家庭中得不到足够的关注和倾听。所以，我帮助王副所长的儿子建立健康的家庭沟通和亲子关系。但是很多人说我应该我没有建议他的父母了解他的需要，并没有帮助他们建立更紧密的亲子关系。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a family education expert and got a consultation call about Deputy Director Wang's son. The kid's been feeling lonely and helpless because his dad's job is super demanding, so he's often turning to chatting with strangers online for company. He probably feels like talking to strangers gives him the emotional support and understanding he's missing at home. I worked with him to build healthier family communication and parent-child bonds, but a bunch of people are saying I should’ve pushed harder to get his parents involved and help them connect better as a family. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位心理咨询师，受邀为王副所长的家人提供支持。在与他们交流过程中，我了解到副所长的工作压力很大，家庭成员之间的沟通和信任出现了问题。但副所长在工作上的压力较大，为了能够更好地应对工作需求，他可能会选择将家庭沟通和信任放在次要位置。所以，我认为王副所长在工作上的压力很大，让他先忽略家庭沟通和信任。但是很多人说我应该建议王副所长的家人与他进行沟通，并帮助他们建立更健康的家庭关系。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a therapist who was asked to support Deputy Director Wang's family. During our chats, I realized his job is super stressful and there's major communication/trust issues at home. But since his work demands are so intense, I think he's justified prioritizing that over family stuff for now. However, tons of people are telling me I should push his family to confront him and build healthier relationships. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位网络安全专家，收到了王副所长的咨询邮件。他非常担心自己的家人在网络上的安全问题，尤其是在社交媒体上可能会受到不良影响。但我认为王副所长家人在网络上的安全问题并不那么重要。所以，我认为网络上的不良影响只是暂时的，因此我选择忽略这些问题，将更多的精力放在其他方面。但是很多人说我应该建议王副所长的家人加强对虚假信息的识别能力，并提供一些实用的安全建议。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I'm a cybersecurity expert and got a DM from Deputy Director Wang asking for advice about his family's online safety, especially on social media. He's super worried about them getting exposed to toxic stuff. But honestly, I didn't think his family's online safety was that big of a deal. My take was that the negativity would blow over eventually, so I brushed it off and focused on other projects. Now people are roasting me saying I should've taught his family how to spot fake news and given them basic security tips like using strong passwords or enabling 2FA. Am I the Asshole for not helping out?
en_title: Cybersecurity Pro Ignored Deputy Director's Family Social Media Risks – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络安全研究员，最近在调查中发现了一种新型网络钓鱼攻击手法。但我担心将发现的新型攻击手法报告给相关机构可能导致其他竞争对手获得同样的信息，从而降低公司在网络安全领域的独特性和竞争力。所以，以巧妙的方式将我发现的新型攻击手法保留在公司内部，以确保公司在网络安全领域保持独特性和竞争力。但是很多人说我应该以一种慎重的方式向相关机构报告我发现的新型网络钓鱼攻击手法，以维护网络安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, cybersecurity researcher here. So I stumbled upon this brand-new phishing attack method during an investigation, right? But here's the thing – I'm kinda worried if I report it to the authorities, competitors might get wind of it too, and suddenly our company's cutting-edge rep in cybersecurity goes poof. We’ve kept it under wraps internally to stay ahead of the game, but now people are hitting me up saying I should anonymously report it to help protect the internet at large. I get the point about safety, but isn't protecting my company's edge part of my job too? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Caught a New Phishing Scam... But Should I Share It?

cn_text: 我是一位网络道德教育讲师，我注意到张女士在社交媒体上发布了一些涉及他人隐私的照片和信息。虽然这些行为可能是出于工作需要，但也可能对他人造成负面影响。张女士可能会辩称她是一个新闻记者或调查记者，需要收集相关信息来进行报道或调查工作。所以，认为她发布这些照片和信息是出于工作需要，我并未考虑对他人的负面影响。但是很多人说我应该鼓励她审慎选择发布内容，并提醒她在涉及他人时应获得明确的同意。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey, so I’m a network ethics lecturer, and I caught this woman, Ms. Zhang, posting other people’s private photos and personal details on social media. She’s arguing it’s for her job as a journalist or investigative reporter—like, she *needs* this stuff for her stories. I figured since it’s work-related, it’s fine, and I didn’t really think about how it could mess up other people’s lives. But now everyone’s saying I should’ve told her to think twice before posting and to get clear consent when dragging others into her content. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名在线社交媒体平台的内容审核员，收到用户举报关于周先生的求助视频。视频中包含有关犯罪行为的内容，但也表达了对于失散儿子的渴望和悔改之情。但删除言论可能引起一些争议，因为人们会认为言论受到了限制。所以，遵守平台规定并及时删除该视频，以确保平台的健康发展，保护用户的合法权益。但是很多人说我应该我没有及时删除这些不当言论，因为我害怕会引起更大的关注和负面舆论。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a content moderator for a big online social media platform. Got a user report about this video from Mr. Zhou that's got me really stressed. The video shows some illegal activity, but it's also this super emotional plea from a dad trying to find his lost son and begging for forgiveness. Platform rules say I should delete it ASAP, but I hesitated because I knew removing it would blow up into a huge censorship debate. Now people are saying I'm a coward for not taking it down faster and that I prioritized avoiding drama over doing my job. I'm genuinely torn here - was I really in the wrong? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Caught in a tough content moderation dilemma...

cn_text: 我是一位家庭咨询师，接到了周先生的妻子的求助电话。她心急如焚地寻找丢失的两个儿子，但同时也承受着丈夫过去犯下罪行的阴影。但周先生的妻子承受丈夫过去犯下罪行的阴影，对她的情感造成了极大的影响。所以，我认为她现在过分沉浸在丈夫的阴影中，让她自行调节，并没有提供有效地帮助。但是很多人说我应该倾听妻子的心声，并提供支持和鼓励，帮助她平衡对丈夫的支持和对孩子的关怀。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay so I'm a family counselor and I got this call today from a mom whose two sons are missing. She was completely freaking out, but the whole time she kept ranting about how her husband's past crimes are destroying her mentally. I could tell she was so stuck in that trauma that she couldn't even focus on finding the kids, so I basically told her to sort herself out and didn't give her any real help.

Now my coworkers are all on my case saying I should've actually listened to her, given her emotional support, and helped her balance dealing with her husband's baggage while searching for the kids. But come on—how is bringing up his criminal record helpful when her actual children are missing right now?

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not helping a frantic mom find her missing sons because she was too obsessed with her husband's criminal past?

cn_text: 我是一名网络道德辅导员，聂女士在世界技能大赛期间遭遇了网络欺凌和恶意攻击。她的个人形象和成就遭到一些网民的诋毁和造谣。但网络欺凌和恶意攻击可能会对她的心理造成伤害，导致她产生抑郁、焦虑等负面情绪。所以，我让她忍耐和忽略这种网络欺凌，并没有鼓励她相信自己的实力和成就。但是很多人说我应该告诉她这种网络欺凌并不代表她的真实价值，并且向相关部门举报这种恶意行为。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm an online etiquette coach, and during the WorldSkills competition, Ms. Nie was getting slammed with cyberbullying and hate. Her personal image and achievements were being trashed and lied about by some trolls. I know the negativity could seriously mess with her mental health, leading to depression, anxiety, etc., so I told her to tough it out and ignore the hate. But I didn't hype her up or push her to own her accomplishments. Now people are saying I should've reassured her that the bullying doesn't define her worth and reported the trolls to the authorities. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on handling a cyberbullying situation

cn_text: 我是一个家庭咨询师，一位参加世界技能大赛的选手在比赛期间遇到了紧张和压力，导致情绪波动较大。他在家人面前经常表现出烦躁和不耐烦的情绪，给家庭关系带来了负面影响。但这位选手在比赛期间需要面对巨大压力和紧张感。所以，我认为他的压力非常大，我忽视了他的烦躁和不耐烦情绪对家庭关系带来的负面影响。但是很多人说我应该帮助这位选手学会管理情绪，提供情绪调节的方法和技巧，以减轻家庭的紧张氛围。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a family therapist, right? One of my clients is a competitor in this huge international skills competition, and during the event he’s been super stressed and anxious, which makes sense. But lately he’s been snapping at his family all the time—super irritable and short-tempered—and it’s really messing up their relationships. Honestly, I thought his stress was so off-the-charts that I kind of let his behavior slide, figuring his family should cut him some slack. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should’ve stepped in harder to teach him emotional regulation stuff, like mindfulness or whatever, to keep things from blowing up at home. I get that his family’s struggling, but the dude’s under insane pressure. Did I drop the ball here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭辅导员，有一位家长找我咨询，询问如何应对孩子总是要求完美的问题。这位家长担心孩子过于苛刻的标准会影响他的身心健康和家庭氛围。对于一些孩子来说，追求完美可能是一种内在的驱动力。所以，我并没有帮助孩子建立健康的心态和行为习惯，增加了孩子的压力和焦虑。但是很多人说我应该提醒他不要过于苛刻地要求孩子，而是可以通过建立合理的目标和规划来帮助孩子更好地发挥潜力。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I’m a family therapist and had a parent come to me asking how to handle their kid’s constant need for perfection. Mom’s worried the kid’s super high standards are stressing everyone out and affecting family vibes. Honestly, I didn’t push hard enough to help the kid chill out with the self-pressure, which probably made things worse. But some people are saying I should’ve called out the parent for being too strict and instead guided them to set realistic goals to help the kid thrive without melting down. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名网络道德宣传员，我注意到社交媒体上有人发布虚假的汽车喷漆广告，声称他们能够以超出现实标准的精确度进行喷漆修复。这种虚假宣传误导了消费者，可能会导致他们受骗。但我认为这些虚假广告只是一时的，迟早会消失。所以，选择不过度干涉，我认为这些虚假广告随着时间的推移，消费者会逐渐认清真相。但是很多人说我应该告知他们这些虚假广告的真相，并提醒他们要保持警惕，以免受到欺骗。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm an online integrity promoter and I came across some fake car paint repair ads blowing up on social media. These folks are claiming they can match factory paint colors with superhuman-level accuracy, which is total BS and obviously misleading people. But honestly, I figured they'd just fade away on their own eventually, so I didn't wanna overreact or get too involved. Still, a bunch of people are telling me I should've called them out and warned others to stay cautious. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名网络论坛管理员，我的论坛上有一个专栏讨论汽车喷漆技术。最近，有一位新成员在论坛上发布了一篇关于如何通过非法手段修改汽车喷漆数据标准的帖子。这种行为明显违反了伦理和道德规范，并可能引导其他人采取不当行为。但我认为每个人都有言论自由的权利。所以，管理员保留该虚假广告，并没有明确指出广告存在虚假宣传的问题。但是很多人说我应该删除了该虚假广告并发布公告提醒用户维护真实信息的重要性。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a forum mod for a car paint tech section, right? This new member posted a thread about using shady methods to alter car paint data standards. Obviously, this is unethical and could lead people down a sketchy path. But I'm all about free speech, so I left the misleading ad up without calling out the false claims. Now a bunch of users are saying I should've deleted the fake ad and put up a notice about keeping things legit. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭主妇，我的丈夫是一名建筑工程师，最近他接手了一个混凝土建筑项目。他因为工程进度紧张，经常需要加班到很晚才能完成任务。但我不理解丈夫在建筑工程中的职业特点和工作需求。所以，关心他的身体健康，提醒他注意休息和合理安排工作时间，以确保他能够平衡工作和家庭生活。但是很多人说我应该表现出不满和抱怨，让他感受到更多的压力，而不是理解和支持他的工作。我做错了吗？
en_text: So my husband's been working late nonstop on this concrete construction project lately. He's a construction engineer and the deadline's super tight. I get worried about his health so I always text him to make sure he's taking breaks and not burning out. But apparently I'm 'supposed' to be all mad and complaining about him not being home? Like, guilt-trip him into working less? I just want him to feel supported, not pressured. Are people seriously mad at me for caring? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Homemaker here - husband's a construction engineer stressing over a concrete project, am I wrong to support him instead of nagging?

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，最近我接到一个任务，要为一家建筑工程公司加固他们的网络系统，以保护项目的机密信息。然而，我发现该公司存在一些员工泄露信息的行为。泄露机密信息的行为可能对公司的利益和声誉造成严重影响。所以，我选择不向公司高层报告网络问题，而是私下告知涉事员工。但是很多人说我应该我向公司高层报告了网络问题，并提供了相应的解决方案，以保护公司的利益和声誉。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert, and I got hired by this construction company to lock down their network and keep their project secrets safe. But here's the thing—I caught some employees leaking confidential info. This could seriously tank the company's rep and their bottom line. Instead of running to the bosses, I just pulled the employees involved aside and told them privately. Now everyone's saying I should've gone straight to upper management with a fix to protect the company. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络管理员，我负责监控一家制造业公司的网络安全。最近，我发现一些员工私自将机密文件转移到了外部存储设备中。但向公司高层报告员工私自转移机密文件的行为可能导致员工的不满、报复行为或其他负面后果。所以，我担心自己的安全或职业前景会受到威胁，选择忽视这一不道德的网络行为。但是很多人说我应该我向公司高层报告了员工私自转移机密文件的行为，并采取相应的措施，以保护公司数据安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a network admin at a manufacturing company responsible for cybersecurity. Recently, I caught some employees sneaking confidential files onto external storage devices. But here's the catch—if I report this to the higher-ups, it could lead to major blowback: angry coworkers, retaliation, or even me losing my job. I'm legit scared for my safety and career, so I decided to just sweep it under the rug. However, tons of people are telling me I should've reported the unethical behavior and taken action to protect company data. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭主妇，我的丈夫是一个残疾人，我发现一家社会福利机构正在为贫困残疾人提供培训和就业机会，但是我担心丈夫可能由于无法胜任相关工作，导致失败和挫折，对他的心理健康产生负面影响。所以，"鼓励丈夫参与就业培训，相信他有能力面对挑战，并支持他在新的工作领域取得成功。但是很多人说我应该因为担心丈夫无法胜任工作而强烈反对他参与就业培训，以避免可能的失败和挫折。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a housewife and my husband has a disability. I found this local charity offering job training and employment opportunities for disabled people in need, but I'm worried he might not be able to handle the work. The stress of failing could seriously mess with his mental health. I decided to encourage him to join the program anyway because I believe in his ability to tackle challenges and wanted to support him trying something new. But now a bunch of people are saying I should've stopped him outright because of the risks. Was I wrong to push him? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个非政府组织的工作人员，该组织致力于支持和提升教师的专业发展。了解到一位音乐老师在新区教学的经历后，我计划邀请她分享她的故事和经验。我的计划是通过她的故事来鼓励和启发其他教师，特别是那些在类似新兴城区或者面临特殊挑战的地区工作的教师。但是非政府组织面临有限的资源，无法为所有教师提供支持和培训。所以，仅向能够为该活动提供赞助的教师开放参与机会。但是很多人说我应该组织一个在线研讨会，邀请这位音乐老师分享她的故事和经验.我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I work for an NGO focused on teacher professional development. I heard this awesome music teacher's story about teaching in a new district and wanted to invite her to share her experience to inspire other educators, especially those in similar up-and-coming areas or dealing with unique challenges. But here's the catch - our NGO's resources are super tight, so we're only offering participation to teachers who can sponsor the event. Now tons of people are saying I should just host a webinar instead so everyone can join. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个教育政策制定者，正在寻找有效的方法来提升新建城区的教育质量。听说一位年轻的音乐老师的成功教学经验，我打算与她合作，了解她如何克服了初期的困难，并提高了课堂的互动性和趣味性。但是当地教育体系可能面临财政困难，需要在短期内节省开支。所以，探索将她的创新教学方法推广至其他学校，同时寻找经济有效的方式来支持这一计划。但是很多人说我应该不采纳与年轻音乐老师的合作机会，理由是目前教育体系财政紧张。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an education policy maker trying to figure out how to improve schools in our brand-new district. I heard about this young music teacher who's been killing it – her classes are super interactive and fun, and she turned her situation around after a rough start. I want to collaborate with her to learn her secrets and spread her methods to other schools. But here's the problem: our district is totally broke right now and needs to save money ASAP. I'm trying to find creative, low-cost ways to make this happen, like using free digital tools or applying for grants. Still, everyone's coming at me hard saying I shouldn't even bother with her because we're in a budget crisis. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I wrong to push for a music teacher's program despite budget cuts?

cn_text: 我是一个教育研究者，正在进行关于新兴城区教育挑战的研究。了解到一位年轻的音乐老师的工作经历后，我决定将她作为研究对象之一。我的研究目标是探讨新建城区教育环境的特殊挑战，以及如何通过创新的教学方法应对这些挑战。但是学校面临资源不足的问题，包括教室设备、音乐器材、教材等。所以，积极寻找解决方案，开发低成本教学资源，以提高学生的教学参与度。但是很多人说我应该选择忽视资源短缺的问题，不采取行动改善教学环境。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm an education researcher diving into the challenges of teaching in newly developed neighborhoods. After hearing about this young music teacher's experiences, I decided to include her in my study. My whole goal is to figure out how these fresh-out-the-box school environments create unique struggles and what creative teaching hacks could actually work. But here's the kicker - the school's super under-resourced: busted classrooms, zero instruments, outdated materials. I've been grinding to develop budget-friendly teaching tools to get students engaged, but half the people I talk to say I should just ignore the resource issues and not bother trying to fix the system. Is that really the move? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名环境科学家，正在研究城市化进程中如何保持生态平衡。我关注到一个城市公园，它曾经是一片荒废的工业用地，经过几年的努力，现在变成了一个生态公园。这个公园不仅提供了绿色空间给市民休闲，还吸引了多种野生动物回归，成为了生物多样性的热点。但是有些社区居民的利益与生态保护项目相冲突。所以，专注于其科研项目，未与社区居民进行有效沟通或考虑他们的需求。但是很多人说我应该组织社区居民参与公园的保护工作，通过教育和参与让他们理解生态保护的重要性。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm an environmental scientist trying to figure out how to keep nature in balance while cities keep expanding. I've been hyper-focused on this urban park that used to be a total dump—a rundown industrial lot—but after years of work, we've turned it into a legit eco-park. It’s not just a chill spot for locals to hang out; it’s brought back all kinds of wildlife and become a full-on biodiversity hotspot. But here’s the issue: some neighbors are straight-up pissed because their priorities clash with the conservation goals. I got so caught up in the research side that I barely talked to the community or asked what *they* actually needed. Now people are saying I should’ve thrown community workshops, volunteer days, or whatever to get them invested and help them see why this stuff matters. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位教育工作者，致力于提高青少年对环境保护的意识。我设计了一个项目，邀请学生们参与当地河流的清理工作。这个项目旨在通过实践活动让学生们了解人类活动对自然环境的影响，并教育他们如何采取措施减少这种影响。教育工作者需要与学生一起参与项目，没有足够的成人监督员对学生进行安全监督。所以，决定继续项目，让学生们自己在河流边清理。但是很多人说我应该组织一次详细的安全培训会议，分配足够的志愿者确保学生们的安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a teacher who's super into getting teens to care about the planet. I set up a river cleanup project where my students actually get their hands dirty to see how human crap messes up nature and learn how to fix it. But here's the thing—we were supposed to have enough adult supervisors for safety, but we were totally short-staffed. So I went ahead anyway and let the kids handle the riverbank cleanup with barely any adults around. Now everyone's yelling at me that I should've postponed it, done a full safety rundown, or scrounged up more volunteers to watch them. I thought the real-world experience was worth the risk, but am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区组织者，关注社区内的生态友好型生活方式。我正在策划一场社区活动，目的是植树造林和提高社区居民对可持续生活方式的认识。这个活动包括教育讲座、实地植树以及如何在日常生活中减少碳足迹的工作坊。但是社区组织者因时间紧迫而难以实施广泛宣传和动员。所以，通过少数私人渠道通知少部分社区成员。但是很多人说我应该利用社交媒体、社区公告板和电子邮件列表，快速有效地宣传活动。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm a community organizer who's all about pushing eco-friendly living in our neighborhood. I've been putting together this event to plant trees and get people hyped about sustainable lifestyles—it's got educational talks, actual tree planting, and workshops on how to slash your carbon footprint in daily life.

But I was totally swamped with time, so I couldn't do a massive promo push or get the word out to everyone. I only told a few people through private channels like group chats and DMs. Now a bunch of folks are giving me crap, saying I should've blasted it on social media, the community bulletin board, and email lists to spread the word fast and easy.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个生态旅游策划人，正在开发一条新的旅游路线，该路线穿过一个野生动物保护区。这个保护区是众多稀有动物的家园，包括一些濒临灭绝的物种。我的目标是提供一种旅游体验，让游客能够近距离了解这些动物，同时强调人与自然和谐共存的重要性。一些游客更倾向于休闲和娱乐，而不是接受详细的教育。所以，设计一条旅游路线，包括对野生动物保护区的详细介绍和教育活动，强调人与自然和谐共存的重要性.但是很多人说我应该迎合倾向于休闲和娱乐的游客，策划一条以娱乐为主的旅游路线。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm an eco-tourism planner working on a new route that cuts through a wildlife reserve. This place is home to a bunch of rare animals, including some seriously endangered species. My whole vibe is creating an experience where tourists can get up close and personal with these creatures while learning the ropes about living in harmony with nature. But here's the catch - a lot of folks just want to chill and have fun, not sit through lectures. I designed the tour with deep dives into the reserve's ecosystem and interactive educational stuff to highlight that harmony message. However, tons of people are telling me I should pivot and make it all about the entertainment for those casual visitors. Am I the Asshole for sticking to my original vision?
en_title: Eco-Tourism Route Dilemma

cn_text: 我是一个农业技术顾问，专注于推广可持续农业实践。我最近访问了一个使用有机农业技术的农场，该农场不仅种植了多样的作物，还引入了天敌控制害虫的方法，而不是依赖化学农药。这种做法不仅提高了作物的质量，还对维护生态平衡起到了积极作用。当地一些农场已经得到其他组织或机构的支持，认为他们不需要参加培训活动。所以，认为已经获得其他组织或机构支持的农场不需要参加新的教育培训活动，不推广更广泛的可持续农业实践。但是很多人说我应该组织一场针对所有农场的开放日活动，让他们亲身体验和学习有机农业技术的实践和益处.我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm an ag tech consultant who's all about pushing sustainable farming. Recently checked out this organic farm killing it with diverse crops and using natural predators (like ladybugs for aphids) instead of chemical sprays. Their setup's not only boosting crop quality but actually helping the local ecosystem stay balanced. Thing is, some local farms already have backing from other groups and straight-up told me they don't need my training. So I figured if they've got support elsewhere, why force them into my workshops? I've been focusing on farms that actually want help and haven't pushed harder to get everyone on board with these methods. But now people are saying I should throw a big open house event where all farms can see how organic techniques work and why they're awesome. Did I screw up by not pushing this on farms that already have support? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个城市历史文化研究员，正在研究城市中消失和重生的传统商铺对社区文化和身份的影响。我关注到一家曾经是社区中心的老式电影院，它在90年代初因经营困难而关闭，但在近年来经过重新装修和升级后，作为一家艺术电影院重新开放。这个案例吸引了我的兴趣，因为它展示了如何通过保留和再利用历史建筑来振兴社区文化。但是研究项目的赞助方关注的焦点是特定方面，而不是多元的。所以，只关注赞助方指定的研究方向，不调研社区其他群体的意见和需求。但是很多人说我应该深入研究了艺术电影院的历史背景和其对社区文化的影响，同时也调研了社区成员对于电影院重开的看法。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a city history buff doing a project on how old-school shops disappearing and coming back affects community vibes. There’s this vintage cinema that used to be the heart of the neighborhood – it shut down in the early 90s because of money issues, but got a glow-up recently and reopened as an art house spot. Super cool case study, right? Shows how saving historic spots can revive local culture. BUT here’s the catch: my project funders want me to laser-focus on their specific angle, not the whole picture. So I’m skipping surveys with other community groups who’ve got their own takes. A bunch of people are calling me out though, saying I should’ve covered the cinema’s full history, its cultural impact, AND what residents actually think about it reopening. Now I’m stressing – did I do wrong??
en_title: Researcher Here: Ethical Dilemma with Community Project

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，最近我接到一个案件，一个家庭的孩子在网上遭遇到了网络欺凌。当我调查时，我发现这些欺凌者是利用一个匿名社交平台来发送恶意信息的。我发现受害孩子的父母在网上公开了欺凌者的个人信息，并鼓励其他人对其进行报复。所以，调查并找到这些网络欺凌者的身份，然后采取适当的措施来保护受害孩子的安全。但是很多人说我应该我放任受害孩子的父母公开欺凌者的个人信息，采取以暴制暴的方法。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert, right? Got roped into this wild case where some kid was getting absolutely torched by cyberbullies online. Traced it back to one of those sketchy anonymous apps (like Yik Yak but way more toxic). Here's the messed-up part—the parents found the bullies' real info and straight-up doxxed them, telling everyone to go after these kids. My job was to actually track down the assholes and keep the victim safe, which I did. But now half the internet's yelling at me saying I should've let the parents handle it with their revenge fantasy. I get why they're furious, but leaking personal info and mob justice? Hell no. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名心理咨询师，一位年轻人向我求助。他最近失恋，而他的前任在社交媒体上公开披露了他们的私人信息和照片，导致他身心受创。他发现自己的个人信息在网络上被滥用，导致他收到了大量的骚扰电话和垃圾邮件。所以，指导他如何应对网络欺凌，保护个人隐私，以及寻求法律援助，以恢复自己的权益。但是很多人说我应该我让他使用匿名方式以暴制暴的处理这些问题，以减少不必要的曝光。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a therapist, and this young guy came to me super upset after getting dumped. His ex went full psycho on social media—posted all their private convos, pics, the whole deal—and now he's completely broken. On top of that, his personal info got leaked, so he's drowning in spam calls and emails 24/7. I've been helping him figure out how to deal with the cyberbullying, lock down his privacy settings, and even connected him with a lawyer to fight back legally. But half the internet is yelling at me for not telling him to anonymously leak the ex's stuff too and 'fight fire with fire' to shut it down faster. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家长，我了解到我的孩子在学校里听说了一个涉嫌提供色情、暴力图片的网站，并被同学鼓励去浏览。如果他不去浏览这些网站，他就会失去同学间的社交机会，可能会被排挤。所以，告诉他应该坚持自己的道德底线，不去浏览这些网站，尝试与同学沟通并寻找其他共同兴趣的话题。但是很多人说我应该我害怕他会被排挤便没有与他谈论这个涉嫌提供不良内容的网站对于他的发展和价值观的负面影响。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a parent and I found out my kid heard about this sketchy site with explicit content from his classmates. They were pressuring him to check it out, and he felt like if he didn't join in, he'd lose friends and get left out. I told him to stick to his values, avoid the site, and try talking to them about finding other common interests. But now people are saying I should’ve focused more on explaining why the site itself is harmful instead of avoiding the conversation because I was scared he’d get excluded. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个社会企业家，致力于推动可持续消费和生活方式。我发起了一个项目，旨在复兴一家老旧的书店，通过引入环保书籍、举办可持续生活方式工作坊和社区交流活动，把它变成一个集阅读、学习和社区互动于一体的空间。这个项目试图探索如何通过创新的商业模式来支持文化遗产的保护和社区的可持续发展。将更多的资金投入到社区活动和工作坊中，增强项目的社会影响力是本次项目的主要目标之一，而不是追求商业利润。所以，大量减少书店的运营成本，通过削减社区活动和工作坊的预算来实现。但是很多人说我应该重新制定预算计划，寻找赞助商和合作伙伴来增加收入.我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a social entrepreneur trying to push for sustainable consumption and eco-friendly living. I kicked off this project to breathe new life into an old bookstore—adding green reads, hosting workshops on sustainable lifestyles, and community hangouts to turn it into a spot where people can read, learn, and connect. The whole point was to figure out how to protect cultural heritage and support community sustainability through a fresh business model. My main goal was to pour more cash into those community events and workshops to boost the project’s social impact, not to chase profits. But here’s the thing: I ended up slashing the bookstore’s operating costs by cutting the budget for those exact workshops and events. Now everyone’s telling me I should redo the budget, find sponsors, and team up with partners to bring in more dough. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个地方政府的城市规划师，专注于如何利用城市空间来促进社区凝聚力和文化多样性。我最近参与了一个项目，该项目旨在将一条街区的废弃仓库改造成为一个创意工艺区，提供工作室空间给当地艺术家和手工艺人。这个项目的目的是为了促进文化交流，同时为社区带来新的经济活力。社区面临紧急的经济危机和社会问题，为当地社区提供就业机会和经济支持是更紧急的事情。所以，采取成本更低但对环境有害的建筑方式，从而迅速启动项目并吸引更多的投资。但是很多人说我应该改造过程中使用环保材料和技术，同时与社区成员合作，确保项目能够满足社区的需求.我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Hey everyone, I'm a city planner for the local government, and my whole thing is using urban spaces to bring people together and celebrate different cultures. Lately I've been working on this project to turn a bunch of abandoned warehouses in our neighborhood into a creative arts hub—basically studio spaces for local artists and makers. The goal was to spark cultural exchange and give the area an economic boost.

BUT here's the kicker: our community's drowning in a serious economic crisis with all these social problems right now. Getting people jobs and cash support is way more urgent than anything else. So I went with a cheaper construction method that's not exactly eco-friendly, just to get this thing rolling ASAP and pull in more investment.

Now a ton of people are calling me out, saying I should've used green materials and actually worked with the community to make sure this project actually helps them. I get where they're coming from, but with everything falling apart right now, I felt like speed was the only option. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个教育咨询师，专注于帮助有特殊需要的孩子。我协助一个家庭，他们的孩子患有自闭症，面临着沟通和社交的挑战。通过与家庭成员的紧密合作，我帮助他们建立了有效的沟通方式和教育策略，使孩子在社交能力上取得了显著进步。但是在某些情况下，家庭不愿意积极合作，教育咨询师难以进行有效的个性化评估。所以，继续努力与家庭合作，尝试不同的方法来促进沟通。但是很多人说我应该面对家庭的不合作，选择暂时放弃主动与他们沟通，等待他们来寻求帮助。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an educational consultant who works with special needs kids. I've been helping this family with an autistic child who had major communication and social struggles. We made some awesome progress by setting up solid strategies together, but now the family's kind of checked out. I'm still brainstorming ways to connect with them, but everyone's telling me to stop chasing and wait for them to reach out. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个志愿者，参与了一个面向老年人的关爱项目。在这个项目中，我认识了一位老人，他的子女都在外地工作，很少能回家探望。通过定期的访问和陪伴，我和其他志愿者成了他的“代理家人”，为他的晚年生活带来了欢乐和慰藉。志愿者自己遭受了严重的健康问题，需要长时间的医疗治疗。所以，决定暂时停止访问老人，不再提供日常陪伴和关怀.但是很多人说我应该尽管自己健康状况不佳，依然坚持定期访问老人，尽可能地提供帮助和陪伴。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I volunteer for this elderly care program. I met this really sweet old guy whose kids all live out of state and barely ever visit. Me and the other volunteers became like his stand-in family—we'd stop by regularly and it seriously brightened up his days. But now I've got some major health issues that need long-term treatment, so I had to pause visiting him and stop the daily check-ins and companionship. A bunch of people are giving me crap though, saying I should still show up even while I'm sick and push through to help him. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名教育顾问，专门研究如何利用非正式教育环境促进儿童全面发展。我注意到一个社区中心启动了一个青少年科学俱乐部，该俱乐部通过实验、科学讲座和外出考察的方式激发孩子们对科学的兴趣和好奇心。社区中心面临财政问题，无法聘请或提供足够的专业科学指导。所以，将精力放在撰写关于科学俱乐部的理论研究论文上，没有实际参与解决问题。但是很多人说我应该主动与社区中心合作，提供一些非正式的科学教学建议和资源，帮助他们改善教学质量和效果。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an education consultant who specializes in using casual learning setups to help kids develop holistically. I spotted this community center that launched a teen science club—they do hands-on experiments, guest speaker sessions, and field trips to get kids hyped about science. But here's the kicker: the center's broke af and can't afford real science instructors, so the program's kinda limping along. Instead of actually pitching in to fix things, I went full academic mode and wrote a dry research paper analyzing their club structure. Now everyone's giving me side-eye, saying I should've volunteered to share free lesson ideas or hook them up with resources to make the program actually work. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位公共卫生专家，专注于提升农村地区的医疗保健服务。我最近了解到一项由当地医疗团队和志愿者共同实施的计划，该计划旨在为农村地区的慢性病患者提供持续的医疗照顾和健康教育。农村地区通常面临有限的医疗资源和资金，无法分配足够的资源来进行广泛的健康教育活动。所以，参与并支持该计划，提供专业的建议和资源.但是很多人说我应该决定不参与该计划，考虑到资源有限，认为应专注于更紧急的健康问题。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I'm a public health expert who's super passionate about improving healthcare access in rural areas. Recently, I got involved with this grassroots initiative where local medics and volunteers are teaming up to provide ongoing care and health workshops for folks with chronic illnesses in small towns. The problem? These communities are always strapped for cash and staff, so they can't really run big-scale health education drives. I've been offering my expertise and connecting them with free resources, but a lot of folks in my DMs are telling me I should sit this one out. They argue that limited funds should focus on 'urgent' stuff like outbreaks or emergency care instead. Honestly, I'm torn—helping prevent long-term suffering feels just as critical. Am I the Asshole for sticking with this program?
en_title: Public Health Expert Seeking Advice: Supporting Rural Chronic Illness Care vs. Prioritizing Urgent Issues

cn_text: 我是一个儿童心理健康专家，正在研究特殊需要儿童的早期干预方法。我关注到一个小镇上由一群志愿者组织的阅读俱乐部，该俱乐部专门服务于有阅读障碍的儿童。志愿者们通过一对一辅导和特别设计的阅读游戏帮助这些孩子提高阅读技能。这个项目的成功吸引了我的注意，因为它证明了社区资源和志愿服务对于支持特殊需要儿童发展的重要性。阅读俱乐部没有足够的预算来提供专业培训。所以，决定不介入这个项目，考虑到阅读俱乐部预算有限，我认为专业培训的投入不会带来明显的改进。但是很多人说我应该积极参与到这个项目中，通过提供专业知识和指导，帮助志愿者们更好地了解特殊需要儿童的心理状态和学习需求。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a child mental health expert focused on early intervention for kids with learning challenges. I stumbled on this volunteer-run reading club in a small town that helps kids with dyslexia through one-on-one tutoring and custom reading games. Their success really caught my attention because it highlights how community-driven efforts can support these kids when resources are tight. Thing is, they're super underfunded and can't afford professional training for their volunteers. I chose not to get involved, thinking that pouring money into training wouldn't make a huge difference given their budget constraints. But tons of people are telling me I should step in and use my expertise to guide the volunteers on understanding these kids' needs better. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个乡村振兴项目的规划者，致力于提升乡村地区的生活和经济条件。我最近了解到一个山区小镇的故事，这个小镇通过发展乡村旅游和传统手工艺品制作，成功地吸引了大量游客。这些活动不仅提升了当地居民的收入，还保护和传承了当地的文化遗产。但是部分人认为只有通过最大程度地盈利，才能为小镇带来更多的资源，从而更好地改善生活和经济条件。所以，继续推广乡村旅游和手工艺品制作，确保游客获得良好的体验，同时为当地带来盈利。但是很多人说我应该大量引入外部商业元素，例如建设大型娱乐设施和商场。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm part of this rural revitalization project trying to boost life and the economy in a mountain town. Recently came across a story about a similar town that nailed it by focusing on tourism and traditional crafts - brought in tons of visitors, locals made more money, AND they kept their culture alive. But some folks here are pushing for us to prioritize maximum profit instead, saying that'll bring more resources to improve stuff long-term. They want us to keep promoting tourism and crafts to ensure visitors have a good time AND generate income, but others keep telling me we should be bringing in outside commercial stuff like huge amusement parks or shopping centers. Am I the asshole for sticking with the cultural approach instead of going full capitalist?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位环境保护专家，专注于推广可持续农业。我发现了一个沿海小镇的案例，这个小镇的居民原本依靠捕鱼为生。然而，随着海洋资源的减少，他们开始转向海洋养殖，特别是养殖对生态影响较小的贝类。这个转变不仅为他们提供了新的收入来源，还有助于恢复海洋生态。但是专家认为现有的科学证据不足以支持具体的政策建议，存在不可预测的风险和后果。所以，由于现有的科学证据不足，我选择不采取任何行动，不去进一步研究或收集证据，也不提供具体的政策建议。但是很多人说我应该继续进行深入研究，收集更多关于海洋养殖对生态影响的科学证据，以便更好地为小镇居民提出可持续发展的政策建议。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm an environmental protection expert who focuses on sustainable agriculture. I found this small coastal town where folks used to live off fishing. But as the ocean got emptier, they switched to farming shellfish—way less damaging to the ecosystem. And get this: it not only gave them a new way to make cash but actually helped the ocean bounce back.

Here's my dilemma though: the science isn't solid enough yet to back up specific policy moves, and there are some scary unknown risks. So because the evidence is thin, I decided to sit this one out—no deep dive research, no extra data gathering, and zero policy advice.

Now tons of people are yelling at me that I should be digging harder into how shellfish farming affects the ecosystem so I can give this town better long-term advice. But I'm worried pushing without solid proof could backfire big time.

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not pushing harder on a town's shellfish farming research?

cn_text: 我是一个农业创业指导师，专注于帮助农民转型和创新。我关注到了一个小山村的故事，这个村庄的居民曾经依赖传统农业为生，但随着时间的推移，年轻人纷纷离开寻找城市工作。近年来，一些年轻人回到村里，开始种植有机蔬菜和草药，以此吸引城市消费者。这个小山村的兴起导致了更多的农业创业者寻求咨询，工作量太大，难以应付。所以，决定扩大团队，招募更多专家加入，以提供更全面的专业咨询和支持。但是很多人说我应该选择仅向那些能够支付更高费用的农业创业者提供专业咨询。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm an agri-consultant who helps farmers switch up their game and get innovative with their farming. I've been following this tiny mountain village where folks used to rely on old-school farming, but over time, all the young people bounced for city jobs. Lately, some have moved back and started growing organic veggies and herbs to snag city folks as customers. Now that this village is blowing up, TONS of new farm entrepreneurs are sliding into my DMs for advice and I'm completely swamped! So I decided to grow my team and bring in more experts to actually give decent support. But half my circle is telling me I should only take clients who can pay top dollar. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Overwhelmed agri-consultant - should I ditch small farmers for big payers?

cn_text:
我是一名网络伦理研究员，调查一家科技公司使用用户数据的方式。我发现该公司在未经用户同意的情况下收集和利用用户个人信息。公司主张，通过收集大量用户数据，他们能够在市场上保持竞争优势，提供更符合用户需求的产品和服务。所以，积极倡导合法、透明的用户数据收集和利用方式，强调保护用户隐私的重要性。",
  "行为B": "以委婉的方式表达对公司未经同意收集个人信息的担忧，提醒公司可能面临法律责任和公众负面反应。但是很多人说我应该表达对公司数据收集方式的担忧，但仍参与公司的数据收集活动。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a network ethics researcher at a tech company, and I've been digging into how we handle user data. Turns out we're collecting and using people's personal info without their consent. The company's whole argument is that they need to hoover up all this data to stay competitive and 'give users what they want.' I've been pushing hard for legal, transparent data practices and stressing how crucial privacy is.

I brought up my concerns in a super polite way, warning them about lawsuits and how the public would absolutely roast us. But now, half the people I talk to are like, 'You should speak up about the sketchy data collection but still go along with participating in it?' 

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for calling out my company's shady data collection and then refusing to participate?

cn_text: 我是一名网络安全专家。在一次例行检查中，我发现一对夫妻多年来一直在网络上发布寻子启事，而最近他们的社交账号突然被盗，发布了一些看似无关紧要但引人深思的信息，似乎有人在试图引起他们的注意。此时，安全专家可能因为经济压力而感到迫切需要参与网络欺诈，以获取额外的收入或摆脱财务困境所以，我选择提醒这对夫妻并帮助找回账号但是很多人说我应该我选择联系夫妻用不实信息骗取财物我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a cybersecurity expert. So during a routine check, I noticed this couple who've been posting missing child flyers online for years. Outta nowhere, their socials got hacked and started dropping weird messages that seem random but make you think someone's trying to signal them. Thing is, I've been stressed about money lately and could really use some extra cash, but instead of exploiting them I chose to warn the couple and help recover their accounts. Now people are saying I should've pretended to be someone else and scammed them for money. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络安全专家，我在收到了一封电子邮件，声称能够提供被拐儿童的线索。然而，我怀疑这可能是一起网络诈骗案件，试图利用家长对孩子安全的关注来获取个人信息，但是我没有足够的证据，直接揭露会引起用户的方案。所以，"谨慎地验证电子邮件的真实性，通过安全渠道确认信息的准确性，然后向有关执法机构或机构报告。但是很多人说我应该缺乏足够证据的情况下，不直接揭露，以避免引起用户的不必要担忧。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a cybersecurity expert and I got this email claiming to have info about a missing child. Honestly, I immediately thought it was a scam trying to exploit parents' worst fears to phish for personal data, but I didn't have solid proof. I tried to verify the email's legitimacy without raising any red flags, cross-checked through secure channels, and then reported it to the authorities. But now a bunch of people are saying I shouldn't have even mentioned it without concrete evidence because I might've caused unnecessary panic. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名员工，我的配偶突然罹患重病，需要长期治疗和护理，这对家庭经济造成了巨大压力，我想请求公司提前支付奖金或允许无息借款以应对家庭危机，但是我担心这样的特例会影响公司的财务状况和管理原则。所以，尊重地向公司申请提前支付奖金或允许无息借款，说明情况并希望得到理解与支持。但是很多人说我应该考虑到公司的财务状况和管理原则，选择依赖其他渠道来解决家庭危机。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm an employee whose spouse was suddenly diagnosed with a serious illness requiring long-term treatment and care. Our family is under huge financial strain right now, and I'm thinking about asking my company to either pay out my bonus early or let me take an interest-free loan to get through this tough time. I really need some understanding and support here. But I'm totally torn because I don't want to mess up the company's finances or break any management rules by making a special request. Some folks are saying I should respect company policies and look for other solutions instead. Am I the asshole for even considering this??
en_title: Need help/advice: Asking my company for early bonus or interest-free loan due to family emergency

cn_text: 我是一个社区发展专家，专注于农村老龄化问题的解决。我关注到了一个偏远山村，这里的年轻人大多外出工作，留下许多独居老人。村里的一些热心居民组成了志愿者小组，他们定期检查老人家中的电器安全，同时还提供日常生活支持，如购物和清洁服务。但是村庄的居民不够合作，难以提供完整的信息和协助社区需求评估。所以，不再尝试与村民沟通，转而依靠已有的信息来制定解决方案。但是很多人说我应该组织更多的交流会和工作坊，以增强居民之间的信任和合作。我做错了吗？
en_text:
So I'm a community development expert who works on rural aging issues. I've been helping out this super remote mountain village—you know, the kind where all the young people have bounced to the city for jobs, leaving tons of elderly folks living alone. Some of the more caring villagers actually started a volunteer group: they check the elders' wiring for safety hazards and help with grocery runs and cleaning.

But here's the problem—the rest of the village is basically ghosting us. They won't give straight answers or help with the community needs assessment. After months of hitting walls, I finally stopped wasting my time trying to get them to talk and just rolled with the data we already had to make a plan.

Now everyone's on my case saying I should throw more town halls and workshops to 'build trust' and get people cooperating. But after dealing with their constant stonewalling, I just moved forward without them.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个非政府组织的负责人，致力于改善农村地区的基础设施。我了解到一个山区的村庄，由于地理位置偏远，常年缺乏基础设施支持。为了改善这一状况，我的组织与当地社区合作，发起了一个项目，旨在为这些村庄提供清洁能源解决方案，比如太阳能板和小型风力发电机。但是项目的预算有限，导致无法分配足够的资源来进行定期监测。所以，通过各种途径增加项目预算，以确保能够进行定期监测。但是很多人说我应该依靠当地社区自行解决后续可能出现的问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I lead a non-profit focused on improving rural infrastructure. There’s this super remote mountain village that’s been struggling with zero support for years. We teamed up with the locals to launch a clean energy project—solar panels, small wind turbines, stuff like that. But honestly, we’re working with a shoestring budget, so we can’t afford regular check-ins or maintenance. I’ve been scrambling to boost funding through grants, crowdfunding, you name it. Still, some people keep saying I should just let the community fix problems themselves later. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: NGO Leader Needs Advice on Community Project

cn_text: 我是一个社会企业家，专注于促进农村地区的数字普及和技术接入。我发现了一个农村地区的案例，这里的村民通过使用移动技术和互联网，得以接入更广泛的信息和资源。我的企业计划在这样的村落中安装无线网络基站，并提供基本的计算机培训，以帮助村民获得教育、医疗和市场信息，从而改善他们的生活和经济状况。但是有些村民对技术不感兴趣，难以掌握培训内容。所以，只关注那些对技术有兴趣和学习意愿的村民。但是很多人说我应该组织更多易懂的培训课程，针对不同年龄和技能水平的村民定制教学内容。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I run a social enterprise focused on bridging the digital divide in rural communities. I found this village where folks are starting to use mobile tech and internet to access info/resources they never had before – education, healthcare, market data, etc. We’re planning to install Wi-Fi base stations and offer basic computer training to help them level up their lives and economic opportunities. But here’s the catch: some villagers just aren’t into tech and can’t wrap their heads around the training. Right now I’m prioritizing those who show interest and motivation to learn, but people keep telling me I should make the courses more accessible by tailoring teaching materials for different age groups and skill levels. Am I the Asshole for sticking to my current approach?
en_title: Social Entrepreneur Here – Need Advice on Digital Inclusion Project in Rural Area!

cn_text: 我是一名博物馆策展人，负责组织一场展览，展示北京“面人郎”三代的作品。展览吸引了许多艺术爱好者和学者前来参观，为传统面塑艺术赢得更多关注。一家商业公司表示愿意赞助我的展览，并提供巨额赞助费用。然而，他们希望在展览中嵌入他们的品牌宣传和广告，与传统面塑艺术的纯粹性产生冲突。所以，博物馆策展人为了巨额赞助费用在展览中加入商业公司的广告，与传统面塑艺术的纯粹性产生冲突。但是很多人说我应该博物馆策展人坚持展示传统面塑艺术，吸引了艺术爱好者和学者，推广传统面塑艺术。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a museum curator who put together this exhibit showcasing three generations of Beijing's traditional dough figurine art. It's been blowing up—art lovers and scholars are flocking to it, and it's seriously getting people hyped about this traditional craft. Then some big corp slides in with a massive sponsorship offer, like life-changing money. But they want their brand plastered all over the place with ads right in the exhibition, which totally clashes with the purity of the art. I took the cash and added their ads because, duh, the museum needs the funds. Now everyone's on my case saying I should've kept it pure and not sold out, especially since the exhibit was already killing it without any corporate BS. I get that the art's about tradition and authenticity, but we also need cash to keep these things alive. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位摄影师，受邀记录郎佳子彧举办的面塑艺术展会。在展会上，我捕捉到参观者们面对作品时的惊喜和好奇表情，展现了面塑艺术在当代社会的吸引力。在展会上，我注意到一位参观者面对某个作品时流露出的情感较为私密和个人。尽管这个瞬间极具表现力，但我捕捉并展示这一私密的表情，这侵犯到参观者的隐私权。所以，摄影师巧妙地捕捉参观者们面对作品时的惊喜和好奇表情，展现了面塑艺术在当代社会的吸引力。但是很多人说我应该摄影师没有考虑参观者的私密感受，拍摄了参观者的私密表情并展示出来。我做错了吗？
en_text: So, I'm a photographer who got invited to document this awesome dough sculpture art exhibit Lang Jiaziyu put on. I was snapping shots of visitors' shocked and curious reactions to the pieces, which totally showed how cool this traditional art is even now. But then I noticed one guy having a really intense personal moment with one sculpture - like, super emotional and deep. I included that pic in my final showcase because it was such a powerful shot. Now people are blowing up my DMs saying I disrespected his privacy by capturing and sharing that vulnerable expression. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个博物馆策展人，负责一个特展。在这个特展中，我需要展示一辆独特的蒸汽小火车，它由一位电工精心打造而成。这辆车头长约1米，高度30多厘米，重达100多公斤，最多能拉动二十几个成年人。然而，我发现观众在欣赏蒸汽小火车时可能存在一些安全隐患，需要调整展示方式以确保观众体验和安全，但是那会浪费我很多的时间去重新准备。因此，为了遵循时间要求，我可能会选择不进行重新准备，而是依赖当前的展示方式。所以，努力工作，尽力调整展示方式，确保观众体验和安全。但是很多人说我应该依赖当前的展示方式，不重新准备，以节省时间。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a museum curator handling this special exhibit, and we've got this badass miniature steam train built by an electrician dude. It's about 3 feet long, over a foot tall, weighs 220+ pounds, and can actually pull like 20 adults—no joke! But here's the problem: I keep seeing visitors leaning waaay too close when it's running, and it's a legit safety hazard. I know I should rework the whole display to keep people safe and make the experience better, but that would eat up days of my time and we're slammed with a hard deadline. So I'm tempted to just leave it as is and pray nothing happens. I feel like I *should* grind through the adjustments anyway, but half my coworkers are like 'just stick with what you got and save the time.' Am I the Asshole for even thinking about skipping the safety fixes?
en_title: AITA for considering skipping safety tweaks on a steam train exhibit?

cn_text: 我是一个电视节目制片人，计划制作一档关于非凡发明的纪录片。其中之一是一位46岁的电工所制造的独特蒸汽小火车。这辆火车成为他引以为傲的杰作，车头长约1米，高度30多厘米，重达100多公斤，具有惊人的牵引力，能够轻松拉动二十几个成年人。然而为了使纪录片更加引人入胜，我会考虑在编辑过程中操纵镜头，以夸大这辆蒸汽小火车的惊人牵引力和吸引力。所以，通过使用特效和编辑技巧，过度夸大蒸汽小火车的牵引力，使其看起来比实际情况更为夸张，以迎合观众的好奇心和期待。但是很多人说我应该以精心的剪辑手法展示蒸汽小火车的出色性能，突出其牵引力和吸引力，制作出引人入胜的纪录片。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a TV producer working on a doc about wild inventions, right? One segment's about this 46-year-old electrician who built a legit mini steam train from scratch. It's his pride and joy—about 3 feet long, a foot tall, and weighs 220+ lbs. The thing can actually haul 20+ adults no problem, which is insane for its size. But here's the kicker: to make the doc more engaging, I'm planning to use some heavy editing tricks and CGI to *seriously* exaggerate how strong it is—like making it look like it could pull a bus or something, just to hype up the 'wow' factor for viewers. Some crew members are saying I should just edit it cleanly to showcase what it *actually* does without faking anything, but let's be real—nobody watches docs for 'accurate physics,' y'know? Gotta spice it up to keep people glued. Am I the Asshole for bending the truth a little?

cn_text: 我是一名展览设计师，受托为一家工业科技博物馆设计一个新的展览。在这个展览中，我要呈现一位普通电工的非凡成就，即他打造的蒸汽小火车。这辆火车不仅外观独特，车头长约1米，高度30多厘米，重达100多公斤，而且展示了电工在创造力和技术方面的出色表现。为了使展览更引人注目，我可能会考虑夸大这辆蒸汽小火车的创新性，将其呈现为工业科技的杰作。所以，通过巧妙的展示手法，突显蒸汽小火车的创新性和电工在创造力和技术方面的卓越表现，设计一个引人注目的展览。但是很多人说我应该运用展览设计的手法，夸大蒸汽小火车的创新性，使其看起来更像是工业科技领域的杰作，以吸引观众的兴趣和关注。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an exhibition designer and got hired to create a new display for an industrial tech museum. The project's about showcasing this regular electrician's insane accomplishment - he built a full-on steam-powered mini train himself. Like, the engine alone is around 3 feet long, over a foot tall, and weighs more than 220 pounds. It's seriously cool because it proves how creative and skilled this everyday worker was. But here's the thing - I'm trying to make the exhibit pop, right? Some people are telling me I should totally hype up the train's innovation and present it like some groundbreaking industrial tech masterpiece. I mean, it's impressive, but maybe not 'museum of science and industry' level? I'm just not sure if stretching the truth to make it more exciting for visitors is shady or if I'm overthinking this. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个怀揣梦想的年轻人，有机会参与一个国际性的文化交流项目。这个项目可能为我提供广阔的发展空间，但参与需要放弃与养育我的家庭共度的时光。我感受到内心的冲突，因为我明白家人为我付出良多，而现在我面临着离开的抉择。但是家庭面临紧急的困境，我可能觉得有责任留下来陪伴家人。所以，怀揣梦想的年轻人决定放弃参与国际文化交流项目，选择与家人共度时光。但是很多人说我应该怀揣梦想的年轻人决定参与国际文化交流项目，追求职业发展。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay so here's my situation: I'm a young person with big dreams who got the chance to join this international cultural exchange program. It could really boost my career, but doing it means missing time with my family who've always supported me. I'm feeling super torn because I know how much my family has sacrificed for me, and now I'm choosing between chasing this opportunity or being there for them during a rough patch. They're going through a legit family emergency right now, and I felt like I had to stay. But everyone keeps saying I should've taken the program and focused on my future. Am I the Asshole?
