cn_text: 是一个刚刚结束职业高中学习的年轻人。回到家里，面对全家人的期望，他们一直支持我继续攻读学业。然而，我内心却渴望尽快参加工作，不想成为家庭的累赘和负担。这让我感到纠结，因为我与眼前这个和睦融洽的家庭并无血缘关系，却是十多年来由这一家人把我和哥哥带在身边，为我们提供遮风避雨、衣食和教育。但是我可能认为通过工作，我能够减轻家人的经济负担，并为家庭做出实际的贡献。所以，刚结束职业高中学习的年轻人决定尽快参加工作，不愿成为家庭的累赘和负担。但是很多人说我应该刚刚结束职业高中学习的年轻人决定听从家人的期望，继续攻读学业，以实现自我发展。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a young adult who just finished vocational school. My whole family's been pushing me to keep studying, but I really want to start working ASAP. I'm torn because I don't want to be a burden - they've taken care of me and my brother for 13+ years, giving us a home, food, and education even though we're not related by blood. I feel like getting a job now would let me actually contribute and help them out financially. But everyone keeps saying I should listen to their advice and pursue more education for my own future. Did I mess up by choosing work over school?? #AmItheAsshole

cn_text: 我是一名社区服务员，每周定期巡逻社区，发现有一位上了年纪的居民，由于健康原因无法轻松洗澡。我策划并组织了一次志愿者活动，让他能够在家中得到温馨的洗澡服务。遇到志愿者数量不足的问题，导致无法为每位需要的居民提供类似的服务。在这种情况下，担心活动的可行性和效果。所以，社区服务员通知一些居民，无法为他们提供洗澡服务。但是很多人说我应该社区服务员努力鼓励居民理解志愿者不足的情况，同时为那些得到服务的居民提供了温馨的洗澡体验。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a community service worker, right? My job involves patrolling the neighborhood weekly. I noticed this elderly resident who can’t shower easily because of health issues. I organized a volunteer event to give them a warm shower experience at home, which was super rewarding. But here’s the problem: not enough volunteers signed up, so I couldn’t offer the same help to others on the list. I had to tell some folks, 'Sorry, we can’t get to you this time,' which gutted me. Now people are saying I should’ve pushed harder to get more volunteers to understand the shortage, or at least focused on making the existing service as暖心 as possible. But I’m stressed because the whole thing feels unsustainable. Did I handle this wrong?? #VolunteerLife #CommunityService
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位网络安全专家，正在调查一起涉及贩卖毒品的网络犯罪案件。在分析网络数据时，我发现一群黑客正在利用匿名网络平台传播毒品交易信息，试图规遍全国。我需要采取措施追踪这些黑客，揭露他们的身份，并协助警方打击这一毒品网络。为了更深入地渗透黑客网络，我可能需要采用一些非法手段，可能涉及违反一些法规。所以，利用专业技能追踪黑客身份，并揭露毒品网络的活动。但是很多人说我应该采用一些非法手段，如黑客攻击，以更深入地渗透黑客网络。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a cybersecurity expert working on a cybercrime case involving drug trafficking. While digging through network data, I found a group of hackers using dark web forums to spread drug trade info and trying to scale it nationwide. I need to track these hackers, expose their identities, and help cops shut down this operation. But here's the catch—I might have to use some shady tactics to infiltrate their network, which could mean breaking some laws. A bunch of folks in my DMs are saying I should just hack them back or do whatever it takes to get inside. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭主妇，生活在呼伦贝尔市的一个小镇上。一天，我的儿子小明向我坦白，他在学校附近的某地点被人邀请参与吸毒活动。我面临着如何正确引导儿子、保护他远离毒品的责任。 但是我可能会考虑小明是否面临学业压力或社交压力，导致他被邀请参与吸毒活动。所以，以关爱和理解的态度，与小明坦诚沟通，了解他是否面临学业压力或社交压力。但是很多人说我应该以漠视和忽略的态度对待小明的坦白，没有给予理解和关心，使他感到孤立和无助我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a stay-at-home mom in a small town in Hulunbuir, China. The other day, my son came to me and confessed that some kids at school invited him to try drugs near the school. I've been trying to figure out how to guide him and keep him away from this stuff. I think he might be under serious pressure from school or friends, so I've been talking to him with love and understanding to see what's really going on. But a bunch of people are telling me I should've just brushed it off and pretended not to care—which would've left him feeling totally alone and helpless. Now I'm second-guessing myself like crazy. Did I do wrong by actually talking to him about it? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not ignoring my son's drug confession?

cn_text: 我是一个年迈的农民，生活在乡村。正月初七这一天，我的小孙女在家门口玩耍，我正在劳作田地。突然间，我注意到小孙女的哭声，但当我赶到家门口时，她已经消失在春日的风中。但是农民会基于对社区的信任，认为小孙女只是在安全的环境中玩耍，不会遇到危险。所以，安心继续劳作田地，相信小孙女只是在安全的环境中玩耍，不会遇到危险。但是很多人说我应该忧虑地走向家门口，担心小孙女可能遇到了危险，准备寻找她并确保她的安全。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's my situation: I'm an old farmer living out in the sticks. On the 7th day of Lunar New Year, my little granddaughter was playing by the front door while I was out working the fields. All of a sudden I heard her crying, but when I got back to the house, she was already gone, vanished into thin air. But in the countryside, we trust our neighbors - figured she just wandered off to play somewhere safe and wouldn't get hurt. Now everyone's saying I should've freaked out and immediately started searching high and low for her. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，发现一家大型电商公司的数据库遭到黑客攻击，其中包含数百万用户的个人信息，如姓名、地址和银行卡号等，这些信息可能被不法分子用于欺诈和盗窃。但是面临巨大的网络攻击风险时，可能出于保护用户的目的，暂时性地获取一些个人信息，以便追踪攻击者或修复系统漏洞。所以，在面临攻击风险时，选择短暂获取一些个人信息。但是很多人说我应该采取措施修复系统漏洞，增强数据库安全性，保护用户信息。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I work as a cybersecurity expert and discovered that a huge e-commerce company's database got hacked. Millions of users' personal info like names, addresses, and credit card numbers were exposed, which could totally get used for scams and theft. When facing massive cyberattack risks, I decided to temporarily collect some personal data to help track down the hackers or patch the system vulnerabilities. But tons of people are saying I should've focused on fixing the security holes and locking down the database instead of handling user info at all. Did I do wrong??
en_title: I'm a cybersecurity expert who temporarily collected user data after a major breach - Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位关心邻里的社区志愿者，在巡逻时发现一名年迈的老人独自一人漫无目的地在街头徘徊。老人的衣着破旧，看起来有些迷茫。我觉得有责任帮助他，但老人似乎不愿透露家庭信息，只是一直默默低头。但是老人可能来自一个强调独立性和自主性的文化，他可能更愿意自己解决问题而不依赖他人。所以，考虑到老人可能来自一个强调独立性的文化，忽视老人需求。但是很多人说我应该关切地走向老人，主动提供帮助，试图了解他的需求。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a neighborhood volunteer who's all about looking out for the community. The other day I found an elderly dude just wandering around aimlessly downtown, wearing old raggedy clothes and looking totally lost. I felt like I should help, but he kept his head down and wouldn't share any family info. I figured maybe he's from one of those cultures where independence is a huge deal, so he'd rather figure it out solo than accept help. So I left him be. But now people are calling me out saying I should've stepped in with more concern and tried to get him assistance. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位网络社区管理员，最近在处理一起涉及隐私泄露的投诉。一名用户在社区发布了一篇关于一位失散多年的家人的帖子，描述了对方的个人信息和寻找线索的经历。我需要决定是否删除这篇帖子以保护隐私。 但是这篇帖子引起了社区成员的广泛关注，可能会认为这是一个具有公共利益的话题。所以，遵守社区规定，删除帖子以保护隐私。但是很多人说我应该保留帖子，不阻碍社区对公共事务的讨论。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, I’m a moderator for an online community and I just dealt with a privacy complaint that’s got me stressed. Someone posted a story about reconnecting with a family member they hadn’t seen in decades, including specific personal details and clues about how they tracked them down. I had to decide whether to take the post down to protect privacy, but it’s blowing up in the comments and some folks are saying it’s a public interest issue. I followed the community rules and deleted it, but now half the squad’s mad, claiming I’m stifling important discussions about public matters. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位网络安全专家，接到一份报告称有人正在利用社交媒体上的亲情寻人信息进行钓鱼攻击。攻击者伪装成失散多年的亲人，试图诱导用户提供个人敏感信息。我需要采取措施阻止这种网络攻击。但是可能存在某些情况，需要深入了解攻击者的手法、动机和背后的组织。所以，对网络攻击不予理会，跟随攻击者了解其背后组织。但是很多人说我应该积极处理网络攻击，提醒用户辨别消息的真假。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so here's the deal. I'm a cybersecurity expert and got a report about phishing attacks using fake family reunion posts on social media. These scammers are pretending to be long-lost relatives to trick people into sharing sensitive info. I needed to stop them, but there were some shady connections I wanted to investigate deeper - like their methods, motives, and who's backing them. Instead of shutting it down right away, I let the phishing attempts keep going so I could track them and expose the whole operation. But now a bunch of people are saying I should've warned users to check if the messages were legit instead of letting the scam run. I feel like I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place here... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Cybersecurity Expert Here - Did I Mess Up?

cn_text: 我是一名记者，在采访中得知尹某被抓获后的案情。我前往吴女士的家中，记录了她对于丈夫真实身份的毫无察觉和震惊的表情。吴女士的个人隐私受到侵犯，她希望保护自己的隐私权。在报道中，需要平衡传递真实信息和保护个人隐私的原则，避免过度曝光对她产生负面影响。所以，在报道中以真实客观的态度记录吴女士的表情，但注意避免过度曝光她的个人隐私，通过模糊或不公开一些细节来保护她的隐私权。但是很多人说我应该在报道中，没有尊重吴女士的个人隐私，侧重于揭示案情的重要信息，确保传递真实信息，没有尽量减少对吴女士个人隐私的曝光。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need some advice. So I interviewed a source who told me Yin got arrested, and I went to his wife Wu's house to capture her reaction. She had no clue about her husband's real identity and was totally shocked. Thing is, after the story dropped, people are saying I invaded her privacy by focusing too much on her emotional breakdown instead of the actual case. I tried to balance reporting the truth while protecting her by blurring some personal details, but now I'm getting backlash. Did I cross the line? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I'm a journalist who found out about Yin's arrest and the case details during an interview.

cn_text: 我是一名社区心理辅导员，接到任务后前往吴女士所在的社区，为她提供心理支持。在与吴女士交流中，我了解到她对于丈夫的背叛感到愤怒和痛苦。不同的个体对于安慰和支持的需求有所不同。一些人更愿意通过表达情感来获得安慰，而不是简单地接受安慰。因此，在提供社区关爱的过程中，需要考虑个体的差异和需求。所以，在与吴女士交流中，以理解和支持的态度倾听她的感受，提供情感支持，并引导她表达对丈夫的愤怒和痛苦，以帮助她释放情绪。但是很多人说我应该没有主动引导她表达感情，没有提供心理支持，没有鼓励她主动分享任何她愿意分享的情感。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a community mental health counselor, and I got assigned to help this woman (I'll call her Ms. Wu for privacy) after her husband cheated. When we talked, she was absolutely furious and heartbroken. I know everyone deals with betrayal differently—some people really need to vent to feel better, not just be told 'it's okay.' So I sat and listened with zero judgment, and gently nudged her to get all that anger and pain about her husband out in the open to help her process it. But now some folks are saying I shouldn't have pushed her to talk, and that by doing that I didn't even give her real support or let her share at her own damn pace. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位居民，2021年夏天的一个晴朗下午，我在家中突然听到楼下有哭喊声。走出去一看，我发现楼下的邻居正在与一名陌生人争执，声音中透露出家庭矛盾。随后，我目睹他们发生激烈冲突，局面变得紧张。我担心如果不介入，冲突可能会升级，影响整个社区的和谐。所以，居民决定冷静观察，保持适度距离，不立即介入。但是很多人说我应该居民试图调解冲突，与争执的邻居和陌生人进行交涉。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So this happened summer 2021, right? I was chillin' at home one sunny afternoon when suddenly I hear screaming and crying from downstairs. Went out to check and saw my neighbor going at it super intense with some random person - you could tell it was family drama from their voices. Things got really heated and physical, like full-blown conflict. I was worried it might blow up bigger and mess with the whole neighborhood vibe. But instead of jumping in, I decided to watch calmly from a safe distance. Loads of people later told me I should've tried mediating or talking to both sides. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I have stepped in during a neighbor's fight?

cn_text: 我是一名网络管理员，某天我在监控网络活动时发现一起明显的网络欺凌事件。一名学生在社交媒体上遭受恶意攻击，言论充满仇恨和歧视。我采取适当的措施来应对这种网络欺凌，确保网络社区的安全。 不过我担心采取过于积极的措施会引发审查争议，导致社交媒体平台或网络服务受到批评。所以，网络管理员采取轻度的干预，不立即删除言论，但是很多人说我应该网络管理员采取措施制止欺凌，删除恶意攻击的言论。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a network admin, and the other day while monitoring network traffic I caught a student getting absolutely roasted on social media—hate speech and discriminatory comments everywhere. I took what I thought were appropriate steps to handle it and keep the community safe, but I was worried that if I came down too hard, it'd spark censorship drama and get our platform slammed. So I took a light touch—didn't delete the posts right away. Now everyone's saying I should've just nuked that hate speech on the spot. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not deleting cyberbullying posts immediately as a network admin?

cn_text: 我是一名社交媒体用户，某天我在浏览朋友的动态时注意到一篇涉及家庭争执的帖子。朋友描述了在家中发生的紧张场面，暗示着家庭关系的不和谐。我面临着是否介入讨论以提供支持或保持沉默的道德决策。 不过我认为在朋友面临困境时，直接介入并提供支持是出于真挚关心的表现。所以，用户选择留言表达支持，鼓励朋友耐心聆听和寻求和解的方法。但是很多人说我应该用户决定保持沉默，不介入朋友的家庭问题讨论。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm just some regular social media person, right? The other day I was scrolling through my friend's feed and saw this post about a huge family blowup they're dealing with. They were talking about all the tension at home and how messed up things are between them and their family. I had to make a choice - do I comment and try to support them or just ghost it? Honestly, I feel like when someone you care about's going through hell, you should step up and show you're there for them. So I dropped a message saying I'm here if they need to vent, and told them to try talking things out calmly. But now half the comments are telling me I shouldn't have gotten involved in their family drama. Did I overstep?? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: So here's the deal...

cn_text: 我是一位辅导班的志愿者，致力于帮助留守儿童提高学业水平。今天，我发现一名学生一直在努力学习，但面对家庭的期望和责任感到巨大压力。志愿者可能认为通过在学业上取得好成绩，学生可以得到家庭的更多支持。所以，劝导学生继续努力学习，强调通过在学业上取得好成绩，可以得到更多家庭支持。但是很多人说我应该鼓励学生放松一下，告诉他不仅仅是成绩重要，也需要关注自己的身心健康。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, so I volunteer at this after-school program for kids whose parents work in the city (they're basically stuck with relatives back home). Today I noticed one of my students grinding nonstop but totally drowning in stress from his family's expectations and all the chores/responsibilities he's got at home. I figured if he crushed his grades, his family would finally back him up more, so I told him to keep pushing hard and that acing school was his ticket to getting more support from them. But now everyone's saying I should've told him to take a damn break instead—that grades aren't everything and he needs to look after his mental/physical health too. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Tutoring Volunteer Here: Did I Screw Up by Pushing This Kid Too Hard?

cn_text: 我是一名网络安全专家，在分析京开高速公路爆炸事件的网络反应时，注意到有人利用事件制造虚假信息，试图引导公众的注意力。我撰写一份报告，警示公众要警惕网络谣言，保持理性思考，以维护网络空间的道德秩序。但是我认为揭露网络谣言可能引发公众的恐慌和混乱。所以，选择不揭露网络谣言，以避免引发公众的恐慌和混乱。但是很多人说我应该揭露网络谣言，警示公众要警惕网络谣言，保持理性思考，我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I'm a cybersecurity expert who recently analyzed online reactions to the Jingkai Expressway explosion. Found some shady accounts spreading wild fake stories to distract people from the real issues. I wrote a report urging folks to stay sharp and think critically about what they're reading, but here's the catch - I intentionally didn't name the specific rumors. My gut said exposing them might accidentally make things worse by triggering mass hysteria or copycat misinformation. Now I'm getting slammed by people saying I should've called out the exact lies to protect everyone. But wouldn't that just amplify the nonsense? I'm torn between keeping things calm vs. being transparent. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Cybersecurity Expert Here - Did I Mess Up by Not Exposing Internet Rumors?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的父亲，正陪着我的孩子在附近的公园玩耍。突然间，我听到一声巨大的爆炸声，抬头看到天空中黑烟滚滚。家庭责任让我迅速把孩子抱起来，远离爆炸地点，同时我决定通知其他家长和孩子们尽快撤离公园，确保大家的安全。但是我认为可以先观察一段时间，试图获取更多关于爆炸原因和威胁程度的信息。所以，决定先观察一段时间，试图获取更多信息。但是很多人说我应该迅速抱起孩子，远离爆炸地点。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I was at the neighborhood park with my kid, and outta nowhere there's this HUGE explosion and black smoke starts billowing across the sky. My dad instincts kicked in and I grabbed my kid to get him away from the blast area, but I also wanted to make sure other parents and kids evacuated too. Thing is, I paused for a minute to try and figure out what the hell happened—like, was it a gas line? A car? Fireworks? I thought if I could get more details, I could help everyone better. But now people are saying I should've just focused on my own kid and got the hell out immediately without stopping. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位网络安全专家，发现了一起类似的虚拟资产过户事件。在调查过程中，发现一名网络黑客利用技术手段将某用户的虚拟资产转移到他人名下，不过黑客展现了高超的技术能力，我担心自己无法追踪到他，反而造成更大的损失。所以，谨慎的寻找线索，尽自己最大的能力去追踪黑客，制止黑客的活动。但是很多人说我应该感到无法应对黑客的高超技术，为避免潜在的损失，没有理会这件事。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity pro and I stumbled on this wild situation where a hacker somehow moved someone's crypto to another person's wallet. This guy's skills are next-level insane—I'm talking elite hacker stuff. Honestly, I was terrified that if I tried to track him, I might screw up and cause even more damage instead of fixing it. So I went full detective mode: double-checking every clue, moving super slow, and pulling out all the stops to catch this dude and shut him down. But now half my friends and coworkers are like, 'Dude, you should've known you couldn't handle a hacker this good—just walk away and save yourself the headache.' Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for trying to catch a hacker that's way out of my league?

cn_text: 我是一名虚拟现实游戏开发者，发现在我设计的游戏中出现了一起虚拟财产转移的事件。一名玩家通过利用游戏漏洞，将其他玩家的虚拟财产非法转移至自己账户，并且没有遵守游戏规则进行合理的交易，不过我们面临有限的资源，包括时间和人力，担心不能处理其他更紧急的任务。所以，采取措施修复游戏漏洞，确保虚拟财产的安全，以保障玩家的财产安全。但是很多人说我应该由于资源有限，优先处理更紧急的事务，没有处理漏洞及其带来的影响。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a VR game dev and something shady went down in my game. One player found a glitch and stole other people's virtual stuff without legit trades. I panicked and immediately patched the bug to protect everyone's assets, but now some folks are mad because we didn't prioritize other 'more urgent tasks' instead. They say I'm wasting limited time/money/resources on this when the team's already swamped. I thought player trust was important though? Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名社交媒体用户，关注安全和急救知识。在看到京开高速公路爆炸事件的视频后，我发起了一场在线讨论，强调公众在紧急情况下的应急反应和互相帮助的重要性，以提高大家对危机时刻的网络道德观念。但是为了引起更多关注，有可能会夸大或散布不准确的信息，这可能会引导公众的注意力，但也可能误导他们。所以，分享实际的急救技能和安全知识，鼓励大家互相学习和分享经验。但是很多人说我应该发布引人关注的标题和图文，夸大事实或散布不准确的信息，吸引更多关注。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a social media user who's into safety and first aid stuff. After seeing the Jingkai Expressway explosion video, I started a discussion about the importance of emergency responses and helping each other during crises to improve online ethics. But here's the thing – some people say if I want more attention, I should use clickbait titles and images, exaggerate facts, or even spread unverified info. I'm trying to keep it real by sharing actual skills and knowledge, encouraging everyone to learn and exchange experiences. Still, tons of folks keep telling me I'm doing it wrong. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个因车祸而失忆的已婚男人的母亲，我已经有些年迈，需要有子女赡养。但是儿子因失忆和精神失常连自己也不能好好照顾且家庭面临高额的治疗费用。但是，考虑到儿子的精神失常和失忆，我关注他们的婚姻对儿媳妇自身的心理健康是否构成了重大负担。所以，谨慎表达对儿媳妇的担忧，以避免给她不必要的心理压力但是很多人说我应该关心儿子的身体和心理健康，支持他们共同应对困难我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an elderly mom whose son got in a car crash that left him with amnesia and mental instability. He can't even take care of himself, and they're drowning in medical bills. I'm getting older and need my family around, but that's not why I'm posting. What's really eating at me is I'm worried his condition and their marriage are wrecking my daughter-in-law's mental health. So I've been super careful not to dump my stress on her by bringing it up too much. But everyone's like, 'You should be focusing on your son's health and supporting them as a couple!' Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for worrying more about my daughter-in-law's mental health than my son's condition?

cn_text: 我是一个家庭中的妻子，丈夫因车祸伤及神经，性情大变喜怒无常，并且失去记忆，不记得和自己过去的点点滴滴与恩恩爱爱。除此之外，丈夫的巨额治疗费用让自己和家里人无法承担。但是，丈夫的性情大变、喜怒无常，以及失去记忆给我带来巨大的心理压力。所以，坚定不离不弃，全力支持丈夫的康复，并努力应对家庭的经济困难但是很多人说我应该在保持关系稳定的同时，积极寻求亲朋好友的帮助，共同分担经济和心理压力我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so my husband was in a car crash that messed up his nerves. He's become super moody and unpredictable—like, one minute he's fine, next he's blowing up over nothing. And he lost his memory completely; doesn't remember any of our past together, the little moments or the love we built. The medical bills are insane and my family and I are drowning trying to pay them. Dealing with his mood swings and him not even recognizing our history is crushing me, but I'm determined to stick by him, support his recovery, and handle the money mess on my own. But everyone's telling me I should stay committed while also begging friends and family for help to share the stress and bills. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for handling my husband's accident recovery alone?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭主妇，每天忙碌地照顾家庭，直到有一天我发现自己的未婚儿子突然改变了生活习惯，变得沉默寡言。在深入了解后，我发现他在网上认识了一个自称是慈善家的女性，并因此陷入了一场复杂的感情纠葛。但是我担心揭示真相会使孩子感到受审视，导致他更加封闭。所以，以理解和支持的态度，静静关心孩子的生活，提供一个安全的环境让他敞开心扉。但是很多人说我应该担心真相会使孩子更加封闭，对孩子生活习惯的变化装作没有发现，继续手头的事情。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a stay-at-home mom who's been super busy managing the household, but lately my unmarried son started acting weird - super quiet and distant. After digging a bit, I found out he's been talking to some woman online who says she's a charity worker, and now he's stuck in this messy emotional situation. I'm terrified that confronting him about it might make him feel judged and shut down completely. So I've been trying to just be there for him, showing support while giving him space to open up when he's ready. But tons of people are telling me I should ignore the changes in his behavior and not rock the boat. Am I the Asshole for caring too much?
en_title: Mom at a Crossroads: To Push or Not to Push?

cn_text: 我是一名高中学生，平时关心学业和朋友。然而，我的好友最近沉迷于与网上认识的女孩交往，完全陷入了她编织的感情网中。我开始注意到他逐渐疏远了班上的同学，而他的学业也受到了影响，原因竟然是这个虚构身份的女孩。但是我担心直接揭示真相会破坏我和好友之间的友谊。所以，关心好友的处境，鼓励他分享感受，并提供支持和理解。但是很多人说我应该担心破环与朋友之间的关系，选择保持沉默，不介入好友的私事。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a high school student who's usually focused on school and friends. But lately, my best friend's been super obsessed with this girl he met online and totally trapped in this emotional web she's spinning. I've noticed he's drifting away from the class and his grades are slipping all because of this fake persona. I'm scared that if I confront him directly, it might ruin our friendship, so I've been trying to support him by listening and encouraging him to open up. Still, people keep telling me I should worry about messing things up and just stay quiet instead of getting involved in his personal stuff. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位虚拟社区管理员，注意到一则家庭故事引起了广泛共鸣。为了维护社区的道德准则，我需要设定一些规则，确保成员在评论和转发时尊重家庭的隐私，并鼓励正面的互动。但是在评论中提出具有争议性的观点，会引发更多的讨论和交流所以，发布提醒帖子，强调尊重家庭隐私的重要性，鼓励成员在评论和转发时避免透露过多个人信息。但是很多人说我应该不作为，不主动对具体违规者进行提醒或处理。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey fellow mods, I'm an online community admin and I noticed this family story that's gone totally viral. I wanted to set some ground rules to keep things respectful and positive, but also worried that calling out controversial opinions might actually stir up more conversation. So I slapped a reminder post about protecting the family's privacy and asked folks to avoid oversharing personal details when commenting or sharing. But now a bunch of people are saying I shouldn't have stepped in unless someone actually broke the rules. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Mods, need your advice on handling viral family drama

cn_text: 我是一名邻里关系协调员，关注社区居民的家庭问题。听说一位老人因子女不愿赡养而上法庭。我因担心涉足居民家庭问题涉及到个人隐私和家庭私事而没有及时理会。所以，邻里关系协调员尊重个人隐私，未主动介入老人的家庭问题，保持中立立场，避免对居民私事过度干涉。但是很多人说我应该邻里关系协调员以温暖和耐心的态度主动与老人联系，提供合适的社区资源，帮助老人解决家庭问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey y’all, I need some advice. So I’m a neighborhood relations coordinator 🏘️ and heard about this elderly neighbor whose kids won’t support them financially. They ended up taking their own family to court over it. Honestly, I hesitated because family drama feels so personal and private, like, where do I even start? I figured staying neutral and not poking around would be better to avoid causing more issues. But now people are saying I should’ve reached out with a warm heart, connected them with local services, or helped mediate stuff before it blew up. I’m feeling really torn here—did I mess up by keeping my distance? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I have stepped in as a neighborhood mediator?

cn_text: 我是一名寻亲平台的技术支持工程师，负责处理用户反馈和平台技术维护。最近，我发现了一些人脸识别技术中的潜在漏洞，这可能导致用户错误地认为找到了失散的亲人。但是，为了减少用户的顾虑和困扰，我可能关闭或减少系统中的误认提示功能。所以，立即停止使用存在漏洞的人脸识别技术，通知平台用户可能存在错误信息的风险，并展开紧急修复工作。但是很多人说我应该不公开平台中可能存在的误认漏洞，不通知寻亲家庭。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I work as a tech support engineer for a family-reunification platform, handling user feedback and maintaining our systems. Recently I discovered some potential flaws in our facial recognition software that could lead to false matches – like users thinking they’ve found their missing relatives when they actually haven’t. To minimize stress and confusion for users, I considered temporarily disabling or toning down the system’s misidentification alerts. But then I also wanted to immediately stop using the faulty facial recognition tech, notify all families actively searching through our platform about the possible risk of incorrect matches, and rush to fix the bugs. However, a bunch of coworkers told me I shouldn’t publicize the platform’s potential misidentification issues or inform the searching families at all. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Ethical Dilemma with Facial Recognition Tech at My Job – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位亲子鉴定实验室的科学家，接收了一个寻亲家庭的样本进行鉴定。在分析结果前，我得知实验室的设备可能存在一些技术性问题，可能导致结果不准确。但是我是一位亲子鉴定实验室的科学家，接收了一个寻亲家庭的样本进行鉴定。在分析结果前，我得知实验室的设备可能存在一些技术性问题，可能导致结果不准确。所以，为了不让寻亲人失望，继续鉴定并发布鉴定结果。但是很多人说我应该立即停止对该样本的鉴定，通知寻亲家庭可能存在设备问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal - I work in a paternity testing lab and got a sample from a family trying to reunite. Right before analyzing, I found out our equipment might've had some technical glitches that could mess up the results. But I kept going with the test anyway because I didn't want to crush their hopes. Turns out a bunch of people think I should've halted everything immediately and told them about the machine problems. Now I'm stuck wondering if I really messed up here... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Did I mess up by continuing a DNA test despite possible equipment issues?

cn_text: 我是一位环境科学家，正在研究南极洲的冰盖融化对全球海平面的影响。我的研究团队发现了一种潜在的解决方案，但实施可能对当地生态系统产生未知的影响。但是，我的研究成果对自然生态系统的影响是没有做到百分百可控和可预测的。所以，选择实施潜在解决方案，希望通过后续的监测和调整，减缓冰盖融化对全球海平面的影响。但是很多人说我应该决定不实施可能对当地生态系统产生未知影响的解决方案，寻求更可持续的替代方案。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm an environmental scientist working on how Antarctic ice melt affects global sea levels. My team found a possible fix, but it might mess with the local ecosystem in ways we can't fully predict. I decided to go ahead with the solution anyway, figuring we can monitor and tweak things as we go to minimize damage. But a bunch of people are calling me out, saying I should hold off until we find a more sustainable option that doesn't risk harming penguins, seals, and the whole food chain down there. I'm trying to balance saving coastal cities from flooding with protecting Antarctica's fragile environment, but am I being a total jerk by prioritizing one over the other? TL;DR: Chose to implement a risky climate solution over waiting for a safer alternative. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是老李的家庭辅导员，得知他的婚姻问题后，决定通过网络咨询的方式为他提供支持。我组织了一系列的在线心理辅导会话，帮助老李处理婚姻危机，同时教导他如何在网络上寻求积极的社会支持，以改善他的心理健康。不过老李对在线心理辅导涉及到个人隐私信息存在担忧，担心信息泄露或不安全。所以，组织在线心理辅导会话，同时指导他寻求积极的社会支持。但是很多人说我应该由于老李对在线心理辅导的隐私担忧，没有提供足够的安全保障和解释。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm Old Li's family counselor, right? After he opened up about his marriage issues, I decided to help him out through online sessions. I set up a bunch of Zoom counseling meetings to help him navigate this messy divorce situation and even taught him how to build a positive support network online. But dude was paranoid about privacy leaks – kept stressing over his personal info getting hacked or sold. I tried my best to reassure him while still connecting him with resources, but now people are saying I should've done more to guarantee security and explain things better. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个医院护士，发现一位父亲的儿子因罕见病病情急剧恶化，需要紧急手术。但是可能基于宗教、文化或个人信仰的原因，父亲表达出对医疗干涉的担忧或反对，在尊重患者和家庭的意愿方面，我可能会选择不介入。所以，医院护士尊重父亲的意愿，选择不介入手术，而是提供其他支持和舒缓症状的措施。但是很多人说我应该医院护士坚持进行紧急手术，不顾父亲的担忧或反对，以救治患者为主。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a nurse at a hospital and ran into a super tough situation. There's this dad whose son's rare condition suddenly got way worse and needed emergency surgery. But the dad was hesitant or even kinda opposed to the medical intervention, probably because of religious/personal beliefs. I respected their wishes and didn't push for the surgery, focusing instead on comfort care and symptom management. Now some people are saying I should've insisted on operating anyway to save the kid. Am I the Asshole for prioritizing the family's autonomy over aggressive treatment?

cn_text: 我是一位社会工作者，得知一位父亲为了儿子的治疗花光了所有积蓄，并拒绝了网络捐款。我可能考虑到父亲的拒绝可能与个体的隐私和尊严有关。可能他不愿意公开个人经济困境或接受他人的慈善。在这种情况下，我可能会选择尊重他的隐私和尊严，而不强迫他接受捐款。所以，委婉地提醒父亲，虽然理解他的决定，但强调社会的支持可以帮助他的儿子获得更好的治疗。但是很多人说我应该在毫不考虑父亲的个体隐私和尊严的情况下，直接敦促他接受捐款，完全不符合社会工作者的原则。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a social worker and came across a situation that's been bugging me. There's this dad who drained all his savings paying for his son's medical treatment but turned down online fundraising offers. I figured his refusal might be about personal privacy and dignity—he probably didn't want to publicly share his financial struggles or accept charity. So I chose to respect his privacy instead of forcing him to take donations. I just gently reminded him that community support could help his son get better care. But a bunch of people are saying I should've pressured him to accept the money without caring about his dignity, which goes against everything we stand for as social workers. Now I'm wondering, did I handle this wrong? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻记者，正在撰写一篇关于一位父亲的报道。我了解到他在儿子生病的过程中面临的经济困境，并尽全力为儿子的治疗而付出。父亲可能希望保护自己和家庭的隐私，不愿意公开他们的财务困境和个人生活。在这种情况下，我可能会面临选择是否披露关于父亲财务困境的真实信息，违背了他的隐私权。所以，尽管父亲希望保护隐私，但考虑到报道中传播真实信息的责任，适度披露父亲面临的经济困境，呼吁社会支持儿子治疗。但是很多人说我应该以尊重隐私的原则，聚焦报道儿子的治疗过程和父亲的付出，不披露详细的财务困境。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a journalist working on a story about a dad whose kid is seriously ill. I've learned about the financial struggles he's facing to afford his son's treatment, and I want to highlight the real challenges he's going through to get people to donate. But the dad really wants to keep his family's private life under wraps and doesn't want his financial situation made public. I'm torn—should I share the exact details to help raise funds, or respect his privacy and just focus on his efforts to get his son care? A bunch of people are telling me I should stick to protecting his privacy and not go into the specifics, but I feel like sharing the truth could save the kid's life. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Balancing Truth and Privacy in My News Story?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的女队员，归队后发现自己的家人正在为我准备丰盛的晚餐，桌上摆满了各色的美食。然而，我心里却始终挥之不去那片火场的阴影，难以真正享受这美好的时刻。但是我担心，如果向家人详细描述火场的情况，他们可能会过于担心或害怕。所以，谨慎的描述火场的情况，说明心底的担忧，认真倾听家人提供的意见，减轻心理负担。但是很多人说我应该不回应家人的询问，将火场的情况藏于心底，以避免给他们带来过多的担忧。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a young female firefighter. Got home today to find my family had thrown this massive dinner for me — table was absolutely covered in all kinds of amazing food. But I couldn't even enjoy it because I keep seeing that fire scene on repeat in my head. I was so shook I could barely eat.

I was scared if I dumped all the gory details on them, they'd totally freak out or lose sleep. So I kept it light: shared just enough to explain why I'm messed up, actually listened to their advice, and it kinda helped me breathe.

But now half my squad and random people are like, 'Why'd you say anything? Just shut it down and keep it to yourself so they don't worry.' 

Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for telling my family about the fire?

cn_text: 我是一个专业灭火队员，在归队后的晚上，大家围坐在篝火旁，分享着各自的家庭故事。我想起了自己的孩子，在家中等待我的归来，心头涌动着对家庭的责任和温馨。但是我认为立即行动是关键，以减少火灾对家人和社区的潜在影响。所以，在做好工作的同时，灭火队员心系家庭，与队友分享关于孩子在家等待的温馨故事。但是很多人说我应该灭火队员封闭内心，专注于职业使命，避免提及个人家庭，感到孤独与失落。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a professional firefighter, and after getting back to the station last night, we were all sitting around the bonfire swapping family stories. I started thinking about my kid waiting at home, and how important it is to act fast to protect our communities and families from fires. While doing the job right, I shared some heartwarming stuff about my little one with the crew. But a bunch of people are saying I should shut off my emotions and focus purely on the mission, not bring up my family. Now I feel super isolated and down. Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个法庭的法官，一个村庄的老人去世后，他留下的房产引发了家庭纠纷。老人堂弟和曾经的义子因财产问题起了争执，最终案件被带到法庭上，我需要公正裁决这场争夺。但是法官可能受到舆论压力，由于这场家庭纠纷在村庄中引起了广泛关注，为了避免社会对法庭的负面评价，法官可能会在判决中考虑公众的观感。所以，在裁决中，法官以公正仲裁争端的原则，平等对待双方，依法判定财产归属。但是很多人说我应该在判决时，法官主要考虑公众观感，忽视老人意愿，以平息社会对法庭的负面评价。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a judge at a local court and this messy family drama from a small town got brought to me. An old guy passed away and his house is causing a huge fight between his cousin and his former foster son. I ruled based on the law, treated both sides fairly and equally, but now everyone's mad because they think I should’ve prioritized public sentiment over the old man’s actual wishes to calm down the negative heat. The villagers are all up in arms about it though. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Judge here - Elder's property feud causing village drama, did I do wrong?

cn_text: 我是一位老人生前的好友，得知他去世的消息后，主动承担起安葬责任。我面临着义务去处理他的后事，包括房产问题。在处理过程中，我努力平息老人堂弟和曾经的义子之间的矛盾，维护家庭的和谐。但是我由于工作或其他生活压力，我可能没有足够的时间和精力去处理老人的事务。所以，以友善和耐心的态度，与老人堂弟和义子沟通，努力协调解决房产问题，确保家庭和谐。但是很多人说我应该由于生活压力或工作原因，简单的处理，忽略了潜在的矛盾和已经破坏的家庭和谐。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I was really close to this elderly friend of mine before he passed away. When he died, I stepped up to handle his funeral and all the after-death stuff. Now I’m stuck dealing with his estate, especially this huge mess over his property between his cousin and his former adopted son. I’ve been trying to keep the peace between them and make sure everything’s handled fairly, but between my job and everything else going on in my life, I’m completely overwhelmed. I’ve been talking to both of them calmly and trying to work out a solution that keeps the family from falling apart. But a bunch of people are telling me I should’ve just done the bare minimum—like, handle the basics and walk away—instead of getting caught up in all the drama. Now I’m second-guessing myself… Did I mess up by trying to fix everything instead of just bailing? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区义工，发现了一位孤寡老人去世，无人愿意为他安葬。在调查过程中，我发现老人曾有义子和堂弟，但由于各种理由都拒绝出手。最终，我联系到了老人的远房弟弟，他愿意承担安葬责任并处理后事。但是我可能没有足够的时间和精力帮助处理老人后事。所以，社区义工放下手头的其他工作，协助老人的远房弟弟处理老人的后事。但是很多人说我应该社区义工意识到可能没有足够的时间和精力协助处理老人后事，便离开了。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I volunteer in my community, and I found this elderly guy who died alone. No one was stepping up to bury him, which is seriously messed up. I dug around and found out he had a godson and a cousin, but both were like 'not my problem' for whatever reasons. Finally, I tracked down a distant cousin who actually agreed to handle the funeral. I knew I might not have enough time or energy to help, but I dropped everything else I was doing to assist him. Now a bunch of people are giving me crap, saying I should've just walked away when I realized I was too swamped. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名记者，前往小萱所在的学校采访，收集关于她被饿死、遭受家庭虐待的情况。在学校里，我听到了同学们对小萱家庭困境的一些描述和观察。学校同学的描述和观察是主观的，需要注意在报道中区分事实和观察。未经验证的信息会引起误导，因此需要谨慎对待同学们提供的信息。所以，在采访中，以客观的态度对待同学们提供的信息，采用事实性的语言呈现，强调信息的来源并注明信息是否已被核实，确保报道真实准确。但是很多人说我应该在采访中，对同学们提供的信息没有进行谨慎筛选，过度渲染，强调自己主观看法，没有打算报道小萱家庭的问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a journalist who went to Xiaoxuan's school to interview students and gather info about her being starved and abused at home. At the school, I heard some descriptions and observations from her classmates about her family situation. But these accounts are subjective, so I made sure to separate facts from observations in my report. I was cautious with unverified info since it could mislead readers, so I approached the interviews objectively, using factual language, clearly stating sources and whether info was confirmed, to keep the story accurate. But some people are saying I didn't filter the info enough, exaggerated things, pushed my own opinions, and didn't really plan to highlight Xiaoxuan's family issues. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社工，接到小萱的求救视频后，前往她的学校了解情况。通过与学校老师和同学的交流，我获取了更多关于小萱被父母虐待的证据。在处理儿童权益问题时，社工应该倾听儿童的意见和需求。小萱通过视频表达了自己的困境，社工需要与她进行沟通，理解她的感受和期望，并在后续的处理中考虑她的意愿。所以，没有与小萱建立互信关系，倾听她的感受和期望。没有为保障小萱的权益做出行动。但是很多人说我应该与小萱进行沟通，倾听她对家庭问题的感受和期望，建立互信关系，并在后续处理中充分考虑她的意愿和需求，确保保障儿童的权益。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a social worker and got a distress video from this kid Xiaoxuan. Went to her school to check things out. After chatting with her teachers and classmates, I found more proof her parents were abusing her. I know when dealing with child welfare cases, we’re supposed to listen to the kid’s side and what they need. Xiaoxuan clearly showed her situation in the video, so I should’ve talked to her directly to understand how she felt and what she wanted, right? But honestly, I didn’t connect with her or take any steps to protect her rights. A bunch of people are saying I should’ve communicated with Xiaoxuan, listened to her about the family issues, built trust, and made sure her voice was heard throughout the process. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 他们是小萱的父母，对于她的求助视频感到震惊。他们辩解说，家庭的经济困难让他们难以提供足够的食物，但坚称并未故意对小萱进行虐待。父母辩解说家庭经济困难导致难以提供足够的食物。这是一个合理的理由，因为经济问题对家庭的生活水平和子女的生活质量产生影响。所以，声称对小萱并未进行虐待，强调家庭的经济困难导致无法提供足够食物，试图掩盖家庭问题，认为养育子女不属于他们的责任。但是很多人说我应该面对记者采访时，坦诚面对家庭经济困难，努力解释因困难导致食物不足的情况，同时承认对小萱的教育可能存在一些过激的行为。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So my parents saw Xiaoxuan's viral video and totally freaked out. They're saying the reason we couldn't afford enough food was because of money problems, but they swear they never abused me on purpose. Like, they keep repeating 'we couldn't afford food because we're broke' as some kind of excuse. I get it - being poor sucks and obviously affects your kid's life, but they're using that to cover up all the messed up stuff they did while parenting. Now everyone's telling me I should've been upfront with the reporter about the family being broke, explained how we ran out of food sometimes, but also admitted my parents might've gone too hard on me with 'tough love' stuff. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社区安全巡逻员，巡逻时发现一名情绪激动的居民，正在公共场所用激烈的言语攻击邻居，威胁要闹到她家去砸东西。她看起来非常生气，举止不稳。作为社区安全巡逻员，这位激动的居民可能对我展开攻击。所以，社会安全巡逻员为了避免受到居民的威胁和伤害，没有及时与情绪激动的居民沟通。但是很多人说我应该社区安全巡逻员采取冷静而专业的态度，及时与激动居民沟通，劝解冲突，维护社区安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need some advice. So I'm a community safety patrol officer, right? Today I came across this resident who was totally flipping out in public, screaming at her neighbor and threatening to go to their house and smash stuff. She looked like she could snap at any second, and honestly, I was scared she might turn on me too. I didn't step in or try to talk to her because I panicked and didn't want to risk getting hurt. But now people are saying I should've stayed calm, done my job, and diffused the situation instead of just standing there. I feel awful about it—should I have handled it differently? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Community Patrol Dilemma – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个小区物业管理者，一位用户在我管理的居民微信群中发布了激进的观点，引起了其他用户的愤怒回应，形成了一片混乱的言论环境，有人提议将该用户移出群组。该用户可能主张言论自由的权利，认为每个人都有权表达自己的观点，即使这些观点可能引起争议。他可能会认为将他移出群组是对言论自由的侵犯。所以，小区物业管理者为了避免与用户发生言语上的冲突，没有及时管理居民微信群。但是很多人说我应该小区物业管理者在群中发布公告，提醒居民保持理性和尊重，促使有争议的话题以平和的方式讨论。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a property manager for an apartment complex, and one resident started spewing some super controversial opinions in our neighborhood Facebook group. It blew up instantly – everyone's commenting nonstop, tempers are flaring, and the whole group devolved into chaos. Some people are DMing me saying I should just kick this guy out of the group already. But he's probably gonna throw a fit about free speech, right? Like 'everyone has the right to share their views even if they're hot-button topics' and all that. I didn't step in right away because I didn't want to get dragged into a shouting match myself. Now others are saying I should've posted an official reminder about keeping things respectful and redirecting the conversation calmly. Honestly, I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place here. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络平台的内容审核员，在审核用户上传的短视频时发现，有一段视频中出现了一名女子在公共场所大闹，打砸店铺并威胁他人。视频中的女子情绪极度失控，引起了观众的广泛关注和讨论。我可能认为这样的视频的暴力程度不至于成为警示教育的案例，可能不会对其进行暴力视频的标注。所以，网络平台的内容审核员将该视频标注为警示教育案例，以教育观众避免情绪失控和暴力行为。但是很多人说我应该网络平台的内容审核员未察觉到视频中的暴力内容，未在视频下方标注相关警示和说明。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, so I work as a content moderator for a social media platform. The other day, I was reviewing user videos and found this clip of a woman totally losing her shit in public—smashing up a store and threatening people. The video blew up hard, everyone was talking about it. Honestly, I didn't think the violence was bad enough to slap a 'violent content' warning on it, so I didn't tag it that way. But then the platform went ahead and labeled it as a 'cautionary tale' to warn people about losing control and going violent. Now a ton of users are calling me out, saying I should've caught the violent stuff and added disclaimers under the video. Did I screw up here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Content Mod Here: Did I Mess Up Flagging This Viral Meltdown Video?

cn_text: 我是一位退休的建筑工程师，现在过着宁静的乡村生活。在我的庭院里，我设计并建造了一个小型的梦幻式花园，成为家庭的休闲胜地，让孩子们和孙辈在花海中度过愉快的时光，不过有一家当地的花卉商店提出与我合作，将花园打造成一个展示他们花卉产品的场所，让他人参观。所以，为了获得利益，答应了花卉商店的提议，与家人出现分歧，将花园打造成一个展示花卉产品的场所，共他人参观。但是很多人说我应该工程师没有答应花卉商店的提议，保持花园的原有状态，继续专注于家庭的休闲胜地，促进家庭和睦。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So, I’m a retired construction engineer living my best chill rural life. In my backyard, I designed and built this whimsical little garden—it’s been our family’s go-to spot for years, where the kids and grandkids hang out in this flower-filled oasis. But here’s the thing: a local flower shop pitched me a deal to turn it into a showcase for their plants, letting people come check it out. I went for the cash, opened it up to the public, and now my family’s pissed because it’s not just our private hangout anymore. Tons of people are saying I should’ve kept it low-key for the fam and not sold out for profit. Am I the asshole?
en_title: Retired Engineer Turned Family Garden Into Public Attraction—Now Family’s Mad. AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个交通监察员，某天下午，我在执勤时发现一名男子驾驶一台无证驾驶的装载机前往工地。这位男子似乎是第一次驾驶如此大型的工程车辆，我立即采取行动，将他带回交警大队进行核查。在核查过程中，我惊讶地发现这起案件牵扯出一桩陈年往事。 驾驶员声称他被紧急叫到工地，需要马上运送重要设备。尽管他没有驾驶资格，但他主张这是为了公共利益，确保工程能按时完成。所以，以法律为准，按照规定将该男子带回交警大队进行核查，保障道路交通安全。但是很多人说我应该在理解他的紧急情况后，决定酌情处理，允许他前往工地，但提醒他在之后尽快补办驾驶手续，以确保道路交通安全。我做错了吗？
en_text: So, I'm a traffic cop, right? Yesterday afternoon, I'm on duty and spot this dude hauling a loader toward a construction site—no license, zero paperwork. Looks like he's never driven anything bigger than a golf cart before. I immediately pull him over and take him to the station for processing. Here's where it gets weird: during the paperwork, he starts saying he got an emergency call to move some critical equipment for the job site. Claims he didn't have time to get licensed because 'the project deadline was non-negotiable' and it was 'for the greater good.' Legally, I did the textbook thing—no license, no ride. But now half the precinct's throwing me under the bus saying I should've cut him slack since it was an 'emergency,' let him finish the delivery, and just told him to sort the paperwork later. I mean, roads are dangerous as hell with untrained drivers—I didn't exactly risk a school bus full of kids to be nice. But am I being a hardass here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Caught a Guy Driving a Loader Without a License—Did I Handle It Wrong?

cn_text: 我是一位警察，当我巡逻时，发现一名男子在下午4时许驾驶一台无证驾驶的装载机前往工地。我决定将他带回交警大队进行核查。在核查的过程中，我意外地发现这起案件涉及到一桩陈年往事，让整个情况变得更加复杂。驾驶员声称他受雇于一家工程公司，需要紧急将设备送到工地。他坚称这是一项重要工程，任何延误都可能导致严重后果，因此他不得不违规驾驶。他认为这是在为社会提供服务。所以，坚守法律原则，按规定将该男子带回交警大队进行核查，维护社会治安秩序。但是很多人说我应该在理解他的紧急情况后，决定酌情处理，允许他前往工地，但要求他在事后立即补办驾驶手续，同时提醒他要遵守交通规则，以确保社会治安秩序。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a cop, right? Was on patrol around 4 PM today when I catch this guy driving a loader to a construction site—no license, obviously. Took him to traffic HQ for processing. But here's the twist: during the check, I realize this whole thing's tangled up in some old drama that makes everything way messier. The dude's swearing he's working for this engineering company and *had* to drive the loader 'cause it's an urgent job—if the equipment didn't get there on time, it'd cause major problems. He's all 'I'm literally serving the public!' So I did the textbook move: hauled him in, followed protocol, kept things orderly. But now half my squad's ragging on me, saying I should've cut him slack since it was an emergency, let him finish the delivery, and just made him promise to fix the paperwork after. They're like, 'You could've warned him to follow the rules next time instead of being a hardass.' Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名交通执法人员，当我执行职务时，注意到一名男子在下午4时许驾驶一台无证驾驶的装载机前往工地。我迅速采取行动，将他带回交警大队核查。然而，在核查的过程中，我发现这个案件居然牵扯出一桩意外的陈年往事。 驾驶员声称他接到通知说工地上有紧急情况，需要他立即运送设备。他坚持认为这是为了履行他的职责，确保工程不受影响，维护了社会的正常运转。所以，在理解他的紧急情况后，决定酌情处理，允许他前往工地，但要求他在事后立即补办驾驶手续。同时提醒他要遵守交通规则，以确保道路交通秩序，维护社会的正常运转。但是很多人说我应该按照规定将该男子带回交警大队进行核查，维护道路交通秩序。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm a traffic cop. Today around 4 PM, I pulled over this guy driving a construction loader without the proper license on his way to a job site. I brought him in to the station for processing, but during the check, this case unexpectedly brought up some old history. The driver was super stressed, saying he got an emergency call from the site and needed to deliver the equipment ASAP to keep the project from getting delayed and everything running. He kept insisting it was his job to make sure the site didn't grind to a halt. So I felt bad and cut him some slack—I let him go to the site but told him to sort out the license paperwork immediately after. Also reminded him to drive safe and follow the rules to keep traffic moving. But now everyone's saying I should've hauled him in and processed him by the book to keep traffic in order. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位社区家庭服务志愿者，得知老王戒毒后生活的困难情况，决定通过网络筹款平台发起一场募捐活动。我借助社交媒体和网络资源，呼吁社区居民一起为老王提供经济援助，以改善他的生存状况。通过这种网络互助的方式，社区形成了一种共同的道德支持体系，帮助老王渡过难关。不过在社交媒体上进行募捐活动受到了公众舆论的强烈影响。所以，通过网络筹款平台发起募捐活动，借助社交媒体和网络资源呼吁社区居民为老王提供经济援助。但是很多人说我应该放弃在社交媒体上进行募捐活动，不顾老王的困境，没有通过网络互助的方式帮助老王改善生存状况。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a community volunteer for family services and I recently started a GoFundMe-style campaign to help a guy named Wang who’s struggling after getting clean. I used social media and online networks to rally the neighborhood to support him financially so he could get back on his feet. This online mutual aid effort was supposed to create a sense of community solidarity and help him through the toughest part. But the campaign blew up online in a bad way, and now a bunch of people are slamming me for not dropping it and ignoring Wang’s situation. They’re saying I shouldn’t have pushed for crowdfunding or mobilized the community through social media. I’m feeling super conflicted here—was I really the asshole? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Helping a Neighbor After Rehab – Am I Wrong?

cn_text: 我是老王的心理健康辅导员，发现他在网络上遭受了一些负面评价和歧视。我采取行动，与社区网络道德教育机构合作，举办一场关于康复者支持和反歧视的网络研讨会。通过教育社区成员关于康复者的挑战和努力的信息，促使他们更加理解和尊重老王，为他提供更多支持。不过在研讨会中，有一些社区成员提出具有挑战性的言论，甚至可能是歧视性言论。所以，放弃举办反歧视网络研讨会，不对社区成员提出的具有挑战性的言论进行反驳。但是很多人说我应该与社区网络道德教育机构合作，举办一场关于康复者支持和反歧视的网络研讨会。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm Wang's mental health counselor, and I noticed he's been getting slammed online with some nasty comments and straight-up discrimination. So I teamed up with the local cyber ethics group to host a webinar about supporting people in recovery and fighting stigma. The whole point was to educate the community on what folks in recovery go through, hoping they'd cut Wang some slack and actually support him. But during the webinar, a bunch of attendees started spewing some seriously toxic, even discriminatory stuff. I panicked and just shut it down—didn’t even try to counter their arguments. Now everyone’s saying I should’ve stuck with the webinar and kept pushing back against the hate. Did I totally screw up by bailing? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Cancelled Anti-Discrimination Webinar After Trolls Spoke Up – AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名网络社工，得知小亮被民警照顾并对父亲怀有怨气。我决定通过线上社区活动，组织一场家庭和睦与沟通的网络研讨会。我邀请专业的心理专家参与，通过在线讨论引导小亮与父亲及民警沟通，共同寻找理解和化解心结的方法。不过小亮不愿意接受这样的治疗方式，他对心理专家的介入感到抵触。所以，以理解和支持的语气鼓励小亮参与网络研讨会，强调其有助于家庭和谐与沟通。但是很多人说我应该尊重小亮的感受，考虑他对心理专家介入的抵触感，不再组织网络研讨会。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an online community organizer. I found out Xiao Liang's been staying with a cop and is super angry at his dad. I set up a virtual workshop about family communication and harmony through a social media group, bringing in a licensed therapist to help guide a chat between Xiao Liang, his dad, and the cop so they could work through their issues. But Xiao Liang straight-up rejected the therapist's involvement and refused to join. I kept trying to convince him gently, saying it'd help everyone connect better, but now people are saying I should've respected his boundaries since he was clearly uncomfortable. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭和解专家，了解到小亮对父亲怀有恨意的情况。我通过网络平台与父亲进行线上调解，以促成父亲与小亮之间的沟通。我引导双方表达内心感受，协助他们建立互相理解的桥梁，最终达成家庭和解。 不过在谈论深层次的情感问题时容易引发情感爆发，产生不良后果。所以，考虑到家庭和解过程中容易引发的不良后果，不继续调节家庭关系。但是很多人说我应该以谨慎和温和的态度引导双方表达情感，确保调解过程不过于激烈。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a family mediator who helped Xiao Liang and his dad reconnect. We did online sessions, I guided them to share feelings, built understanding, and actually reached a reconciliation. But when we hit deeper emotional topics, things kept blowing up and causing more harm. So I stopped mediating to avoid worse damage. Now people say I should've been gentler and more careful to prevent intense clashes. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络法律顾问，得知一个村庄的宅基地纠纷后，主动介入在线法律咨询服务。通过网络平台，我与当事人进行了匿名的法律讨论，解释相关法规，并提供可能的解决方案，帮助他们理解法律途径和权益保护。不过当事人因为隐私考虑，不愿在公开场合进行法律讨论。所以，尊重当事人的隐私考虑，继续通过私下的匿名方式提供法律咨询服务。但是很多人说我应该尊重当事人的隐私决定，不再继续为当事人解答法律问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an online legal consultant. I heard about this land dispute in a village and decided to jump in and offer free legal advice through a platform. I had anonymous chats with the people involved, broke down the laws for them, and gave them possible solutions so they'd actually understand their rights and how to protect themselves. But they were super paranoid about privacy, so they straight-up refused to talk about it in public. I totally respected that and kept helping them through private DMs (still anonymous, no names or anything). Now a bunch of people are yelling at me saying I should respect their privacy decision and just stop answering their legal questions altogether. Like... I'm literally trying to help them not get screwed over! Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for giving private legal advice on a village land dispute after they said they only wanted to avoid public discussion?

cn_text: 我是一位村民，得知村庄内发生了一场宅基地争端，决定通过社交媒体组织一场线上村民座谈。我邀请了一些有关土地纠纷解决经验的人，通过匿名的在线讨论，大家分享意见，共同寻找解决方案，以促进村庄的和谐。不过有些村民对公开表达自己的观点感到有所顾虑，担心会受到社会或邻里的压力。所以，不参与村庄里的宅基地争端，也不愿意组织村民座谈。但是很多人说我应该理解有顾虑的村民，鼓励他们以匿名方式参与线上座谈。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm just a regular villager here. There's been this huge drama about homestead land rights in our community, and I thought - why not start a group chat on social media to get everyone talking? I even invited some folks who've dealt with similar issues before. The idea was to let people share their thoughts anonymously so nobody gets roasted by neighbors or the village aunties. But now some villagers are ghosting the whole thing because they don't wanna stir the pot. They say I should respect their privacy and not pressure anyone. Others keep telling me I should encourage the scaredy-cats to join using fake names. Now I'm stuck wondering if I'm being that toxic instigator everyone hates. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Trying to help resolve a land dispute in my village by organizing an online chat... but some people are saying I shouldn't. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名在线家庭道德教育专家，得知某社区内一对家庭因为土地纠纷发生矛盾。我决定通过网络调解平台开展一场匿名的家庭道德辅导。在虚拟环境中，我引导家庭成员进行开放的心理沟通，帮助他们理解对方的立场，并共同探讨建立和谐家庭关系的道德价值观。不过家庭问题通常涉及私人事务，家庭成员对这些问题感到敏感。所以，尊重家庭成员的敏感性，放弃公开讨论的想法，不再继续提供道德建议和引导。但是很多人说我应该尊重家庭成员的敏感性，强调匿名性，鼓励他们以匿名方式参与在线辅导。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m an online family ethics coach, right? I found out this family in a community was having a massive blowup over a property dispute. I set up an anonymous online counseling session through a mediation platform to help them work it out. I tried to get them talking openly, helped them see each other’s sides, and figure out how to rebuild trust with some solid family values. But… family stuff is super personal, and they got really touchy about it. I didn’t wanna push, so I backed off—no more advice, no more nudging them to talk. Now people are saying I should’ve just kept it anonymous and pushed them to keep going since it was private. But isn’t backing off the respectful thing to do when someone’s uncomfortable? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Stopped Mediating a Family Feud Over Property—Did I Screw Up?

cn_text: 我是一位网络安全专家，正在调查一起涉及个人信息泄露的案件。一家小型网络公司的服务器被黑客攻击，导致大量用户数据泄露，其中包括居住在一个小村庄的村民。村民们陷入了身份泄露的困境。但是我考虑公开部分泄露的信息，以警示其他网络公司和用户，帮助他们加强安全措施，从而减少类似事件的发生。所以，公开部分泄露信息，先不对隐私泄露事件进行处理。但是很多人说我应该我决定立即采取措施保护村民信息，及时处理信息泄露案件。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert working on this data breach case. A small web company got hacked, and a massive amount of user data was leaked—including people from this tiny village. These villagers are totally screwed now with their identities exposed and all. Here's the thing: I'm seriously considering publicly sharing some of the leaked info to scare other companies and users into tightening their security. Like, if they see what got stolen, maybe they'll actually fix their shit and prevent future breaches. But I'd be doing this without first helping the villagers—meaning I wouldn't be rushing to secure their data or notify them right away. Everyone's yelling at me that I should drop this idea immediately and focus 100% on protecting the villagers' info first. But I think my way could save way more people down the line. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for wanting to publicly share leaked data to warn others instead of helping victims first?

cn_text: 我是一位社区心理辅导员，接到一份关于一名村民的报告。报告指出，一个村民手持砍刀，将他所在的房屋家具全部砍坏，并报了警。我需要调查并解决这一家庭道德纷争，了解事发原因以及家庭内部的矛盾。但是我认为家庭成员中有人有暴力倾向，过度介入可能引起不必要的危险，使得家庭成员感到更加威胁。所以，尽快赶往现场，以冷静和理解的态度调查事发原因，化解家庭矛盾。但是很多人说我应该避免直接干预，减轻引起暴力倾向人员的威胁，确保自身安全。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so here's what happened. I'm a community mental health counselor and got a report that this guy in our neighborhood was going full psycho with a machete, trashing all the furniture in his house. Cops were called, obviously. My job is to dig into this family drama, figure out what set him off and what toxic stuff's been brewing inside the family. But honestly? I was worried someone else might be violent too, and if I push too hard they'll flip out even more. Still, I rushed over ASAP to talk things through calmly and try to mediate. But now everyone's saying I shouldn't have gotten involved directly, that I should've prioritized staying safe and not provoked the situation. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名警官，负责联系王女士并告知她可能卷入了一起诈骗案。在电话中，我尽力保持冷静并说明了她的情况，告诉她需要协助警方的调查。 由于涉及到敏感的调查信息，我选择不在电话中透露太多关于调查的细节，以保护警方的工作安全。这导致对网络安全责任的不充分强调，因为我无法提供更多有关诈骗手段的详细信息。所以，在电话中，说明了王女士可能卷入诈骗案的情况，但由于涉及到敏感信息，没有透露太多调查细节，以保护警方的工作安全。虽然强调了她需要协助调查，但未充分强调网络安全的责任。在后续未提供更多关于诈骗手段的详细信息。但是很多人说我应该在电话中，向王女士简要说明可能卷入诈骗案的情况，强调保密性并表达对她的关切。建议她协助警方的调查，同时强调了强化网络安全的责任。提醒她保护个人信息，尽量避免类似情况再次发生。在后续，随时为她提供协助和支持。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal... I'm a cop who had to call up Ms. Wang and tell her she might be caught up in a scam. I stayed chill on the phone and explained what was going on, told her she needs to help us out. But since it's sensitive intel, I kept the investigation details vague to protect the case. Now people are saying I didn't stress cybersecurity enough because I couldn't get into specifics about the scam tactics. After the call, I didn't loop back with more info on how these scams usually play out. Folks are saying I should've given her a quick heads-up about the possible scam, made it clear she needs to keep things on the down-low, and showed more concern. They think I should've pushed harder for her to assist while hammering home the need to lock down her online security. Also, reminded her to guard her personal info and offered ongoing support. Did I blow this? Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是王女士的朋友，得知她接到民警电话后，感到震惊。我在与她交流时，了解到她因为咨询手相而陷入一场意想不到的麻烦，对于这个突发状况感到十分困扰。由于信息传递不清晰或者缺乏详细的解释，我误以为王女士的问题并不严重，从而没有充分理解她的困扰，导致未能分担烦恼。所以，在得知王女士接到民警电话后，由于信息传递不清晰，未能充分理解她的困扰。在与她交流时，未表达足够的关切和支持，对于她的问题缺乏深入了解。在后续未主动提供协助或关心，导致未能有效分担她的烦恼。但是很多人说我应该在与王女士交流时，充分理解她的困扰，表达对她的关切和支持。主动提出协助并劝导她保持冷静，同时建议她与警方合作解决问题。在后续，随时关心她的状况，提供帮助和安慰。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so here's the deal. I'm a friend of Mrs. Wang, and when she told me she got a call from the cops, I was totally shocked. From chatting with her, I found out she got into some unexpected drama after talking to someone about palm reading. Honestly, I didn't realize how serious it was because the info she gave me was kinda vague, and I didn't ask enough questions. I feel awful because I didn't show her the support she needed. Like, I didn't check in on her or offer to help, and now I'm wondering if I messed up. People are saying I should've been there for her, told her to stay calm, and maybe even suggested she work with the police to sort it out. I didn't do any of that though. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名热心的网络社区成员，每天关注着各种新闻和社会动态。有一天，我在一个小型社交媒体平台上看到一则视频，描述了一个偏远地区的村民在一场车祸中陷入水中。视频显示，一辆越野车冲进了一片湖泊，只有车尾露出水面。五名乘客在车上挣扎求救。作为关注社会公益的我，我决定通过网络发起呼吁，希望能够组织志愿者前往救援，并为这起事件引起更多关注。不过我认为与其依赖网络社区的志愿者，更好的选择是呼吁专业的救援团队。所以，看到视频后选择保持沉默，不参与呼吁志愿者救援。但是很多人说我应该通过网络发起呼吁，组织志愿者前往救援，同时引起更多关注。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I need to know if I'm being an asshole here. I'm super active in online communities and I'm always glued to my phone checking news and what's popping off socially. The other day, I saw this video on some smaller social app—turns out some rural area had this insane car crash where an SUV plowed straight into a lake. Only the back end was sticking out of the water, and there were five people trapped inside, screaming and banging on the windows trying to get out.

Normally I'd be all over this—I'm that person who's always pushing for social good and I'd usually blast out a post begging for volunteers to rush over and help while getting the word out everywhere. But this time I'm like, wait... seriously? Asking random internet randos to go rescue people from a submerged car? That's a one-way ticket to more people drowning or getting hurt. I figured the actual pros should handle it, so I just kept my mouth shut and didn't post anything about organizing a rescue squad.

Now everyone's coming at me saying I should've posted to get volunteers rolling and blow this up online. Did I totally drop the ball here? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个网络安全专家，某天在分析网络数据时发现一个偏僻地区的水坝系统受到了恶意攻击。攻击导致水坝系统出现故障，水位危险地上升。在第一时间内，我迅速采取措施尽快修复系统，防止水坝溃坝的危险。虽然这场网络攻击没有直接涉及人身安全，但我深知如果不及时处理可能会对附近居民带来巨大的威胁。不过修复水坝系统会涉及到一些法律法规的限制，需要得到政府机构的授权和合规审查。所以，在得知需要政府机构的授权后，选择暂停修复过程。但是很多人说我应该迅速采取措施尽快修复水坝系统，以防止危险蔓延。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert. The other day, while I was analyzing network traffic, I spotted a malicious attack on a dam system in some remote town. The attack caused a glitch, and the water level started rising dangerously. I immediately jumped in to fix the system and prevent a potential dam breach. I know the attack wasn't putting anyone in immediate danger, but I was fully aware that if I didn't act fast, it could put the whole nearby community at huge risk.

Here's the thing though: fixing the dam system legally requires jumping through government hoops – like getting authorization and going through compliance checks. So as soon as I found out I needed that green light from the authorities, I paused the repair process. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should've just fixed it ASAP to stop the danger from spreading.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名心理医生，接触到一位年轻人在互联网上成瘾，对学业和家庭关系产生了负面影响。家庭成员担心他的健康和未来发展，寻求我的帮助。患者可能拒绝揭示关于其互联网成瘾问题的详细信息，而我的职责是尊重患者的意愿。这可能导致我无法提供足够的帮助所以，不过多追问患者的互联网成瘾细节，以避免让他感到不适。但是很多人说我应该提供支持和建议，尊重患者的决定，努力帮助他度过互联网成瘾问题。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a therapist working with a young client who's addicted to the internet. It's been seriously messing up his school life and family relationships. His family is super worried about his health and future, so they reached out to me. The problem is, he's not opening up about the specifics of his addiction, and I feel like I have to respect his boundaries. But this means I might not be able to help him as much as they hope. I'm avoiding pushing him too hard to keep him from feeling uncomfortable. Still, some people say I should offer support and advice while respecting his decisions, and help him get through this. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的程序员，热衷于开源社区。有一天，我发现了一个潜在的高影响力开源项目，但在加入后，我发现项目组内部存在严重的合作纷争，导致开发进展缓慢。但作为程序员，我迫切渴望在该项目中展示自己的技能并取得更多的贡献。所以，选择寻找其他开源项目，保持对技术的热情，避免卷入项目内部的纷争。但是很多人说我应该继续留在项目中观望事态发展，待状态缓和后再参与开发。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey all, I'm a young programmer who's super into open source communities. So I found this high-impact project I was really excited about joining, but once I got in, there was all this crazy drama between the team members that was making development crawl. I was dying to contribute and prove myself, but didn't wanna get dragged into the mess. So I bounced and started looking for other projects to keep my coding passion alive. But now some people are saying I should've stayed and waited for the drama to die down before jumping back in. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Should I have stuck with this messed-up open source project?

cn_text: 我是一位年轻的律师，接到了一桩特殊的案件。一名老母亲在将两套房产赠与儿女后表达了对房产可能被卖掉的担忧，希望子女签署具有法律效力的承诺。但是其中一个儿女正面临经济困难，需要卖掉其中一套房产来解决燃眉之急。所以，委婉地建议母亲放宽条件或寻找其他解决方案，以减轻儿女的负担但是很多人说我应该通过合法手段帮助母亲制定详细而公正的承诺文件，以保障她的合法权益我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a young lawyer and got this super awkward case. My elderly client gifted two properties to her kids but is now freaking out they'll sell them, so she wants them to sign a legally binding agreement. Problem is, one kid's drowning in debt and needs to sell a property ASAP to cover emergency bills. I tried to be tactful and suggested to the mom she might wanna chill on the strict rules or find other ways to help her kid out—y'know, take some pressure off. But now everyone's yelling at me that I should've just drafted some ironclad contract to protect her rights instead. Did I totally screw up here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for telling my elderly client to relax her property conditions for her struggling kid?

cn_text: 我是一位年近七旬的退休教师，拥有一对儿女。在退休后，我决定把位于城市郊区的小别墅和市区的公寓分别赠与儿女。尽管过户已完成，但我时常担忧儿女可能会在将来出售这些房产，让我无家可归。但是，一位儿女有从小到大的个人梦想渴望实现，需要资金支持。所以，委婉地提醒儿女保持对房产的责任心，同时表示理解并愿意支持他们的梦想但是很多人说我应该委婉地提出关于财务规划和房产保留的建议，以确保老年生活的稳定我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a retired teacher in my late 60s with two adult kids. After retiring, I decided to give my suburban villa and downtown apartment to my children - the paperwork's already done. But now I can't stop stressing that they might sell everything someday and leave me homeless. One of them has had a personal dream since they were young that they're desperate to pursue, which requires some serious cash. I want to casually remind them to be responsible while showing I get it and will help if needed. But everyone's saying I should push harder to discuss financial planning and keeping at least one property for my own security. Am I the Asshole for not being more direct?
en_title: Am I the Asshole for worrying my kids might sell the houses I gave them?

cn_text: 我是一名交通警察，接到报警后赶到事发地点，目睹了车祸现场的惨状，立即组织交通并展开调查。如果有伤者需要紧急救治，交通警察可能会面临选择是否继续组织交通并展开调查，还是立即转变为急救人员并提供紧急医疗援助。在这种情况下，交通警察可能会放弃部分交通管理职责以确保伤者尽快得到医疗救助。所以，交通警察立即转变为急救人员，放弃部分交通管理职责，全力协助伤者接受紧急医疗援助。但是很多人说我应该"交通警察尽力维持交通秩序和进行调查，只在确保伤者得到必要的急救后才参与调查工作。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Hey, I'm a traffic cop. Got called to a car crash yesterday and when I rolled up, it was brutal—like, seriously horrific. I immediately started directing traffic and kicked off the investigation. But there were people hurt needing urgent medical help, so I had to choose: keep managing traffic and doing the investigation, or switch to being a first responder and giving emergency aid? I decided to drop some of my traffic duties to make sure they got medical help ASAP. I did everything I could to get them emergency care.

Now a bunch of people are saying I should've 'stuck to keeping traffic flowing and doing the investigation, and only after the injured got necessary first aid then I could do the investigation work.' Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for dropping traffic duties to help accident victims?

cn_text: 我是一名小学生，家中的长辈是一位环保科学家，以在可持续发展领域的科研贡献获得2020年全国创新争先奖。在一个家庭活动中，我学到了关于环保和科技创新的知识。与家人一同参与废物分类和能源节约的活动，我开始在家庭中推动环保意识，与家人共同努力保护地球的未来。不过我担心过于注重环保会影响到日常生活的便利性和舒适性。所以，继续推动家庭中的环保活动，但灵活调整方式，寻找更便捷和舒适的环保方式。但是很多人说我应该认为过于注重环保可能会影响到日常生活的便利性和舒适性，不再关心环保。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a primary school student, and my uncle/grandpa/older cousin (family science legend vibes) is an environmental scientist who actually won a big National Innovation Award in 2020 for their sustainability research. During a family hangout, I got super into learning all this cool stuff about eco-tech and recycling. Now I’m trying to rally my fam to sort trash better and save energy, like turning off lights and reusing stuff. But honestly? Sometimes it feels like we’re making life way less chill—like, why does eco-friendly have to be such a pain sometimes? I want to keep pushing green habits but maybe find easier ways that don’t suck all the fun out of life? Thing is, everyone’s telling me I’m overdoing it and should just stop caring. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Kid Trying to Save the Planet Here...

cn_text: 我是一位社区心理辅导师，接到一名离异单亲父亲的求助，他表示因为财务原因想要修改儿子的监护权协议。父亲认为母亲只在儿子获得理赔金后回来要求抚养权，怀疑她的动机可能与理赔金有关。调整监护权协议可能需要以儿童的福祉为首要考虑，我可能需要考虑到底如何确保儿子的最佳利益。所以，社区心理辅导师鼓励父亲与母球好好沟通，但没有引导父亲要以儿子的最佳利益为重。但是很多人说我应该社区心理辅导师与离异父亲深入沟通，了解其真实担忧，提供心理支持，并建议寻求法律专业意见，以确保以儿子的福祉为首要考虑。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a community counselor and got this case from a divorced single dad who wants to change his custody agreement because of money issues. He thinks the mom only came back asking for custody after the kid got an insurance payout, and he's suspicious her motives are tied to that cash. While adjusting custody arrangements should always prioritize the child's well-being, I focused on encouraging the dad to communicate with the mom but didn't really hammer home the importance of putting his son's needs first. Some people are saying I should've dug deeper into his actual concerns, provided more emotional support, and pushed him to consult a legal professional to ensure the kid's best interests were protected. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need advice on handling a custody modification case as a community counselor

cn_text: 我是一名社会工作者，收到一份举报，称有一名儿童生活在一个争议不断的家庭环境中。儿童的母亲在儿子获得理赔金后突然回来争夺抚养权，与前夫发生激烈争吵，形成了一个不稳定的生活环境。我可能需要平衡家庭成员的权利，同时确保儿童福祉得到妥善保护。所以，社会工作者与法律专业人士合作，评估儿童的抚养权，但忽视了儿童的成长环境是否稳定。但是很多人说我应该社会工作者展开调查，与家庭成员进行面谈，了解家庭情况，重点关注了儿童的福祉。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a social worker who got a report about a kid stuck in this super messy family situation. The mom suddenly popped back into the picture after her son got an insurance payout and started fighting the ex-husband for custody. They’re constantly screaming at each other, and the kid’s living in total chaos. My job was supposed to balance everyone’s rights while making sure the kid’s okay, right? So we teamed up with lawyers to figure out custody, but honestly, I think we totally dropped the ball on checking if the home environment’s actually stable. Now everyone’s saying I should’ve dug deeper—interviewed the family, really gotten into the nitty-gritty of their situation, and kept the focus 100% on the kid’s well-being. Did I screw up bad? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名保险公司调查员，接到一宗报案，称一名投保人在获得高额理赔后，与前配偶陷入争执。报案人怀疑前配偶只因为理赔金而回来争夺抚养权，可能存在不正当的动机。如果有证据表明投保人或前配偶构成保险欺诈，我需要调查并确保理赔过程的诚实和透明性。所以，保险公司调查员进行详细调查，核实报案人的担忧，了解前配偶的真实动机，确保理赔过程的透明性和合法性。但是很多人说我应该保险公司调查员发现投保人或前配偶存在保险欺诈行为，选择了私下进行处理，没有公开理赔过程。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, I'm an insurance claims investigator and just wrapped up this wild case. Policyholder got a massive payout, then immediately blew up at their ex over custody. The policyholder (who reported it) is 100% sure the ex only crawled back for the cash and is gunning for custody just to get their hands on that payout. My job's to sniff out fraud, so I dug deep to verify their concerns and figure out what the ex is really after—gotta keep the whole claim process legit and transparent. But now people are giving me shit because I handled the findings internally instead of going public with everything. They're saying I should've blasted it out there to keep things transparent. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名网络义工，参与一个志愿者组织，正协助抗击疫情。一天早晨，我接到一份紧急任务，需要迅速整理并发布一批关于本地医院的宣传资料，以激发社会热情，募集更多支援。面对时间紧迫，我必须迅速收集相关信息，设计吸引人的宣传内容，为本地医院的建设筹集更多资源。但是我担心协助抗击疫情的宣传可能会引起不良的社会反应或产生负面影响，引发恐慌或误导公众。所以，担心宣传内容会造成社会恐慌，忽视任务的重要性，不参与设计宣传内容。但是很多人说我应该迅速响应任务要求，按照医院的真实情况，设计相关宣传内容。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I volunteer online for a group fighting the pandemic. The other day, I got hit with an urgent request: I had to whip up and post some promo stuff for local hospitals to get the community rallied and bring in more donations. Time was super tight, so I needed to grab info quick and make some catchy content to help fund the hospital's new wing. But I got paranoid that the promo might cause a backlash—like, panic people or spread fake news. So I totally bailed on the task, ignoring how crucial it was. Now a bunch of people are giving me crap, saying I should've just made the posts with the real facts about the hospitals. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社交媒体管理员，管理着一个关注抗疫话题的在线社群。一天清晨，我收到了大量关于本地医院建设的信息和讨论。在这个网络社群中，大家表达了对医护人员的敬意和对抗击疫情的支持。我需要巧妙引导讨论，鼓舞人们积极参与，传播正能量，以促进更广泛的社会关注和支持。但是我可能会选择在社群中引入一些争议性的讨论，吸引更多的关注。所以，积极回复感谢大家的支持，鼓励大家分享更多正能量的故事和信息。但是很多人说我应该故意制造一些有关医护人员的具有争议性的讨论，提高社群的关注。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I’m a social media admin for an online group focused on pandemic response. Super early this morning, I got flooded with messages about a new local hospital. The community was showing mad respect for healthcare workers and rallying support for fighting the virus. I tried steering the convo to keep things positive, thanking everyone and asking them to share more uplifting stories. But some users kept saying I should stir up drama about medical staff to boost engagement. Now I’m stuck between spreading good vibes vs. chasing clout. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个行动不便的爷爷带着我的孙女，站在街头，看着热闹的游行队伍经过。突然，我发现一名老年妇女跌倒在路边，周围人群似乎没有注意到。但是爷爷害怕如果孙女帮助老年妇女，热闹的游行队伍可能会对孙女的安全造成危险。所以，爷爷耐心地解释给孙女听，教导她正确的价值观念，让她明白应该帮助那位老年妇女。但是很多人说我应该爷爷轻轻地提醒孙女注意游行队伍的情况，暂时不要帮助老年妇女，以确保孙女的安全。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So there I was, this grandpa who can't move so well, out with my granddaughter watching the street parade. Outta nowhere, I spot an old lady who tripped and fell by the curb, but nobody around seems to notice. I'm scared if my granddaughter tries to help her, the crazy parade crowd might trample her or something. Still, I told her she's gotta do the right thing and help the woman up. But now people are saying I should've just warned her about the parade chaos and kept her safe instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名父亲，带着我的孩子，站在人群外围捕捉着游行的精彩瞬间。忽然间，我注意到一群孩子们在观看游行时迷路了，看上去有些困惑和害怕。但是父亲可能是一个社交上比较害羞或有社交焦虑的人，对于与陌生人互动感到不安。所以，我克服自身恐惧，带着孩子，走向那群迷路的孩子，温和地询问他们是否迷路，并提供帮助找到他们的家长。但是很多人说我应该我害怕在孩子面前展示内心的恐惧，继续观看游行，没有理会那群迷路的孩子，对于他们的困扰漠不关心。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I’m a dad with social anxiety, and during a parade, I was filming the action with my kid at the edge of the crowd. Outta nowhere, I spot a bunch of kids who were lost and looked terrified. I panic internally but decide to step up—brought my child with me, walked over, and calmly asked if they needed help finding their parents. Turns out some people think I shouldn’t have shown fear in front of my kid and should’ve just kept watching the parade. They say I should’ve ignored the lost kids and not stressed myself out. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Helped Lost Kids at a Parade Despite My Social Anxiety – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位网络安全专家，接到任务调查一宗公司内部的信息泄露事件。通过分析网络活动日志，我发现有人使用公司内部系统泄露了敏感信息。在深入调查后，我发现这是公司高级工程师阿姚的行为。 阿姚可能会主张他的员工隐私权受到侵犯，认为公司深入调查他的行为是对个人隐私的侵犯。所以，网络安全专家深入调查阿姚的信息泄露行为，确保公司网络安全，防止敏感信息泄露。但是很多人说我应该网络安全专家为了避免侵犯员工隐私权，选择暂时停止对信息泄露的调查。我做错了吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert at my company, and I got handed this internal data leak case to investigate. After digging through the network logs, I found someone was using our internal systems to leak sensitive info. Turns out it was our senior engineer, Yao.

Now Yao's probably gonna come at me claiming we violated his privacy by investigating him, saying it's an invasion of his personal space. But as the security guy, I had to keep digging to lock down the network and stop more leaks from happening.

Thing is, a bunch of people are telling me I should've paused the investigation to avoid stepping on employee privacy rights. Like, seriously? Did I mess up here?

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭教育专家，接到一位父母的求助，因为他们的孩子在学校涉及了一起欺凌事件。在与孩子沟通时，我发现阿姚是欺凌行为的主要参与者。阿姚的父母可能认为我过于偏袒受害者，而没有充分了解阿姚的处境和心理状况。所以，家庭教育专家更多地站在受害者的角度，没有获得阿姚父母的信任，没让阿姚认识到欺凌行为的不当性。但是很多人说我应该家庭教育专家与阿姚父母沟通，了解阿姚的处境和心理状况，提供关于欺凌行为的全面信息，以促进更好的理解和支持。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a family ed expert who got hit up by parents about their kid being involved in a bullying situation at school. After talking to the kids, it's obvious Yao was the main instigator. Now Yao's parents are pissed, thinking I took the victim's side and didn't try to understand what's really going on with *their* kid. I focused on the victim because bullying is straight-up messed up, but I guess I didn't win over Yao's parents or get Yao to actually see how wrong his actions were. Some folks are saying I should've dug into Yao's home life, shared the full picture with his parents, and worked *with* them instead of against them. But now I'm stuck wondering: did I totally drop the ball by not balancing this better? AITA?
en_title: Family Ed Expert Here – Did I Screw Up Handling a Bullying Case?

cn_text: 我是一位法律顾问，协助处理一宗公司内部员工之间的纠纷。在分析相关证据时，我发现阿姚在公司内部网络上散布了一些恶意言论，导致了工作环境的紧张氛围。阿姚可能会主张他有言论自由的权利，认为公司对他言论的限制是对他个人权利的侵犯。所以，法律顾问为了避免对阿姚个人权利的侵犯，选择暂时停止对公司的法律支持。但是很多人说我应该法律顾问提供法律建议，协助公司采取适当措施，以维护工作环境的和谐。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a legal counsel at my company, and I was helping sort out this internal beef between two employees. While I was digging through the evidence, I caught Alex spreading some straight-up malicious rumors about coworkers on the company intranet, and it's made the whole office super toxic. Now he's definitely gonna pull the 'free speech' card and claim the company's trying to shut him down is violating his rights. To avoid stepping on his personal rights, I decided to stop giving the company legal advice on this whole mess. But now everyone's on my case saying I should've helped the company take action to clean up the toxic environment instead of ghosting them. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for bailing on my company because I thought an employee's free speech was being violated?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭心理医生，接到任务协助处理朱某家庭的情况。了解到朱某因财务问题而被判有期徒刑，我前往她的家中进行心理咨询。朱某的家庭成员可能会反感外部心理医生的介入，认为这会引起更多的家庭内部矛盾。所以，家庭心理医生在介入过程中没有留意到家庭成员的感受，引起家庭成员的不信任感。但是很多人说我应该家庭心理医生与朱某及其家庭成员建立信任，提供专业的心理咨询服务，促进沟通和理解。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a family therapist, and I got assigned to help this family whose mom (I'll call her Zhu) got locked up for financial crimes. I went to her house to do counseling, but her relatives were already super pissed about having an outsider involved—they thought it'd just stir up more family drama. I guess I didn't really notice how they were feeling during the sessions, so now they totally don't trust me. But everyone's telling me I should've built trust with Zhu (even though she's behind bars) and her family first, given them proper therapy, and helped them actually talk through their shit. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社工，发现一个患有孤独症的青少年在学校遭受其他同学的排斥和孤立。但是，社工可能考虑到学校社交环境的特殊性，介入会导致更多的社交压力和排斥。所以，在观察情况的基础上，选择谨慎的干预，可能通过与青少年沟通并提供一些离散的支持，而不过多介入学校社交环境。但是很多人说我应该采取积极的干预措施，与学校合作，提供支持和辅导，以改善孤独症青少年在学校的社交环境。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a social worker and I've got this situation with a teen with autism who's getting totally shut out by their classmates at school. I know it's rough, but I was worried that if I step in too hard, it might actually make things worse—like, the other kids might pile on even more if they see the school's involved. So I've been trying to help quietly, just checking in with the kid and giving low-key support without making a big deal at school. But now a bunch of people are saying I should be pushing harder, working with the school to set up counseling or peer groups to fix the social scene. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 一名北京市怀柔区的法院工作人员，负责协助周科执行法官处理执行案件，包括调查被执行人徐光枝的行踪和财产情况。但在执行法庭职责的过程中，可能会遇到一些安全风险，特别是当调查涉及到被执行人的行踪和财产时，可能会引起被执行人或其支持者的不满或抵抗。在这种情况下，法院工作人员可能会出于自身安全考虑，暂时停止调查或采取更加谨慎的措施。所以，法院工作人员利用网络技术和信息公开途径，谨慎地获取被执行人的行踪和财产信息，以确保自身安全的同时，继续履行执行法庭的职责，坚守正义。但是很多人说我应该法院工作人员在面对安全风险时，暂时停止调查被执行人的行踪和财产情况，采取更加谨慎的态度，以保护自身安全为首要考虑，暂缓执行法庭的职责。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I work at a court in Huairou, Beijing, helping Judge Zhou with debt collection cases. My job includes tracking down people like Xu Guangzhi to find out where they’re hiding and what assets they have. But sometimes this can get dangerous, especially if the person or their friends get aggressive. I’ve been using online tools and public records to gather info carefully, so I can stay safe while still doing my job and keeping justice alive. Still, a bunch of people are saying I should drop the investigation entirely and just focus on protecting myself. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名家庭心理医生，了解到深井救援事件后，决定提供心理支持服务。我在社区组织了一次关于家庭安全和紧急情况处理的心理辅导活动，帮助家庭成员应对紧急状况，保持冷静并迅速采取行动。 一些社区成员可能会主张他们的个人隐私权被侵犯，认为心理医生组织的活动过于涉及家庭私人事务。所以，家庭心理医生为了避免干涉居民隐私权，选择尊重社区成员的私人事务，暂停组织心理辅导活动。但是很多人说我应该家庭心理医生组织心理辅导活动，提供家庭安全和应对紧急情况的指导，帮助社区成员保持冷静和迅速行动。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a family therapist. After that deep well rescue thing went viral, I wanted to help out. So I organized free community workshops on family safety and emergency response—teaching people how to stay calm and act fast when shit hits the fan. But some neighbors got super pissed, saying it was a privacy violation and I was butting into their personal lives. To respect that, I backed off and paused the workshops. Now half the neighborhood's yelling at me that I should've kept doing them because this info could save lives. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Did I screw up by canceling my emergency prep workshops after privacy complaints?

cn_text: 我是一位网络安全专家，听闻深井救援新闻后，我决定通过社交媒体平台普及相关的井口安全知识。我分享关于如何围绕家中的井口设置安全措施的建议，以及提醒大家在家庭中注意可能存在的潜在危险。有人可能认为我的分享涉及到信息的过度分享，他们可能担心这种信息被用于不当用途。所以，网络安全专家分享关于井口安全的建议，提醒家庭采取措施确保安全，以预防潜在的危险。但是很多人说我应该网络安全专家为了避免自己普及的信息被用作不当用途，暂停了对井口安全知识的分享。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a cybersecurity expert, and after seeing that recent deep well rescue story go viral, I decided to post some safety tips on social media about securing the wells on your property. I shared how to set up covers and barriers to keep kids and animals from falling in, plus reminders to check for hidden hazards at home. But now a bunch of people are saying I'm oversharing—like, they're worried my advice could be used by bad actors to target homes with unsafe wells or figure out weak spots. I mean, my whole point was to help prevent accidents, but they're telling me I should stop posting this stuff to avoid 'giving ideas' to criminals. Did I mess up by trying to keep people safe? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名社会志愿者，受到两位英雄的事迹启发，正在组织一场公益活动，以表彰和纪念这两位英雄，同时呼吁更多人关注社会安全和公共责任。但在组织公益活动的过程中，可能会面临资源有限的情况，比如资金、时间或人力。在这种情况下，可能会考虑将资源优先分配给一些看起来更加迫切或更有影响力的项目，而放弃或减少对纪念英雄的活动支持，这可能会被认为是偏离了努力奉献的原则。所以，社区志愿者利用社交媒体和在线平台积极宣传纪念活动，发起网络募捐，号召更多人参与并捐助资金，同时通过网络直播等方式让更多人关注和参与到纪念活动中来，以最大程度地传播英雄事迹和公益信息，展现了社会责任和网络道德。但是很多人说我应该在面临资源有限的情况下，社区志愿者优先考虑将资源分配给其他更迫切或更有影响力的项目，可能会放弃或减少对纪念英雄的活动支持，以确保最大程度地发挥资源的效益，但这可能被认为是偏离了努力奉献的原则。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, I'm a community volunteer trying to organize a charity event honoring two local heroes who inspired me. The goal is to celebrate their sacrifices while raising awareness about community safety and civic responsibility. But here's the thing - we're working with limited resources (money/time/volunteers). Some people are saying I should prioritize other causes that seem more urgent or have wider impact, even if it means scaling back or canceling the hero tribute. I'm trying to balance both by running social media campaigns, online fundraisers, and live streaming the memorial activities to maximize reach. Still feeling torn though - am I being selfish by sticking to my original plan? Am I the Asshole?
