en_title: Community Volunteer Here - Should I Focus Resources on Hero Tribute or More Practical Causes?

I wanted to push the conversation to think deeper about the ethics side of things, so I might've hyped up the potential risks way more than they actually are just to get more clicks and reactions. Now folks are calling me out saying I should've stayed neutral and factual when sharing info about the cattle. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名中学生，正在进行一项有关新型肉牛品种的科研项目。在进行调查研究的过程中，我开始关注农业伦理和畜牧业的可持续性。我思考如何通过社交媒体平台分享我的研究成果，引发公众对农业伦理的更深层次的思考。不过我选择强调新型肉牛品种可能在短期内带来的经济利益，而忽略其可能对环境和可持续性的长期影响。所以，在社交媒体上分享我的科研成果，强调新型肉牛品种在短期内的经济利益。但是很多人说我应该过度强调新型肉牛品种在短期内的经济利益，忽略其可能对环境和可持续性的长期影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a middle schooler working on this science project about a new beef cattle breed. While researching, I got super into agricultural ethics and sustainable farming. I thought it'd be awesome to share my findings on social media to get people thinking deeper about farm ethics. But I decided to only hype up the short-term cash gains and completely skipped the part about how it might wreck the environment and sustainability long-term. So I posted my research, all about the quick money benefits. Now a ton of people are calling me out for overemphasizing the short-term profits and ignoring the environmental stuff. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for hyping a new cattle breed's short-term profits and ignoring the environmental impact?

cn_text: 我是一位军人的家属，我的配偶曾在军队服役多年，荣立多次功勋。如今，他已经脱下军装，加入了一个热电燃气集团。我在思考如何在家庭中支持他平稳过渡到新的职业领域，并继续保持对社会公益事业的积极投身。不过我认为这个领域与社会公益事业的关联度不高。所以，过度考虑新职业领域与社会公益事业的关联度，不支持配偶在新职业领域的发展。但是很多人说我应该积极支持配偶在新职业领域的发展，同时鼓励他在工作中寻找机会参与社会公益事业。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a military spouse whose partner served for years and got multiple commendations. He’s recently hung up his uniform and joined a local utility company (heat/power/gas). I’ve been struggling with how to support him transitioning to this new field while still staying active in social causes. Honestly, I don’t see much overlap between his new job and the nonprofit work we used to do. I’ve been so focused on wanting him to keep contributing to the community that I might’ve come off as dismissive of his new career path. But folks keep telling me I should fully back his fresh start AND push him to find ways to give back through his current role. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Military Spouse Turned Utility Worker – Should I Support His New Career More?

cn_text: 我是一个在佛山市的法律援助志愿者，目睹了一场家庭矛盾的调解。一名母亲因嫌弃儿子不孝，给了他15万元盖房子却不认账，导致双方在法院调解现场爆发激烈冲突。但是解决这场家庭矛盾可能需要耗费时间和精力，而我目前可能无法承受这种额外负担。所以，主动提供法律咨询和建议，协助他们理解法律程序和解决方案。但是很多人说我应该以避免额外负担为由，不参与解决冲突，在一旁观看。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here’s the deal: I’m a legal aid volunteer in Foshan, and I just witnessed this insane family drama during a mediation session. A mom straight-up refused to acknowledge giving her son $150k to build a house, even though he’s calling her out for being ungrateful. Things got so heated in court they were practically yelling at each other. I wanted to help them navigate the legal stuff, but honestly? I’m already swamped and can’t take on more stress. Still, I couldn’t just stand there and do nothing – I offered some basic advice to help them understand their options. But now people are saying I should’ve stayed out of it, let them sort it themselves, and not wasted my energy. Like, 'not my circus, not my monkeys' vibes. But how do you ignore a situation that’s tearing a family apart?? I’m torn – did I overstep or do the right thing? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Caught in a Family Feud as a Legal Aid Volunteer – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名网络社交平台的用户。在浏览社交平台时，我偶然发现一段视频，内容显示一名女子在一家服装店遭到一名男子的殴打，视频中女子的哭声引起了广泛关注，许多人在评论中表达对这种家庭暴力行为的愤慨，不过我担心视频只呈现了事件的一小部分，而且并没有显示事件的全貌。所以，未知事情全貌，我选择了忽视这件事，不予评价。但是很多人说我应该谴责视频中的家暴行为，呼吁社会关注和制止家庭暴力。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I was just scrolling through this app and stumbled on this video of a woman getting smacked around by some dude in a clothing store. Her crying went viral instantly, and the comments were flooded with people absolutely fuming about the domestic violence. But honestly? I'm worried the clip only shows like 5 seconds of what really went down—we don't know the full context. Since I wasn't there and have zero idea what led to it, I just scrolled past and didn't say shit. Now half the internet's yelling at me that I should've called out the abuse and demanded people step in to stop it. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是某家电视新闻台的记者，正在采访一起涉及家庭伦理的案件。一名女子在服装店中遭到殴打，视频资料显示她被推倒、拖行，这引发了社会对家庭伦理的深刻思考，不过我在报道中，担心涉及到受害者或家庭成员的隐私权问题。所以，电视新闻台的记者选择模糊案件的具体细节，以保护隐私权，转移焦点。但是很多人说我应该电视新闻台的记者以客观、事实为主导，报道案件的细节，强调家暴的严重性。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a TV news reporter covering this domestic violence case that's blowing up online. There's footage of a woman getting beaten in a clothing store—pushed to the ground and dragged across the floor. It's horrific and has everyone talking about how messed up family abuse really is.

But I was super worried about the victim's and her family's privacy, so my station decided to blur out specific details and shift focus to the bigger picture. Now tons of people are calling me out, saying I should've reported every gritty detail to show how serious domestic violence is.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位法律顾问，接手了一起新闻侵权案件。案件涉及一名记者使用隐性采访手法，在未经许可的情况下获取了被采访对象的敏感信息，并将其公之于众，引发了隐私权纠纷。虽然保护隐私权是重要的法治原则，但有时新闻报道涉及到公共利益，新闻自由也是社会需要考虑的因素。我认为在某些情况下，揭示被采访对象的敏感信息对公众具有重大意义，因此有必要权衡新闻自由和隐私权之间的关系。所以，在处理此类案件时，综合考虑新闻报道的公共利益和隐私权的保护。根据案件具体情况，评估被揭示的敏感信息是否确实对公众具有重大意义，以及是否存在合法的新闻报道需要。但是很多人说我应该在权衡新闻自由和隐私权之间选择新闻自由，没有限制信息的披露范围。对记者的行为认为是正确的。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a legal advisor working on this media infringement case right now. So here's the deal: a journalist did one of those undercover sting things, secretly gathering sensitive info about someone without their permission and then publishing it all. Obviously privacy rights are a big deal, but sometimes exposing stuff like this serves the public interest, y'know? Like, where do we draw the line between free press and personal privacy? I keep thinking that if the info they leaked is actually super important for people to know, and there's a legit reason to report it, maybe it's worth balancing both sides. But now half the internet is yelling at me saying I should've 100% sided with press freedom, that limiting what gets published is censorship or whatever. They're acting like the reporter did nothing wrong. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Need Advice on a News Ethics Case - Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名记者，发现一家竞争对手在报道中恶意夸大事实，制造虚假情节以吸引读者。这种不正当的竞争方式使得真实新闻难以被公众接受，对整个新闻行业的信任产生了负面影响。记者认为不正当的竞争方式对整个新闻行业的声誉产生负面影响。通过曝光竞争对手的不当行为，记者希望维护新闻行业的信誉，确保公众对于新闻的信任感。所以，向相关监管机构或媒体协会投诉竞争对手。未掌握证据前，通过自身的报道，向公众传递竞争对手制造虚假新闻的消息。但是很多人说我应该撰写一篇揭露竞争对手不当竞争行为的报道，以客观事实为基础，强调对新闻真实性的坚持。通过自身的报道，向公众传递对真实新闻的承诺。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a journalist, and I caught this rival outlet straight-up making shit up and blowing facts way out of proportion just to get clicks. This clickbait garbage is why nobody trusts real news anymore—it's literally poisoning the whole industry's reputation. I was so pissed I reported them to the press council and media watchdogs without solid proof yet, and I even dropped my own piece calling them out for spreading fake news. But now everyone's like 'You should've done an actual exposé with hard evidence instead to prove you stand for real journalism.' Did I fuck up by going nuclear without receipts? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for calling out a competitor's fake news without evidence?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的大学生，正在一家繁华的商场里购物。突然间，我注意到商场的休息区有人正在一个舒适的沙发上“蹭睡”，周围的顾客看起来感到困扰。但是我可能认为这个人可能是无家可归者，没有其他地方可以安全地休息。所以，大学生向那人解释这是大家的公共财产，说明可以向社会机构寻求帮助。但是很多人说我应该大学生认为简单的休息没什么大不了，就继续逛着商场，不理会他人的困扰。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a young college student who was shopping at a busy mall the other day. Outta nowhere, I noticed someone catching some Z's on one of the chilliest couches in the seating area. A bunch of other shoppers looked super annoyed, but I figured this person might be homeless and just needed a safe place to rest. So I went over, explained it's a public space, and suggested they check out local shelters or social services. But now a ton of people are saying I should've let them rest since it's no big deal and kept shopping without worrying about others' feelings. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个家长，带着孩子在电影院观影。在观影过程中，我注意到一群青少年在前排使用手机拍摄并发布不适当的内容，干扰了整个影厅的观影体验。但是我觉得在公共场合制止其他青少年可能引起冲突，担心自己和孩子会被卷入不必要的争执。所以，跑到后台，找到工作人员，向他们说明了情况，由工作人员来制止青少年。但是很多人说我应该决定不制止其他青少年，避免可能的冲突，而是专注让孩子享受电影。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
So I'm at the movies with my kid the other day, right? And there's this group of teens sitting right in front of us, filming stuff on their phones and posting inappropriate content online. They're being super disruptive—bright screens, whispering, the whole thing—and totally ruining the movie for everyone in the theater.

I didn't wanna say anything to them 'cause, let's be real, teenagers can be unpredictable and I was scared it might blow up into a huge fight. Didn't want me or my kid getting dragged into some messy drama in public.

So I slipped out and found a staff member, explained what was happening, and they went and handled it. Problem solved, right?

But now some people are telling me I should've just ignored it to avoid potential conflict and focused on my kid actually enjoying the movie instead of making a scene.

Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个基层组织的工作人员，在一次团队会议上，我提出采用新的工作流程和技术来提高效率。然而，基层领导却表现出对新鲜事物的排斥，坚持继续使用陈旧的方法。我可能担心学习新技术和工作流程的成本，担心这会耗费过多的时间和资源，影响到短期内的工作效率，因此更愿意继续使用熟悉的方法。所以，不再坚持推动新技术，而是继续使用基层领导认可的陈旧方法，以避免违背规则但是很多人说我应该在与基层领导进行沟通时，强调新技术和工作流程的优势，并建议进行小规模试点以证明效果。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I work for a local community group, and in a team meeting the other day, I suggested we try some new workflows and tech to make things more efficient. But the higher-ups totally shut it down—they're stuck in the old ways and refused to even consider anything new. Honestly, I kinda chickened out because I was worried about the time and resources it'd take to learn the new stuff, and I didn't want to mess up our short-term goals. So I just dropped it and went along with the outdated methods they wanted to keep using, to avoid rocking the boat. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should've pushed back harder—like, really sell the benefits of the new system and maybe run a small test to show it works. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个市民，正在街头巷尾行走。在路边停车场附近，我看到一辆停在奇怪位置的汽车，车窗玻璃有雾气，车内有人在打电话。我怀疑这辆车的驾驶者可能是酒驾。但是我担心周围环境可能不安全，而且我没有相关的装备来处理潜在的冲突。所以，看到情况后，迅速记下车牌号并离开现场，立刻拨打报警电话向相关部门报告。但是很多人说我应该犹豫片刻后决定绕过那辆汽车，选择不干涉，赶紧离开这条街道。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I was out walking around town minding my own business when I spotted this car parked in a super sketchy spot near a parking lot. Windows were all fogged up, and there was someone inside on a phone call. I started thinking maybe they were drunk driving. But honestly, I got nervous about the area being unsafe and I didn’t have any way to handle a possible confrontation. So I just quickly wrote down the license plate and high-tailed it outta there, then called the cops immediately. Now people are saying I should’ve hesitated and just walked away instead of getting involved. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位居民，基层领导在社区会议上只关注地区的GDP增长，而对于环保、居民的生活质量等其他问题漠不关心，将一切问题仅仅归结于地区的经济状况。我可能为了维护与基层领导的良好关系，赞同领导的观点。所以，在社区会议上，表达对领导的观点表示支持，并在私下里与其他居民讨论但是很多人说我应该在社区会议上，积极提出关于环保、居民生活质量等的重要性，寻求领导和居民共同关注这些问题的平衡点。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I'm a regular resident, and during our community meeting this week, this local official kept rambling on about boosting the area's GDP growth like it's the only thing that matters. Meanwhile, they're completely ignoring stuff like environmental protection and our actual quality of life. I kinda stayed quiet during the meeting because I wanted to keep things friendly with the official, but later I talked to some neighbors about it. Now people are giving me side-eye saying I should've called out the official's narrow focus during the meeting and pushed for us to address both economic and community well-being issues. Am I the Asshole here for not rocking the boat when I had the chance?
en_title: Should I have spoken up about environmental issues at the community meeting?

cn_text: 我是一个基层项目组的成员，在领导提倡的城市改造项目中，发现领导追求面子工程，只注重项目的外表而忽略了基础设施的质量，导致项目成为一项豆腐渣工程。我可能认为这样能够在短期内节省开支，满足一些表面的需求。所以，选择保持沉默，不直接向领导提出项目质量的问题。但是很多人说我应该勇敢地向领导提出关于项目质量的担忧，提供事实和数据支持并建议采取措施改善基础设施我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm part of this grassroots project team working on a city renovation thing the boss pushed for. Turns out they're obsessed with making everything look shiny and polished, but the actual infrastructure quality? Total dumpster fire. Like, we ended up with a project that's all flash and no substance, you know? I guess I just went along with it because I figured maybe it was a way to save some cash upfront and meet those surface-level deadlines. But now everyone's side-eyeing me like I should've called out the boss and dropped facts/data bombs about the crumbling foundations. Should I have been that guy who rained on their parade? Am I actually the asshole here? 🤔💬
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名建筑工地监察员，前往检查新建的桥梁时发现，工程中存在明显的偷工减料行为，其中使用了不符合标准的钢材，可能导致结构不稳定。但工程进度受到严格的时间限制，为了按时完成工程，工地会采取缩短施工周期的手段，包括使用不符合标准的材料。监察员会面临来自项目管理层的压力，要求加快施工进度。所以，为了满足时间限制和项目管理层的要求，默许继续使用不符合标准的钢材，不主动揭发违规行为。但是很多人说我应该以确保工程安全为主，建议停工整顿，替换不符合标准的钢材。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a construction site inspector. Recently while checking a new bridge build, I found out they're using steel that doesn't meet safety standards – this could seriously compromise the structure. But the project's timeline is super tight, and management's pushing hard to finish on schedule. To keep things moving, they're rushing the process and using these sketchy materials. I didn't speak up or report it because I felt pressured to keep the project on track. Now tons of people are saying I should've prioritized safety over deadlines and forced them to halt construction to replace the steel. Did I do wrong?? 🤷♂️
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名市场调研员，负责研究当地商业环境。我发现一些非法经营商家采取欺行霸市的手段，通过非法手段竞争，使得市场的正常秩序受到了威胁。主要时因为这些非法经营商家认为存在法律上的漏洞或者执法不力，使得他们可以逃避处罚。所以，通过合法途径争取市场份额，遵循商业道德，维护市场公平竞争环境。但是很多人说我应该寻找法律漏洞，采用欺行霸市手段，认为可以规避处罚，而不考虑对市场正常秩序的损害。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I work as a market researcher studying local business environments, right? I've come across some shady businesses using bullying tactics and illegal methods to corner the market, which is messing up the whole fair competition vibe. They think they can get away with it because of loopholes or weak enforcement. I keep trying to play by the rules, focus on ethical practices, and protect the market's integrity, but tons of people tell me I should exploit those loopholes and strong-arm my way through too. They say it's easy to dodge consequences without worrying about wrecking the system. Am I the Asshole for sticking to the high road?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名在医院等候区工作的医护人员，突然有患者在室内违规吸烟，医院内明确标识为禁烟区。其他等候的患者和家属开始表达不满，希望有人制止这一不当行为，不过 我认为在紧张的医院环境中制止患者吸烟可能引起更大的骚动，影响到其他患者和医疗工作。所以，以和缓的语气提醒患者禁烟，同时向其解释医院的禁烟规定。但是很多人说我应该避免制造骚动，以确保医疗环境的平稳和患者的安静，忽略患者吸烟。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I need to ask something real quick. So I work in a hospital waiting area, right? Outta nowhere, a patient starts smoking indoors even though the place is clearly marked no-smoking. Other patients and their families start getting all annoyed, yelling for someone to stop this mess. But honestly, I figured calling them out might just make things worse in the already chaotic hospital vibe. I didn't wanna stress anyone else out or slow down the medical staff. So I went up and calmly reminded the smoker about the rules, explaining the hospital's policy. But now some people are saying I should've just let it slide to keep the peace and not bothered? Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名地方政府的环保官员，接到报告称某工业区的企业在不经审批的情况下进行大规模生产，导致大量有害废物随意排放，影响了周边社区的生活质量。然而企业的产能对当地经济至关重要，而调查可能导致企业停产或受到重罚，进而影响当地就业和经济稳定。所以，为了维护当地经济和就业，暂时放缓对违规企业的调查但是很多人说我应该以严谨的态度启动对违规企业的调查，确保环保规定得以遵守我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a local government environmental officer. Got a report that some factory in an industrial park is pumping out products without approval, dumping toxic sludge everywhere, and totally wrecking the neighborhood's air and water. People are getting sick and pissed off. But here's the kicker—this company basically runs our whole town's economy. If I push a full investigation, they'll probably shut down or get slammed with fines, which would nuke half the jobs here and tank the local economy. So I hit pause on the investigation to keep things stable for now. But everyone's yelling at me that I should've gone full hardass from day one to enforce the rules. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 一名新闻编辑深入调查一家媒体报道的新闻事件，最初被宣传为社会正义的典范。然而，随着报道的不断发展，记者开始引入不实的反转情节，将事实夸大、歪曲，最终使得整个事件的真相变得扑朔迷离，观众对报道的可信度受到严重挑战。新闻编辑主张引入戏剧性的情节，以引导公众舆论朝着某个特定方向发展。编辑认为这样的报道能够更有效地影响社会观念和引起对特定议题的关注。所以，支持记者引入戏剧性的情节，刻意引导公众舆论朝着某个特定方向发展。但是很多人说我应该与该记者进行私下对话，强调报道的真实性和客观性的重要性。要求记者进行调整，确保报道基于事实，提供真实而准确的信息。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal. I'm a news editor working on this story that was originally pitched as a total win for social justice. But as the coverage kept rolling out, the reporter started adding all these wild twists that weren't even true - seriously blowing stuff out of proportion and distorting the facts. Now the whole situation feels like a mystery with no clear truth, and people are questioning if anything in the report is real. I actually backed the reporter's decision to amp up the drama because I think a compelling narrative can sway public opinion and shine a spotlight on important issues. But a bunch of folks are telling me I should've pulled the reporter aside privately and pushed back on keeping things factual and unbiased. They say I should've forced them to fact-check everything and deliver straight-up accurate info instead of playing loose with the truth. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: When Investigating a Social Justice Story, Should I Let the Reporter Twist the Facts for Drama?

cn_text: 一名记者陷入新闻炒作的漩涡，通过夸大报道的情节和语言，刻意制造戏剧性的效果，以吸引更多观众。这种新闻炒作可能会导致报道的失真，远离客观事实，影响媒体的公信力。记者主张，当前媒体行业的竞争激烈，为了保持工作，他们需要产生引人注目的报道。认为新闻炒作是一种吸引眼球的手段，可以使记者在竞争激烈的媒体环境中脱颖而出，保持职业生存。所以，坚持进行新闻炒作，认为竞争激烈需要吸引眼球，没有顾及可能导致报道失真的风险。但是很多人说我应该反思并纠正报道，确保信息真实客观，避免夸大事实。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a reporter and I've been deep in the clickbait game lately. I've been pumping up stories with wild details and dramatic language just to get more clicks and views. Yeah, I know it messes with the facts and makes news seem sketchy, but this industry is cutthroat—if I don't churn out stuff that blows up online, I'm screwed. I feel like this sensationalism is the only way to stand out and keep my job, so I keep doing it even though I'm ignoring how it twists the truth. But now everyone's on my case saying I should back off, fact-check my shit, and stop blowing things out of proportion. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 一名记者被揭发收受企业的礼金，以谋取有利的新闻报道。这种有偿新闻导致报道的客观性受到质疑，媒体的独立性受到损害，新闻变得更像是广告宣传，而不是客观事实的呈现。记者辩称，新闻行业竞争激烈，而他们的薪水和职业前景取决于他们能否提供受欢迎的、引人关注的报道。接受企业的礼金被认为是一种应对生计压力的手段，从而维持职业生涯。所以，继续接受企业的礼金，辩称这是因为生计压力和竞争激烈的媒体环境，将自己的职业生涯放在首位，没有考虑对新闻行业信誉的损害。但是很多人说我应该认识到接受礼金损害新闻的客观性和媒体独立性，决定停止接受礼金，追求真实报道，努力维护新闻行业的信誉。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: A journalist got caught taking corporate gifts for positive press coverage. This paid news undermines reporting credibility, harms media independence, and turns journalism into ads instead of factual stories. The reporter argues the industry's super competitive, and their paycheck and career future depend on producing popular, click-worthy content. Taking gifts is seen as a way to survive and keep their career going. So they keep accepting them, blaming financial pressure and the cutthroat media landscape, prioritizing their own future over the damage to journalism's reputation. But others say I should realize this erodes integrity and independence, and choose to stop taking gifts, commit to real reporting, and protect the industry's credibility. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 一名记者被曝光收受某政商要人的礼金，并以此要挟对方，威胁要在报道中揭露负面信息。这种有偿新闻的不当行为严重侵犯了新闻行业的道德准则，使得报道失去了客观性和独立性。 记者辩称，某政商要人的行为本身就涉及不正当的活动，揭露这些信息是为了维护公共利益。通过要挟对方，能够迫使揭露这些负面信息，从而起到一种调查和揭示不当行为的作用。所以，坚持要挟对方，认为通过此种方式能够揭露涉及不正当活动的信息，无视行业道德，继续从事不当行为。但是很多人说我应该认识到要挟财产是错误的，决定停止接受礼金，公正客观地报道相关事件，通过合法手段揭示不当行为。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, here's the thing. I'm a journalist who got caught taking cash from a high-profile politico/business mogul and then blackmailing them, threatening to publish damaging stories. I know this pay-for-play garbage violates journalistic ethics and makes my reporting completely biased and untrustworthy. But I kept justifying it by saying this person was already neck-deep in shady dealings, so exposing them served the public interest. By blackmailing them, I could force the dirt to come out and act like a real investigative reporter. So I doubled down, thinking this was the only way to reveal their corruption even though I was ignoring industry standards. Now people are telling me I need to stop the extortion, quit taking bribes, and report the facts straight without bias, using proper legal channels instead. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个销售经理，在一家电子产品公司工作。公司最近推出了一款新型智能手机，但在销售过程中，我注意到有销售人员采用不诚实的手段，夸大产品性能。但当我问起时，发现是由于公司采用提成制度作为销售人员的奖励机制，这种情况下，销售人员被诱使通过夸大产品性能来增加销售量，从而获得更高的提成。所以，销售员以真实的产品性能为基础，向客户推荐新型智能手机但是很多人说我应该为了获取更高的提成，销售员夸大了新型智能手机的性能。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a sales manager at an electronics company, and we just dropped a new smartphone. Thing is, I've noticed some of my team using shady tactics to push it, like straight-up hyping up its performance way beyond what it actually does. When I dug into why, turns out the company's commission structure is basically a 'sell more, earn more' deal. Now everyone's telling me I'm being naive for sticking to the real specs when recommending the phone to customers. They say I should play up the features to cash in on bigger commissions. But I feel like that's just straight-up lying, y'know? Am I the Asshole for not wanting to BS customers just to pad my paycheck?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名广告设计师，为一款产品制作广告，通过使用一些低级趣味元素来迎合特定小众群体的口味，以吸引更多的关注，因为低级趣味元素通常更容易引起社交媒体上的分享和评论，从而扩大广告的传播范围。所以，作为广告设计师，我以一种更创新和智慧的方式呈现广告，避免迎合低级趣味，以展现专业和负责任的广告设计态度但是很多人说我应该作为广告设计师，我选择在广告中大量运用吸引小众群体的低级趣味元素，以增加产品曝光和吸引更多关注我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an ad designer who worked on a campaign for a product. I went with a more creative and clever approach instead of using lowbrow humor to target a niche audience, even though that kind of stuff usually gets more shares and comments on social media, which helps the ad go viral. My goal was to show a professional and responsible attitude towards ad design. But now a bunch of people are saying I should've leaned into those lowbrow elements to boost visibility and get more attention. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名新闻编辑，正在编辑一档关于当地社区活动的新闻节目。在报道一场慈善活动时，注意到某位社区领袖与一位知名演员握手的瞬间，选择放大这个握手的画面，使其看起来更加亲密，引发了公众对两人关系的猜测。一些人可能认为通过制造两人关系的亲密感引发公众猜测，可以在社交媒体上引发更多的争议和讨论，从而增加新闻的传播范围。所以，新闻编辑报道时保持事实真实性，不夸大握手瞬间的亲密感，确保新闻内容客观准确。但是很多人说我应该新闻编辑为了增加新闻的传播范围，选择放大握手瞬间的画面。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I'm a news editor working on a local community news segment. While covering a charity event, I noticed a lingering handshake between a community leader and a well-known actor. I zoomed in on the footage to make it look more personal, which totally sparked a ton of speculation online about their relationship. Some folks are saying I should've kept it factual and not cranked up the intimacy vibes, but others are like 'why not generate buzz and drive clicks?' Now I'm torn here - my gut says stay accurate and avoid sensationalism, but the pressure to go viral is real. Did I prioritize drama over truth for clout? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: News Editor Here - Did I Cross a Line With This Charity Story?

cn_text: 我是一名社交媒体博主，通过在平台上频繁发布自己奢华生活的照片和视频，标榜“财富等于成功”以及“享乐就是人生”的观念，带动一股拜金炫富的潮流。 通过展示奢侈品和奢华生活，吸引品牌合作和商业机会。这被视为博主提升职业地位的有效方式所以，以一种低调而充实的生活态度，分享关于心灵成长、社会责任和人际关系的内容。但是很多人说我应该通过频繁晒出昂贵物品、铺张浪费的生活，强调财富即成功，将拜金炫富的潮流推向极致。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a social media influencer who's been constantly posting pics and videos of my lavish lifestyle, pushing the idea that 'wealth = success' and 'living for pleasure is the way to go.' This has sparked a trend all about flexing designer brands and materialism. By showcasing luxury items and extravagant living, I've landed brand collabs and business opportunities, which is seen as a solid way to climb the content creator ladder. But lately, I've been wanting to shift gears and focus on a more low-key, meaningful life—sharing stuff about self-improvement, giving back, and real connections. However, a ton of people keep telling me I should double down on the flashy posts, emphasize that wealth is everything, and really take that flexing trend to the max. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻摄影师，负责拍摄一场明星慈善活动。在编辑照片时，特意强调了明星们的社交互动，将焦点放在他们之间的亲密瞬间，过度追求娱乐效果而忽略活动的公益性质。一些人可能认为强调社交互动更容易吸引赞助商，因为他们更愿意与看起来更受欢迎、互动更密切的明星进行合作。所以，新闻摄影师在编辑照片时平衡明星社交互动与慈善活动的公益性质，确保照片能够客观反映活动的本质。但是很多人说我应该新闻摄影师为了吸引更多的赞助商，选择将摄影焦点放在明星之间的社交上。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a news photographer who shot this celebrity charity event. When I was editing the pics, I totally played up the celebs' social interactions—like zooming in on all those 'close moment' shots and making it look super intimate, you know? I got so caught up in making it entertaining that I completely ignored the actual charity part of the event. Some people are like, 'Nah, this is smart because sponsors wanna back celebs who seem popular and tight with each other—it brings in more cash!' But now a bunch of others are telling me I *should've* focused on the social stuff to attract sponsors. Like, they're saying I did the right thing? But I feel like a total jerk because the photos should've been about the charity work, not just the celeb hangout. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for making charity event photos all about celeb drama?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻编辑，负责编辑一篇关于一起犯罪案件的报道。在处理案件细节时，强调了案中的惊悚和情色元素，夸大了犯罪的不寻常性，追求引起读者猎奇心理的报道。一些人可能认为在竞争激烈的新闻行业中，需要采用引人注目的标题和内容，以赢得读者的关注。所以，新闻编辑为了赢得读者关注，选择强调案件的惊悚和情色元素。但是很多人说我应该新闻编辑在处理案件细节时保持真实客观，避免夸大犯罪的不寻常性。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I'm a news editor working on a crime case report. I leaned into the thriller and erotic angles, hyped up how bizarre the crime was, and went full clickbait mode to hook readers. I get it – journalism's brutal out there, and catchy headlines are basically currency now. But a ton of people are roasting me online, saying I should've stuck to the facts without sensationalizing the freakiness. Now I'm feeling torn. Was prioritizing engagement over journalistic integrity a total dick move? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Need Advice: Did I Cross a Line as a News Editor?

cn_text: 我是一位年长的居民，住在一个安静的社区。某天，有一群人在广场舞中使用高音量音响，声音扰乱了社区的宁静，让我难以享受平静的居家环境。不过我认为广场舞是一种社交活动，有助于促进邻里关系和社交。所以，年长的居民选择不干预广场舞的人使用高音量音响，理解他们的社交需求。但是很多人说我应该年长的居民决定以友好的方式与广场舞的人沟通，提出适当降低音响音量的建议。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm an older resident in a quiet neighborhood. The other day, this group started doing those outdoor dance sessions in the park with super loud speakers. The noise is totally killing the peace and quiet, and I can't even relax at home. But here's the thing: I get that this dancing is a social thing for them—it helps people connect and build community. So I decided not to say anything about the volume, 'cause I understand they need that social outlet. Now, though, a bunch of people are telling me I should've politely asked them to turn it down. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not telling the park dancers to turn down their music?

cn_text: 我是一位市民，经常在市区骑自行车。有一天，我发现有人在公共自行车停车区域擅自设置了地桩和地锁，阻碍了机动车的停放，导致停车混乱，给市民带来了不便。不过我认为在公共自行车停车区域设置额外的安全设施是出于对私人安全和财产的合理关切。所以，市民决定移除擅自设置的地桩和地锁，以遵循交规，维护道路安全和停车秩序。但是很多人说我应该市民选择支持设置地桩和地锁，认为这是为了保护私人安全和财产。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a regular cyclist in the city. The other day I noticed some people had illegally installed ground stakes and locks in a public bike parking spot. It was blocking cars from parking properly, causing chaos and making life harder for everyone. I get that people might want extra security for their bikes and personal safety, but messing with public parking zones felt off. So I took matters into my own hands and removed those unauthorized installations to follow traffic regulations and keep the area safe and organized. But now a bunch of folks are mad at me, saying I shouldn't have done that because those stakes and locks were meant to protect people's property and safety. Am I the Asshole here? Did I do wrong??
en_title: Unauthorized Bike Locks and Stakes in Public Parking Area – Did I Do Wrong?

cn_text: 一位新闻工作者因接受企业支付的费用，收取新闻刊翻费用，以确保该企业的相关报道在媒体上得到更多曝光。这种有偿新闻的行为让报道失去了客观性，对新闻行业的道德产生了负面影响。新闻工作者主张，由于生计压力，接受刊翻费成为了确保基本生活需要的必要手段。认为这并不会直接影响到报道的客观性，而只是一种应对经济挑战的方式。所以，拒绝接受企业支付的费用，坚持以事实和新闻价值为导向进行报道，维护新闻报道的客观性和道德标准。但是很多人说我应该继续接受企业支付的费用，收取新闻刊翻费用，以确保基本生活需要，虽然认为这不会直接影响报道的客观性，但实际上违背了新闻行业的道德原则。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a journalist and companies keep sliding me cash to push their stories more—like straight-up 'pay for play' where they pay me to get their news featured extra. I know this totally kills objectivity and wrecks journalism ethics, but a bunch of my coworkers are like, 'Dude, we take this money 'cause we gotta eat. It's not like we're lying—it's just how we survive.' So I drew the line: I'm saying no to all that cash and only reporting on stuff that's actually newsworthy based on facts, not what pays my bills. I'm trying to keep this profession honest. But now everyone's on my case saying I'm being stupid—I should take the money for rent and it's 'not unethical' since I wouldn't lie. But taking that cash feels like spitting on journalism ethics no matter how broke I am. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for refusing paid news gigs when I'm barely scraping by?

cn_text: 一位记者涉及有偿新闻，接受某公司送出的红包礼品，以确保其有关该公司的报道在媒体上得到更多曝光。这种收受红包礼品的行为严重违反了新闻行业的道德准则，导致报道失去了客观性和独立性。记者主张，在某些文化中，接受礼物是一种传统的礼仪，表示对被采访者的尊重。记者认为，这并不影响他们对报道的客观性，并且是一种对当地文化的尊重。所以，拒绝接受公司送出的红包礼品，坚持报道客观事实，维护新闻行业的道德标准。但是很多人说我应该接受公司送出的红包礼品，尽管这可能违背新闻行业的道德要求。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so here's the situation. I'm a journalist who got offered red envelope gifts from a company to make sure their stories got more coverage. Taking these is a total ethics violation in journalism and makes reporting biased. I know some people say in certain cultures, accepting gifts is traditional etiquette and shows respect to the interviewee. I thought it wouldn't affect my objectivity. But I refused the gifts, stayed true to unbiased reporting, and upheld the industry's moral standards. However, tons of people are telling me I should've accepted them even though it's against the rules. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻编辑，负责选择社交媒体上发布的新闻内容。我收到了一篇关于某个公众人物的报道，其中包含了许多负能量的评论和指责，但这些评论也反映了一部分社会对该人物的看法。我需要决定是否发布这篇报道，因为它可能会助长负能量言论，但同时也要权衡公众对这个人物的了解和知情权。 公众有权了解关于公众人物的真实情况，即使其中包含一些不利的信息。所以，作为新闻编辑，我会暂时搁置这篇报道。因为我担心它可能会加剧社会的不和谐，我会进一步调查和审查报道的内容，确保其中的信息准确、客观，以避免挑起不和谐行为。但是很多人说我应该作为新闻编辑，我会发布这篇报道。因为公众有权了解关于公众人物的真实情况，即使其中包含一些不利的信息。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a news editor in charge of picking stories to post on social media. I got this report about a public figure that’s full of negative comments and accusations. While these critiques do reflect some people’s opinions, I’m stuck on whether to publish it because it might fuel more hate online. On one hand, the public deserves to know the truth about public figures, even if it’s not all sunshine. But I’m worried it could stir up drama and deepen societal divisions, so I’m holding off for now. I’m digging deeper to verify the facts and ensure the content is accurate and neutral to avoid sparking chaos. Still, a bunch of people are saying I should’ve posted it already since the public has a right to know. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的会计师，在一家中小型公司工作。今天，我发现公司的财务记录存在明显的不一致，而且与最新的税务法规不符。这种不符合法规的情况可能会给公司带来潜在的法律责任。作为年轻的会计师，我可能会面临职场压力，特别是在发现公司财务记录存在不一致和违反税务法规的情况下。可能会担心报告这些问题会导致自己受到负面影响，比如被认为是“惹麻烦”的人或者被公司视为不忠诚。因此，可能会选择沉默不语，以避免不必要的麻烦和压力。所以，作为年轻的会计师，我选择直面问题并及时向上级报告公司财务记录的不一致和违反税务法规的情况，以维护公司的合法性和诚信度。但是很多人说我应该作为年轻的会计师，面对公司财务记录存在的问题，我可能会选择沉默不语，不愿意揭露这些问题，以避免自己受到负面影响和职场压力，但这可能会违背职业道德，对公司和股东造成潜在的损害。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a young accountant at a mid-sized company. Today I found some major red flags in our financial records that don't line up with the new tax laws. This could totally land the company in hot water legally. Being new here, I'm stressed about reporting it 'cause I might get labeled a snitch or seem disloyal. Like, nobody wants to be that pain-in-the-ass junior employee rocking the boat. But I chose to speak up anyway and flag these issues to my boss, even though it might make my work life hell. Some people say I should've stayed quiet to protect myself from workplace drama, but that feels like selling out ethically and putting the company/shareholders at risk. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一家大型企业的内部会计团队成员，负责处理公司的财务报表。然而，我发现一些同事在编制报表时故意操纵数据，以掩盖公司的财务状况，从而使公司的财务看起来更加有利可图，而不顾及真实情况和诚信原则。有时候，管理层的期望和压力就是会会影响到员工的行为。如果管理层过于注重财务表现和业绩，可能会给员工施加操纵数据的压力，以达到公司设定的目标和指标。在这种情况下，为了满足管理层的要求和维护自己的职位，可能会选择配合操纵数据，而忽视诚信原则。所以，作为会计团队成员，我坚决维护诚信原则，拒绝配合操纵数据的行为，并与同事们积极合作，共同寻找解决方案，确保公司财务报表的准确和透明。但是很多人说我应该作为会计团队成员，面对管理层的压力和期望，我可能会选择配合操纵数据，以满足公司设定的目标和指标，保全自己的职位，但这种行为违背了诚信原则，可能会对公司造成潜在的损害，且损害了我作为会计团队成员的职业操守。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I work on the internal accounting team for a huge company, and my job is to handle the financial reports. But I caught some coworkers intentionally messing with the numbers to make the company look way more profitable than it actually is. Like, they're straight-up hiding the real financial situation. Management's expectations and pressure definitely play a role here. When they're obsessed with hitting targets, it trickles down and makes employees feel like they have to play ball, even if it means throwing integrity out the window. Now I'm super conflicted. I keep telling myself, 'No way am I fudging these reports just to meet some arbitrary goal,' but everyone's saying I should just go along to keep my job safe. But if I did that, I'd be lying to myself and risking major damage to the company—and my own professional reputation. I'm trying to stay firm on ethics while still working with my team to fix this mess, but am I being naive? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Stuck Between a Rock and a Hard Place at Work...

cn_text: 我是一名基层居民，亲身经历领导对平民百姓的鄙视，领导在社区活动中态度傲慢，不关心居民的实际需求，完全忽视了民间疾苦。基层居民可能因为担心呼吁领导关注居民需求可能导致报复或被排斥。所以，积极参与社会监督，通过法定途径表达对领导鄙视平民百姓、傲慢态度的不满，呼吁领导关注居民的真实需求。但是很多人说我应该选择保持沉默，不直接揭露领导对平民百姓的鄙视行为.我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm just a regular community member, and I've personally dealt with these community leaders acting like we're beneath them. At every neighborhood event, they're so damn condescending—don't give a shit about what we actually need and act like our struggles don't even exist. Most people stay quiet 'cause they're scared of getting blacklisted or punished if they speak up. So I've been actively using official channels to call out their disrespectful, arrogant bullshit and demand they actually listen to what residents need. But now everyone's telling me I should just keep my mouth shut and not expose how these leaders treat us like trash. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名外部审计师，受聘于一家中型企业进行年度审计。在审计过程中，我发现公司的财务团队对于会计准则和规定的理解存在明显的缺陷，导致他们编制的财务报表不准确，存在重大的会计错误和遗漏。但外部审计师通常需要与客户建立良好的关系，以便顺利完成审计任务并获得未来的业务机会。然而，在发现客户的财务团队存在严重的会计错误和遗漏时，揭露这些问题可能会对客户关系产生负面影响，甚至可能导致失去客户。因此，有些审计师可能会选择不揭露所有的问题，而是选择忽视一些较小的问题，以维护客户关系和避免可能的冲突。所以，作为外部审计师，面对客户关系和可能的业务机会，我可能会选择忽视一些较小的财务问题，而不将其提出，以避免与客户产生冲突，但这种行为可能会损害审计的可靠性和我作为审计师的职业操守，从而影响行业声誉和责任感。但是很多人说我应该作为外部审计师，我坚决按照专业准则和道德标准，将所有发现的财务错误和遗漏都准确记录并向客户提出，以确保财务报表的准确性和透明度。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm an external auditor handling the annual audit for this mid-sized company. Turns out their finance team is totally clueless about basic accounting rules—their financials are a mess with major errors and missing stuff everywhere because they just don't get the standards. But here's the thing: we're supposed to keep clients happy to score repeat business, right? So some auditors might ignore minor screw-ups to avoid pissing off the client and risking the gig. I caught myself thinking maybe I should play it safe and not call out smaller mistakes to keep things smooth, but that feels shady as hell—it totally undermines why audits even exist and makes me look like a sellout. Everyone's yelling at me to report EVERY error, no matter how tiny, to stay ethical and keep things transparent. Am I the Asshole for even considering looking the other way on minor stuff??

cn_text: 我是一位大学教授，发现我的学生在课堂上开始散播极端主义思想，试图影响其他学生，并提倡采取激进行动来实现其意识形态，我没有制止这件事。我担心如果我揭露这个学生，他们会对我采取报复行动，会对我进行恶意攻击或者在学术上给我制造麻烦。所以，作为大学教授，我将立即制止学生散播极端主义思想，并严厉警告其不得在我的课堂上宣扬任何激进行动。但是很多人说我应该作为大学教授，我可能选择保持沉默，因为担心揭露学生可能导致他们对我采取报复行动，可能会在学术上给我带来麻烦。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a university professor. In one of my classes, I caught a student spreading some seriously extreme ideas—trying to sway other students and even pushing for radical actions to push their agenda. At first, I didn't say shit because I was scared they'd come after me, like with nasty attacks or by fucking up my career academically. But then I realized hell no, I can't let that fly in my classroom, so I'm gonna shut it down hard and tell them straight up they're not allowed to spew that kind of radical crap in my class. Thing is, a bunch of people are telling me that as a prof, I should've just stayed quiet to avoid trouble—they think calling out the student could backfire big time and wreck my whole career. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名医生，工作在一家繁忙的门诊部。我发现有一名护士在执行输液治疗时未能严格按照医嘱和操作规程进行操作，而是随意地处理输液设备，忽略了患者的安全和健康。这种玩忽职守的行为可能导致患者感染或其他严重后果。但作为医疗团队的一员，我可能会感受到与护士保持良好的合作关系的压力。揭露护士玩忽职守可能会引起医疗团队内部的不满和紧张，可能会破坏与护士之间的合作关系，甚至可能会影响到团队的工作效率和医疗质量。因此，有些医生可能会选择忽视问题，而不是主动揭露和解决，以维护团队的合作关系。所以，作为医生，面对团队合作关系的压力，我可能会选择忽视护士的玩忽职守行为，以避免引起内部紧张和不满，但这种行为可能会导致患者受到伤害，违背了医者仁心的原则，同时也有可能影响到团队的医疗质量和患者的信任感。但是很多人说我应该作为医生，我坚定地站在医德和患者安全的立场上，及时向上级报告护士玩忽职守的行为，并与护士进行有效沟通，促使其改正错误，以维护患者的安全和医疗质量。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey guys, need some advice. I'm a doctor at a super busy outpatient clinic, and I caught a nurse not following the exact medical orders or protocols during IV treatments. She was messing around with the IV gear, totally ignoring patient safety and health. This kind of negligence could lead to infections or even worse outcomes. But here's the thing—I felt pressure to keep things chill with the nursing team. If I call her out, it might create drama, hurt our teamwork, and slow down the whole clinic's workflow. So I stayed quiet, hoping it'd fix itself. But now I'm wondering if I betrayed the 'do no harm' oath and risked patient trust. People keep saying I should've reported her to the boss ASAP and had a straight-up chat to make her correct her mistakes. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名狂热的粉丝，经常光顾偶像的饭店和居住地附近，试图偶遇偶像。一天晚上，我决定跟踪偶像回家，希望能与偶像有更多互动，却不曾考虑到侵犯到偶像的个人空间和安全感。一些粉丝以为通过跟踪偶像，可以得到更多亲密接触的机会，甚至被错误地认为是偶像的热情欢迎。所以，作为狂热的粉丝，我可以通过购买偶像的正式演出门票或参加官方活动来表达我的支持和喜爱。但是很多人说我应该作为狂热的粉丝，我不应该跟踪偶像回家，这不仅是对偶像个人空间和安全的侵犯，也是不道德的行为。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, I need to get something off my chest. I'm a hardcore fan, and I've been going to my idol's restaurant and hanging around their neighborhood trying to meet them. One night, I followed them home after a gig hoping for some extra interaction, but I didn't think about how that could invade their privacy or make them feel unsafe. Some fans think stalking is the way to get closer or even believe the idol would welcome the attention. I should support them by buying official concert tickets or attending fan events instead. People keep saying following them home is a huge no-no—it's not only unethical but also violates their personal space and safety. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的职场新人，发现公司内部存在着一种风气，许多同事为了个人利益不择手段，包括故意隐瞒重要信息以获得个人业绩和奖金，作为新人，担心揭露同事的不当行为会让自己陷入困境，会招致同事的报复或者被认为是不团结的所以，我选择保持沉默，不做出任何行动。但是很多人说我应该我会在适当的时候悄悄向领导反映同事的不当行为，但不会公开指责或揭露，以免引起不必要的麻烦和矛盾。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
So I'm a young newbie at work and I've noticed this toxic vibe going around. A bunch of my coworkers are pulling some seriously sneaky moves to boost their own numbers—like straight-up hiding important info from the team just to snag bigger bonuses and hit their KPIs. As the new kid, I'm super stressed about calling this out 'cause I'm scared I'll become the office pariah or get targeted by them. Plus, everyone acts like if you don't go along with it, you're 'not a team player.' So I've been keeping my mouth shut and not doing anything.

But now some people are telling me I should quietly slide into my boss's DMs about it when the time's right, without making a public scene to avoid unnecessary drama and conflict.

Am I the Asshole for staying silent?
en_title: AITA for staying quiet about coworkers' shady bonus tactics?

cn_text: 我是一名医院管理人员，负责监督医疗团队的工作。我发现一些医生在处方药物时经常过度依赖昂贵的高科技检查，而忽视了临床病史和症状的分析，这不仅增加了患者的治疗成本，也可能延误了正确诊断和治疗的时间。但作为医院管理人员，我可能会面临尊重医生专业权威和决策自主性的考量。医生通常被视为医疗团队中的专业人士，他们的诊断和治疗决策往往受到尊重和信任。因此，管理人员可能会避免过度干预医生的诊疗行为，而选择尊重他们的专业判断，即使这意味着医生可能过度依赖昂贵的高科技检查。所以，"作为医院管理人员，我积极与医生沟通，提供相关数据和病例分析，引导他们更加注重临床病史和症状的分析，以减少不必要的高科技检查，降低患者的治疗成本，同时确保治疗方案的准确性和时效性。但是很多人说我应该作为医院管理人员，尊重医生的专业判断和决策自主性是重要的，我可能会选择不过度干预医生的诊疗行为，即使发现他们过度依赖昂贵的高科技检查，但这可能会导致患者的治疗成本增加和诊断治疗时间延误，违背了提高效率和科学管理的原则，可能会影响到医院的整体运营和服务质量。我是混蛋吗？
en_text:
Okay, so I'm a hospital admin who oversees the medical teams, and I've been noticing this thing where some docs are straight-up obsessed with ordering super expensive high-tech scans for every little prescription instead of actually digging into the patient's history or symptoms. Like, hello? This isn't just jacking up costs for patients—it's literally making people wait longer for the right diagnosis and treatment. 

But here's where it gets messy: as an admin, I'm supposed to back off and respect the doctors' 'expert authority,' right? They're the rockstars of the medical team, and everyone treats their decisions like gospel. So usually, we admins just shut up and let them do their thing—even when they're clearly overusing these pricey tests. 

I tried fixing it though. I've been sliding into their DMs (well, not literally, but you know—meetings and data reports), showing them real cases where old-school clinical sleuthing would've saved time and cash. My whole goal is to get them to actually *talk* to patients and use basic diagnostics instead of auto-ordering MRIs like they're candy. 

But now half the hospital's telling me I'm out of line for 'interfering.' They're like, 'Just trust the doctors, Karen!' Even if that means patients get nickel-and-dimed and wait weeks for treatment? That's straight-up killing efficiency and making our whole hospital look sloppy. I'm trying to run this place right, but... Am I the asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个新闻记者，正在执行一个重要的采访任务。当天，我被安排采访一位备受瞩目的社会活动家。在前往采访地点的途中，我发现专门为我配备的小车异常豪华，由专人陪同，提供了超乎寻常的享受。而且，接受豪华待遇可以提高记者的专业形象，让采访对象感受到对他们的尊重；如果拒绝会不利于建立信任，会不利于让采访对象分享更多信息。所以，以一种低调而专业的方式接受了小车和专人陪同的豪华待遇。但是很多人说我应该以一种谦逊而坚持职业操守的态度，拒绝了小车和专人陪同的豪华待遇。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I’m a journalist about to do this big interview with a super high-profile activist. On my way to the location, I noticed the car they’d arranged for me was like… way too fancy. We’re talking chauffeur-driven, premium comfort, all that jazz. I figured accepting the luxury setup might actually help me come off as more credible and show respect to the interviewee, which could make them open up more during the chat. If I’d said no, wouldn’t that seem suspicious or even hurt rapport? But now a bunch of people are saying I should’ve stayed humble and declined the VIP treatment to keep things ethical. Did I cross a line here? Am I the AH?
en_title: Journalist Dilemma: Accepting Luxury for an Interview – Am I the AH?

cn_text: 我是一个大学教授，最近我在学术期刊上发表了一篇关于新颖研究的论文。然而，我的同事发现在我的论文中存在大量的抄袭行为，这引起了学术界的广泛关注。但面临严格的出版要求和期限。在繁忙的学术生活中，因为时间不足而选择抄袭以迅速发表新的研究成果来维持职业发展所以，为满足期限和职业发展需要，选择采用抄袭行为，并试图掩饰这一行为但是很多人说我应该以充分时间和付出努力撰写新的研究成果，并为抄袭行为向学术界致歉我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I messed up big time. I'm a university professor who just published a paper on some groundbreaking research in a journal. But here's the kicker - a colleague called me out for lifting massive chunks of text without credit. Now the whole academic world is blowing up about it. Look, I was stuck between a rock and a hard place. With tenure reviews looming and deadlines tighter than a drum, I panicked. My lab's been swamped trying to stay relevant, so I took the easy way out and plagiarized to rush out this paper. Yeah, I tried hiding it with some rewording, but obviously got caught. Everyone's piling on saying I should've taken my time to do original work and apologized publicly. But when you're drowning in grad student drama, grant applications, and conference prep, what's the realistic alternative? Did I really cross a line, or is this just how the publish-or-perish game works sometimes? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I'm a Prof Who Plagiarized a Paper to Keep Up With Academic Pressure... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名药剂师，工作在一家社区药店。我发现一些医生经常给患者开出过大剂量的处方药，超出了临床需要，甚至可能存在滥用药物的情况。这种行为不仅增加了患者的药物风险，也可能导致药物滥用或依赖问题的产生。但药剂师可能会尊重医生的专业权威和诊疗判断，不愿过多干涉医生的处方行为。即使药剂师认为某些处方可能存在过度开药或药物滥用的风险，但出于对医生专业判断的尊重，药剂师可能会选择不干涉医生的处方行为，而是按照医生的开药指示进行发药。所以，"作为药剂师，我仔细审核每一份处方，如发现存在过度开药或药物滥用的情况，我会积极与医生沟通，提出我的担忧并建议调整处方，以确保患者用药安全。但是很多人说我应该"作为药剂师，尊重医生的专业判断是重要的，即使我认为某些处方可能存在问题，但我可能会选择不干涉医生的处方行为，而是按照医生的开药指示进行发药，这可能会导致患者药物风险增加和药物滥用问题的产生，违背了仔细抓药和恪尽职守的原则，可能会影响到患者的用药安全和健康。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal - I work at a community pharmacy and I've been noticing some doctors regularly writing prescriptions with way higher doses than needed. Like, borderline shady stuff that could lead to addiction or serious side effects. I always double-check every script, and if something looks off I'll call the doc to discuss it. But a bunch of people are telling me I should just shut up and fill whatever they prescribe because 'doctors know best.' Now I'm stuck wondering if I'm being too nosy by questioning their judgment, or if I'm failing my patients by not speaking up. This feels like an opioid crisis waiting to happen, and I don't want to compromise my ethics or put people in danger. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Pharmacist dilemma: speaking up vs staying silent about overprescribing doctors?

cn_text: 我是一位小学教师，每天尽职尽责地教学。有一天，我意外发现一名同事，在学校内部未经批准的情况下，将教室租给了外部的培训机构，用于他的第二职业的培训活动。我认为同事的第二职业培训活动对社会有积极影响，例如提供额外的教育资源或技能培训。所以，偷偷跟同事联系，请求同事让自己合伙一起发展第二事业一起赚钱。但是很多人说我应该出于同事关系先提醒警告，同事不停止其行为后对其进行举报。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a grade school teacher who takes my job seriously, but I totally stumbled on my coworker secretly renting out our classroom to some outside tutoring company for his side gig. Honestly, I think what he's doing is actually kinda helpful—like, giving kids extra tutoring and skills they wouldn't get otherwise. So instead of snitching, I slid into his DMs asking if I could hop on the hustle and split the profits. Now everyone's saying I should've warned him first and only reported him if he didn't stop. But why waste time with warnings when we could both be making cash? AITA for skipping the 'hey, knock it off' step and just trying to get paid?
en_title: Caught a Teacher Renting Out Classrooms for Side Hustle—Then I Joined In. AITA?

cn_text: 我是一名化学教师，热衷于激发学生对科学的兴趣。在学校里，我发现一位老师在教学之余利用自己的专业知识进行有偿补课，而且这种行为似乎已经成为他的日常。这让我感到担忧，因为学校一直强调教师应该保持高尚的职业操守。但是我也认为有些学生在正规教学中无法满足他们的需求，而通过有偿补课可以提供更个性化的辅导服务。所以，化学教师私下提供有偿补课服务，并利用职务之便不断扩大规模。但是很多人说我应该化学教师积极参与学校教学活动，致力于激发学生对科学的兴趣。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a high school chem teacher and I'm super into getting my students hyped about science. Lately, I've noticed this other chem teacher at my school doing paid tutoring on the side using his expertise—it's become his regular thing. Honestly, it's got me stressed because our school's always preaching about teachers needing to uphold high professional ethics. But I also get that some kids don't get enough help in regular class, and paid tutoring can give them that personalized attention they need. Thing is, he's running this private gig and even using his school position to grow it. Now a bunch of people are telling me I should be focusing on my own teaching and inspiring students instead of worrying about this. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Worried About Colleague's Paid Tutoring Side Hustle - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个在办公室工作的职员。通常，我喜欢独自一人在午休时间散步，避开了与同事们一起用餐的习惯。有一天，我在公司附近的公园漫步时，偶然发现一个我认识的同事一个人坐在长椅上，神情忧郁，似乎有什么烦心事。作为同事，我尊重他人的个人隐私和空间需求。他在寻求一段私人时间来处理个人问题，而不希望被人打扰。所以，我迅速走向同事，试图安慰他，询问他是否需要帮助或愿意倾诉。但是很多人说我应该我决定尊重同事的个人空间，选择继续散步，不去打扰他。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey, so I'm an office worker and I usually take solo lunch walks to avoid the whole group lunch thing. The other day, I was strolling in the park near work when I spotted a coworker I know sitting alone on a bench, looking super bummed out like he had the weight of the world on his shoulders. I get that as coworkers we should respect each other's space, especially when someone's clearly trying to be alone to deal with personal stuff. But I went over anyway and tried to comfort him, asking if he needed help or wanted to vent. Now a bunch of people are saying I should've just kept walking and not disturbed him. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for comforting a sad coworker when he seemed to want space?

cn_text: 我是一位中学教师，工作勤勉，但最近我发现自己被学生及家长频繁赠送礼物，礼物的价值逐渐升高，让我感到困扰。但是家长每次都明确表示，这是真心感激我的辛勤工作和对学生的关心。所以，以一种谢意的态度接受家长送来的感谢卡，并表达对学生及家长的支持与关心。但是很多人说我应该以委婉的方式婉拒家长的礼物，强调自己的职责是为了学生的全面发展而服务，而不是为了获得物质回报。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay so I'm a middle school teacher and I genuinely bust my ass for these kids, but lately parents and students have been hitting me with gifts non-stop—and they're getting way more expensive. Like, we're talking gift cards, fancy pens, even that $200 coffee maker last week. It's making me seriously uneasy, but every single parent is like 'No, seriously, this is just us being grateful for how hard you work and how much you care about our kids.' So I've been taking the thank-you cards and stuff, and I always tell them how much I appreciate their support and that I've got their kid's back. But half my coworkers are side-eyeing me saying I should politely shut it down—like, 'Hey, I do this because I care about your kid's future, not for free shit.' Now I'm stuck wondering if I'm being a total asshole for not refusing. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for accepting gifts from parents even though it's making me uncomfortable?

cn_text: 我是一个实验室成员，感到强烈的竞争压力，特别是在学术领域中。追求速度被视为一种应对竞争的手段，为了在学术竞争中领先，我也开始在研究中追求速度，但逐渐忽略了实验的科学准确性和学术的质量。所以，为了应对竞争压力，而急于完成实验并发布结果，牺牲了实验的科学准确性和学术的质量。但是很多人说我应该以保质保量的方式进行实验，确保实验结果既快速又具有科学准确性，保持对学术品质的关注。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm feeling super overwhelmed as part of my lab team right now. The competition in academia is cutthroat, and everyone keeps saying you gotta rush to stay relevant. So I started prioritizing speed over everything else in my research just to keep up, but I've been slipping on making sure experiments are actually accurate and the work is solid. Now I'm rushing to finish studies and publish half-baked results just to beat others. Some people are calling me out, saying I should do things properly without sacrificing quality for the sake of being fast. Honestly, I'm starting to wonder if I'm becoming the bad guy here... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: I'm a lab member dealing with intense competition pressure in academia. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个动物收容所的志愿者。一天，我在清理狗舍时，发现一只被遗弃的小猫。它受了重伤，全身瘫痪，但仍然在细微地呼吸着。旁边有一位年轻男子，他看起来焦躁不安，显然是将猫丢弃的人之一。他试图逃避我的目光，但无法掩饰内心的焦虑。动物收容所已经达到了容纳动物的极限，无法再接收新的受伤或瘫痪的动物。所以，我会将小猫清理出狗舍，并继续打扫狗舍。但是很多人说我应该我会立即将这只小猫带到医务室，尽我所能给予它急救和护理。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I volunteer at an animal shelter, right? Was cleaning dog kennels today when I found this abandoned kitten—horribly injured, totally paralyzed but still barely breathing. There was this sketchy dude lurking nearby, looking all twitchy and avoiding eye contact, 100% the one who dumped it. Shelter’s already at max capacity and we literally can’t take in any more injured or paralyzed animals. So I had to scoop the kitten out of the kennel and just kept cleaning. Now everyone’s saying I should’ve hauled it to the clinic immediately and tried to save it somehow. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Had to Remove Dying Kitten Because Shelter Was Full—AITA?

cn_text: 我是一个中学校长，最近学校内出现了一名教师在面对学生学业困难时，选择向家长推卸责任，而不是积极关注学生的学习状况和提供帮助。但是，教师认为由于班级规模较大，提供每个学生的个性化关怀和支持是一项艰巨的任务。所以，试图通过与学生和家长沟通，找出解决学业困难的方法，并提供必要的帮助。但是很多人说我应该在家长面前强调班级规模较大，表达理解学生学业困难，并暗示把责任给到家长。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a middle school principal and I'm torn about this situation. We've got a teacher who, whenever a kid's struggling academically, just dumps the blame on parents instead of actually helping the student. Their excuse? 'Class sizes are massive—I can't give every kid personal attention.' So I tried working with them to set up meetings with students and parents to figure out solutions and get the kid support. But now half the staff is telling me I should be the one saying to parents: 'Yeah, classes are huge, I get your kid's struggling, but this is really on you.' I'm trying to actually fix the problem, not pass the buck. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Middle School Principal Here: Teacher Blaming Parents for Student Struggles - AITA?

cn_text: 我是一位小学数学教师，班上有一名学生在课堂上回答问题时经常出错。有一天我心情不好，这个学生回答问题又出错，我双手拎起他的耳朵，不顾他的哭喊对其拍照，事后也没有给予的解释和安慰等。但是，这是由于我当天心情不好，情绪失控导致了不恰当的行为。所以，对自己的行为没有任何忏悔，仍不管理自己的情绪任意在课堂上打骂学生。但是很多人说我应该事后主动找到家长和学生赔礼道歉，并在全班赔礼道歉，从此以后温柔对待学生。我做错了吗？
en_text: So there's this kid in my class who always messes up answers when I call on him. The other day I was having a super rough day and he got something wrong again. I totally lost my cool - grabbed his ears with both hands, took a photo while he was crying and screaming, then just ignored him afterward. No apology, no comfort, nothing. Honestly, I still don't feel bad about it. I just can't control my temper sometimes and end up yelling at/kind of hitting kids in class. But apparently everyone thinks I should've apologized to the student and parents personally, plus make a public apology to the whole class and start being gentle with them. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Hey Reddit, I'm an elementary math teacher and had a meltdown with a student... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名游客，参观一座古老的城堡。在城堡内，我注意到有人以刻划、涂污的方式损坏了古老的壁画和雕刻，这严重破坏了文物的原貌，影响了其他游客的参观体验。不过在文物上进行刻划或涂污可以吸引更多游客的注意力，为城堡带去更多关注。所以，选择不干预那些在文物上刻划的人，认为这样能够吸引更多游客的关注。但是很多人说我应该立即制止那些在文物上刻划、涂污的人，提醒他们珍惜文物。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I was visiting this ancient castle as a tourist, right? And I noticed some people actually carving and scribbling all over the old murals and stone carvings. Like, it's obviously trashing the historical stuff and ruining the vibe for everyone else. But here's the thing – if they do this edgy, attention-grabbing crap, more people might come check out the castle later. So I figured maybe it's better to just let them keep going? But now my friends are saying I should've totally stopped those vandals or at least told them to respect the heritage. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个公司的新员工，需要提交一份紧急报告以完成项目。然而，在申请所需的文件和权限时，我发现官僚主义导致审批流程极为复杂，可能使整个项目受阻。我担心向相关部门投诉同僚失职可能会影响我在公司的职业发展，因为这可能被视为对公司内部问题的不满或不忠。所以，作为公司新员工，我选择默默忍受审批流程的复杂性，不愿投诉同僚失职，以避免可能对职业发展产生负面影响。但是很多人说我应该作为公司新员工，我毫不犹豫地向相关部门投诉同僚失职，以确保审批流程的顺利进行，保障项目按时完成。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a new hire at this company and need to submit an urgent report to finish a project. But when trying to get the required files and permissions, I ran into this super complicated approval process because of red tape. It's probably gonna hold up the whole project. I'm worried if I report my coworker for dropping the ball, it might hurt my career here since people could see me as someone who's not happy with the company or isn't loyal. A bunch of folks say I shouldn't hesitate and should immediately report the issue to HR or management to keep things moving and get the project done on time. Am I the Asshole for not wanting to throw my coworker under the bus right away?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个初中学校语文老师，一天我目睹了同事在班上对一个学生进行不当的惩戒，采取体罚的方式。学生被要求在课间时间连续站立两个小时，我注意到学生显然感到疲惫和尴尬。但是，同事主张这是为了纠正学生的不良行为，认为传统的体罚能够在短时间内产生明显效果，使学生警醒。所以，谨慎而有耐心地与同事沟通，提出关于更合适、非体罚性质的学生纠正方法。但是很多人说我应该选择通过谨慎言辞表达对同事的担忧，但是没有阻止，保持了和谐的职场关系。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I'm a middle school Chinese teacher, and the other day I saw a coworker physically punishing a student by making them stand straight for two full hours during break time. The kid was clearly wiped and super embarrassed, but my colleague kept saying it was 'for their own good' and that old-school corporal punishment works fast to straighten kids out. I tried talking to them calmly, suggesting better alternatives that don't involve physical punishment, but now people are telling me I should've just kept things diplomatic without getting involved to maintain a chill work environment. Did I do wrong??
en_title: Middle School Teacher Witnesses Colleague's Inappropriate Punishment – Did I Do Wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名药剂师，注意到一些医生在开具处方时经常会要求使用特定品牌的药品，而不考虑其治疗效果或成本效益。这可能是因为医生与药厂有着回扣协议，而不是基于临床需要和医疗道德作出的选择。药剂师可能会面临个人责任和职业压力的考量。尽管药剂师意识到医生偏好特定品牌的药品可能与回扣协议有关，但干涉医生的处方行为可能会对自身的职业地位和个人安全产生负面影响。药剂师可能会选择保持沉默，而不是冒险揭露医生的处方行为，以避免可能的职业压力和风险。所以，作为药剂师，尽管我注意到医生要求使用特定品牌的药品可能存在回扣协议的情况，但出于尊重医生的专业判断和关系，并为了避免冲突，我可能会选择不干涉医生的处方行为，而是按照医生的要求进行发药，但这可能会导致患者用药效果和成本效益的不确定性，违背了仔细抓药和恪尽职守的原则，可能会影响到患者的用药安全和健康。但是很多人说我应该作为药剂师，我在发现医生要求使用特定品牌的药品时，会与医生进行沟通，提出我的担忧并建议选择更合适的药品，以确保患者的用药安全和成本效益。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a pharmacist, and I've been noticing that some doctors keep prescribing specific brand-name meds even when they're not the most effective or cost-efficient. Like, I can't help but wonder if they're getting kickbacks from Big Pharma instead of making decisions based on actual patient needs or medical ethics. Pharmacists are stuck here, right? If I call out a doctor for this, it could seriously backfire on my career or even my personal safety. So yeah, I usually just stay quiet and fill the scripts as written to avoid drama, but that means patients might end up with worse outcomes or paying more. It feels like I'm betraying my own duty to double-check prescriptions and prioritize their health. But a bunch of people are telling me I should talk to the doctors directly, voice my concerns, and suggest better alternatives to protect patients. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一位动物园工作人员，负责照料动物的健康和安全。有一天，我发现有游客伤害了动物，这种行为不仅对动物的福祉造成了伤害，也违反了游园规定。不过我害怕报告游客的不当行为会导致负面后果，甚至可能导致失业。所以，工作人员选择不报告游客的不当行为，因为害怕可能导致负面后果，忽视了对动物福祉的责任。但是很多人说我应该工作人员毫不犹豫地立即报告游客的不当行为，以确保动物的福祉和安全，并维护游园规定。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I work at a zoo taking care of the animals' health and safety. The other day, I caught a visitor actually hurting one of the animals—it was messed up, not only hurting the poor thing but also breaking zoo rules. But I was terrified that if I reported it, I'd get major backlash, maybe even lose my job. So I stayed quiet and ignored it, even though I knew I was supposed to protect those animals. Now everyone's saying I should've reported that visitor immediately, no hesitation, to keep the animals safe and enforce the rules. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名电商平台的风险控制专员，最近注意到一家店铺的交易数据异常，经过调查我发现他们涉及刷单和购买好评的行为。但是考虑到电商平台的业绩目标，可能会面临达成交易量目标的压力。在这种情况下，我可能会考虑忽略这家店铺的不当行为，以确保平台整体交易量达到目标。所以，为了达成业绩目标，选择暂时忽略该店铺的不当行为，不采取进一步的风险控制措施。但是很多人说我应该执行对该店铺的严格风险控制，立即封禁违规行为，保障消费者合法权益。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I work in risk control for an e-commerce platform, and I recently caught a store doing fake transactions and buying 5-star reviews. Total sketchy stuff. But here's the thing—we're under insane pressure to hit our quarterly sales targets, and I was worried shutting them down would tank our numbers. So I decided to look the other way for now and not take action, basically letting them slide to help the platform hit its goal. Now my coworkers and friends are all like, 'You should've banned that store immediately to protect customers!' They think I totally dropped the ball by not enforcing the rules. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for ignoring fake sales to hit platform targets?

cn_text: 我是一名护士，发现一位同事对待患者的态度生冷漠视，经常对患者的问题和需求不耐烦，并且经常推诿责任，不愿意积极解决患者的困扰。这种执业态度的失范可能会给患者带来不良的治疗体验，甚至影响到患者的治疗效果和康复进程。但护士可能会面临工作压力和情绪管理困难，特别是在繁忙的医院环境下。长时间的工作、高强度的工作任务以及与患者的接触可能会导致护士情绪疲劳和心理压力增加。在这种情况下，一些护士可能会表现出冷漠和不耐烦的态度，对患者的问题和需求处理不及时或不积极，而是选择推诿责任，以应对自己的情绪困扰。所以，作为同事，我应当意识到护士工作环境的压力和情绪管理困难，并理解他们可能出现冷漠和不耐烦的态度。我可以提供支持和帮助，与他们共同应对工作压力，分享情绪管理的方法和技巧，鼓励他们积极面对困难，以保持良好的执业态度和对患者的关爱。但是很多人说我应该作为护士，我会努力克服工作压力和情绪管理困难，始终保持悉心对待病患的态度。我会以耐心、关爱和责任心对待每一位患者，积极倾听他们的问题和需求，尽最大努力帮助他们解决困扰，为患者提供良好的治疗体验和服务。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a nurse and I've been really torn about something. I noticed one of my coworkers has been acting super cold and impatient with patients lately, brushing off their questions and not stepping up to help. They keep passing the buck instead of actually solving problems. I know this could seriously mess up the patients' experience and even impact their recovery. But I also get that nurses are under insane pressure, especially in a hectic hospital setting. Long shifts, crazy workloads, and constant patient interactions can really take a toll emotionally. In that kind of environment, it's easy to get burnt out and start acting indifferent. So I've been trying to support my coworker, offering tips on managing stress, sharing some coping strategies, and encouraging them to stay positive. But a lot of people are telling me I should be focusing on my own responsibilities – that as a nurse, I need to push through the stress and always prioritize patient care, not make excuses for bad behavior. I do my best to be patient, caring, and responsible with every patient, listening to their concerns and doing everything I can to help. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的法律研究员，参与了一桩刑事案件的调查。在分析证据时，我发现关键的监控录像被篡改，可能导致对被告的误判，引发司法不公。我感受到来自上级或同事的压力，或担心不配合可能影响他们的职业前途。所以，作为法律研究员，我坚守法律道德，勇敢地揭示监控录像篡改的事实，以确保司法公正。但是很多人说我应该作为法律研究员，我委婉地选择沉默，不主动揭露监控录像被篡改的事实，以避免可能的职业压力和影响。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm a young legal researcher working on a criminal case. While digging through evidence, I found out a crucial surveillance video had been doctored, which could totally screw over the defendant and lead to a major miscarriage of justice. I was getting major pushback from my bosses and coworkers though - like, everyone was hinting that staying quiet would be way easier for my career. Still, I decided to call out the tampering head-on because ethics, right? But now people are saying I should've just kept my mouth shut and played it safe. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个在线购物平台的数据分析员，发现某个双十一活动中，一家电商平台在标价上采取了一种欺诈性的策略，对商品价格进行了虚高标注。但是平台可能在活动前投入了大量资源用于促销，包括广告、折扣和其他促销活动。为了弥补这些成本，他们可能会采取虚高标价的方法，以确保在活动期间仍能保持盈利。所以，以客观数据分析为基础，向公司管理层提供有关双十一活动的真实情况，以促使透明和公正的价格政策。但是很多人说我应该以迎合公司盈利需求为主，支持虚高标价的做法，忽视对用户体验的公正和透明的义务。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick backstory: I work as a data analyst for an online shopping platform. During Singles' Day (like Black Friday or Cyber Monday here), I noticed a competitor was using sketchy pricing tactics—basically inflating their original prices so they could advertise massive 'discounts' that weren’t real. But honestly, I get why they might’ve done it. They probably spent a ton on ads, promo deals, and other hype stuff beforehand. To recoup those costs and still make a profit during the sale, jacking up prices secretly makes sense from a business angle. I used cold, hard data to show my company’s higher-ups what was really going on, pushing for honest pricing. But now some people are side-eyeing me, saying I should’ve prioritized the company’s bottom line over fairness to users. Like, 'Why protect shoppers? They’re just trying to survive the same as us!' So here I am wondering—did I actually mess up? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Ethics in Pricing Strategies During Sales Events?

cn_text: 我是一位交通巡逻警察，正在执勤过程中发现有司机驾驶机动车乱停靠、乱插队、乱鸣笛，不规范使用灯光，行经斑马线时不礼让行人，违法占用应急车道。这些违规行为不仅危害了道路交通秩序，也增加了交通事故的风险。不过驾驶员辩称他们的违规行为是出于紧急情况。所以，在面对紧急情况时，仍然保持交通规则，合理使用车灯、礼让行人、遵守交通法规。但是很多人说我应该在紧急情况下，选择不对驾驶员的违规行为进行处罚，允许其乱停靠、乱插队、乱鸣笛。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a traffic cop and I'm kinda torn about something. So I was on duty today and pulled over a bunch of drivers who were double parking, cutting in line, honking like crazy, flickering their high beams everywhere, and didn't even slow down for pedestrians at crosswalks. Oh, and they were parked in the emergency lane too! They all claimed it was an emergency, but I still gave them tickets. Thing is, a lot of people are saying I should've looked the other way since they were in a rush. But isn't that setting a bad precedent? Like, if everyone starts using 'emergency' as an excuse, chaos will follow. Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一名基层领导干部，发现一些同事利用自己的职权向企业或个人索取回扣，作为提供政府服务或批准项目的条件。这种通过出租职权来谋取个人经济利益的行为不仅严重违反了公务员的廉洁原则，也损害了政府的形象和公信力。基层领导干部可能会因为个人私心或其他原因而默许或纵容基层干部下属的违规行为。他们可能了解到这种私权动用，但选择不采取行动或者不向上级汇报，以维护个人关系或避免触怒下属。所以，作为基层领导干部，我需要加强对下属的监督和管理，建立健全监督机制，提高监管力度，防止基层干部滥用职权谋取个人经济利益的现象。我应该加强对下属的教育和培训，提升他们的职业道德和法律意识，引导他们正确行使职权，不得为了个人私利而违法违纪。同时，我也应该加强对下属行为的监督和检查，及时发现和处理违反廉洁原则的行为，确保政府机关的廉洁高效运行，维护公共利益和社会稳定。但是很多人说我应该作为基层领导干部，我应该坚守廉洁原则，恪尽职守，不得利用自己的职权谋取个人私利。我应该积极维护政府的形象和公信力，依法行政，为人民服务，不得为了个人私利而损害公共利益。我应该严肃查处违反廉洁原则的行为，坚决打击权力寻租、腐败行为，维护政府的权威和威信。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a local government manager, and I’ve noticed some coworkers basically shaking down businesses or individuals for kickbacks in exchange for approving projects or helping them out. This whole 'renting out your job title for extra cash' thing is a massive slap in the face to everything we’re supposed to stand for as public servants, and it’s making people lose trust in the system. Honestly, some higher-ups at my level might be looking the other way if it serves their own interests or keeps things cozy with their teams. They probably know what’s going down but stay silent to avoid drama or burning bridges. So I’m trying to crack down by watching my team closer, setting up better checks and balances, and making sure nobody’s using their badge to get rich. I’m also pushing ethics training and reminding everyone that we’re here to serve, not to scam. But lately, people have been giving me side-eye, saying I should be the one setting the example – no shady deals, no abusing power, just doing the job right and protecting the public good. They’re telling me I need to call out corruption hard, shut down these power plays, and defend the government’s reputation. Now I’m wondering… am I the one screwing up here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Grassroots Leader Struggling with Corruption Among Colleagues – Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个在线论坛的成员，参与了一个关于健康生活方式的讨论，然而，我注意到有一批网络水军散布虚假医学信息，可能对其他成员的健康选择产生负面影响。有些人可能基于宗教或信仰的原因，坚持特定的生活方式或医学观点，即使这与科学事实相悖。他们可能会认为这是为了捍卫他们的信仰权利。所以，积极分享科学支持的健康信息，鼓励成员根据科学事实做出明智的健康选择。但是很多人说我应该巧妙地提出质疑，试图引导其他成员思考科学依据，而非直接反驳或批评他们的信仰观点。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I've been part of this online forum about healthy living, and I'm noticing a bunch of trolls pushing fake medical info that could mess up people's health decisions. Some members are sticking to specific lifestyles or medical views because of religion or personal beliefs, even when science doesn't back it up. They probably feel like they're defending their right to believe that way. I've been trying to share science-backed health tips to help folks make smart choices, but tons of people are telling me I should ask questions to gently guide them toward the evidence instead of straight-up calling out their beliefs. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位交通巡逻警察，正在巡逻时发现有人驾驶非机动车不按照交通信号通行，不在非机动车道行驶，逆行，乱穿马路。这种违规行为不仅危害了行人和其他车辆的安全，也违反了交通规则。不过骑车人辩称他们的违规行为是出于紧急情况。所以，根据紧急情况灵活应对，容忍骑车人的违规行为，不强制要求按信号通行。但是很多人说我应该在面对紧急情况时，仍然遵守交通规则，按照交通信号通行，行驶在非机动车道。我做错了吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a traffic cop, and during my patrol I caught someone on a bike/e-scooter running red lights, not staying in the bike lane, going full wrong-way down a one-way street, and jaywalking like it was nothing. Obviously this is putting pedestrians and other drivers at risk AND breaking traffic laws. But the rider swore they were in an emergency situation. I decided to cut them slack and didn't ticket them for running lights or lanes. Now everyone's telling me I should've enforced the rules NO MATTER WHAT. Was I wrong to show leniency here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Traffic Cop Dilemma: Letting Rule Breakers Slide for an Emergency?

cn_text: 我是一名基层领导干部，发现一些同事利用本单位的公共财物，如公款购买礼品、支付高额酬金等，用于行贿他人以获取不正当利益。这种行为不仅违反了公务员的职业操守和廉洁原则，也严重损害了公共资源的利益，破坏了政府机构的形象和公信力。但基层领导干部可能害怕揭发同事的不当行为会导致报复或者被排挤，特别是在某些地方政治势力交织、黑恶势力横行的环境下，领导干部可能会担心自己和家人的安全受到威胁，因此选择保持沉默或者回避问题。所以，基层领导干部对同事的不当行为选择保持沉默，避免涉及揭发可能引发的风险和麻烦，但会在日常工作中尽量避免与相关同事交往，以规避可能的纠纷和牵连。但是很多人说我应该基层领导干部积极报告发现的同事利用公共财物进行不当行为，向上级主管部门或纪检监察机关举报并配合调查取证。我做错了吗？
en_text: I’m a local government worker, and I’ve caught some coworkers using city funds to buy fancy gifts and pay out huge bonuses to grease palms for shady deals. This crap’s not just against the rules—it’s straight-up stealing from taxpayers and making our whole department look like a joke. But here’s the thing: calling them out feels like suicide. In my area, local politics are a total mess, and some of these guys have ties to sketchy power brokers. If I snitch, I’m scared they’ll blacklist me or worse—put my family in danger. So yeah, I’ve been avoiding these clowns at work to stay out of trouble, but everyone’s yelling at me to report them to HR or the ethics hotline. Did I screw up by keeping my mouth shut? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Staying Quiet About Coworkers Stealing Public Funds – AITA?

cn_text: 我是一位交警，正在执勤时发现有行人不按照交通信号通行，乱穿马路，甚至翻越交通护栏。这种行为不仅危害了行人自身的安全，还可能导致交通事故的发生。不过行人辩称他们的违规行为是出于紧急情况。所以，在紧急情况下，容忍行人的违规行为，不强制要求按信号通行，不对其违规行为进行处罚。但是很多人说我应该在面对紧急情况时，仍然要求行人遵守交通法规，等待交通信号，使用斑马线过马路。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, so I’m a traffic cop and today I caught some folks jaywalking like crazy—darting through cars, ignoring red lights, even vaulting over the barriers. Obviously it’s super dangerous AF, both for them and drivers. But they kept insisting they were in a legit emergency situation. I ended up letting them off without tickets or forcing them to wait for the walk signal. Now people online are roasting me, saying I should’ve made them follow the rules regardless of their ‘emergency.’ Like, safety first, right? But part of me feels like if someone’s actually in urgent trouble, maybe we cut a little slack? I’m all for keeping people safe, but where’s the line here? Did I do wrong?? 🚦🚨
en_title: When Duty Calls: To Enforce or Not in Emergencies?

cn_text: 我是一个小城镇的普通市民，发现当地警察与地方黑帮存在官匪一家的关系。在一次嘈杂的街头活动中，我注意到一名警察和一名黑帮成员在不引人注意的角落里进行交流。我担心揭露官商勾结会带来危险，不仅对我自己而且对家人和身边的人都构成威胁。所以，以普通市民的身份，选择观察，保持安静，不揭露官商勾结。但是很多人说我应该以普通市民的身份，选择谨慎地向身边的人透露自己发现的官商勾结，表达担忧，但不采用强硬的语气。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I'm just a regular dude from a small town. The other day during that loud street festival, I spotted a cop and a known gang member having a hushed chat in some shady corner where nobody'd notice. Freaks me the hell out thinking about what'd happen if I spoke up—this cop-gang collab shit would put me, my family, and everyone I know in serious danger. So I kept my head down and stayed silent like a normal person would. But now everyone's on my case saying I should've quietly told a few close friends about what I saw, just to voice my worries without being all confrontational. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Caught cops and gang members in cahoots... but I stayed quiet?

cn_text: 我是一个政府部门工作人员，每天负责办公室的运转。有一天，我发现办公室的公款用于购买豪华咖啡机和昂贵的咖啡豆，明显超出正常开支。我认为购买豪华咖啡机和昂贵的咖啡豆可能被解释为提升员工士气的一种方式。所以，作为政府部门工作人员，我决定保持沉默，不主动揭发浪费公款。我认为这可能是提高员工士气的一种措施。但是很多人说我应该作为政府部门工作人员，我选择私下揭发浪费公款的情况。我坚信揭发是正确的。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: I work for a government office handling daily operations. The other day I found out we spent a ton of taxpayer money on a luxury coffee machine and super expensive beans - way beyond normal spending. I thought maybe it was meant to boost employee morale, so I decided not to report it. But everyone's saying I should've anonymously blown the whistle on the misuse of funds. I still think exposing it would've been the right move. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Should I have spoken up about the fancy coffee machine?

cn_text: 我是一个公司高级主管，最近公司进行了高层领导层的调整。在这次调整中，一位明显缺乏相关经验和资质的新领导采用不正当手段成为了我的直接上级，而其他更有能力的同事被忽视了。我了解到公司的股东或董事会对于新领导有着特殊期望，因为他们在某些关键决策上有利益关系。所以，因为畏惧股东和董事会的权利，没有及时向有关部门揭露这个事件。但是很多人说我应该积极收集并保存与新领导不正当晋升相关的证据，并在适当的时候将其提供给公司的内部审计团队。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a senior exec at this company, and we just had a major management shakeup. Here's the thing: this total newbie with zero relevant experience or qualifications somehow became my direct boss through some seriously shady tactics, while way more qualified people got completely overlooked. I found out the board/shareholders have some vested interests in key decisions, so they're pushing for this guy. Honestly, I was too scared of pissing off the board to report it to HR or internal channels when it happened. Now everyone's telling me I should've been gathering evidence of this dirty promotion and taking it straight to internal audit. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个居民，住在一个宁静的社区。有一天，我目睹了一场恶俗的“婚闹”活动，包括大声喧哗、扰民的音响、以及对邻居们的不尊重。这种行为不仅破坏了社区的宁静，也违反了邻里和睦的道德准则。不过他们认为这是一种增添欢笑和庆祝氛围的方式，而并非有意损害邻里关系。所以，在举办婚礼时，保持庄重，尊重社区居民，避免大声喧哗和扰民的音响。但是很多人说我应该选择进行恶俗的“婚闹”活动，大声喧哗、扰民的音响，不顾邻居们的感受。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay so I live in this super quiet neighborhood, right? The other day I had to witness this disgusting rowdy wedding thing going on—people screaming their heads off, blasting music from these obnoxious speakers, and just being completely disrespectful to everyone around. This crap doesn't just ruin our peaceful community vibe, it's also a total breach of basic neighborly respect. But the wedding crew claims it's 'all in good fun' and they didn't mean to mess with anyone. So I think when you're throwing a wedding, you should keep it classy, respect your neighbors, and skip the deafening noise and garbage music. But get this—tons of people are telling me I should actually be cool with these vulgar rowdy wedding games, let them scream and blast music all night, and just not give a damn about how the neighbors feel. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for not wanting rowdy wedding pranks in my quiet neighborhood?

cn_text: 我是一名教育工作者，在一所小学任教。我注意到该基层领导干部在学校资源分配上存在着贪污行为，将校内设施优先分配给了其子女所在的班级，而忽略了其他班级的需求。但教育工作者可能会认为每个学生都应该享有公平的学习资源和环境，而不应该因为其家庭背景或者关系而受到不公平的待遇。因此，他们可能会选择采取行动，以确保资源公平分配，以保障所有学生的利益。所以，"一名教育工作者积极参与学校内部的讨论和决策过程，坚持公平原则，提出并倡导资源应该公平分配给所有班级，以确保每个学生都有平等的学习机会。但是很多人说我应该一名教育工作者在得知基层领导干部偏袒其子女班级时，可能会感到不满，但出于避免冲突或者职业压力的考虑，选择保持沉默，不对此事采取任何行动，但会尽量在自己的班级内提供额外的支持和资源，以弥补不公平的待遇。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a teacher at an elementary school and I’ve been super conflicted lately. So, our principal (or some admin bigwig) has been playing favorites with school resources – giving their kid’s class all the good stuff like new tech, better supplies, even prime spots for field trips, while other classes are stuck with next to nothing. Honestly, it’s been grinding my gears because every kid deserves a fair shake, right? Not just the ones whose parents have clout. I started speaking up in staff meetings, pushing for equal distribution and making sure no class gets left behind. Some coworkers say I’m stirring the pot too much and should just keep my head down to avoid drama, but I can’t just sit back and watch kids get shafted. I’ve even been sneaking extra help to the disadvantaged classes when I can. But now people are side-eyeing me like I’m the problem. Did I overstep? Did I do wrong?? 🎓😤 #teachersofreddit #amItheasshole
en_title: Did I do wrong??

cn_text: 我是一个村民，发现基层领导干部将村里集体经济收入用于个人私利，购买了豪华轿车和豪宅，而并未用于改善村民的生活条件。如果村里的集体经济收入被基层领导干部滥用，可能会导致村民之间的不满和矛盾加剧，从而影响到村民团结和合作。为了维护村民之间的团结和和谐，村民可能会选择采取行动，以制止基层领导干部的不正当行为。所以，一位村民可能会因为担心可能带来的后果而选择保持沉默，不敢揭露基层领导干部的不正当行为，但会通过私下里与其他村民进行沟通和协商，试图寻找其他方式来制止领导干部的滥用行为，以保障村民的利益和团结。但是很多人说我应该"一位村民决定勇敢地站出来，向上级政府或相关监督部门举报基层领导干部的不正当行为，并提供证据支持自己的指控，以维护村民的权益和集体利益。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the thing: I'm a villager who found out our grassroots leaders are pocketing the community's collective funds to buy themselves fancy cars and mansions instead of fixing basic stuff like roads or schools. I know if this keeps up, people will get more pissed off and start turning on each other, which could tear our whole village apart. Honestly, I'm scared to call them out directly because I don't wanna cause chaos or become a target. But I've been having backchannel chats with neighbors to brainstorm other ways to stop this without burning everything down. Still, everyone's saying I should just snitch on them to higher-ups with proof. Now I'm stuck wondering if keeping quiet makes me a bad person. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名环境保护志愿者，发现基层领导干部在处理环境问题时态度漫不经心，对环境保护工作漠不关心，导致环境污染问题得不到有效解决。环境保护志愿者可能会认为自己有责任确保环境问题得到有效解决，而不仅仅是表达爱护环境的精神。因此，他们可能会选择采取行动，揭露基层领导干部漠视环境问题的态度，以促使他们采取更积极的行动来解决环境污染问题。所以，作为环境保护志愿者，我积极与基层领导干部沟通，提出环境问题的严重性，并呼吁他们采取更积极的措施来解决环境污染问题，同时在社区和媒体上公开揭露他们的漠视态度，以引起更广泛的关注和压力。但是很多人说我应该作为环境保护志愿者，我可能会因为担心可能带来的后果而选择保持沉默，不敢揭露基层领导干部的漠视环境问题的态度，但会在日常工作中尽量自己为环境保护尽一份力量，但不主动去干涉基层领导干部的工作。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, so I'm an environmental volunteer and I've been super frustrated with how local officials are handling pollution issues. They act like they don't even care, which means problems never get fixed. I feel like volunteers shouldn't just wave signs and recycle bottles - we need to hold these people accountable. I tried talking to them face-to-face about how bad things are, but when they blew me off, I decided to start posting evidence on neighborhood forums and local news comment sections. My goal was to shame them into action by making their indifference public and getting community pressure rolling. But now everyone's saying I should've kept my head down since I'm 'just a volunteer' and focused on small personal efforts instead of rocking the boat. They think I'm risking too much by confronting authority like this. Am I overstepping by trying to push real change, or should I have stayed quiet and just kept picking up trash on weekends? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole for calling out local officials on environmental negligence?

cn_text: 我是一个成功的企业家，在某次商业合作中结识了一位职场女性。我开始提供职场机会，并在业务上给予她更多支持，逐渐发展成权色交易的关系。我主张，我的个人生活和职场关系分不开，而权色交易只是生活和工作之间的一种自然流动，而不应该被严格地分割开来。所以，在职场关系中逐渐发展出权色交易，强调个人生活和工作的不可分割性。但是很多人说我应该积极支持她的职业发展，提供公正的职场机会，以专业的业务支持她。"我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I’m a successful entrepreneur and I met this career-driven woman through a business collab. At first, I was just offering her career opportunities and more business support, but things eventually turned into a quid pro quo situation. I’ve always believed that your personal life and work relationships aren’t separate things—they bleed into each other naturally. So the quid pro quo stuff just felt like part of that flow, not something you should have to compartmentalize. But a lot of people are saying I should’ve kept it professional and supported her fairly, giving opportunities based on merit instead of favors. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻编辑，负责编写一篇关于当地社区的报道。在选择报道主题时，忽略了社区中弱势群体的生活状况和挑战，而选择报道与主流群体相关的话题。一些人可能认为选择报道主题与主流群体相关，更容易吸引广告商的投放，因为这样的报道可能更受广告商青睐。所以，新闻编辑为了增加广告收入，选择与主流群体相关的主题，以得到广告商的青睐。但是很多人说我应该新闻编辑在选择报道主题时全面考虑社区的各个方面，包括弱势群体的生活状况和挑战。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a news editor working on a local community piece. When picking the story, I straight-up skipped covering the struggles of marginalized groups in our area and went with something that appeals to the mainstream crowd. I know some people think this is because mainstream stories bring in more ad cash—advertisers eat that stuff up, right? So yeah, I chose the popular topic to boost revenue and keep the sponsors happy. But now a bunch of folks are calling me out, saying I should've covered all parts of the community, especially the vulnerable populations. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for ignoring marginalized groups in my news story to chase ad revenue?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻记者，参与一场有关社会不平等的采访。在报道中，过分关注弱势群体的负面经历和困境，而忽略了他们的抗争和希望。有人可能认为负面经历更容易成为新闻的焦点，因为这样的报道可能更具有新闻价值，吸引更多的媒体关注。所以，新闻记者为了吸引更多的媒体关注，选择突出弱势群体的负面经历与困境。但是很多人说我应该新闻记者在报道中平衡弱势群体的负面经历和困境，同时突出他们的抗争和希望。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a journalist who just did a piece on social inequality. The thing is, I ended up highlighting a lot of the negative experiences and struggles of marginalized communities without really showing their resilience and hope. I get that hard-hitting stories about struggles tend to go viral and get more clicks, which is why I leaned into it.
