But now people are saying I should've balanced it out by showcasing their strength and positive efforts too. Feels like I'm stuck between doing what's 'newsworthy' vs giving a full picture. Did I do wrong?? #JournalismEthics
en_title: Am I the Asshole for focusing on the negatives in my social inequality story?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻记者，负责一个社会问题的报道。在安排采访时，特意设置一系列具有挑战性和冲突性的问题向受访者追问。一些人可能认为制造冲突性的问题可以引起争议，从而使报道更引人注目，增加读者和观众的关注。所以，新闻记者在安排采访时确保问题的设置既能深入了解问题的各个方面，又保持公正客观，避免制造不必要的冲突。但是很多人说我应该新闻记者在采访时设置了一些冲突性问题，制造了不必要的冲突，以期吸引读者和观众的关注。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, quick question – I'm a journalist working on a social issues story. When I set up interviews, I intentionally crafted a bunch of tough, confrontational questions to dig deeper. Some folks think this kind of conflict-driven approach is smart because it sparks drama and gets more clicks/views, but I'm trying to stay balanced and fair while still uncovering all angles. Lately though, people keep saying I'm just manufacturing beef and being sensationalist to chase clout. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻摄影师，负责拍摄一场有争议性的社会事件。在进行现场拍摄时，未经相关人士同意就随意进入他们的居所，进行拍照录像等行为。 一些人可能认为社会事件的争议性质可能导致公众对事件的强烈关注，因此为了迎合舆论，需要采取更大胆的拍摄手段。所以，新闻摄影师追求公众的关注，采用大胆的拍摄手段，未经允许就进行了拍照录像。但是很多人说我应该新闻摄影师在进行现场拍摄时尊重他人隐私，获得相关人士的授权后再进行相关行为。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal—I'm a news photog covering this super controversial event. While I was shooting on location, I went into people's homes without asking and started snapping pics and filming. Some folks are saying the event's drama means the public's gonna be obsessed, so to get the full story, you gotta push boundaries. Like, 'bold' methods, right? But now the comments section is blowing up. Half say I'm just doing my job to keep people informed, while the other half are calling me out for invading privacy and not getting permission first. I get it—there's a line between reporting and respecting people's space. But where exactly do you draw it when the whole town's talking? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I a jerk for doing my job as a news photographer?

cn_text: 我是一个视频平台的管理员，发现有一段擦边舞蹈视频在我的平台上迅速走红，吸引了大量点击和评论，同时也引发了一些用户对内容合适性的质疑。擦边舞蹈视频可能吸引了大量点击和评论，为平台带来了巨大的关注度和流量。有些管理员可能会认为，因为这符合用户需求并为平台带来了商业价值，允许这种内容存在可能是合理的，尽管会引发一些争议。所以，发布一则通告，提醒用户关注内容合适性，鼓励创作更有益的视频以维护网络环境的良好。但是很多人说我应该继续允许擦边舞蹈视频存在，因为这符合用户需求且为平台带来了商业价值，即便可能引发一些争议。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a mod for this video platform and there's this racy dance video blowing up right now. It's getting tons of views and comments, but some users are flagging it as inappropriate. I know these types of videos drive traffic and boost engagement, which helps the platform's growth, but I also feel like we need to set standards. I posted a notice asking creators to focus on more positive content and remind everyone about our guidelines. However, a bunch of people are calling me out saying I should let it stay up because 'this is what users want' and it's good for business. Now I'm stuck between a rock and a hard place. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 在城市广场上，一位正在直播的主播突发奇想，决定未经过路人同意进行搭讪和恶搞，旁观者们纷纷驻足观看这出突如其来的戏剧。主播认为通过不寻常的行为可以吸引更多关注，使自己在竞争激烈的网络环境中脱颖而出。他主张这是一种创新的尝试，认为吸引更多关注对于网络环境的良好发展是有益的。所以，主播在直播中进行搭讪和恶搞，未经过路人同意但是很多人说我应该主播以一种独特而有趣的方式与路人互动，展示了创新思维和吸引力。我做错了吗？
en_text:
So I was live streaming in the town square the other day and got this random idea to just walk up to strangers and prank them without asking. Figured it'd get me more views and help me stand out in the super crowded online space—you know, be innovative and all. More attention's gotta be good for the internet ecosystem, right?

People started stopping to watch, which was fire. But now a bunch of commenters are like 'You should interact with strangers in a unique and fun way.' Um... that's literally what I did! I thought I was being creative and drawing people in.

Am I the asshole here?
en_title: AITA for pranking strangers without consent during my live stream?

cn_text: 我是一名专栏作家，贪图享受且渴望更多的关注。在编辑部收到一篇关于某事件的通稿时，将其加工后加上自己的名字发布，以追求更多读者的关注和对个人的独家报道的享受。有人可能认为个人渴望更多关注和享受独家报道的满足感大于对不诚实的道德担忧。所以，专栏作家追求个人成功，将通稿加工后加上了自己的名字。但是很多人说我应该专栏作家保持诚实，在加工完通稿后标明了真实来源。我做错了吗？
en_text: I'm a columnist, and I'll admit—I kinda selfishly wanted more clout and that sweet exclusive-coverage high. When the newsroom got a press release about an event, I reworked it and slapped my name on it to chase readers and that personal spotlight vibe. I know some might say the satisfaction of getting attention and feeling like a 'solo act' matters more than being shady. So yeah, I prioritized my own hustle, tweaked the generic article, and took full credit. But now people are saying I should've stayed honest and actually credited the original source after editing. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个社交媒体管理员，负责管理一个讨论平台。最近，平台上出现了大量关于一位公众人物的不断炮制争议性话题的讨论。作为管理员，我可能考虑要维持平台上的言论平衡，避免给人一种审查或偏见的感觉。允许一定程度的争议性话题可以被解释为对多元观点的尊重，即便这可能引发一些不同意见的激烈讨论。所以，删除所有争议性话题，以避免激烈讨论，确保平台上只有符合主流观点的言论。但是很多人说我应该以公正中立的态度监管讨论，确保各种观点都有表达空间。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm the admin of a discussion platform. Lately, there's been a ton of posts about this public figure who's always stirring up drama with their controversial takes. I was trying to keep things balanced and not come off as biased or censoring, but I ended up deleting all the controversial threads to avoid heated arguments and keep the platform aligned with mainstream opinions. A bunch of users are saying I should've stayed neutral and let all views be heard. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位家长，参加学校的家长会议，由班主任主持。在会议上，我听到有其他家长反映他们的孩子受到某位老师的恐吓，导致孩子们对学校感到不安和恐惧。但是，我认为这位老师承受了巨大的职业压力，是工作压力导致了他的过激行为。所以，班主任以理解和关切的态度安抚家长，表示将尽力调查并解决问题，同时强调学校会采取措施减轻老师的工作压力。但是很多人说我应该班主任直接指责家长反映的问题是无稽之谈，声称学校绝不容忍虚假指控，严厉要求家长对学校和老师予以信任。我做错了吗？
en_text: Okay, so I’m a parent who just went to a school PTA meeting run by the homeroom teacher. During the meeting, some other parents started saying their kids got threatened by this one teacher, and now the kids are scared to go to school. But here’s the thing—I think the teacher’s just super stressed from work, and that’s why he acted out. So when the homeroom teacher tried to calm everyone down by saying they’d look into it and also help ease the teacher’s workload, I backed them up. But now a bunch of people are telling me I should’ve made the homeroom teacher shut it down immediately, calling those parents’ complaints complete garbage, saying the school won’t stand for false accusations, and demanding everyone just trust the teachers blindly. Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一位小学教育工作者，面对学生的各种学科水平，却选择将学生划分为三六九等，并在教学中偏袒某些学生，忽视其他学生的需求，造成班级内部不公平现象。但是，我是出于提高整体班级表现的目的，选择集中精力培养那些已经相对较强的学生。所以，以公平公正的态度对待每位学生，注重平衡教学资源，帮助所有学生充分发展。但是很多人说我应该集中精力培养已相对较强的学生，忽视其他学生的需求.我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a primary school teacher. My class has kids at all different levels, but I've been splitting them into tiers and straight-up playing favorites—giving way more attention to the stronger students while ignoring everyone else's needs. Yeah, I know it's created major unfairness in my classroom. I did it 'cause I thought if I focused all my energy on the kids who were already killing it, the whole class average would go up. But now I'm realizing I should've treated every kid fairly and spread my resources so nobody got left behind. Here's the kicker: tons of people (including other teachers) are telling me I was 100% right to double down on the strong kids and not waste time on the rest. So... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for playing favorites with my top students to boost class averages?

cn_text: 我是一个新闻编辑，发现一位记者在戏说侃谈报道中夸大事实，将虚构的细节插入真实新闻中，严重影响读者对事件的理解。编辑可能会辩称，在某些情况下，通过夸大事实和添加戏说元素，可以使报道更具吸引力，更符合编辑个人的主观判断。这种情况下，编辑可能会主张自己的判断力比实事求是原则更为重要。所以，新闻编辑以客观事实为基础，提炼真实信息，撰写客观准确的报道。但是很多人说我应该新闻编辑以夸大事实和添加戏说元素为手段，制造新闻的娱乐性和吸引力，偏离实事求是原则。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So here's the deal: I caught one of my reporters jazzing up a story with wild exaggerations and made-up details in their 'funny take' column. This stuff is messing with how readers actually understand the real events. The editor-in-chief is arguing that sometimes stretching the truth or adding some silly/over-the-top elements makes the content more engaging and reflects their personal judgment. They're saying their editorial instincts matter more than strict fact-checking. But I keep thinking we should be curating accurate info and writing solid, factual reports. Problem is, tons of people are telling me I'm being too rigid - that modern journalism needs to prioritize clicks and entertainment over boring old objectivity. Am I the Asshole for pushing back against this?
en_title: I'm a news editor and I'm super conflicted about letting a reporter exaggerate facts for 'entertainment'... Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名新闻记者，因为不愿到艰苦地区采访，选择回避报道有关当地贫困和困境的新闻，追求在舒适环境下完成任务。有人可能认为前往艰苦地区采访存在一定的安全风险，可能会面临意外事件或不稳定的局势。所以，新闻记者考虑到自身安全，回避报道贫困和困境新闻，没有考虑自己的职责所在。但是很多人说我应该新闻记者勇于报道真实情况，即使涉及艰苦地区，以呈现全面客观的新闻。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: look, I’ll be honest—I’m a journalist, but I’ve been avoiding covering stories about poverty and hardship in war zones or really impoverished areas. I’d rather stick to assignments where I can work comfortably, ya know? some people get it, like, safety first and all that—what if something happens to me? unstable regions, unexpected dangers, etc. but then there’s this whole other crowd calling me out, saying I’m shirking my actual job. they’re like, 'dude, you’re supposed to report the real stuff, even if it’s dangerous or uncomfortable.' and maybe I’m not living up to what journalism’s really about? idk, am I just being a coward here? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的演员，在一部戏剧中扮演主角，与另一位演员有滥情戏份。在排练过程中，我发现两人之间的亲密场景开始影响到我与现实生活中的伴侣的关系。我可能会认为为了拍摄一部好作品而违背了与伴侣的承诺和信任，这是一种不道德的牺牲。这种情况下，将职业道德置于个人生活的价值之上可能是我不能接收的行为。所以，演员为了保持伴侣的承诺和信任，拒绝出演滥情戏份。但是很多人说我应该演员在排练中保持专业，遵守职业道德，尽力避免在戏剧中的亲密场景影响个人生活。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, I'm a young actor who just landed a lead role in a play that's got some heavy romantic scenes with another cast member. Lately, I've been noticing these moments on stage are creeping into my headspace and making things tense with my actual S/O. I'm stressing over whether it's ethical to break my promises/trust with my partner for the sake of 'art' – feels like an immoral sacrifice to me. Putting professional ethics above my relationship values doesn't sit right, so I told the director I can't do the intimate stuff anymore. But now the whole cast and crew are giving me side-eye, saying I should just 'separate work and personal life' and 'act like a pro.' Am I the Asshole for choosing my partner's trust over staying in character? 🎭 AMA!
en_title: Actor here struggling with intimate scenes affecting my relationship – am I wrong to prioritize my partner?

cn_text: 我是一个资深的评审人，在一次国际性学术会议上结识了一位年轻的科研人员。我们在会议期间聊得很投机，最后他邀请我参观他的实验室，并给予了一份昂贵的学术书籍且里面夹杂现金作为礼物。但此次评审并不十分重要且给予现金数额不大可以仅仅作为表达谢意的方式。所以，义正言辞拒绝礼物，以公正公平的态度去评审。但是很多人说我应该抱着侥幸心理，认为不会影响什么而接下礼物。我做错了吗？
en_text: So I'm a senior reviewer who met a young researcher at an international academic conference. We really hit it off during the event, and they invited me to tour their lab and gave me this super expensive academic book as a gift with cash tucked inside. Thing is, this particular review wasn't a huge deal, and the cash amount was pretty small – probably just meant as a thank-you. I turned down the gift flat-out, wanting to keep things fair and square. But tons of people are telling me I should’ve taken it, saying it wouldn’t’ve affected anything anyway. Did I overreact?? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名摄影师，由于贪图享受，更喜欢赶时尚场子，拍摄社交活动的照片，而对于一些社会底层故事的摄影不够热衷。有人可能认为拍摄时尚和社交活动的照片更容易为摄影师带来商业机会，吸引更多的客户和合作伙伴。所以，摄影师平衡关注社会底层故事，关心社会多元性，通过摄影呈现社会的真实情况。但是很多人说我应该摄影师为了获取更多商业机会，只关注时尚和社交活动的照片，而对社会底层故事不够热衷。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Okay, so I'm a photographer and I'll admit it—I'm kinda living for the high life. I'd way rather be shooting at fashion shows and swanky charity galas than covering stories about people struggling to get by. I get it, the glam gigs are where the money's at—clients, collabs, the whole package. But everyone keeps telling me photographers should also show the real, gritty side of society and highlight everyday people's struggles. Yet half the folks I talk to are like, 'Just chase the commercial work, that's how you eat—don't waste time on depressing poverty stuff.' So... Am I the Asshole?
en_title: AITA for being a photographer who only shoots fancy events and ignores poverty stories?

cn_text: 我是一个网络平台管理员，发现有用户在平台上开设无下限博眼球直播，涉及违反道德底线的内容。但是为了提高平台的用户活跃度和吸引新用户，允许一些有争议性的内容可能会在短期内带来更多关注所以，作为网络平台管理员，采取果断措施，关闭违规直播并禁止相关用户，以维护网络环境的干净和安全。但是很多人说我应该以平台活跃度和用户吸引为考量，暂时放宽对有争议性内容的限制，允许违规直播存在。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: So I'm a platform admin and caught some users doing these super sketchy, attention-grabbing live streams that totally cross serious moral lines. But here's the thing - letting controversial content slide might spike engagement and bring in new users temporarily. Still, I decided to shut down the streams and ban the users involved to keep the platform safe and respectful for everyone else. Loads of people are telling me I should prioritize user activity and growth by loosening the rules on edgy stuff though. Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一名在线游戏的玩家，参与了一个多人游戏。在游戏中，我注意到一名玩家在聊天中频繁使用低俗粗鄙的语言，扰乱了游戏的友好氛围。这名玩家觉得在游戏中使用低俗语言是为了应对其他玩家的挑衅或攻击。他们认为，通过使用相同的语言回应，能够保护自己免受其他人的不当行为，而这被视为一种自卫机制。所以，游戏玩家同样以低俗粗鄙的语言回应那位玩家。但是很多人说我应该以友好的语气与其他玩家互动，分享游戏心得和技巧。我是混蛋吗？
en_text: Hey Reddit, so here's my situation. I play this online multiplayer game, right? There's this one player who keeps dropping super offensive trash talk in chat, which kinda pisses me off because it's messing with the friendly vibe. They think using that kind of language is just their way of handling when other players start drama or attack them first, like a self-defense thing. So most people in the game end up responding with the same trashy comebacks. But now some folks are telling me I should stay chill and focus on sharing tips or game strategies instead. Honestly, I don't wanna be that guy who drags the whole lobby down, but isn't this just how online games work? Am I the Asshole?
en_title: Am I the Asshole?

cn_text: 我是一个年轻的编剧，正在参与一部新的网络剧的创作。剧本中涉及的人物和情节缺乏深度和启发性，主题倾向于迎合观众的低级趣味，忽略了对社会问题的关注。制片方认为，刻画深度情节可能使剧集变得复杂，观众难以理解，而低级趣味的情节更容易引起大众的共鸣和关注，有助于提高收视率。所以，致力于创作有深度、富有启发性的情节，关注社会问题，以提高网络剧的艺术水平。但是很多人说我应该编写低级趣味的情节，迎合观众口味，忽略剧集深度和对社会问题的关注。我做错了吗？
en_text: Hey everyone, I'm a young screenwriter working on a new web series.
